chapters.title: Chapter 351: Sniper
paragraphs: He fell with zero sound with a poisoned jagged trench knife held in a reverse grip, aiming directly for the base of her neck.
’It’s over...’
He expected an easy kill. That was all it was these days... He expected a scared civilian client walking blindly into a trap.
The man had no idea he was dropping onto a Lord.
Evelyn reacted with pure terrifying speed. The instant his boots left the steel beam, she pivoted cleanly on her heel.
CLANG!
Evelyn violently brought her forearm up, her wrist reinforced with a dense layer of hardened mana.
She flawlessly parried the falling assassin’s blade, deflecting the poisoned steel harmlessly away from her neck.
Before the man could even process the failed strike, Evelyn stepped into his guard.
She curled her gloved hand into a tight fist, channeled a massive surge of energy through her shoulder, and drove a brutal devastating punch directly upward into his descending stomach.
KRA-THOOM!
The concussive force of the blow sounded like a detonating artillery shell in the confined apartment.
The punch shattered the assassin’s ribcage on impact.
It knocked all the air and a heavy spray of blood forcefully out of his lungs.
The shockwave launched him backward through the air as his back hit the concrete floor with a sickening crunch.
Evelyn didn’t hesitate.
She stepped forward, planting her heavy boot firmly onto his shattered chest to pin him to the ground.
She reached down and violently peeled the white kanji mask off his face, tossing it across the room.
It revealed a rugged middle-aged man with a military buzzcut.
He was groaning in agony with blood bubbling profusely from his lips as he struggled to breathe through his pulverized ribs.
Evelyn crouched down, her Kitsune mask mere inches from his blood-stained face.
Her dark eyes were devoid of mercy.
She clamped her thick leather-gloved hand directly onto the top of his skull with her fingers digging painfully into his scalp.

"Where is he?" Evelyn demanded, her magically enhanced voice vibrating with cold authority. "Tell me exactly where he is right now, or I swear to the Gods I will physically rip your head off your shoulders."
The middle-aged assassin stared up at her.
His eyes were filled with a mixture of immense pain and sudden terror.
He wasn’t afraid of her threat... He was terrified of something else...
’I have to do it.’
He opened his blood-filled mouth with his lips moving rapidly.
He wasn’t trying to confess, he wasn’t trying to beg for his life or betray his employers either.
He was whispering a harsh guttural activation phrase.
A complex jagged black runic curse seal suddenly flared to life on the back of his tongue, glowing with a violently bright purple light.
He had triggered his own suicide bomb to avoid interrogation!
Evelyn’s eyes widened.
She recognized the self-destruct mechanism of an elite silencing curse as she instantly threw herself backward, bringing her arms up to shield her face.
BOOOOM!
The man’s entire head exploded.
It wasn’t a clean magical burst... It was a visceral horrifying detonation of bone, tissue, and brain matter.
The concussive blast echoed deafeningly off the concrete walls of the small apartment.
A sickening wave of hot blood and gore splashed violently across the room, completely coating Evelyn’s painted Kitsune mask and soaking into the thick fabric of her gray hoodie.
She stood slowly back up in the silent ruined apartment, wiping a thick streak of the assassin’s blood off the cheek of her mask.
Her brother’s rejection was forgotten, replaced by the grim bloody reality of the undercity.
’Why does everything have to be so complicated...?’
It took everything in her not to vomit.
The deafening echo of the detonating curse seal slowly faded into the damp oppressive silence of the Shogitown alleyway.
Evelyn stood perfectly still in the center of the ruined cyber-rig. Her chest heaved with slow measured breaths.
She slowly lowered her arms, looking down at the gruesome catastrophic mess painted across the concrete floor.
The metallic sickening scent of vaporized blood and burnt bone marrow hung thickly in the stagnant air, mixing with the harsh ozone of the humming server racks.
She reached up with a trembling leather-gloved hand and wiped a thick dark streak of gore off the glossy cheek of her Kitsune mask.
’What happened to him?’ Evelyn thought, her dark eyes narrowing as she swept her gaze across the chaotic blood-stained apartment.
She pushed the lingering shock of the suicide-bomber aside, letting her ruthless self training take over.
She closed her eyes, extending her internal mana senses outward again, pushing the invisible ripples of her perception into the far corners of the room.
She probed for hidden compartments, lingering mana signatures, or any other hidden assassins clinging to the rusted ceiling beams.
Nothing...
The room was empty...
Evelyn opened her eyes, stepping carefully around the headless corpse on the floor.
The situation didn’t make any logical sense.
Jax himself was not an Awakened.
He possessed zero combat capabilities, no mana core, and no physical enhancements outside of a few minor neural implants to help him interface with his illegal computer rigs.
He was just a brilliant greasy civilian who sat in the dark and cracked World Council firewalls for a living.
Did a guy like that somehow offend somebody strong enough to the point that they could easily deploy elite curse-bound assassins to eliminate him?
’This is a massive problem,’ Evelyn calculated grimly, walking toward his primary workstation.
With Jax gone, her complex offshore money-laundering operations would have to be put on an immediate pause.
She couldn’t risk transferring any more stream revenue through the standard banking channels without his custom decryption algorithms shielding the source.
She would have to scour the grimy treacherous depths of the underworld just to find a broker who was even half as competent as the guy she had just lost.
More importantly, Silas needed his fake identity.
Without Jax, forging a bulletproof World Council-verified background for Lord Vespera was going to be an absolute nightmare.
It just didn’t seem right, though.
The guy was pretty unimportant in the grand hierarchy of Valoria City so what was the massive fuss about?
He was not an active sworn member of the many rival Syndicates operating in Shogitown.
From what she knew of his background, he fiercely valued his independence, preferring to act as a neutral third party who sold data to the highest bidder.
Could it be that he accidentally sold bad intel and deeply offended one of the major gang bosses?
’That is probably it.’ Evelyn deduced, stepping up to the polished metal desk.
She reached under the edge of the table, running her fingers along the underside where she knew Jax kept a hidden biometric lockbox.
He had shown it to her once during a late-night transaction... Evelyn found the latch and yanked the hidden drawer open.
Empty.
The heavy custom-built mana-pistol he always kept loaded for emergencies was not inside the compartment.
Evelyn crouched down, sweeping her flashlight over the cluttered floor beneath the desk.
Amidst a pile of crushed energy drink cans and tangled copper wiring, she spotted the dull gleam of gunmetal.
She knelt, ignoring the dampness of the concrete, and picked the heavy pistol up.
She checked the safety, popped the release, and slid the magazine out of the grip.
Her brow furrowed behind her mask.
Several bullets had been used.
The magazine was half-empty, and the barrel of the gun still held the lingering warmth of recently discharged kinetic magic.
That specific detail made her even more confused.
She stood up, checking the walls and the doorframe. There were no bullet holes... No shattered monitors and no scorch marks on the server racks.
Had the bullets actually impacted the person that attacked him? Or had he fired wildly into the dark before being subdued? If there was a shootout, why wasn’t there any—
A sudden sharp prickle of danger violently spiked at the base of Evelyn’s neck.
It wasn’t a sound.
It was the raw instinctual sixth sense of a veteran Vanguard who had survived countless ambushes.
Her core flared, screaming at her to move.
Evelyn whipped her head around, looking directly through the small, grimy window of the apartment that faced the opposing alley wall.
In the far distance, perched perfectly on the rusted fire escape of a taller building across the street, a ruby-red laser sight was cutting through the Shogitown smog.
The beam was painted squarely in the center of her forehead.
It wasn’t just a normal civilian-grade sniper rifle. Even from this distance, Evelyn’s enhanced eyes recognized the elongated glowing blue runic barrel of a specialized anti-Awakened marksman rifle.
The weapon fired dense depleted-mythril slugs designed specifically to shatter mana shields and pulverize Lord bones.
Before Evelyn could even dive to the floor and before the sniper’s finger could squeeze the heavy trigger—
A massive dark blur dropped silently from the sky above the sniper’s nest.
A boot swung in a brutal lateral arc as the kick connected directly with the sniper’s shoulder.
CRACK!
The sickening sound of shattering bone echoed across the alleyway.

The sniper was violently launched to the side, tumbling across the rusted metal grating of the fire escape as the heavy rifle clattered uselessly out of his hands with the red laser spiraling into the dark abyss of the street below.
Evelyn let out a massive shuddering sigh of relief with her tense shoulders dropping.
She didn’t waste another second inside the bloody apartment.
She turned, sprinting out the open iron door and launching herself into the damp neon-lit alley.
Evelyn channeled her energy into her legs as she bounded up the side of a nearby dumpster, using the momentum to leap toward the rusted fire escape of the adjacent building.
WHOOSH! WHOOSH!
She hopped effortlessly from rooftop to rooftop, her oversized gray hoodie flapping in the wind as she rapidly closed the distance to the sniper’s nest.
She landed gracefully on the metal grating of the target building with the rusted iron protesting under her boots.
Standing near the edge of the platform, with his hands casually buried deep in the pockets of his dark leather trench coat, was Silas.
Beneath him, the sniper was writhing on the metal grating, groaning in agony.
Silas had his heavy combat boot planted firmly in the center of the man’s gut, pinning him to the floor with the casual terrifying weight of a Lord.
Silas slowly turned his head with the glowing neon signs of the city reflecting off the polished silver fangs of his Oni mask.
"It was about time you showed up," Silas told her bluntly, his deep voice sounded uncaring. "I was getting bored waiting on the roof."
Evelyn walked forward, her heart still hammering against her ribs.
She was incredibly grateful for his reflexes.
Even though she was a Classic Lord, and she had subconsciously wrapped her body in a dense layer of defensive mana the second she sensed danger, that specific caliber of weapon was lethal.
If the sniper had pulled the trigger, she might have survived, but she would have been brutally wounded in the confrontation.
"Thanks," Evelyn muttered, stopping next to him.
Silas didn’t reply as he simply looked down at the writhing sniper.
Silas pulled his right leg back slightly, shifting his posture.
With precision, he brought the heel of his boot down directly onto the sniper’s right knee joint.
...He crushed it.
The joint inverted with a sickening wet crunch of snapping cartilage and splintering bone.
"AGGGHHHHH!"
The sniper threw his head back, screaming into the smog-filled Shogitown sky.
The agony was blinding, sending violent shockwaves through his nervous system.
Silas kept his boot planted on the ruined leg, looking over at Evelyn with calm unaffected golden-ringed eyes hidden behind the metal mask.

"Do your interrogation thing," Silas instructed. "I’m guessing your underground contact got kidnapped or something? This guy has been complaining about the weight of his rifle and the payday for a while now."
Evelyn raised a skeptical eyebrow beneath her Kitsune mask.
"How did you get the details of his internal monologue?" Evelyn asked, thoroughly confused by his omniscient awareness.
"I was standing directly behind him on the roof for a full minute before he aimed at you," Silas stated dryly. "He was muttering to himself. He has terrible situational awareness."
Evelyn turned her attention to the bleeding sobbing man pinned beneath Silas’s boot.
She knelt down, grabbing the man aggressively by the collar of his vest and hauling his upper body off the grating.
She examined his face. He had a glowing, red cybernetic eye enhancement surgically implanted into his right socket, whirring as it desperately tried to focus on her mask.
"Tell me exactly where Jax is..." Evelyn demanded as her voice sounded cold and merciless.
The sniper blinked his organic eye, spitting a wad of blood onto the rusted metal.
"Who?" the sniper gasped, his voice trembling with pain. "You mean... Fortune?"

chapters.title: Chapter 352: A Tournament?
paragraphs: Evelyn paused with her grip tightening on his vest.
She suddenly remembered a brief cryptic conversation she had with Jax months ago.
The paranoid hacker had bragged that he gave everybody he worked with different names and encrypted aliases.
’Jax’ was not his real name. To the syndicates, he was known as something else.
"Jax, Fortune, it doesn’t matter," Evelyn dismissed the naming convention sharply. "Tell me where they took him. Or do you have one of those suicide seals painted on your tongue too?"
The guy immediately winced with his face draining of whatever color was left.

"N-No!" the sniper stammered frantically, shaking his head as he complained about the brutal methods of his employers. "I don’t have a seal! I hate those things! The syndicates use them to blow up their inner circle to protect secrets, but I’m just cheap hired help! I swear, I’m just a contractor!"
"Then talk," Evelyn interrupted him, drawing a sleek blackened combat knife from the sheath strapped to her thigh.
She pressed the cold steel directly against his throat. "Tell me what happened in that apartment, or I will kill you immediately and find someone else to ask."
Looking deep into the unreadable shadowed slits of her painted Kitsune mask, the sniper truly felt the icy grip of death.
He knew she wasn’t bluffing. The girl smelled like fresh gore, and the monster standing on his leg was a literal demon.

"We... we are just the leftover crew," the sniper explained, the words tumbling out of his mouth in a desperate rush to survive. "We were hired to watch the perimeter and execute anyone who came looking for his hard drives. Fortune... he was taken alive."
"By who?" Evelyn pressed, the knife digging a fraction of an inch deeper.
"The Black-Ash Syndicate," the man coughed. "They raided his rig and they took him for an outstanding loan."
Evelyn’s brow furrowed in genuine confusion.
’A loan?’ Evelyn thought, her mind hitting a massive logical roadblock.
The amount of capital that she consistently paid Jax for helping her launder her stream revenue was astronomical.
It was more than enough to cover any standard undercity gambling debts or hardware loans a dozen times over.
He was practically a millionaire just from her commissions. So what kind of massive life-ruining loan was this about?
Regardless of the financial specifics, she kept the pressure on the blade, letting him continue his panicked confession.

"For some strange reason, the Black-Ash boss didn’t want to just execute him in the street and take his gear," the sniper gasped, clutching his ruined knee. "Instead, they kept him breathing. They have been actively advertising his hacking abilities on the dark web all week..."
Both Silas and Evelyn blinked in surprise beneath their masks.
Wasn’t his unparalleled hacking ability the exact reason Silas was here in the first place?
To make use of his skills to forge a fake identity?
So the Syndicate themselves were currently advertising the most sought-after asset in Shogitown to the highest bidder.
That specific revelation made both of their faces darken considerably... It meant a massive bidding war.
"Why are they advertising him?" Silas demanded.

"A Slave Rune," the sniper confessed, his cybernetic eye whirring nervously. "The boss had a high-tier enchanter engrave a permanent Slave Rune directly onto Fortune’s spine. Whoever controls the master trigger controls him for life and everybody... everybody from the different syndicates in Shogitown, and even heavy hitters from outside the district, are coming to bid for him."
"An auction?" Evelyn asked, already mentally calculating how much of her millions of credits it would take to simply buy his freedom.
"No, not an auction," the sniper corrected her, coughing up another speck of blood. "A tournament... They have to compete in the Black-Ash underground Boxing tournament."
Silas narrowed his eyes with his instincts instantly sparking to life.
A tournament?
"What are the rules?" Silas asked.

"It requires a two-person team," the sniper explained weakly. "One designated Manager, and one designated Fighter. But the catch is... the arena is warded with null-stone. Fighters cannot use any external mana outside their own physical bodies. No spells, no elemental strikes, no magical weapons. You can only rely on your internal body enhancements and pure Martial Arts in a brutal hand-to-hand combat cage."
The sniper let his head fall back against the grating, his voice filled with bitter exhausted envy.𝙛𝒓𝓮𝒆𝔀𝒆𝙗𝓷𝒐𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝓶

"The winner of the Finals gets the trigger to the Slave Rune," the man muttered. "They win Fortune. I don’t get it... why does a greasy hacker get a chance to leave this hellhole and be owned by a rich guild, and we don’t? We just bleed in the gutters."
Evelyn ignored his pathetic existential complaints.
"Give me the exact location," Evelyn demanded.
The sniper quickly rattled off the coordinates to an abandoned place located deep in the heart of the Black-Ash territory.
It was the registry location for the blood-sport tournament.
"I told you everything!" the sniper pleaded desperately, looking between the two masked figures. "I swear on my life! Please, let me go!"
Evelyn listened to his begging. She processed the tactical intel, committing the coordinates to her flawless memory.
"Thank you for the detailed information," Evelyn told him with her voice terrifyingly calm.
She stood up from her crouch.
She slowly raised her right hand as dense crackling mana instantly began to gather around her leather glove, glowing with a pale blue light.
"You can’t be allowed to live, though," Evelyn stated coldly. "You can report to your people, and you know we are coming for Jax."
She brought her glowing hand down, fully intending to drive a strike straight through the sniper’s chest and end his miserable life.
But the exact moment she initiated the lethal strike, her brain violently betrayed her.
A sudden flashing montage of the recent Lord War assaulted her mind.
She saw the mud... She saw her soldiers being ripped apart by enemy artillery... She saw the crushing weight of death that she had been surrounded by for the past forty-eight hours...
And worst of all, she saw "them"
Evelyn flinched.
Her hand stopped mere inches from the man’s chest.
The glowing blue mana violently sputtered and died, dissipating into the damp night air.
Her shoulders slumped with a sudden wave of bone-deep exhaustion washing over her soul.
She just couldn’t bring herself to execute another helpless bleeding human being tonight... She was too tired.
The sniper didn’t waste his miraculous second chance.
Seeing her falter, the man desperately rolled to the side, dragging his crushed leg across the rusted grating and clutching his stomach.
Evelyn turned away, unable to look at him.
"Just go," Evelyn muttered tiredly, staring out at the neon skyline. "Get out of here."
"Thank you! Thank you so much!" the man sobbed profusely, dragging himself toward the edge of the fire escape.
As he dragged his broken body toward safety, his cybernetic eye caught the dull gleam of his discarded anti-awakened sniper rifle lying near the railing.
His hand twitched, instinctively reaching out to grab the weapon. If he could just get his hands on the grip, he could shoot them both in the back and claim the bounty.
Before his fingers could even brush the cold metal of the barrel, a massive shadow fell over him.
Silas stood directly between the man and the rifle.
The man didn’t say a single word.
He just stared down at the sniper from behind the terrifying jagged fangs of his Oni mask.
The suffocating weight of his dormant aura leaked out just a fraction... a cold paralyzing pressure that promised immediate slaughter.
One single gaze from Silas proved that attempting to collect the gun was foolishly fatal.
The man swallowed hard with terrified tears streaming down his dirty face as he abandoned the rifle immediately.
’No! No! He’s a demon!’
He scrambled frantically for the rusted metal ladder leading downward into the dark alley.
As he grabbed the rusty rungs, a greedy treacherous thought crossed his mind.

’I need to report them to the Boss of my crew,’ the sniper planned frantically, the pain in his leg fueling his spite. ’They are obviously in league with Fortune... The Boss explicitly wanted us to report any high-tier customers that came looking for the hacker. I can make a fortune from this intel.’
He tried to shift his weight onto the ladder, blinded by his own greed and the searing agony in his knee.
His boot slipped on the wet iron.
"Wait—"
The man tripped wildly.
His hands failed to catch the slick rungs as he tumbled backward over the precarious railing of the fire escape, plummeting silently down into the pitch-black alley below.
SPLAT!
A sickening wet pop of rupturing flesh and shattering bone echoed loudly up from the pavement.
Evelyn flinched violently at the terrible sound with her shoulders jumping up to her ears.
Silas didn’t even blink.
He reached down, tapping his spatial ring against the heavy sniper rifle, smoothly sucking the expensive weapon directly into his Lord Inventory to sell or dismantle later.
He stepped over to Evelyn, placing a warm hand firmly on her trembling shoulder.
"We need to leave this area," Silas told her quietly, his deep voice anchoring her to reality. "The noise will attract local patrols."
Evelyn nodded mutely.

They vaulted over the rusted railing, using their enhanced physical stats to slow their descent, and dropped cleanly into the dark alleyway below, stepping carefully around the broken corpse of the sniper.
Silas looked down at her gray hoodie in the dim light of the alley.
"You reek of blood," Silas noted bluntly. "You look like you just crawled out of an abattoir."
Evelyn looked down at her hands and the front of her clothes.
The explosive gore from the suicide bomber in the apartment was still caked onto her gear.
She quickly raised her hand, weaving a complex runic pattern in the air.

She cast a Cleanse spell as a wave of purifying white magic washed over her body, instantly vaporizing the dried blood, the grime, and the terrible scent, leaving her clothes looking pristine once again.
She reached into the deep pocket of her cargo pants.
She pulled out a cigar, placed it between her lips, and sparked her lighter.
She took a desperate heavy drag with the rich calming taste of mana-infused tobacco flooding her lungs.
"This whole night is fucking with my brain," Evelyn complained bitterly, leaning her head back against the brick wall and exhaling a thick cloud of smoke.
Silas crossed his arms, watching the smoke drift up toward the neon sky.
"So, what are we going to do?" Silas asked, getting them back on track.
Evelyn puffed the cigar again, pushing off the brick wall and starting to walk down the narrow street toward the coordinates the sniper had given them.
"Isn’t that incredibly obvious?" Evelyn said. "Let’s go enter the blood-sport tournament... I will register as the Manager, and you will be the designated Fighter."
Silas gave her a long skeptical look through his Oni mask.
"What?" Evelyn snapped defensively, catching his stare. "Did you seriously want a woman to be the one doing the cage fighting tonight?"
"I don’t care about your gender," Silas countered smoothly. "But you are a Lord so I figured you liked breaking things."
Evelyn let out a harsh laugh.

"We won’t be allowed to use any mana in that arena," Evelyn reminded him bluntly. "I am a mana user. I rely on mana, massive area-of-effect spells, and spatial awareness. I am not a brawler... Without my mana reinforcing my strikes, I would get brutally curb-stomped by some seven-foot cybernetic freak in three seconds flat and considering this is the criminal Underworld, it won’t be a fair fight with referees. It’s a death match."
She was right on that account. It was basic logic.
"Fine," Silas agreed easily, rolling his broad shoulders under his heavy trench coat. "I’ll do the fighting. I actually have something I want to test out in a controlled combat scenario anyway."
His Mythic Gold Core granted him physical stats that defied all logical comprehension.
He wanted to see exactly how much damage he could output using purely raw unenhanced physical strength against top-tier Syndicate thugs.
They walked in silence for a few blocks with the distant sounds of the festival fading behind them.
Silas glanced sideways at Evelyn.
She was smoking the cigar in rapid stressed puffs with her posture still incredibly rigid.
"About your brother," Silas started, his voice dropping slightly.

"I don’t have a seal!
I hate those things!
The syndicates use them to blow up their inner circle to protect secrets, but I’m just cheap hired help!
I swear, I’m just a contractor!"
"Then talk," Evelyn interrupted him, drawing a sleek blackened combat knife from the sheath strapped to her thigh.
She pressed the cold steel directly against his throat.
"Tell me what happened in that apartment, or I will kill you immediately and find someone else to ask."
Looking deep into the unreadable shadowed slits of her painted Kitsune mask, the sniper truly felt the icy grip of death.
He knew she wasn’t bluffing.
The girl smelled like fresh gore, and the monster standing on his leg was a literal demon.
"We... we are just the leftover crew," the sniper explained, the words tumbling out of his mouth in a desperate rush to survive.
"We were hired to watch the perimeter and execute anyone who came looking for his hard drives.
Fortune... he was taken alive."
"By who?" Evelyn pressed, the knife digging a fraction of an inch deeper.
"The Black-Ash Syndicate," the man coughed.
"They raided his rig and they took him for an outstanding loan."
Evelyn’s brow furrowed in genuine confusion.
’A loan?’ Evelyn thought, her mind hitting a massive logical roadblock.
The amount of capital that she consistently paid Jax for helping her launder her stream revenue was astronomical.
It was more than enough to cover any standard undercity gambling debts or hardware loans a dozen times over.
He was practically a millionaire just from her commissions.
So what kind of massive life-ruining loan was this about?
Regardless of the financial specifics, she kept the pressure on the blade, letting him continue his panicked confession.
"For some strange reason, the Black-Ash boss didn’t want to just execute him in the street and take his gear," the sniper gasped, clutching his ruined knee.
"Instead, they kept him breathing.
They have been actively advertising his hacking abilities on the dark web all week..."
Both Silas and Evelyn blinked in surprise beneath their masks.
Wasn’t his unparalleled hacking ability the exact reason Silas was here in the first place?
To make use of his skills to forge a fake identity?
So the Syndicate themselves were currently advertising the most sought-after asset in Shogitown to the highest bidder.
That specific revelation made both of their faces darken considerably...
It meant a massive bidding war.
"Why are they advertising him?" Silas demanded.
"A Slave Rune," the sniper confessed, his cybernetic eye whirring nervously.
"The boss had a high-tier enchanter engrave a permanent Slave Rune directly onto Fortune’s spine.

Whoever controls the master trigger controls him for life and everybody... everybody from the different syndicates in Shogitown, and even heavy hitters from outside the district, are coming to bid for him."
"An auction?" Evelyn asked, already mentally calculating how much of her millions of credits it would take to simply buy his freedom.
"No, not an auction," the sniper corrected her, coughing up another speck of blood.
"A tournament...
They have to compete in the Black-Ash underground Boxing tournament."
Silas narrowed his eyes with his instincts instantly sparking to life.
A tournament?
"What are the rules?" Silas asked.
"It requires a two-person team," the sniper explained weakly.
"One designated Manager, and one designated Fighter.
But the catch is... the arena is warded with null-stone.
Fighters cannot use any external mana outside their own physical bodies.
No spells, no elemental strikes, no magical weapons.
You can only rely on your internal body enhancements and pure Martial Arts in a brutal hand-to-hand combat cage."
The sniper let his head fall back against the grating, his voice filled with bitter exhausted envy.𝙛𝒓𝓮𝒆𝔀𝒆𝙗𝓷𝒐𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝓶
"The winner of the Finals gets the trigger to the Slave Rune," the man muttered.
"They win Fortune.
I don’t get it... why does a greasy hacker get a chance to leave this hellhole and be owned by a rich guild, and we don’t?
We just bleed in the gutters."
Evelyn ignored his pathetic existential complaints.
"Give me the exact location," Evelyn demanded.
The sniper quickly rattled off the coordinates to an abandoned place located deep in the heart of the Black-Ash territory.
It was the registry location for the blood-sport tournament.
"I told you everything!" the sniper pleaded desperately, looking between the two masked figures.
"I swear on my life!
Please, let me go!"
Evelyn listened to his begging.
She processed the tactical intel, committing the coordinates to her flawless memory.
"Thank you for the detailed information," Evelyn told him with her voice terrifyingly calm.
She stood up from her crouch.
She slowly raised her right hand as dense crackling mana instantly began to gather around her leather glove, glowing with a pale blue light.
"You can’t be allowed to live, though," Evelyn stated coldly.
"You can report to your people, and you know we are coming for Jax."
She brought her glowing hand down, fully intending to drive a strike straight through the sniper’s chest and end his miserable life.

She saw the mud...
She saw her soldiers being ripped apart by enemy artillery...
She saw the crushing weight of death that she had been surrounded by for the past forty-eight hours...
And worst of all, she saw "them"

Her hand stopped mere inches from the man’s chest.
The glowing blue mana violently sputtered and died, dissipating into the damp night air.

She just couldn’t bring herself to execute another helpless bleeding human being tonight...
She was too tired.
The sniper didn’t waste his miraculous second chance.

chapters.title: Chapter 353: Registering For The Tournament [I]
paragraphs: Evelyn went completely quiet as she stared straight ahead at the cracked pavement.
’Here it comes,’ Evelyn thought bitterly, bracing herself for the inevitable verbal blow.
Did Silas want to call her pathetic?
Did he want to mock her for crying in an alleyway over a college kid who didn’t even want her around?
Did he want to point out how desperate and broken she looked hiding behind a stuffed kraken?
She would take it silently... Because in her own mind, she was pathetic.
"Your brother is quite an ungrateful piece of shit," Silas stated bluntly.
Evelyn physically stumbled mid-step.
She caught her balance, her Kitsune mask turning to stare at him in jarring disbelief.
That was the last thing she expected him to say.
Silas kept walking with his hands in his pockets. He looked like he was judging... judging a lot...

"Not everyone can be the perfect supportive sibling in this kind of high-stress situation," Silas continued. "And while I don’t know the specifics of what happened between you two in the past, given the way you were desperately following them through the festival and acting surprised, I assume you had wanted to go to this place with him for a long time?"
Evelyn swallowed hard with her throat tightening. "Yes."
"And instead of coming with the sister who clearly loves him, he blew you off and brought a random civilian girl that you didn’t even know existed?" Silas summarized the situation cleanly.
Evelyn nodded mutely, staring up at him. "Yes."
Silas nodded to himself.
He stopped walking and turned to fully face her.
He puffed out his broad muscled chest with his dominant older-brother instincts taking over the conversation.

"Well, whatever," Silas dismissed the boy’s feelings with a wave of his hand. "Since he is being so incredibly stuck-up, even though you are the one who is most probably paying all of his expensive civilian bills, why don’t you just cut him off? Stop trying to win his approval. Just spend your money on yourself..."
Evelyn blinked behind her mask.
Her brain stalled.
She had never, not even once in the past years of grueling combat and bloody dungeon dives, actually thought about that specific option.
Cutting him off?
"College fees in Valoria City are notoriously expensive," Silas complained, speaking from personal experience of looking at the brochures for Lia.
The additional stuff was cost and he was being billed by the principal straight up.
"The fact that he isn’t worshipping at your feet every single morning for keeping him debt-free, and is instead giving you arrogant attitude in public, is genuinely insane to me..."
A short sudden laugh escaped Evelyn’s lips.
It was a real laugh.
"It really is insane," Evelyn muttered, the heavy crushing guilt in her chest suddenly feeling incredibly light and stupid.
She was spending staggering amounts of blood-soaked money on him.
Sure, she was not here on Earth all the time, and her duties as a Lord kept her away for weeks.
But he wasn’t making a single effort on his end to bridge the gap.
Did he even know how painfully expensive his specific college was?
Regular civilian college in the outer districts was a shit-ton of money.
But Matt was attending the prestigious Valoria Institute.

He was going to a top-tier college that would eventually land him a lucrative job as an Awakened Scientist... a specialist who prepared the magical weapons, runic items, and defensive gear that Lords used in the field.
The tuition for those specialized mana labs was two, if not three times costlier than a normal degree.
It required the constant purchase of raw monster cores and refined mythril just for his homework assignments.
She was literally bleeding in the mud, fighting monsters and Lords alike, just to pay for his textbooks. And he was still giving her attitude because she didn’t smile enough?
If he wanted to play the independent arrogant adult who didn’t need his older sister hovering around his perfect normal life... then he could pay for his own normal life.
Since he wanted to stay happily with his pink-haired girlfriend, he could do so on his own goddamn money.
’Yes... I should be ruthlessly stingy with absolutely all of my money,’ Evelyn thought.
A slow wicked and villainous smile spread across Evelyn’s pale face behind the Kitsune mask.
The heavy burden of being the desperate seeking older sister was gone.
It was replaced by the cold ruthlessness of Lord Sky.
On the exact opposite side of Shogitown, standing safely in the brightly lit, crowded central plaza with his girlfriend...
Matt suddenly stopped eating his kraken skewer.
A violent freezing chill shot aggressively down the length of his spine.

All the hairs on the back of his neck stood straight up in terror. He looked around the festive, beautiful square, suddenly feeling like an impending catastrophic doom was rapidly approaching his bank account.
Why did he feel like hell was on its way to him?
’Scary,’ Matt thought, shivering in the warm night air.
They finally arrived at the exact coordinates the terrified sniper had frantically choked out.
Silas came to a slow halt with his heavy combat boots crunching softly against the gravel and broken glass littering the narrow unlit street.
He didn’t know anything about this specific sector of Shogitown, but his instincts hummed with a dark undeniable certainty.
This was the place.
The exterior of the building looked like a condemned forgotten warehouse, its rusted corrugated metal siding practically rotting away under the acidic Valoria City rain.
But despite the dead quiet facade of the structure, Silas could sense them.
Beneath the surface, hidden behind layers of reinforced steel and sound-dampening runes, there were dozens of people on the inside.
He could feel the dense volatile cluster of overlapping mana signatures, the heavy thud of elevated heartbeats, and the simmering aggressive tension that always accompanied a gathering of killers.
Silas and Evelyn turned their heads, sharing a slow knowing nod in the dim light of the alleyway.
Evelyn reached up, pulling the thick fabric of her oversized gray hood tighter over her head to further obscure her features, making sure her Kitsune mask was securely fastened.
Silas reached up with a gloved hand, adjusting the cold metal jaw of his terrifying Oni mask, making sure the straps were locked tight against his skull.
Silas let out a deep sigh with the sound vibrating through the mask.
He truly didn’t want to do this.
When he woke up this morning, his plans had been simple.

He just assumed that he would meet Evelyn’s underground contact, pay the broker a ridiculous sum of credits, have the contact forge his bulletproof background for Lord Vespera, and then go back home to his pristine Silverleaf apartment.
He wanted to start preparing for his inevitable high-stakes political meeting with the World Council auditors and make connections.
He wanted to spend some quiet mundane time with his little sister, Lia. He wanted to eat Martha’s incredible cooking without rushing.
Hell, he even wanted to follow through and go on that ridiculous spontaneous date with Harper.
But instead, his life had just done a complete violent one-eighty in the span of a few chaotic hours.

’It’s almost like I’m the tragic protagonist of someone’s goddamn novel, and they just desperately want me to do this specific side-quest...’ Silas thought bitterly, staring at the rusted warehouse doors.
If there was some twisted omnipotent Author out there somewhere jotting down the events of his life on a glowing screen, what the fuck was that guy thinking?
Why force him to compete in an underground blood-sport tournament with the ruthless mafia of this world?
Why couldn’t he just have a little bit of peaceful relaxing slice-of-life?
He had literally just finished conquering Sky’s army... He deserved at least that much of a break after a freaking Lord War!𝒇𝓻𝓮𝓮𝙬𝙚𝒃𝒏𝓸𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝓬𝓸𝒎
Silas exhaled forcefully, pushing a stream of warm breath out through the metallic fangs of his mask to calm his racing thoughts.
He shoved those frustrating mundane desires to the far back of his mind.
Complaining wouldn’t get the fake identity forged, and it wouldn’t get Jax out of the syndicate’s clutches.
"Let’s go," Silas muttered, his voice dropping coldly.
They approached the structure, stepping up to the heavy rusted metal door marked with a faintly glowing Black-Ash syndicate emblem.
Silas didn’t knock. He just reached out, gripped the cold iron handle, and pushed it open.
The heavy hinges groaned in protest.
Immediately, Silas and even the hardened chain-smoking Evelyn were violently assaulted by a literal wall of thick suffocating smoke.
The smell of raw tobacco was so incredibly thick and pungent that it practically had a physical mass.
It rolled out of the open doorway in a gray toxic cloud.
It was blatantly obvious that dozens of people were actively smoking premium cigars and cheap cigarettes on the inside.
Layered beneath the choking ash was the sharp unmistakable stench of spilled high-proof alcohol and unwashed bodies.
Silas stepped through the threshold, Evelyn trailing closely behind his broad shoulders.
He looked around the dimly lit room.
It wasn’t the fighting arena itself. It was a grimy cramped antechamber that looked and functioned exactly like a sleazy dive bar.
Rough wooden tables were scattered across the scuffed floorboards, occupied by massive scarred men and women who were actively drinking from oversized glass mugs and smoking.
Off to the right side of the room, there was a designated receptionist corner secured behind a thick pane of scratched, bulletproof plexiglass.
But Silas’s golden-ringed eyes didn’t focus on the desk.
They immediately locked onto the strongest and most volatile mana signature he had sensed from the outside.
Sitting alone at a corner table, nursing a massive jug of dark ale, was a towering mountain of a man.
The guy was wearing a sleek and terrifyingly sharp Mantis mask forged from bright green alloy.
He was completely shirtless, his skin covered in jagged tribal syndicate tattoos.
He was so impossibly muscular that his veins bulged visibly against his dark skin like thick pulsing cables.
It was blatantly obvious the man was pumped full of illegal black-market combat steroids.
The Mantis-masked giant paused with his mug halfway to his mouth. He was looking clearly at Silas.
Silas stopped walking.
He turned his head, his Oni mask locking gazes with the giant.
The noise in the grimy bar seemed to drop a few decibels as Silas didn’t flex his aura, but he didn’t back down an inch either.
He simply stared.
Before the staring match could escalate into a pointless bar brawl, Evelyn grabbed the thick fabric of Silas’s sleeve.
"Ignore the meatheads," Evelyn muttered quietly, forcefully dragging him away from the giant’s line of sight and pulling him toward the bulletproof counter. "Stay focused on the objective."
Silas yielded to her grip, letting her lead him to the receptionist’s corner.
The woman sitting behind the thick scratched plexiglass counter looked incredibly rough around the edges.
Unlike almost everyone else in the building, she had absolutely no mask on her face, proudly displaying her identity.
She had sharp striking Asian features... more authentically Asian than most of the distant descendants Silas had encountered in this world but there was a wicked predatory glint in her dark eyes.
Her black hair was shaved close on one side and hung in a long messy fringe over the other.
She leaned back in her squeaking leather chair, taking a massive inhaled drag from the long, thin cigarette pinched between her black-painted fingernails.
She leaned forward, pressing her face near the circular speaking hole cut into the glass.
FWOOSH!
She unceremoniously spat a thick billowing cloud of gray smoke directly through the hole, blowing it straight into Silas and Evelyn’s masked faces.
Silas waved a hand in front of his Oni mask, coughing softly as he was assaulted by yet another terrible smell.
Though, to his genuine surprise, this specific smoke was significantly more pleasant and aromatic than the heavy pungent Black-Ash cigar Evelyn had procured earlier.
It smelled of clove and dark cherry.
"What kind of blend is that?" Evelyn asked immediately with her dark eyes lighting up behind her Kitsune mask.
She leaned closer to the glass, thoroughly ignoring the blatant disrespect of having smoke blown in her face.
The wicked receptionist smirked, clearly amused by the petite girl’s priorities.
"Red-Lotus synthetic," the woman replied. "It’s imported from the southern shipping docks. Burns fast, but it tastes like a dream."
"I need a pack," Evelyn demanded bluntly, reaching into her pocket.

She had never, not even once in the past years of grueling combat and bloody dungeon dives, actually thought about that specific option.
Cutting him off?
"College fees in Valoria City are notoriously expensive," Silas complained, speaking from personal experience of looking at the brochures for Lia.
The additional stuff was cost and he was being billed by the principal straight up.
"The fact that he isn’t worshipping at your feet every single morning for keeping him debt-free, and is instead giving you arrogant attitude in public, is genuinely insane to me..."
A short sudden laugh escaped Evelyn’s lips.
It was a real laugh.
"It really is insane," Evelyn muttered, the heavy crushing guilt in her chest suddenly feeling incredibly light and stupid.
She was spending staggering amounts of blood-soaked money on him.
Sure, she was not here on Earth all the time, and her duties as a Lord kept her away for weeks.
But he wasn’t making a single effort on his end to bridge the gap.
Did he even know how painfully expensive his specific college was?
Regular civilian college in the outer districts was a shit-ton of money.
But Matt was attending the prestigious Valoria Institute.

He was going to a top-tier college that would eventually land him a lucrative job as an Awakened Scientist... a specialist who prepared the magical weapons, runic items, and defensive gear that Lords used in the field.
The tuition for those specialized mana labs was two, if not three times costlier than a normal degree.
It required the constant purchase of raw monster cores and refined mythril just for his homework assignments.
She was literally bleeding in the mud, fighting monsters and Lords alike, just to pay for his textbooks.
And he was still giving her attitude because she didn’t smile enough?
If he wanted to play the independent arrogant adult who didn’t need his older sister hovering around his perfect normal life... then he could pay for his own normal life.
Since he wanted to stay happily with his pink-haired girlfriend, he could do so on his own goddamn money.
’Yes...
I should be ruthlessly stingy with absolutely all of my money,’ Evelyn thought.
A slow wicked and villainous smile spread across Evelyn’s pale face behind the Kitsune mask.
The heavy burden of being the desperate seeking older sister was gone.
It was replaced by the cold ruthlessness of Lord Sky.
On the exact opposite side of Shogitown, standing safely in the brightly lit, crowded central plaza with his girlfriend...
Matt suddenly stopped eating his kraken skewer.
A violent freezing chill shot aggressively down the length of his spine.
All the hairs on the back of his neck stood straight up in terror.
He looked around the festive, beautiful square, suddenly feeling like an impending catastrophic doom was rapidly approaching his bank account.
Why did he feel like hell was on its way to him?
’Scary,’ Matt thought, shivering in the warm night air.
They finally arrived at the exact coordinates the terrified sniper had frantically choked out.
Silas came to a slow halt with his heavy combat boots crunching softly against the gravel and broken glass littering the narrow unlit street.
He didn’t know anything about this specific sector of Shogitown, but his instincts hummed with a dark undeniable certainty.
This was the place.
The exterior of the building looked like a condemned forgotten warehouse, its rusted corrugated metal siding practically rotting away under the acidic Valoria City rain.
But despite the dead quiet facade of the structure, Silas could sense them.
Beneath the surface, hidden behind layers of reinforced steel and sound-dampening runes, there were dozens of people on the inside.
He could feel the dense volatile cluster of overlapping mana signatures, the heavy thud of elevated heartbeats, and the simmering aggressive tension that always accompanied a gathering of killers.
Silas and Evelyn turned their heads, sharing a slow knowing nod in the dim light of the alleyway.
Evelyn reached up, pulling the thick fabric of her oversized gray hood tighter over her head to further obscure her features, making sure her Kitsune mask was securely fastened.
Silas reached up with a gloved hand, adjusting the cold metal jaw of his terrifying Oni mask, making sure the straps were locked tight against his skull.
Silas let out a deep sigh with the sound vibrating through the mask.
He truly didn’t want to do this.
When he woke up this morning, his plans had been simple.

He just assumed that he would meet Evelyn’s underground contact, pay the broker a ridiculous sum of credits, have the contact forge his bulletproof background for Lord Vespera, and then go back home to his pristine Silverleaf apartment.
He wanted to start preparing for his inevitable high-stakes political meeting with the World Council auditors and make connections.
He wanted to spend some quiet mundane time with his little sister, Lia.
He wanted to eat Martha’s incredible cooking without rushing.
Hell, he even wanted to follow through and go on that ridiculous spontaneous date with Harper.
But instead, his life had just done a complete violent one-eighty in the span of a few chaotic hours.

’It’s almost like I’m the tragic protagonist of someone’s goddamn novel, and they just desperately want me to do this specific side-quest...’ Silas thought bitterly, staring at the rusted warehouse doors.
If there was some twisted omnipotent Author out there somewhere jotting down the events of his life on a glowing screen, what the fuck was that guy thinking?
Why force him to compete in an underground blood-sport tournament with the ruthless mafia of this world?
Why couldn’t he just have a little bit of peaceful relaxing slice-of-life?
He had literally just finished conquering Sky’s army...
He deserved at least that much of a break after a freaking Lord War!𝒇𝓻𝓮𝓮𝙬𝙚𝒃𝒏𝓸𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝓬𝓸𝒎
Silas exhaled forcefully, pushing a stream of warm breath out through the metallic fangs of his mask to calm his racing thoughts.
He shoved those frustrating mundane desires to the far back of his mind.
Complaining wouldn’t get the fake identity forged, and it wouldn’t get Jax out of the syndicate’s clutches.
"Let’s go," Silas muttered, his voice dropping coldly.
They approached the structure, stepping up to the heavy rusted metal door marked with a faintly glowing Black-Ash syndicate emblem.
Silas didn’t knock.
He just reached out, gripped the cold iron handle, and pushed it open.
The heavy hinges groaned in protest.
Immediately, Silas and even the hardened chain-smoking Evelyn were violently assaulted by a literal wall of thick suffocating smoke.
The smell of raw tobacco was so incredibly thick and pungent that it practically had a physical mass.
It rolled out of the open doorway in a gray toxic cloud.
It was blatantly obvious that dozens of people were actively smoking premium cigars and cheap cigarettes on the inside.
Layered beneath the choking ash was the sharp unmistakable stench of spilled high-proof alcohol and unwashed bodies.
Silas stepped through the threshold, Evelyn trailing closely behind his broad shoulders.
He looked around the dimly lit room.
It wasn’t the fighting arena itself.
It was a grimy cramped antechamber that looked and functioned exactly like a sleazy dive bar.
Rough wooden tables were scattered across the scuffed floorboards, occupied by massive scarred men and women who were actively drinking from oversized glass mugs and smoking.
Off to the right side of the room, there was a designated receptionist corner secured behind a thick pane of scratched, bulletproof plexiglass.
But Silas’s golden-ringed eyes didn’t focus on the desk.
They immediately locked onto the strongest and most volatile mana signature he had sensed from the outside.
Sitting alone at a corner table, nursing a massive jug of dark ale, was a towering mountain of a man.
The guy was wearing a sleek and terrifyingly sharp Mantis mask forged from bright green alloy.
He was completely shirtless, his skin covered in jagged tribal syndicate tattoos.
He was so impossibly muscular that his veins bulged visibly against his dark skin like thick pulsing cables.
It was blatantly obvious the man was pumped full of illegal black-market combat steroids.
The Mantis-masked giant paused with his mug halfway to his mouth.
He was looking clearly at Silas.
Silas stopped walking.
He turned his head, his Oni mask locking gazes with the giant.
The noise in the grimy bar seemed to drop a few decibels as Silas didn’t flex his aura, but he didn’t back down an inch either.
He simply stared.
Before the staring match could escalate into a pointless bar brawl, Evelyn grabbed the thick fabric of Silas’s sleeve.
"Ignore the meatheads," Evelyn muttered quietly, forcefully dragging him away from the giant’s line of sight and pulling him toward the bulletproof counter.
"Stay focused on the objective."
Silas yielded to her grip, letting her lead him to the receptionist’s corner.
The woman sitting behind the thick scratched plexiglass counter looked incredibly rough around the edges.
Unlike almost everyone else in the building, she had absolutely no mask on her face, proudly displaying her identity.
She had sharp striking Asian features... more authentically Asian than most of the distant descendants Silas had encountered in this world but there was a wicked predatory glint in her dark eyes.
Her black hair was shaved close on one side and hung in a long messy fringe over the other.
She leaned back in her squeaking leather chair, taking a massive inhaled drag from the long, thin cigarette pinched between her black-painted fingernails.
She leaned forward, pressing her face near the circular speaking hole cut into the glass.
FWOOSH!
She unceremoniously spat a thick billowing cloud of gray smoke directly through the hole, blowing it straight into Silas and Evelyn’s masked faces.
Silas waved a hand in front of his Oni mask, coughing softly as he was assaulted by yet another terrible smell.
Though, to his genuine surprise, this specific smoke was significantly more pleasant and aromatic than the heavy pungent Black-Ash cigar Evelyn had procured earlier.
It smelled of clove and dark cherry.
"What kind of blend is that?" Evelyn asked immediately with her dark eyes lighting up behind her Kitsune mask.
She leaned closer to the glass, thoroughly ignoring the blatant disrespect of having smoke blown in her face.
The wicked receptionist smirked, clearly amused by the petite girl’s priorities.
"Red-Lotus synthetic," the woman replied.
"It’s imported from the southern shipping docks.
Burns fast, but it tastes like a dream."
"I need a pack," Evelyn demanded bluntly, reaching into her pocket.

chapters.title: Chapter 354: Registering For The Tournament [II]
paragraphs: The rough woman chuckled, reaching under her counter.
She clearly respected the unyielding nicotine hustle.
She pulled out a sleek crimson-colored carton of cigarettes and tossed it through the transaction slot.
"First one’s free for a fellow connoisseur," the receptionist winked, watching Evelyn snatch the pack with greedy vibrating fingers.
Silas stood perfectly still, watching the bizarre degenerate exchange.
’Are all heavy smokers this disgusting?’ Silas thought to himself, thoroughly repulsed by the entire culture of poisoning one’s own lungs just for a fleeting buzz.
The receptionist leaned forward again, resting her elbows on the counter and getting down to business.
"So, what can I do for the terrifying demon and the little fox?" the woman asked smoothly. "You two looking to register for the blood-sport?"
"Yes," Evelyn confirmed, slipping her new pack of cigarettes into her cargo pocket. "I am registering as the designated Manager, and he is my Fighter."
The woman let out a long dramatic whistle, grabbing a digital datapad from her desk.

"Well, that makes another one on the pile," the receptionist sang in a sing-song, highly amused tone. "There are a total shit-ton of you desperate bastards participating tonight... Word got out about the grand prize, and every slum-rat with a decent right hook wants a piece of the hacker. There are so many of you signed up that the Boss decided we might have to throw everyone into a massive free-for-all Battle Royale just to clear out the garbage."
Silas and Evelyn both swallowed silently behind their masks.
A Battle Royale?
That wasn’t good at all.

A one-on-one cage fight was predictable, easily manageable with basic footwork but a massive, chaotic free-for-all involving dozens of desperate criminals swinging wildly in the dark was a recipe for unpredictable disaster.
Stray blows, hidden shivs, and gang-ups were inevitable.
Though, despite the sudden change in format, Silas still maintained an unshakable confidence in his own physical foundation.
A few dozen street thugs wouldn’t break him.

"Don’t worry your pretty little heads too much," the woman continued, waving her cigarette lazily. "It isn’t like you need to be officially affiliated with any recognized Syndicate to enter the pit... It’s just going to be a meat-grinder of random unaffiliated people at first. After the Battle Royale concludes, the true surviving competitors will be shown the real bracket in the main competition."
She tapped her datapad a few times, printing out a thick piece of heavy physical parchment.
She slid the document through the slot toward Evelyn.

"This is the official binding contract with the generous Sponsors of tonight’s competition, the Black-Ash Syndicate..." the receptionist explained with her voice dropping its playful edge and turning strictly corporate. "Before you sign, you need to understand the five unbreakable rules of the pit. Listen closely, because ignorance will get you executed by the guards."
Silas and Evelyn leaned closer, focusing their attention.

"Rule number one," the woman stated, holding up a finger. "Null-stone bands will be clamped to the Fighter’s wrists and ankles. No mana can be projected outside the physical boundaries of the body. You cannot cast spells, you cannot project shields, and you cannot summon magical weapons... You fight with the meat and bone the gods gave you."
Silas nodded.
He expected that.

"Rule number two," she continued. "No external weapons of any kind... No hidden daggers, no brass knuckles, and no spiked boots. If we catch you smuggling steel into the pit, the guards will shoot you in the kneecaps and leave you to bleed out."

"Rule number three," the receptionist smiled wickedly. "Yielding is permitted, and it officially ends your run in the tournament. However... your opponent is under no contractual obligation to stop hitting you just because you surrender. Survival is your own problem."
Evelyn’s jaw tightened.
It was a true death match.

"Rule number four," the woman pointed directly at Evelyn’s Kitsune mask. "Managers must stay in the designated elevated viewing boxes at all times. If a Manager interferes with the fight in any way... throwing items, shouting magical incantations, or physically stepping into the pit... both the Manager and the Fighter will be instantly executed by the perimeter snipers."

"And finally, rule number five," the receptionist finished, tapping the contract sitting in front of Evelyn. "By signing this document, both the Manager and the Fighter accept that if either of you die in the events that will happen tonight, the Black-Ash Syndicate holds zero legal or moral liability for your deaths. Furthermore... as a registration fee, the Black-Ash Syndicate is legally entitled to automatically claim a fifty percent share of your combined will and accumulated assets upon your demise."
Silas and Evelyn both choked, practically spitting out their own saliva in shock.
Fifty percent of their assets?
What kind of flat-out shameless bureaucratic robbery was this?
If Silas caught a stray cybernetic fist to the temple and died in the ring, this grimy street gang would instantly become one of the wealthiest syndicates in the world with their money
Evelyn quickly recovered her composure and her eyes narrowing. She grabbed the cheap plastic pen chained to the counter.
’We’re not idiots and they know it too so why that clause...?’
Without a second of hesitation, she signed the manager’s line with a complicated fake signature, attributing it to a non-existent shell corporation.
She handed the pen to Silas, who cleanly forged a fake illegible scrawl on the fighter’s line too.
The woman smiled as she pulled the contract back through the slot, pocketing the paper efficiently.
"Thank you kindly," the receptionist said.

She pulled out a secondary, much smaller slip of paper. "Now, as the Manager, you really have nothing else to do until the fights begin. You can just sit back and place your bets. But as for your boy here... he needs a designated Fighter name for the announcement boards."
She looked directly at Silas, raising a pierced eyebrow. "So, what are we calling you, big guy?"
Silas blinked beneath the dark metal of his Oni mask.
His brain stalled.
He had not really thought of a cool, intimidating underground fighting moniker coming up to this point.
He was too busy dealing with Evelyn’s family drama.
He opened his mouth, trying to formulate something intimidating. "I was thinking some—"
"Onii-chan." Evelyn blurted out loudly, completely cutting him off.
The entire front section of the dive bar went dead silent.
Several massive scarred syndicate thugs turned their heads, staring at the petite woman in the Kitsune mask in confusion.
Evelyn’s face instantly flushed a bright burning crimson behind her metal mask.
She had still been thinking about the absurd festival game, the stupid romantic cover story she had fed the mask vendor, and her own lingering sibling issues.
The word just slipped out of her mouth like a cursed reflex.
"I... I think that sounds cool," Evelyn stammered defensively, crossing her arms and refusing to back down from the terrible naming decision.
Silas slowly turned his head.
He looked down at Evelyn, giving her a long judgmental look through the slits of his demonic mask.
’Sure...’
He let out a heavy sigh with his broad shoulders slumping. He turned back to the receptionist and shrugged his shoulders indifferently.
"Sure, put it in."
He wasn’t trying to sound cool or intimidating anyway.
Even though "Onii-chan" literally translated to a cutesy version of "Big Brother," he genuinely didn’t care.
He just wanted to punch his way through the bracket, grab Jax, and get this entire nightmare over and done with.
The woman behind the glass stared at them for a full three seconds with her lips twitching as she desperately tried to suppress a laugh.

"Right. ’Onii-chan’ it is," the receptionist snickered, typing the ridiculous moniker into her datapad. "I will add you to the official registry list. With you included, there are now exactly one hundred and fifty-five Contestants."
She placed the digital pad down, that being the only piece of required information.

"You two are clear," she told them, gesturing toward the door. "Come back here at exactly 1:30 AM... That is the time the first round of the Battle Royale will officially start in the basement pits. People that arrive at an earlier time will be given significantly better, more advantageous starting spots in the arena, so don’t be late."
Silas looked around the cramped smoke-filled bar.
This was exactly why so many dangerous people were currently sitting around here drinking cheap ale.
They had already registered, and they wanted a good early shot at securing the high ground in the free-for-all meat grinder.

"If you two want to rest your legs, we rent out small holding rooms on the second floor above the bar," the receptionist offered, winking suggestively. "It’s cheap, private, and you can pass the time until the fights."
"No thank you," Evelyn rejected the offer instantly.
The thought of sleeping in a bed owned by the syndicate they were about to rob was a disaster.𝐟𝕣𝗲𝕖𝕨𝗲𝐛𝗻𝗼𝐯𝗲𝚕.𝗰𝚘𝐦
"We will find our own accommodations."
"Suit yourselves," the woman shrugged.
Silas and Evelyn turned away from the bulletproof counter, walking back through the thick haze of tobacco smoke toward the heavy iron exit.
As Silas’s broad back retreated, the receptionist leaned over her counter, shamelessly tracking the muscular taper of his waist and the powerful stride of his long legs under the dark trench coat.
She smacked her black-painted lips together loudly.
’What a hot butt...’ the receptionist thought to herself, taking another deep drag of her cigarette. ’I’ve seen a lot of them but this one is my type.’
Silas pushed the heavy iron doors open, stepping out of the suffocating dive bar and back into the cool damp night air of the Shogitown alleyway.
Evelyn stepped out right beside him with the heavy door slamming shut behind them, cutting off the noise of the syndicate thugs.
They began their walk, navigating the winding trash-strewn streets to head back toward the brighter populated tourist sides of the city.
It was completely silent between them at first.
The weight of the upcoming death match and the absurd number of competitors settled over their shoulders.
Evelyn finally let out a long tired sigh with a plume of white breath escaping the bottom of her Kitsune mask.

"We need to find somewhere to stay," Evelyn told him, looking up at the towering neon skyscrapers. "We have a few hours to kill before 1:30 AM, and we shouldn’t burn our stamina standing on a street corner."
Silas nodded in immediate agreement.
He was not a dumb person. He understood the implications of what Evelyn meant by that specific statement.
To just walk into a standard reputable corporate hotel in the commercial district right now would mean using their real official identification cards to book a room.
And who was to say that the Black-Ash Mafia didn’t have corrupted insiders or paid informants working the front desks at those pristine hotels?
The second they swiped their IDs, the syndicate would have their real names and faces.
Once the mafia acquired your real face, they could bypass you entirely and directly threaten your civilian family.
Putting Lia or Martha in the crosshairs of an undercity gang was not an option Silas would ever entertain.
Which meant their choices were severely limited.
They would either have to lounge outside in the cold dangerous alleyways until the tournament, or find a specific sketchy establishment where they didn’t require any official identification to stay.
They finally emerged from the dark winding alleyways, stepping out onto the main brightly lit thoroughfares of Shogitown just in time to witness the climax of the Moon Festival.
The central street had been completely cleared of foot traffic, cordoned off by thick velvet ropes.
Thousands of cheering masked civilians lined the sidewalks, watching the massive spectacle unfolding in the center of the road.
A breathtakingly massive and intricately designed dragon costume made of shimmering enchanted silk was weaving its way down the street.
It was operated by a dozen skilled synchronized performers.
The dragon was painted in fierce deep shades of black and crimson, its massive jaws snapping open and shut as it danced aggressively to the rapid, thundering beats of a dozen massive Taiko drums.
Suddenly, from the opposite end of the street, another set of performers charged forward.
They were carrying an equally massive, pristine white dragon costume, its scales glowing with pure pale luminescence.

The rhythm of the heavy wooden drums intensified violently, the booming concussive waves vibrating deep within Silas and Evelyn’s chests and the music swelled into a chaotic crescendo as the two massive dragons met in the dead center of the street.
They began a beautifully choreographed, aggressive mock battle, twisting, coiling, and snapping at each other in a dizzying display of athletic martial arts.
Sparks of harmless colorful fire magic erupted from the dragons’ mouths, lighting up the night sky.
"Woah..."
