’What a hot butt...’ the receptionist thought to herself, taking another deep drag of her cigarette. ’I’ve seen a lot of them but this one is my type.’
Silas pushed the heavy iron doors open, stepping out of the suffocating dive bar and back into the cool damp night air of the Shogitown alleyway.
Evelyn stepped out right beside him with the heavy door slamming shut behind them, cutting off the noise of the syndicate thugs.
They began their walk, navigating the winding trash-strewn streets to head back toward the brighter populated tourist sides of the city.
It was completely silent between them at first.
The weight of the upcoming death match and the absurd number of competitors settled over their shoulders.
Evelyn finally let out a long tired sigh with a plume of white breath escaping the bottom of her Kitsune mask.
"We need to find somewhere to stay," Evelyn told him, looking up at the towering neon skyscrapers.
"We have a few hours to kill before 1:30 AM, and we shouldn’t burn our stamina standing on a street corner."
Silas nodded in immediate agreement.
He was not a dumb person.
He understood the implications of what Evelyn meant by that specific statement.
To just walk into a standard reputable corporate hotel in the commercial district right now would mean using their real official identification cards to book a room.
And who was to say that the Black-Ash Mafia didn’t have corrupted insiders or paid informants working the front desks at those pristine hotels?
The second they swiped their IDs, the syndicate would have their real names and faces.
Once the mafia acquired your real face, they could bypass you entirely and directly threaten your civilian family.
Putting Lia or Martha in the crosshairs of an undercity gang was not an option Silas would ever entertain.
Which meant their choices were severely limited.
They would either have to lounge outside in the cold dangerous alleyways until the tournament, or find a specific sketchy establishment where they didn’t require any official identification to stay.
They finally emerged from the dark winding alleyways, stepping out onto the main brightly lit thoroughfares of Shogitown just in time to witness the climax of the Moon Festival.
The central street had been completely cleared of foot traffic, cordoned off by thick velvet ropes.
Thousands of cheering masked civilians lined the sidewalks, watching the massive spectacle unfolding in the center of the road.
A breathtakingly massive and intricately designed dragon costume made of shimmering enchanted silk was weaving its way down the street.
It was operated by a dozen skilled synchronized performers.
The dragon was painted in fierce deep shades of black and crimson, its massive jaws snapping open and shut as it danced aggressively to the rapid, thundering beats of a dozen massive Taiko drums.
Suddenly, from the opposite end of the street, another set of performers charged forward.
They were carrying an equally massive, pristine white dragon costume, its scales glowing with pure pale luminescence.

The rhythm of the heavy wooden drums intensified violently, the booming concussive waves vibrating deep within Silas and Evelyn’s chests and the music swelled into a chaotic crescendo as the two massive dragons met in the dead center of the street.
They began a beautifully choreographed, aggressive mock battle, twisting, coiling, and snapping at each other in a dizzying display of athletic martial arts.
Sparks of harmless colorful fire magic erupted from the dragons’ mouths, lighting up the night sky.
"Woah..."

chapters.title: Chapter 355: A Place To Stay
paragraphs: Evelyn, completely mesmerized by the beauty of the ancient tradition, unknowingly reached out her hand.
Her smaller leather-gloved fingers wrapped tightly around Silas’s large calloused hand.
Silas blinked in genuine surprise, looking down at their joined hands, and then up at her Kitsune mask.
But he didn’t pull away.
He gently squeezed her fingers back, turning his attention to the dancing dragons.
It was a truly beautiful breathtaking display.
For a few minutes, the blood, the syndicates, and the looming death match faded into the background.
...They were just two tired people enjoying a festival.
At the end of the long intricate play, the drums slowed to a deep heartbeat.
The black and red dragon bowed its massive head, and the white dragon intertwined its long, silk body around its rival.
The two dragons settled peacefully against the cobblestone, warming up to each other in a symbol of harmonious balance.
The massive crowd erupted into deafening joyous cheers, tossing handfuls of pink cherry blossom petals into the air.
Evelyn reluctantly let go of Silas’s hand as the crowd dispersed.
They continued walking down the sidewalk as the noise returning to normal.

"That was incredible," Evelyn blabbed enthusiastically, her voice uncharacteristically light and full of wonder. "The coordination required to move those silk constructs without tangling the mana lines is top-tier. I am really thankful that you pushed me to stay here and see it with you, Silas..."
Silas smiled beneath his Oni mask, glad he could bring a fraction of normal joy to her chaotic life.
Suddenly, Evelyn stopped walking. She snapped her fingers with an epiphany striking her brain.
"I know exactly where we can stay without using our IDs in this district," Evelyn announced, her dark eyes shining with sudden mischievous brilliance.
Silas blinked, crossing his arms.
"Are you sure? It has to be completely off the grid."
"I am positive," Evelyn nodded. But as she spoke, a sudden blush crept up her neck, visibly reddening her pale skin even behind the edges of her mask.
She quickly grabbed his sleeve again, forcefully carrying him off down a side street.
Ten minutes later, they arrived in front of their destination.
Silas stared up at the massive gaudy building.
It was painted entirely in a blinding shade of neon pink, decorated with glowing pulsing heart-shaped runes.
The sign above the automatic sliding doors read "Lover’s Rest" in bright cursive holographic letters.
It was a classic Love Hotel.
"Uhh..." Silas muttered, his brain completely short-circuiting as he stared at the sleazy architecture.
"Do not make this weird," Evelyn commanded him fiercely with her own face burning as she forcefully dragged him through the automatic glass doors and into the heavily perfumed lobby.
The lobby was decorated in tacky red velvet wallpaper and plush, curved sofas.
Soft incredibly sleazy jazz music played through hidden speakers.
They walked up to the front desk.
The receptionist, an older woman wearing far too much makeup and a low-cut blouse, looked up at the broad-shouldered young man in the demonic mask and the petite young woman in the Kitsune mask.
She didn’t ask for names, IDs, or guild affiliations as discretion was the entire business model.
The woman smiled a wide inappropriate smile, instantly jumping to the most degenerate conclusions.
"Welcome, young lovers," the woman purred, sliding a heavy brass key across the counter.
She didn’t even bother charging them upfront. "I have a room for you... Room 402, top floor. It has a reinforced reinforced bed frame."
Evelyn snatched the key, trying to walk away, but the woman leaned over the counter.
"You two should procreate like wild beasts tonight," the receptionist encouraged them shamelessly, winking at Silas. "Make sure to do it loudly! We pride ourselves on a lively atmosphere!"
Silas stared at the woman in horror.
’Elu already milked me...’
The woman suddenly reached into a glass bowl on the counter and grabbed a handful of small glowing blue capsules.
She forcefully shoved the pills directly into Silas’s large hand.
"Here, big guy, take some stamina boosters on the house," the woman urged him enthusiastically. "You are going to need them to last longer with a fiery girl like her! Make sure you fill her up good!"
Both Silas and Evelyn physically cringed, their souls trying to leave their bodies to escape the agonizing excruciatingly awkward conversation.
"We are leaving now," Silas stated flatly, grabbing Evelyn by the hood of her sweater and speed-walking directly toward the velvet-lined staircase.
They practically sprinted up the four flights of stairs.
As they climbed higher into the building, the noise became undeniable.
Muffled thumping, heavy panting, and loud explicit moans echoed from almost every single closed door they passed.
’Are people really this constantly sexually active?’ Silas wondered to himself, genuinely disturbed by the volume of reproductive energy happening around them.
Not that he minded but then again, he wasn’t here with his girls or he would have joined in... If they wanted...
’Elu would though, she’s kinky like that but for Morwenna... I’m not so sure.’
They finally got to room 402 and shoved the key into the lock. They burst inside, slamming the heavy wooden door behind them.
Strangely, despite the sleazy exterior and the terrifying lobby, the room was incredibly clean.
’Damn...’
Silas had fully sworn that the bedsheets would be filthy and the floors sticky, but it was actually quite luxurious.
A massive circular bed sat in the center of the room, positioned beneath a large mirror bolted to the ceiling.
Evelyn didn’t waste a second admiring the decor.
She immediately raised her hands, extending her dense blue mana outward.
She expertly wove a complex soundproof barrier, sealing the entire room off from the horrific moaning sounds of the hallway.
She then reached deep into her cargo pocket, pulling out a small sleek metallic gadget.
She tapped the button on the top.
BZZZT.
A silent invisible localized EMP wave pulsed outward from the device, instantly sweeping the room.
Within seconds, Silas heard the distinct popping sounds of several hidden recording devices, cameras, and audio bugs hidden in the lamps and mirrors violently short-circuiting and dying.
"There," Evelyn exhaled a massive breath of relief, putting the EMP gadget away. "We are finally alone... It is quiet, it is secure, and nobody knows we are here."
They were going to be locked in the same intimate room with a massive circular bed for the next few hours, but Silas genuinely didn’t mind.
It was a necessity, and they were both exhausted.
Silas walked over and sat down heavily on the edge of the plush bed with the mattress sinking under his weight.
He unbuttoned the top of his heavy trench coat to vent some heat.
"What is the exact time right now?" Evelyn asked, walking over to the small attached bathroom to inspect the facilities.
Silas reached into his pocket, pulling out his smartphone. He tapped the screen, checking the digital clock.
"It’s exactly 9:00 PM," Silas reported, shaking his head.
Time was flying by so incredibly fast today.
He had woken up in the real world and now he was sitting in a Valoria City Love Hotel.
"I am going to call Martha quickly to check in," Silas told her, unlocking the phone.
"Okay, it’s safe to broadcast through the barrier," Evelyn called out from the bathroom.
She poked her Kitsune mask out the door. "I am going to take a quick bath to wash the rest of the alleyway grime off my skin."
She closed the bathroom door, and seconds later, Silas heard the sound of rushing water.
Silas hit the call button. The line rang twice before a familiar warm voice picked up.
"Master Silas!" Martha answered happily. "Is everything going well with your business meeting?"

"Yes, Martha, it’s fine," Silas lied smoothly, omitting the part about the suicide bombers and the blood-sport tournament. "But I wanted to let you know that I will be out for quite a while. I have a lot of paperwork to sort through, and I won’t be able to come back home tonight. I’ll see you tomorrow or so."

"Oh, I completely understand, Master," Martha replied, her voice taking on a sudden motherly tone. "You are a growing, successful young man. It is only natural that your ’meetings’ run late into the night..."
Silas frowned. "It really is just business, Martha."
"Of course it is," Martha agreed entirely too quickly.

There was a brief pause, followed by a hushed serious whisper. "But Master Silas... please, make sure to use proper protection tonight. Before the woman you left with uses your child to lock you down and extract heavy child support from your new funds."
Silas stared at his phone in blank disbelief.
Martha genuinely thought he was out trying to impregnate Evelyn in a hotel room right now.
Silas couldn’t help it as he burst out laughing.
"I will keep that advice in mind, Martha," Silas chuckled, shaking his head. "Just make sure Lia finishes her homework and stays safe."
"Always, Master. Have a wonderful night," Martha promised, hanging up the call.
Silas shut his phone off, tossing it onto the bedside table.
He leaned forward, resting his elbows on his knees, and closed his eyes.
He needed to focus. He was going to be in a brutal, bare-knuckle fist brawl with dozens of trained enhanced criminals in a few hours.
And with the null-stone bands clamped to his wrists, he wouldn’t be able to project any of his vast oceanic mana outside of his physical body.
But the receptionist had specifically stated the rules.
You couldn’t use mana outside but she never said anything about circulating mana internally.
Silas wanted to use his internal mana to activate the Second Form of his Tide-Blade Arts: Rip Current Perception.

Usually, this technique required him to project a wide thin film of water into the air around him, allowing him to physically feel the subtle shifts in air currents and perfectly read the weak points of his enemies.
That was exactly how he wanted it to function in the cage tonight.
He wanted to see their physical weak points without expending a single drop of mana outside of his body.
If he could achieve that, he could strike them with precision, ending massive brawls instantly with a single devastating punch to a flaw in their stance.
Silas focused his mind, drawing the crushing weight of his Gold Core up through his chest.
He tried to carefully manifest the thin, magical film of water directly behind his own retinas, keeping the spell entirely contained within his own skull.
He pushed the mana into his eyes.
Instantly, a sharp stinging pain flared behind his ocular nerves.
Silas gasped with his eyes flying open.
His vision was completely blurred, like he was trying to look through a thick pane of frosted glass underwater.
The light of the room smeared into painful streaks of neon pink.
He blinked rapidly, cutting off the mana flow until his vision slowly cleared.
He tried again... He used different, highly complex variations of the internal mana flow, trying to thin the water film, trying to mix it with energy.
But every single attempt yielded the same terrible result. It just blurred his vision, making him effectively blind.
He let out a frustrated sigh, rubbing his temples.
It was a brilliant theory, but the execution was immensely difficult to master on such short notice.
Click!
The sound of the bathroom door unlocking broke his concentration.
Silas looked up, his instincts expecting Evelyn to walk out fully dressed and ready to plot their tournament strategy.
As the wooden door swung open, a thick humid cloud of warm steam rolled out from the bathroom, carrying the sweet scent of cheap hotel soap.
Evelyn stepped out into the bedroom.
She wasn’t wearing her oversized gray hoodie or her baggy cargo pants.
She had apparently washed her clothes in the sink and hung them up to dry as she was currently wearing nothing but a small, incredibly thin white hotel towel wrapped securely around her chest.
Her dark hair was soaking wet, clinging to her pale damp shoulders. A blush painted her cheeks as she realized how compromising the situation was.
"I had to wash my clothes, they smelled like gore even with the spell so I am drying them s—" Evelyn started to explain defensively, taking a step forward onto the carpet.
But her wet bare foot caught the slick, polished brass transition strip separating the bathroom tile from the bedroom floor.
Evelyn mistakenly slipped as her balance completely vanished.
"Haah..."
She let out a sharp gasp with her reflexes instantly kicking in.
She threw her arms out wildly, managing to twist her body and catch her balance just before she could crash violently onto the floor.
She managed to stop herself from falling so she was safe.
But in the frantic twisting motion to save her balance, her arms had abandoned the towel.
The thin white fabric slipped cleanly from her chest. It fell silently to the floor, pooling in a damp heap around her ankles.
Evelyn froze.
She stood there, undeniably naked in the center of the brightly lit neon-pink hotel room.
Silas, still sitting on the edge of the circular bed, still wearing his dark trench coat and his terrifying metal Oni mask, blinked his golden-ringed eyes.
He stared directly at her exposed flawless form, his brain completely flatlining as it tried to process the sudden escalation of events.
"...Oh?" Silas muttered with the single syllable echoing loudly in the quiet soundproof room.

chapters.title: Chapter 356: Freedom
paragraphs: Evelyn sat rigidly on the edge of the plush circular bed.
The heavy soundproofed silence of the neon-pink Love Hotel room pressed against her eardrums.
Her painted Kitsune mask rested casually on the bedside table, exposing the deep anxious frown marring her pale face.

She was currently wearing a completely different set of clothes. After the disastrous towel-drop incident that had effectively short-circuited both of their brains just ten minutes prior, she had desperately raided her inventory.
Her heavy gray combat hoodie and cargo pants were still damp from the emergency sink-wash so she didn’t have any spare gear.
She had fully expected this Shogitown excursion to be a fast single-way trip.
Get in, pay the hacker, get the identity forged, and get out. She had not packed for an overnight stay in a sleazy brothel.
Her only backup clothing was a set of casual loungewear she kept stashed away for emergencies.
She was wearing a massive oversized red hoodie that swallowed her petite frame as the sleeves hung past her knuckles.
Paired with it was a pair of extremely short, black athletic shorts that exposed the long pale length of her thighs.
It wasn’t like she actively wanted to wear it.
It offered zero protection and lacked any hidden holsters for her daggers.
She felt exposed, vulnerable, and very embarrassed too as she sat with her knees pulled tightly together, staring at the floor.
Silas sat opposite her, leaning back against the velvet headboard of the bed.
He still wore his dark trench coat and his heavy boots. His terrifying Oni mask remained firmly clamped over his face.
He had his arms crossed over his broad chest, and his golden-ringed eyes were shut tight behind the metal slits.
Evelyn watched him for a long quiet moment.

"Do you want to sleep or something?" Evelyn asked, her voice quiet and breaking the heavy silence. "We have a few hours before we have to head back into the streets. You could take the bed. I’ll take the velvet chair..."
"No," Silas answered bluntly, not opening his eyes.
His deep voice rumbled through the mask.
"I don’t feel sleepy at all," Silas added.
His biology was fueled by a Mythic-tier Gold Core.
While normal humans required eight hours of rest to repair their cellular damage, his body was practically a self-sustaining engine.
’Even though Elu drained me... Sleep is merely an option.’
He could fight for days on end without feeling a single drop of fatigue and right now, his mind was racing too fast to even consider resting.
Silas let out a slow measured sigh.
He needed a viable way to handle this upcoming tournament without putting himself through unnecessary stress.
The null-stone bands were the main issue.
The receptionist had explicitly stated the rules... There was no pushing mana outside the physical boundaries of the body. No spells, no external shields, no elemental blasts.
’Not that I need them.’
But Silas was cautious as he knew exactly how the criminal underworld operated.

If pushing mana outside was strictly prohibited, but using mana inwardly was left unmonitored or technically allowed by the bands, then every single Syndicate thug in that cage was going to exploit that loophole.
They would use their internal mana to aggressively strengthen their muscle fibers, harden their bones, and accelerate their reflexes.
It would turn a standard boxing tournament into a high-speed meat grinder.
’It’s not like I’m scared,’ Silas thought calmly to himself in the dark.
He wasn’t.
He was a Lord and he possessed a physical foundation that defied all metrics.
He was far more powerful than any street-level criminal, cybernetic or otherwise.
But he didn’t want to take any stupid chances right now.

One lucky strike to the temple from a guy with a reinforced steel fist could do some damage depending on who did it but right now, he wanted to continue his training... He wanted to use his Tide-Blade Arts.
Evelyn noticed the subtle tension radiating from his broad shoulders as she knew that brooding posture all too well.
"I will take a rest, then," Evelyn announced, shifting her weight.
She swung her bare legs up onto the plush mattress, lying down on her back and staring up at the mirrored ceiling.
The physical exhaustion of the day was finally catching up to her.
Silas kept his eyes closed.
"Wait. Before you go to sleep."
Evelyn cracked her dark eyes open, looking over at him.
She reached into the deep pocket of her red hoodie.
Her trembling fingers pulled out another Silverleaf cigar she had been saving.
She desperately needed the nicotine to calm her racing nerves so she placed the dark tobacco between her lips and reached for her plasma lighter.
SMACK!
Silas’s hand blurred. He didn’t even open his eyes as he just whipped his arm out and slapped the cigar cleanly out of her mouth.
The tobacco tube bounced off the wall and rolled across the neon-pink carpet.
"Hey!" Evelyn hissed, sitting up with a glare. "That cost me a fortune!"

"You are not smoking that foul burning garbage inside a sealed and soundproofed hotel room," Silas stated firmly, dropping his hand back to his chest. "I refuse to smell like an ashtray while I’m trying to think."
Evelyn grumbled under her breath, crossing her arms over her chest, but she didn’t try to retrieve the cigar.
She knew he was right. The ventilation in this sleazy room was nonexistent...
"What did you want to ask me?" Evelyn prompted, sinking back down into the pillows.
Silas opened his eyes, the golden rings glowing in the dim light of the room as he turned his head to look at her.

"I need to know about your contact," Silas started, his voice serious. "Why, even with all of the highly lucrative top-tier work that you funnel to this Jax person, does he not just pack up and leave Shogitown?"
It was a glaring flaw in the hacker’s lifestyle.

"Think about it," Silas continued. "I’m guessing you pay him millions of credits to launder your stream revenue. He is practically rich... If he had just taken his servers and left this polluted syndicate-run district, this whole kidnapping situation wouldn’t have happened. Why stay in the gutter?"
Evelyn was quiet for a long bit. The neon lights from the window flickered across her face.
She let out a soft sigh, staring at the ceiling.
"You aren’t wrong," Evelyn admitted. "I asked him the exact same question a year ago. I told him I would buy him a secure penthouse in the commercial district, just to keep my data safe."
She turned her head on the pillow, looking at Silas’s masked face.

"I got my answer," Evelyn said, her voice dropping into a whisper. "Apparently, in the much earlier stages of his life, before he became the best broker in the city, he had been deep in league with a Syndicate or rather, he was directly related by blood to a high-ranking member."
Silas listened closely, analyzing the intel.

"And like most of the core members, and specifically the people born into that vicious family structure, they don’t get to just walk away," Evelyn explained, her eyes darkening. "They had a micro-explosive chip surgically implanted directly into his upper spine."
Silas frowned behind his mask.

"It’s wired into his nervous system," Evelyn continued. "If he tries to leave the boundaries of Shogitown, the signal drops and the chip detonates. It blows his spinal cord in half and severs his brain stem."
Silas absorbed the reality of the underworld.
"Oh..." Silas muttered with the pieces finally clicking together.
That explained the intense paranoia.
Jax wasn’t staying in Shogitown because he liked the grit... he was a literal hostage to his own biology in a way.
"This is why winning this tournament is actually a great opportunity for us," Evelyn stated, her brain spinning the disaster into a net positive.
She sat up on her elbows, her dark eyes shining with sudden determination.

"The winner gets the master trigger to his Slave Rune," Evelyn planned out loud. "If we manage to win the bracket and free him, I’m sure they will remove the chip and we could take him out of here for good."
Silas nodded slowly.

"I could give him significantly better living opportunities," Evelyn continued. "I could move him into the city... He could be my full-time, exclusive data broker. No more dealing with shady street gangs or worrying about rival Lords intercepting my bank transfers or trying to hack into my account."
Silas nodded again with the logic aligning perfectly.
This was a bit of good news amidst the chaos.
If Evelyn secured Jax as a permanent safe asset, Silas wouldn’t have to enter the filthy treacherous innards of Shogitown anymore to get his fake documents updated.
He could just visit his place.
But despite the advantage, Silas still couldn’t help but feel a deep unsettling weirdness about the whole situation.
Participating in a blood-sport to win a human being as a prize felt incredibly dystopian, even for the Sovereign Realm.
"We will win the trigger," Silas assured her with his voice sounding absolute. "We will get your hacker back."
Evelyn smiled softly with a genuine look of gratitude crossing her tired face.
"Thank you for all the trouble you are going through tonight, Silas," Evelyn told him sincerely.
She settled back down under the thin hotel sheets. "If you want, I will pay you a massive premium for fighting in the cage, too. My treat."
"Let’s see..." Silas said. "I just want to get my identity forged first."
Evelyn let out a soft hum of agreement. Within minutes, the crushing exhaustion overtook her.
Her breathing evened out, and she fell fast asleep, curled up in the oversized red hoodie.
Silas turned his head, looking at her sleeping face.
Without the arrogant Lord persona, without the nicotine, and without the constant stress of command, she looked remarkably peaceful.
’She’s quite cute,’ Silas thought to himself with the observation slipping through his mind.
He quickly shook the thought away, turning his gaze back to the mirrored ceiling.
He closed his eyes, focusing his mind back on the immediate lethal problem at hand.
The restriction of external mana.
He needed a way to use his Tide-Blade Arts as he needed Rip-Current Perception.
’Let’s try again...’
He pictured the flow of his Gold Core.
Usually, he pushed the liquid mana out of his pores, creating a thin invisible film of moisture in the air to read his opponent’s movements and structural flaws.
He tried to force it into his eyes earlier, but it just blurred his vision.
Suddenly, it was as though a bright blinding light bulb lit up in his Warlord brain.
’Ah,’ Silas thought with his lips curling into a sharp grin behind the Oni mask. ’Why didn’t I think of this earlier?’
He had been approaching the problem like a mage, trying to cast a spell internally but he wasn’t a mage.
Not a full one anyway... He was a physical fighter.
The human eye was already filled with a clear fluid which was known as the aqueous humor.
He didn’t need to generate new magical water to coat his eyes as he just needed to use his internal mana to vibrate the existing biological fluid already resting inside his retinas.
’It might work...’
He had found another way to use Rip-Current Perception inwardly.
Silas focused his oceanic mana pool. Instead of pushing it outward, he threaded a microscopic razor-thin needle of pure Gold Core energy up his spine and directly into his optic nerves.
He didn’t add volume as he just changed the frequency.
He vibrated the natural fluid in his eyes at the exact frequency of his Tide-Blade Arts and Silas opened his eyes.
There was no pain and no blurry vision.
The neon-pink hotel room snapped into hyper-focused clarity.
But more than that, he could see the structural integrity of everything around him.
He looked at the wooden bedside table.
He could see the microscopic fault lines in the grain of the wood. If he tapped it with two pounds of pressure at the exact right angle, the entire table would shatter into splinters.
He looked at the locked hotel door as he could see the mechanical weak point in the brass tumbler.
It worked.
He could see the weak points of physical matter without expending a single drop of mana outside of his own body.
’Though it’s only for a bit at a time... it works... I can’t wait to see the look on Morwenna’s face.’
The digital clock on Silas’s phone read exactly 1:10 AM as the two of them arrived back outside the heavy iron doors of the Black-Ash registration building.

The winding trash-strewn alleyway was dead quiet. The distant drums of the Moon Festival had long since faded into the night and the damp smog hung low over the pavement, illuminated only by the flickering harsh neon signs of the undercity.
Silas wore his dark trench coat with his metal Oni mask secured tightly.
Evelyn walked beside him with her gray hoodie zipped up to her chin and her painted Kitsune mask hiding her face once again.
They pushed the heavy iron doors open and stepped inside.

chapters.title: Chapter 357: Black-Ash Uniform
paragraphs: The registration office was still as grimy and bland as ever, except there were bright harsh fluorescent lights currently coming from the ceiling panels, illuminating the stale room.
The oppressive suffocating smell of cheap tobacco and spilled alcohol was still baked into the wooden floorboards, but the massive crowd of cybernetic thugs and syndicate muscle had entirely left.
The wooden tables were empty, littered with crushed glass mugs and overflowing ashtrays.
The wicked black-haired receptionist was the only person left in the room.
She welcomed them, stepping out from behind the thick scratched glass pane she had sat behind earlier as she was wearing a sleek tailored black suit that screamed corporate mafia.
"Well, look who made it back," the receptionist smirked, looking them up and down. "You are a bit early, but it is expected for first-timers. The nerves usually keep people from sleeping..."
"We are ready," Evelyn stated bluntly.
"I can see that," the receptionist chuckled, taking a drag from her Red-Lotus cigarette.
She turned around, gesturing toward the back of the dive bar.
She explained the layout quickly as the main event which was a massive Battle Royale to thin the herd, would begin within twenty minutes.
She pointed her cigarette in two different directions.
First, she pointed to a massive reinforced steel vault door located on the far left wall leading down a steep flight of concrete stairs.

"That path leads down to the holding pens," the receptionist instructed, looking directly at Silas. "Onii-chan, you head down there... You will join the rest of the meat in the locker rooms to get prepped and suited up."
Silas didn’t react to the ridiculous fighter name as he just nodded his masked head.
Next, she pointed to a much cleaner carpeted staircase on the right side of the room, leading upward.

"As for you, little manager," the woman told Evelyn. "You take those stairs up to the VIP viewing stands... You will join the other sponsors and high-rollers while the fighters get prepared in the dirt below."
Evelyn nodded, committing the layout to memory.
"Oh, right, I almost forgot the most important part," the receptionist muttered, reaching into her tailored suit jacket.
She pulled out a set of heavy dull-gray metal bracelets.
They didn’t reflect the fluorescent lights as they seemed to absorb the ambient energy around them, radiating a cold oppressive aura.
These were Null-stone bands.
She tossed the heavy metal bands to Evelyn.

"As the manager, you should be the one to officially put the Null-stone bands on your boy’s wrists," the receptionist grinned sadistically. "Lock them tight... The runes will automatically engage and nullify all of his external mana projection. If he tries to cast a spell, the bands will shock his nervous system until he passes out."
Evelyn caught the heavy bands as she walked over to Silas.
Silas held out his hands.
"There..."
Evelyn snapped the thick gray metal around his thick wrists and the locks clicked into place with a heavy sound.
’Haah... weird...’
Instantly, Silas felt a cold suffocating weight crash down on his Gold Core.
It was a bizarre and uncomfortable sensation. It felt like a thick rubber dam had been violently shoved over the flowing river of his mana.
He couldn’t push his aura out but as he focused his mind, a sharp grin spread across his face beneath the Oni mask.
The null-stone only blocked the exit points as the internal river was still flowing.
Silas pushed a surge of raw Gold Core mana into his biceps.
The muscle fibers instantly hardened, growing dense and vibrating with terrifying potential.
He pushed the mana up his spine and into his eyes as his vision snapped into the focused look of before for a moment.
’Good...’
He could still use it to internally strengthen his muscles as the tournament organizers had left a massive loophole for a physical Lord.
Or did they?
The two of them looked at each other in the dim light of the bar. They gave each other a firm silent nod.
The plan was solid.
’Good luck Silas...’ Evelyn thought as Silas turned on his heel and walked over to the heavy steel vault door leading below.
Evelyn turned and walked toward the carpeted door leading above.
As they both stepped onto the first rung of their respective stairs, they each felt a sudden weird sensation wash over their bodies.
It wasn’t a physical elevator... The air around them warped and stretched, smelling sharply of burnt copper.
The wicked receptionist stood in the center of the empty bar, taking a long drag of her cigarette.
She watched them both silently vanish into thin air before her very eyes, just like all the other contestants had done before them.
The stairs were teleportation wards.
She looked at the empty space where Silas had stood, exhaling a cloud of sweet-smelling smoke.
"Good luck down there, big guy," the receptionist muttered to herself, turning back to her desk. "Shame to see such a fine ass get beaten to a bloody pulp."
Silas felt a brief nauseating wave of spatial disorientation.
His vision swam with streaks of violet light, and his stomach did a slow flip.
It was remarkably similar to the uncomfortable stretching feeling of entering the Secret Realm of Ititus a while ago.
The Black-Ash syndicate clearly possessed a high-tier spatial mage on their payroll to move contestants securely without alerting the city enforcers above ground.
His heavy combat boots hit solid metal grating with a loud clang as the spatial warp vanished.
Silas blinked with his instantly mapping his new surroundings.
Apparently, those simple concrete stairs in the bar had been spatial portals leading somewhere massive.
He was now standing in an incredibly spacious and cavernous underground area.
It was a humongous holding facility.
The ceiling stretched at least forty feet high, lined with humming industrial-grade mana lamps casting a harsh sterile white glow.
The room was packed with hundreds of people and long endless rows of gray metal lockers.
It looked to be a militarized dressing room.

The air was thick with the stench of sweat and something weird as well and the noise was deafening... men shouting, fists slamming against metal lockers, and the whirring of cybernetic limbs being calibrated for violence.
Before Silas could take a step forward, a man in a pristine tailored black suit with a white bow tie materialized at his side.
"Welcome, Contestant," the butler greeted him.
Silas looked down at the man.
The butler wasn’t human... He was a high-tier, fully autonomous mechanical construct designed for service and security.

"This is the primary staging area and dressing room," the robotic butler explained, gesturing across the massive sea of criminals. "There are currently two hundred and thirty-six of the registered two hundred and fifty contestants present in this room, including yourself. The Battle Royale will commence shortly."
Silas scanned the crowd.
It was a terrifying assortment of the worst scum Valoria City had to offer.
He saw hulking eight-foot-tall mutants injected with troll blood. He saw wiry assassins with four cybernetic arms.
He saw disgraced scarred Adventurers who had turned to the syndicates for credits.
’Damn man... the underworld is a really scary place.’
"Follow me, please," the butler requested, turning on his polished heel.
Silas followed the construct down a narrow aisle between the towering rows of gray lockers.
They bypassed dozens of fighters who glared at Silas’s Oni mask with murderous intent.
The butler stopped in front of locker number 155.
"This is your designated station," the butler instructed. "You will have to wear the official uniform of the event to enter the arena as your street clothes are strictly prohibited."
He escorted Silas closer, gesturing for him to open the metal door. Silas reached out, popping the latch and pulling the locker open.
Inside, hanging on a simple metal hook, was a sleek featureless black bodysuit. It looked like it was made of thick liquid rubber, shimmering under the harsh lights.

"This is the Black-Ash combat uniform," the butler explained in his robotic monotone. "It possesses the exact same Null-stone properties as your wristbands. It will ensure you cannot project mana outside your body to cheat..."
The construct paused with its optical sensors flashing blue.

"Furthermore," the butler added, "the suit is lined with an EMP mesh. It violently suppresses the unfair abilities of electronic implants, cybernetic strength enhancers, and subdermal plating. This ensures the safety and fairness of the regular human contestants in the pit."
Silas stared at the liquid-black suit.
’Yeah, right,’ Silas thought to himself while rolling his eyes.
For some obvious reason, he immensely doubted that claim.
He looked around the room.
The massive cyborgs were already wearing the black suits, and their mechanical arms were still whirring with unrestricted power.
The Syndicate wasn’t suppressing their own heavy hitters... they were just lying to the independent fighters to give them a false sense of security before the slaughter began.
"How do I put this on?" Silas asked, poking the liquid rubber with his gloved finger.
"Simply remove your outer garments and press the suit against your chest," the butler instructed. "The smart-fabric will do the rest."
The butler bowed perfectly and walked away, disappearing into the chaotic crowd.
"I wish you luck, Contestant."
Silas unbuttoned his dark leather trench coat, folding it neatly and placing it in the bottom of the locker alongside his heavy combat boots and cargo pants.
He kept his Oni mask securely fastened to his face.
He stood in his basic undershirt and shorts. He reached out, grabbing the thick liquid-like fabric of the uniform.
’Well how are you supposed to work no–’
He pressed the cold material against his broad muscular chest and instantly, the suit reacted.
It didn’t just drape over him... it turned to liquid.

The cold black substance rapidly crept over his skin, spreading outward from his chest like a living predatory symbiote. It wrapped tightly around his massive biceps, flowed down his abdomen, and encased his legs.
Within five seconds, the liquid hardened into a sleek skin-tight combat suit. It felt like wearing a second layer of durable flexible armor.
Silas flexed his arms, surprised by the mobility the suit allowed.
He closed his eyes for a split second, testing his internal mana flow.
The suit was definitely heavy with Null-stone dust, blocking any external spells.
But his internal river still flowed perfectly.
’Alright, I can use it,’ Silas thought, his blood pumping with sudden anticipation.
He opened his eyes with the Rip-Current Perception locking onto the room.
’This will be a part of my training,’ Silas decided.
He could use Rip Current Perception flawlessly like this, even with this restrictive Null-stone suit suffocating his body.
He was glad.
He didn’t have to hold back his physical strength anymore to avoid breaking civilian structures as he was in a cage designed for monsters.
All that was left was to go crazy.
’Perhaps this stupid arc isn’t so bad.’
Suddenly, a loud, violent crash echoed from the far side of the massive locker room.
Silas turned his masked head, peering over the rows of gray metal.
A few aisles down, a scraping thud echoed over the noise as a massive brute wearing a crude, blood-stained leather executioner’s hood had just violently shoved a smaller wiry man backward.
The smaller fighter’s spine slammed hard against a locker, violently rattling the metal doors.
The brute stepped forward as his heavy boots thudded against the grating.

"Hand over the token, gutter-rat," the brute growled, his voice a distorted rumble. "You drew a center-ring starting position. I’m taking it... Give me the chip right now, or I’ll snap your spine before we even reach the dirt."
The wiry man didn’t back down. He spat a wad of blood onto the floor, glaring up at the giant with feral intensity.

"Eat shit, you rusted-out freak," the smaller man hissed, his eyes going wide with adrenaline. "I earned this spot. You think just because you bolted some scrap metal to your arms you run this pit? Come take it from me."
The smaller man didn’t wait to get grabbed again as he reached down to his ankle in a blur of motion.
He pulled a smuggled jagged shiv from his boot.
The rusted metal edge was completely coated in some dark coagulated poison.
’Fucking idiots...’
He had clearly ignored the receptionist’s second rule of the arena.
Silas leaned back against his own locker, crossing his heavy arms over his chest.
He didn’t intervene as he didn’t care.
Instead, the Lord focused his internal Rip-Current Perception on the two combatants.
This was a perfect opportunity to gauge the base skill level of the Syndicate’s underground fighting circuit.
He wanted to see real refined Martial Arts.
Silas wanted to see exactly how regular humans compensated for the Null-stone bands.
"FUCK YOU!"
"YOUR MAMA!"
They both roared, launching into a brutal bloody pummeling match right there in the narrow aisle.
The wiry man lunged first. He thrust the poisoned shiv directly toward the brute’s jugular, aiming for a quick lethal kill and Silas let out a disappointed sigh behind his Oni mask.
’What was I expecting...?’
It was completely pathetic.

sentences.text: The registration office was still as grimy and bland as ever, except there were bright harsh fluorescent lights currently coming from the ceiling panels, illuminating the stale room.
The oppressive suffocating smell of cheap tobacco and spilled alcohol was still baked into the wooden floorboards, but the massive crowd of cybernetic thugs and syndicate muscle had entirely left.
The wooden tables were empty, littered with crushed glass mugs and overflowing ashtrays.
The wicked black-haired receptionist was the only person left in the room.
She welcomed them, stepping out from behind the thick scratched glass pane she had sat behind earlier as she was wearing a sleek tailored black suit that screamed corporate mafia.
"Well, look who made it back," the receptionist smirked, looking them up and down.
"You are a bit early, but it is expected for first-timers.
The nerves usually keep people from sleeping..."
"We are ready," Evelyn stated bluntly.
"I can see that," the receptionist chuckled, taking a drag from her Red-Lotus cigarette.
She turned around, gesturing toward the back of the dive bar.
She explained the layout quickly as the main event which was a massive Battle Royale to thin the herd, would begin within twenty minutes.
She pointed her cigarette in two different directions.
First, she pointed to a massive reinforced steel vault door located on the far left wall leading down a steep flight of concrete stairs.
"That path leads down to the holding pens," the receptionist instructed, looking directly at Silas.
"Onii-chan, you head down there...
You will join the rest of the meat in the locker rooms to get prepped and suited up."
Silas didn’t react to the ridiculous fighter name as he just nodded his masked head.
Next, she pointed to a much cleaner carpeted staircase on the right side of the room, leading upward.
"As for you, little manager," the woman told Evelyn.
"You take those stairs up to the VIP viewing stands...
You will join the other sponsors and high-rollers while the fighters get prepared in the dirt below."
Evelyn nodded, committing the layout to memory.
"Oh, right, I almost forgot the most important part," the receptionist muttered, reaching into her tailored suit jacket.
She pulled out a set of heavy dull-gray metal bracelets.
They didn’t reflect the fluorescent lights as they seemed to absorb the ambient energy around them, radiating a cold oppressive aura.
These were Null-stone bands.
She tossed the heavy metal bands to Evelyn.
"As the manager, you should be the one to officially put the Null-stone bands on your boy’s wrists," the receptionist grinned sadistically.
"Lock them tight...
The runes will automatically engage and nullify all of his external mana projection.
If he tries to cast a spell, the bands will shock his nervous system until he passes out."
Evelyn caught the heavy bands as she walked over to Silas.
Silas held out his hands.
"There..."
Evelyn snapped the thick gray metal around his thick wrists and the locks clicked into place with a heavy sound.
’Haah... weird...’
Instantly, Silas felt a cold suffocating weight crash down on his Gold Core.
It was a bizarre and uncomfortable sensation.
It felt like a thick rubber dam had been violently shoved over the flowing river of his mana.
He couldn’t push his aura out but as he focused his mind, a sharp grin spread across his face beneath the Oni mask.
The null-stone only blocked the exit points as the internal river was still flowing.
Silas pushed a surge of raw Gold Core mana into his biceps.
The muscle fibers instantly hardened, growing dense and vibrating with terrifying potential.
He pushed the mana up his spine and into his eyes as his vision snapped into the focused look of before for a moment.
’Good...’
He could still use it to internally strengthen his muscles as the tournament organizers had left a massive loophole for a physical Lord.
Or did they?
The two of them looked at each other in the dim light of the bar.
They gave each other a firm silent nod.
The plan was solid.
’Good luck Silas...’ Evelyn thought as Silas turned on his heel and walked over to the heavy steel vault door leading below.
Evelyn turned and walked toward the carpeted door leading above.
As they both stepped onto the first rung of their respective stairs, they each felt a sudden weird sensation wash over their bodies.
It wasn’t a physical elevator...
The air around them warped and stretched, smelling sharply of burnt copper.
The wicked receptionist stood in the center of the empty bar, taking a long drag of her cigarette.
She watched them both silently vanish into thin air before her very eyes, just like all the other contestants had done before them.
The stairs were teleportation wards.
She looked at the empty space where Silas had stood, exhaling a cloud of sweet-smelling smoke.
"Good luck down there, big guy," the receptionist muttered to herself, turning back to her desk.
"Shame to see such a fine ass get beaten to a bloody pulp."
Silas felt a brief nauseating wave of spatial disorientation.
His vision swam with streaks of violet light, and his stomach did a slow flip.
It was remarkably similar to the uncomfortable stretching feeling of entering the Secret Realm of Ititus a while ago.
The Black-Ash syndicate clearly possessed a high-tier spatial mage on their payroll to move contestants securely without alerting the city enforcers above ground.
His heavy combat boots hit solid metal grating with a loud clang as the spatial warp vanished.
Silas blinked with his instantly mapping his new surroundings.
Apparently, those simple concrete stairs in the bar had been spatial portals leading somewhere massive.
He was now standing in an incredibly spacious and cavernous underground area.
It was a humongous holding facility.
The ceiling stretched at least forty feet high, lined with humming industrial-grade mana lamps casting a harsh sterile white glow.
The room was packed with hundreds of people and long endless rows of gray metal lockers.
It looked to be a militarized dressing room.

The air was thick with the stench of sweat and something weird as well and the noise was deafening... men shouting, fists slamming against metal lockers, and the whirring of cybernetic limbs being calibrated for violence.
Before Silas could take a step forward, a man in a pristine tailored black suit with a white bow tie materialized at his side.
"Welcome, Contestant," the butler greeted him.
Silas looked down at the man.
The butler wasn’t human...
He was a high-tier, fully autonomous mechanical construct designed for service and security.
"This is the primary staging area and dressing room," the robotic butler explained, gesturing across the massive sea of criminals.
"There are currently two hundred and thirty-six of the registered two hundred and fifty contestants present in this room, including yourself.
The Battle Royale will commence shortly."
Silas scanned the crowd.
It was a terrifying assortment of the worst scum Valoria City had to offer.
He saw hulking eight-foot-tall mutants injected with troll blood.
He saw wiry assassins with four cybernetic arms.
He saw disgraced scarred Adventurers who had turned to the syndicates for credits.
’Damn man... the underworld is a really scary place.’
"Follow me, please," the butler requested, turning on his polished heel.
Silas followed the construct down a narrow aisle between the towering rows of gray lockers.
They bypassed dozens of fighters who glared at Silas’s Oni mask with murderous intent.
The butler stopped in front of locker number 155.
"This is your designated station," the butler instructed.
"You will have to wear the official uniform of the event to enter the arena as your street clothes are strictly prohibited."
He escorted Silas closer, gesturing for him to open the metal door.
Silas reached out, popping the latch and pulling the locker open.
Inside, hanging on a simple metal hook, was a sleek featureless black bodysuit.
It looked like it was made of thick liquid rubber, shimmering under the harsh lights.
"This is the Black-Ash combat uniform," the butler explained in his robotic monotone.
"It possesses the exact same Null-stone properties as your wristbands.
It will ensure you cannot project mana outside your body to cheat..."
The construct paused with its optical sensors flashing blue.
"Furthermore," the butler added, "the suit is lined with an EMP mesh.
It violently suppresses the unfair abilities of electronic implants, cybernetic strength enhancers, and subdermal plating.
This ensures the safety and fairness of the regular human contestants in the pit."
Silas stared at the liquid-black suit.
’Yeah, right,’ Silas thought to himself while rolling his eyes.
For some obvious reason, he immensely doubted that claim.

chapters.title: Chapter 358: Betting Board
paragraphs: The smaller man’s footwork was entirely nonexistent.
He threw his balance entirely forward, leaving his center of gravity completely exposed.
There was no feint, no defense and no weight transfer. It was just blind panicked street aggression.
’I really don’t know what I was expecting...’
The brute in the executioner’s hood didn’t even try to dodge as he simply raised his thick leather-wrapped forearm.
CLANG!
The jagged shiv struck the brute’s arm, but it didn’t pierce the flesh.
The sickening sound of metal grinding against metal echoed loudly.
Underneath the synthetic skin, the brute’s entire skeletal structure was reinforced with heavy industrial-grade cybernetic plating.
"Hehehe..."
The brute let out a mechanical wheezing laugh.
He reached out with a massive hand, his fingers lined with hydraulic pistons that hissed with pressurized air.
He grabbed the smaller man directly by the throat, completely lifting his kicking struggling body off the ground.
"What were you saying... huh? I can’t hear you!"
The cyborg brute pulled his right fist back.
WHAM!
He drove a piston-powered punch directly into the wiry man’s ribcage and the sickening crunch of shattering ribs snapped through the air.
"Gahk!"
The smaller man choked on his own blood.
WHAM!
Another massive mechanical hook crashed into the man’s jaw, instantly dislocating it.
Blood and shattered teeth splattered violently against the gray metal doors of the lockers but the brute didn’t stop.
He just kept mercilessly hammering his metal fists into the smaller fighter, completely turning his torso into bruised pulverized meat.
WHAM! WHAM! WHAM! PTCH! PSSH!
The surrounding crowd of fighters cheered wildly for the early violence, slamming their fists against the lockers in a primal rhythm.
Silas just watched, feeling underwhelmed.
It wasn’t a fight... It was just a sloppy unrefined beatdown by a guy who bought expensive robot arms.
If this was the peak competition of the Underworld, the Battle Royale was going to be a boring joke.
The brute raised his metal fist for a final skull-crushing blow.
CRACK! CRACK!
Two deafening concussive gunshots rang out, echoing like thunder through the cavernous room.
The massive brute in the executioner’s hood violently jerked forward, a massive gaping hole blowing out the front of his throat, severing his hydraulic spinal cord in a shower of sparks and blood.
A fraction of a second later, the smaller wiry man’s head simply ceased to exist, exploding into a fine red mist as a secondary high-caliber slug completely pulverized his skull.
Both men crumpled to the floor in a tangled bloody heap, dead before they even hit the metal grating.
Silas looked up with his enhanced eyes instantly tracing the invisible thermal trajectory of the bullets.
High above the locker room, perched silently on hidden suspended steel catwalks cloaked in shadow, were a dozen Syndicate snipers holding heavy smoking rifles.
The loud chaotic locker room went instantly silent as the message was brutally clear.
The snipers didn’t issue warnings and they didn’t break up fights. They just executed anyone who broke the pre-game rules.
Every single fighter in the room, from the massive cyborgs to the desperate slum-rats swallowed hard, suddenly realizing that this shit was incredibly serious.
Well except Silas.
’They could have had better aim to be honest.’
Far above the bloody holding pens, Evelyn materialized in a flash of spatial light.
She stepped out of the warp with her boots hitting plush, expensive red carpeting.
She adjusted her oversized gray hood and her Kitsune mask, stepping forward to the edge of a sleek glass-paneled railing.
"Haah..."
Evelyn appeared right at the top of the VIP viewing stands and she looked down with her breath catching in her throat.
It was a massive and staggering underground arena.
It looked like an ancient Rumen colosseum ripped from the history books and fused with brutal cyberpunk architecture.
The stadium seating wrapped around in a massive circle, packed shoulder-to-shoulder with thousands of screaming bloodthirsty spectators.
The noise was a physical pressure against her eardrums.
Blinding high-intensity spotlights swept across the crowd, casting dramatic shadows.
But the centerpiece of the cavernous room was the arena floor itself.
It was a sprawling flat expanse of packed, blood-stained dirt, enclosed entirely by a massive fifty-foot-high cage made of thick, glowing Null-stone bars.
It was a literal meat-grinder designed to trap the fighters inside until some remained.
Evelyn gulped with her mind racing as she calculated the sheer scale of the blood-sport.
Silas was going to be thrown into that pit with over two hundred killers.
Before she could fully process the nightmare, a polite voice broke her concentration.
"Excuse me, Ma’am?"
Evelyn turned. A young woman dressed in a pristine traditional black-and-white maid outfit walked up to her.
"You possess a Manager’s token, correct?" the maid asked politely, gesturing to the glowing red badge pinned to Evelyn’s hoodie.
Evelyn simply nodded, keeping her rigid untouchable persona intact.
The maid smiled warmly, bowing with elegance.

"Well then, Ma’am," the maid offered, extending a white-gloved hand toward a row of private luxury viewing boxes suspended over the arena. "Let me show you around to your designated suite as the slaughter is about to begin."
The polite uniformed maid walked with practiced, elegant strides down the dimly lit plush-carpeted hallway of the VIP sector.
Evelyn followed closely behind her with her boots sinking softly into the expensive crimson-dyed fabric of the floor.
The transition from the filthy smoke-filled dive bar on the surface to this luxurious sound-dampened subterranean corridor was still very jarring.
The air up here smelled of rich mahogany, expensive colognes, and chilled wine, completely masking the scent of the slaughterhouse waiting below.

"The warehouse on the surface," the maid explained, her voice sounding smooth as she looked over her shoulder, "is simply a spatial anchor point. A portal gateway if you will... The actual fighting arena is located far beneath the deepest known bedrock of Shogitown, secured within a reinforced subterranean cavern. It keeps the noise down and keeps the World Council enforcers completely ignorant of our operations."𝗳𝚛𝗲𝕖𝕨𝕖𝗯𝚗𝚘𝕧𝕖𝗹.𝗰𝗼𝕞
Evelyn adjusted the oversized sleeves of her hoodie, processing the staggering cost of maintaining a permanent two-way spatial anchor in the middle of a crowded city.
The Black-Ash Syndicate possessed resources that rivaled guilds.

"As a registered Manager, you hold a very specific crucial position in the hierarchy of tonight’s events," the maid continued, gesturing with a white-gloved hand as they walked past a row of locked, polished oak doors. "You are the lifeline to your Fighter... Under the official rules of the pit, if a Manager explicitly demands that their Fighter be removed from the tournament, the Syndicate guards are contractually obligated to extract them immediately. The match ends, and they forfeit."
Evelyn’s dark eyes narrowed behind the narrow slits of her painted Kitsune mask.
Her mind instantly caught the sinister, underlying implication of that specific rule.
She felt a cold prickle of realization.

"That means," Evelyn reasoned out loud, her voice echoing slightly in the quiet hall. "even if a Fighter is winning, even if they desperately want to keep fighting and claim the prize, their Manager can unilaterally pull them out against their will."
The maid offered a polite closed-mouth smile. She didn’t confirm or deny the statement, but the silence was deafening.
Evelyn understood the grim reality of the criminal Underworld.
It was a massive exploitative leverage system.
A Syndicate could simply kidnap, threaten, or bribe a Manager sitting safely in the stands.
They could coerce the Manager into surrendering the match, effectively eliminating a dangerous independent Fighter without ever having to defeat them in the Null-stone cage.
It was a rigged game from the very start.
Well, that specific vulnerability was not an issue for her.
Evelyn was a Classic Lord and while she was not as powerful as Silas, she was still powerful in her own right.
Nobody in this grimy undercity was going to successfully coerce, bribe, or intimidate her into pulling Silas out of that pit.
But still, she couldn’t help but question the overwhelming scale of the event.

"Is the prize really that important?" Evelyn asked, probing for intel. "A single hacker with a Slave Rune? Why go through the massive logistical trouble of hosting a two-hundred-man death match just to auction off a data broker?"
The maid slowed her pace, glancing back at Evelyn with an assessing look.
"Wasn’t that the exact reason why you registered tonight, Ma’am?" the maid countered smoothly, deflecting the question. "To claim the prize for your own operations?"
Evelyn didn’t react, keeping her posture rigid and unreadable.
The maid sighed softly with her professional facade cracking just a fraction.
She leaned closer, dropping her voice to a hushed conspiratorial whisper.
"How would a lowly, contracted hospitality maid such as myself have the definitive answer to the inner workings of the Syndicate?" the maid prefaced, covering her tracks.

She thinned her lips, glancing nervously down the empty hallway. "But... I hear things. I serve the drinks to the high-rollers. There is a very prominent rumor circulating through the staff that the hacker in question is directly related to the Boss by blood. That is why this is such a massive guarded event. It is family business masquerading as a blood-sport."
Evelyn went completely silent.
Her previous deduction in the hotel room was confirmed. They weren’t just stepping into a gang dispute over stolen credits... they were stepping into the middle of a vicious family war.
The maid straightened her posture, instantly returning to her polite corporate demeanor as they rounded a corner and entered a wide brightly lit atrium.

"Now, before I escort you to your designated seating arrangement," the maid announced, gesturing to a massive glowing structure occupying the center of the atrium wall, "allow me to introduce you to the official betting board."
It was a staggering piece of magical technology.
A huge sweeping holographic display board projected crystal-clear images and scrolling text into the air, illuminating the plush carpets with a chaotic flurry of neon numbers.

"This is the primary wagering terminal," the maid explained. "People sitting in the viewing boxes can place immense sums of money on the heads of the combatants they want to win. You essentially stake a given amount of spirit credits against the house odds... You can pick someone right now, but you do not need to bother with an immediate upfront physical payment. The original bet pay and any potential winnings will be collected and distributed after the Battle Royale concludes."
Evelyn walked up to the glowing interface.

"Once the Battle Royale officially starts," the maid added, pointing to a sleek metallic datapad resting on a nearby pedestal, "every Manager and VIP spectator will have a personal synchronized tab in front of them in the stands if they wish to adjust their wagers dynamically but the first, preliminary bet available right now is a survival wager. You must select a specific candidate that you believe possesses the skill to survive the initial meat grinder and enter the Top Twelve."
Evelyn’s ear twitched beneath her hood.
The Top Twelve.
Out of two hundred and fifty men, only twelve would survive the free-for-all to reach the actual tournament bracket.
She stepped closer to the massive board. It displayed rows upon rows of glowing pictures, accompanied by names and odds.
Evelyn realized with a jolt of surprise that the pictures were stealthily taken headshots.
The wicked receptionist behind the glass desk in the dive bar had clearly been using a hidden magical lens to photograph every single fighter as they signed the bloody contract.
She scanned the sprawling rows of masked killers, cybernetic mutants and scarred veterans until her dark eyes locked onto a familiar image.
It was Silas.
The photograph captured his upper torso and head perfectly.
He looked very... devilish.
The dark trench coat blended into the shadows, making his broad muscled shoulders look like a looming mountain.
But it was the Oni mask that stole the focus.
The harsh fluorescent lighting of the bar had caught the jagged silver fangs of the demon visage, casting menacing shadows over the metal.
His golden-ringed eyes glowed with a terrifying intensity through the narrow slits.

If Evelyn didn’t know the surprisingly responsible young man resting behind that terrifying mask, she would have genuinely thought of him as the most intimidating and cold-blooded monster on the entire roster.
’I’ll bet on him all the way,’ Evelyn decided instantly in her mind.
While she was a chronic chain-smoker and a ruthless tactician, she wasn’t exactly a habitual gambler.
She preferred calculated investments over games of chance.
But looking at the staggering odds stacked against the unknown "Onii-chan" she saw an opportunity to rob the Black-Ash Syndicate blind.
What other choice did she have?
As she raised her hand toward the holographic interface, the maid gently cleared her throat.

"Ma’am, a word of advice, if I may," the maid offered, pointing a slender, white-gloved finger at a different portrait on the board. "Even though you are the registered Manager for someone else, there is no rule stating you must bet on your own Fighter. If you want to guarantee a massive return on your investment, you should bet on this man."
Evelyn blinked, tracking the maid’s finger.
