She stepped out of the warp with her boots hitting plush, expensive red carpeting.
She adjusted her oversized gray hood and her Kitsune mask, stepping forward to the edge of a sleek glass-paneled railing.
"Haah..."
Evelyn appeared right at the top of the VIP viewing stands and she looked down with her breath catching in her throat.
It was a massive and staggering underground arena.
It looked like an ancient Rumen colosseum ripped from the history books and fused with brutal cyberpunk architecture.
The stadium seating wrapped around in a massive circle, packed shoulder-to-shoulder with thousands of screaming bloodthirsty spectators.
The noise was a physical pressure against her eardrums.
Blinding high-intensity spotlights swept across the crowd, casting dramatic shadows.
But the centerpiece of the cavernous room was the arena floor itself.
It was a sprawling flat expanse of packed, blood-stained dirt, enclosed entirely by a massive fifty-foot-high cage made of thick, glowing Null-stone bars.
It was a literal meat-grinder designed to trap the fighters inside until some remained.
Evelyn gulped with her mind racing as she calculated the sheer scale of the blood-sport.
Silas was going to be thrown into that pit with over two hundred killers.
Before she could fully process the nightmare, a polite voice broke her concentration.
"Excuse me, Ma’am?"
Evelyn turned.
A young woman dressed in a pristine traditional black-and-white maid outfit walked up to her.
"You possess a Manager’s token, correct?" the maid asked politely, gesturing to the glowing red badge pinned to Evelyn’s hoodie.
Evelyn simply nodded, keeping her rigid untouchable persona intact.
The maid smiled warmly, bowing with elegance.
"Well then, Ma’am," the maid offered, extending a white-gloved hand toward a row of private luxury viewing boxes suspended over the arena.
"Let me show you around to your designated suite as the slaughter is about to begin."
The polite uniformed maid walked with practiced, elegant strides down the dimly lit plush-carpeted hallway of the VIP sector.
Evelyn followed closely behind her with her boots sinking softly into the expensive crimson-dyed fabric of the floor.
The transition from the filthy smoke-filled dive bar on the surface to this luxurious sound-dampened subterranean corridor was still very jarring.
The air up here smelled of rich mahogany, expensive colognes, and chilled wine, completely masking the scent of the slaughterhouse waiting below.
"The warehouse on the surface," the maid explained, her voice sounding smooth as she looked over her shoulder, "is simply a spatial anchor point.
A portal gateway if you will...
The actual fighting arena is located far beneath the deepest known bedrock of Shogitown, secured within a reinforced subterranean cavern.
It keeps the noise down and keeps the World Council enforcers completely ignorant of our operations."𝗳𝚛𝗲𝕖𝕨𝕖𝗯𝚗𝚘𝕧𝕖𝗹.𝗰𝗼𝕞
Evelyn adjusted the oversized sleeves of her hoodie, processing the staggering cost of maintaining a permanent two-way spatial anchor in the middle of a crowded city.
The Black-Ash Syndicate possessed resources that rivaled guilds.

"As a registered Manager, you hold a very specific crucial position in the hierarchy of tonight’s events," the maid continued, gesturing with a white-gloved hand as they walked past a row of locked, polished oak doors.
"You are the lifeline to your Fighter...
Under the official rules of the pit, if a Manager explicitly demands that their Fighter be removed from the tournament, the Syndicate guards are contractually obligated to extract them immediately.
The match ends, and they forfeit."
Evelyn’s dark eyes narrowed behind the narrow slits of her painted Kitsune mask.
Her mind instantly caught the sinister, underlying implication of that specific rule.
She felt a cold prickle of realization.
"That means," Evelyn reasoned out loud, her voice echoing slightly in the quiet hall.
"even if a Fighter is winning, even if they desperately want to keep fighting and claim the prize, their Manager can unilaterally pull them out against their will."
The maid offered a polite closed-mouth smile.
She didn’t confirm or deny the statement, but the silence was deafening.
Evelyn understood the grim reality of the criminal Underworld.
It was a massive exploitative leverage system.
A Syndicate could simply kidnap, threaten, or bribe a Manager sitting safely in the stands.
They could coerce the Manager into surrendering the match, effectively eliminating a dangerous independent Fighter without ever having to defeat them in the Null-stone cage.
It was a rigged game from the very start.
Well, that specific vulnerability was not an issue for her.
Evelyn was a Classic Lord and while she was not as powerful as Silas, she was still powerful in her own right.
Nobody in this grimy undercity was going to successfully coerce, bribe, or intimidate her into pulling Silas out of that pit.
But still, she couldn’t help but question the overwhelming scale of the event.
"Is the prize really that important?" Evelyn asked, probing for intel.
"A single hacker with a Slave Rune?
Why go through the massive logistical trouble of hosting a two-hundred-man death match just to auction off a data broker?"
The maid slowed her pace, glancing back at Evelyn with an assessing look.
"Wasn’t that the exact reason why you registered tonight, Ma’am?" the maid countered smoothly, deflecting the question.
"To claim the prize for your own operations?"
Evelyn didn’t react, keeping her posture rigid and unreadable.
The maid sighed softly with her professional facade cracking just a fraction.
She leaned closer, dropping her voice to a hushed conspiratorial whisper.
"How would a lowly, contracted hospitality maid such as myself have the definitive answer to the inner workings of the Syndicate?" the maid prefaced, covering her tracks.
She thinned her lips, glancing nervously down the empty hallway.
"But...
I hear things.
I serve the drinks to the high-rollers.
There is a very prominent rumor circulating through the staff that the hacker in question is directly related to the Boss by blood.
That is why this is such a massive guarded event.
It is family business masquerading as a blood-sport."
Evelyn went completely silent.
Her previous deduction in the hotel room was confirmed.
They weren’t just stepping into a gang dispute over stolen credits... they were stepping into the middle of a vicious family war.
The maid straightened her posture, instantly returning to her polite corporate demeanor as they rounded a corner and entered a wide brightly lit atrium.

"Now, before I escort you to your designated seating arrangement," the maid announced, gesturing to a massive glowing structure occupying the center of the atrium wall, "allow me to introduce you to the official betting board."
It was a staggering piece of magical technology.
A huge sweeping holographic display board projected crystal-clear images and scrolling text into the air, illuminating the plush carpets with a chaotic flurry of neon numbers.
"This is the primary wagering terminal," the maid explained.
"People sitting in the viewing boxes can place immense sums of money on the heads of the combatants they want to win.
You essentially stake a given amount of spirit credits against the house odds...
You can pick someone right now, but you do not need to bother with an immediate upfront physical payment.
The original bet pay and any potential winnings will be collected and distributed after the Battle Royale concludes."
Evelyn walked up to the glowing interface.

"Once the Battle Royale officially starts," the maid added, pointing to a sleek metallic datapad resting on a nearby pedestal, "every Manager and VIP spectator will have a personal synchronized tab in front of them in the stands if they wish to adjust their wagers dynamically but the first, preliminary bet available right now is a survival wager.
You must select a specific candidate that you believe possesses the skill to survive the initial meat grinder and enter the Top Twelve."
Evelyn’s ear twitched beneath her hood.
The Top Twelve.
Out of two hundred and fifty men, only twelve would survive the free-for-all to reach the actual tournament bracket.
She stepped closer to the massive board.
It displayed rows upon rows of glowing pictures, accompanied by names and odds.
Evelyn realized with a jolt of surprise that the pictures were stealthily taken headshots.
The wicked receptionist behind the glass desk in the dive bar had clearly been using a hidden magical lens to photograph every single fighter as they signed the bloody contract.
She scanned the sprawling rows of masked killers, cybernetic mutants and scarred veterans until her dark eyes locked onto a familiar image.
It was Silas.
The photograph captured his upper torso and head perfectly.
He looked very... devilish.
The dark trench coat blended into the shadows, making his broad muscled shoulders look like a looming mountain.
But it was the Oni mask that stole the focus.
The harsh fluorescent lighting of the bar had caught the jagged silver fangs of the demon visage, casting menacing shadows over the metal.
His golden-ringed eyes glowed with a terrifying intensity through the narrow slits.

If Evelyn didn’t know the surprisingly responsible young man resting behind that terrifying mask, she would have genuinely thought of him as the most intimidating and cold-blooded monster on the entire roster.
’I’ll bet on him all the way,’ Evelyn decided instantly in her mind.
While she was a chronic chain-smoker and a ruthless tactician, she wasn’t exactly a habitual gambler.
She preferred calculated investments over games of chance.
But looking at the staggering odds stacked against the unknown "Onii-chan" she saw an opportunity to rob the Black-Ash Syndicate blind.
What other choice did she have?
As she raised her hand toward the holographic interface, the maid gently cleared her throat.
"Ma’am, a word of advice, if I may," the maid offered, pointing a slender, white-gloved finger at a different portrait on the board.
"Even though you are the registered Manager for someone else, there is no rule stating you must bet on your own Fighter.
If you want to guarantee a massive return on your investment, you should bet on this man."
Evelyn blinked, tracking the maid’s finger.

chapters.title: Chapter 359: Bet On Onii-Chan
paragraphs: It was a picture of the massive shirtless giant wearing the bright green Mantis mask.
It was the exact same steroid-pumped cybernetic freak they had seen drinking ale in the dive bar earlier.
The maid leaned in close, whispering softly so the nearby guards wouldn’t hear.

"He is the son of the Black-Ash Boss," the maid revealed the ultimate insider secret. "The tournament is a spectacle, but the ending is already written. He will most certainly win. The Syndicate will ensure it..."
Evelyn looked at the picture of the Mantis brute with her mind rapidly processing the implications.
’What a complicated day...’
The Boss’s son was fighting in the pit to win back the Boss’s other son.
The entire event was a rigged theatrical display of power designed to funnel massive gambling losses from independent fools directly into the Syndicate’s deep pockets.
"I appreciate the information," Evelyn said, genuinely grateful for the maid’s dangerous honesty. It confirmed exactly what Silas would be dealing with down in the dirt.
But Evelyn didn’t change her mind.
The Boss’s son had cybernetics and rigged rules. She knew exactly where the smart money belonged.
They moved on, leaving the atrium and walking down another long opulent corridor leading toward the viewing boxes.

"The private isolated luxury viewing boxes are located at the far end of the hall," the maid gestured vaguely as they passed several heavily guarded gilded doors. "Those are reserved exclusively for the inner circle of the Syndicate, wealthy guild masters, and elite corporate sponsors. They are not for the general Manager tier for now..."
Evelyn smacked her lips in quiet annoyance behind her mask.
She had figured as much.
The Underworld always adhered to a strict unforgiving hierarchy.
But still... she really wanted her own private soundproofed privacy to smoke her premium Red-Lotus cigarettes and stress-pace in peace.
Sharing a room with a bunch of sweaty nervous Underworld managers sounded exhausting.
"Will the entire event, from the Battle Royale to the final bracket, take place throughout tonight?" Evelyn asked, checking the time on her datapad.

"Yes, Ma’am," the maid confirmed with a polite nod. "It is meant to be a rapid, brutal one-day event. The Boss prefers to conclude business before the sun rises over Shogitown... It will be a long night, of course, featuring a staggering amount of death."
As they moved further down the plush hallway, the muffled sound of a struggle echoed from a nearby door.
Evelyn stopped with her hand instinctively twitching toward the hidden daggers strapped to her thighs.
The heavy oak door burst open.
Two massive armored Black-Ash syndicate enforcers dragged a screaming, thrashing man out into the hallway.
The man was dressed in an expensive suit with a Manager’s token pinned to his lapel.
One of the enforcers slammed the struggling Manager against the wall, pressing the cold heavy barrel of a pistol directly against the back of his skull.
"Move," the enforcer growled, shoving the terrified man forward. "Down to the lower stands."
"No! Please! I can pay the debt!" the Manager sobbed hysterically, stumbling down the hallway at gunpoint with tears streaming down his face. "Give me another week!"
Evelyn watched the grim procession disappear around the corner with her mind instantly connecting the brutal dots.
’Did something happen down in the locker rooms?’ Evelyn thought, her pulse quickening.
The Battle Royale hadn’t even officially started yet.
The only way a Manager was being forcefully escorted away at gunpoint to collect a death-debt was if their designated Fighter had already died before reaching the dirt.
It was a chilling violent reminder of the fifty-percent asset forfeiture clause she had signed.
The Black-Ash didn’t play games with their contracts.
’I see... they’ll detain you so even if you used fakes, they can still collect it but how do they handle the other part?’
The maid ignored the screaming man, gesturing for Evelyn to step through a wide open archway.
"Here is your designated section, Ma’am," the maid announced, bowing once more before retreating down the hall.
Evelyn stepped through the archway and entered a very spacious, tiered viewing box.
It was essentially a massive luxury suite suspended directly over the arena.
The room was packed with dozens of other people, all sitting comfortably on plush leather chairs, gripping datapads, and nervously being served dark liquor by a team of silent waiters.
These were the other Managers.
They were a diverse sketchy mix of minor gang leaders, desperate debt-brokers, and wealthy thrill-seekers looking to strike it rich on a long-shot fighter.
Evelyn found an empty leather chair situated near the back corner of the room, far away from the loudest groups.
She sat down, pulling her oversized hood lower over her masked face, blending into the shadows.
A few minutes passed in tense simmering silence.
The heavy muffled roar of the massive crowd in the stadium outside bled through the thick walls.
Suddenly, the heavy double doors at the front of the viewing box swung wide open.
The room went instantly silent as every single Manager stiffened, putting their drinks down.
A middle-aged man walked into the room.

He moved with the slow terrifying grace of a predator as he possessed striking sharp features with a remarkably handsome face forged by years of ruthless combat, and perfectly styled slicked-back silver and white hair.
He wore a pristine impeccably tailored dark suit.
But the most defining intimidating feature was the sprawling, jagged black tattoo etched directly across the left side of his face, winding from his jawline up to his temple.
It was the crest of the Black-Ash Syndicate.
This was the Boss.
’Or rather... Jax’s father.’
He exuded an aura of crushing authority.
He didn’t possess a Lord core, but the concentrated weight of the blood he had spilled to build his empire commanded immediate suffocating respect.
’I can also sense he uses mana... but how...?’
The Boss walked to the front of the room, standing before the massive, opaque blast-shield that currently blocked their view of the arena below.
He clasped his hands behind his back, looking over the nervous crowd of Managers with a cold smile.
"Welcome, ladies and gentlemen, to the culmination of the Black-Ash tournament," the Boss began, his voice echoing as a deep baritone that filled the room without him needing to raise it.
He paced slowly across the front of the box.

"I apologize that the invitations were sent out on such incredibly short notice, especially considering the registration only opened earlier this week," the Boss continued with his tone mockingly polite. "But I am genuinely glad that so many of you were able to gather the funds and find the courage to come."
He snapped his fingers.
Instantly, the massive opaque blast-shield sealing the front of the viewing box hissed with pressurized air.
The heavy metal plating retracted upward, sliding smoothly into the ceiling.
A massive unobstructed pane of reinforced crystalline glass was revealed, giving the Managers a proper dizzying view of the staggering, colossal dirt arena situated hundreds of feet downward.
The deafening roaring noise of the thousands of spectators washed into the suite like a physical wave.
Not only that, but the exact second the glass opened, a sleek glowing holographic tab materialized out of thin air, hovering directly in front of every single person’s face in the room.
The tab displayed a full, high-definition, multi-angled view of the massive dirt arena below, alongside a sprawling list of odds, names, and betting options.
The Boss sat down heavily in a luxurious, throne-like leather chair positioned at the very front of the glass.
He crossed his legs with a cruel entertained smirk playing on his lips.

"Enjoy the show, my friends," the Boss told them, gesturing to the violent spectacle waiting below. "After all, it has been quite a while since we had so many interesting, desperate fighters taking place in the pit at the same time."
Evelyn ignored his theatrical speech, focusing her intense, calculating gaze entirely on the glowing holographic tab hovering in front of her Kitsune mask.
The tab was intuitive.
It gave her the immediate choice of who to bet on, allowing her to scroll through the massive roster of names and adjust the specific amount of spirit credits she wished to wager.
A large crimson digital timer was ticking down rapidly in the top right corner of the screen, indicating that the betting window for the preliminary Battle Royale was about to close permanently.
"Place your wagers now," the Boss called out over the roar of the crowd, raising a glass of dark liquor in a mock toast. "Go big, or go home in a body bag."
The room erupted into frantic whispered chaos as every Manager began desperately typing on their holographic tabs, betting massive sums on cybernetic mutants and syndicate favorites.
Evelyn didn’t hesitate.
She scrolled past the heavily favored Mantis brute and she scrolled past the giant troll-blooded mutants.
She found the name.
She clicked on ’Onii-Chan’, letting out a soft dry chuckle at the absurdity of the moniker sitting amidst a list of terrifying blood-soaked killer aliases.
’Why did he even let me do this...?’
She tapped the wager interface but Evelyn didn’t bet a safe conservative amount. She typed in 1,000,000 spirit credits, betting that Silas would survive the meat grinder and enter the Top Twelve.
Immediately, the system calculated the staggering long-shot odds. The interface flashed a bright green confirmation prompt.
It showed her exact massive payout if he succeeded.
Her balance would jump from a 1,000,000 credit wager directly to a 5,500,000 credit return!
’Ah... all this money for me? I love gambling!’
A glowing ’CONFIRM’ button pulsed at the bottom of the screen.
Evelyn reached out and pressed the button.
The system locked the bet, encrypting the wager against her anonymous shell corporation and the exact second she confirmed, the timer hit zero.
The betting tab vanished from front of her face, and simultaneously disappeared from everyone else’s view in the massive stadium.
It was time.
The waiting was over as it was time for the slaughter to begin.
Deep down in the sunken cavernous pit of the arena, the earth began to shake.
Several massive heavy steel hatches built directly into the towering walls of the Null-stone cage began to grind open.
Rusted chains screamed in protest as the heavy iron grates were hauled upward as people began flooding into the dirt field.
It was a tidal wave of flesh, metal, and violent intent.
Over two hundred desperate adrenaline-fueled fighters charged out of the dark tunnels, spreading out across the blood-stained earth.
Some carried themselves with disciplined martial stances while others screamed like feral beasts, beating their chests.
Evelyn stood up from her chair, stepping closer to the thick glass overlooking the drop.
She strained her enhanced eyes, desperately scanning the massive chaotic sea of black uniforms to see whether she could spot his broad-shouldered frame among the crowd.
But the sheer volume of bodies, combined with the blinding sweep of the stadium spotlights, made it impossible.
She couldn’t find him manually.
She resorted to using her secondary datapad, pulling up the live-feed tracking cameras assigned to her specific fighter to monitor his vitals.
Down below, the deafening roar of the thousands of spectators reached a fever pitch.𝓯𝓻𝓮𝙚𝙬𝓮𝙗𝒏𝙤𝒗𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝒐𝓶
Suddenly, a sleek glowing anti-gravity platform shot out from the side of the arena, hovering precariously over the center of the dirt pit.
Standing on the platform was a man wearing a violently bright, neon-purple suit adorned with flashing light-runes.
The Announcer.
He tapped a magically amplified microphone against his chin with the feedback booming like thunder across the colosseum.
"Ahem!"
He immediately cleared his throat, commanding the attention of every single soul in the place.
"Listen up people!"
He took his floating platform down slightly, hovering just ten feet above the heads of the filling field, feeding off the aggressive violent energy of the combatants.

"LADIES, GENTLEMEN, AND DEGENERATES OF THE UNDERWORLD!" the Announcer screamed into the microphone, his voice echoing with insane hype. "Welcome to the grandest, bloodiest spectacle in Shogitown! Welcome to the Black-Ash Blood-Sport!"
The crowd went violently feral.
They stomped their feet against the metal bleachers, the rhythmic booming sound vibrating the very bedrock of the city.

"Today, we do not deal in petty street credits! We do not deal in empty promises!" the Announcer roared, spinning around on his platform to hype up every section of the arena. "Today, we deal in flesh! We deal in data! We deal in what one might call... destiny!"
He pointed a dramatic glowing finger down at the massive, chaotic swarm of fighters standing in the dirt.

"You all know the grand prize waiting at the end of the bracket! You all know the staggering unparalleled value of the asset on the line tonight!" the Announcer hyped the crowd further, refusing to say Jax’s name, letting the mystery fuel the greed. "And you all know the exact unforgiving stakes!"
He raised both hands high into the air as the heavy steel hatches built into the arena walls slammed shut with a deafening final boom.
The locks engaged as there was no way out.

"Two hundred and thirty-four desperate souls stand in the dirt right now!" the Announcer screamed, his voice reaching a hysterical pitch that made even Evelyn surprised. "But this is the preliminary Battle Royale! There are no referees! There are no rounds! There is no mercy! You fight until only the twelve strongest and most ruthless bastards remain breathing in the mud!"

The betting tab vanished from front of her face, and simultaneously disappeared from everyone else’s view in the massive stadium.
It was time.
The waiting was over as it was time for the slaughter to begin.
Deep down in the sunken cavernous pit of the arena, the earth began to shake.
Several massive heavy steel hatches built directly into the towering walls of the Null-stone cage began to grind open.
Rusted chains screamed in protest as the heavy iron grates were hauled upward as people began flooding into the dirt field.
It was a tidal wave of flesh, metal, and violent intent.
Over two hundred desperate adrenaline-fueled fighters charged out of the dark tunnels, spreading out across the blood-stained earth.
Some carried themselves with disciplined martial stances while others screamed like feral beasts, beating their chests.
Evelyn stood up from her chair, stepping closer to the thick glass overlooking the drop.
She strained her enhanced eyes, desperately scanning the massive chaotic sea of black uniforms to see whether she could spot his broad-shouldered frame among the crowd.
But the sheer volume of bodies, combined with the blinding sweep of the stadium spotlights, made it impossible.
She couldn’t find him manually.
She resorted to using her secondary datapad, pulling up the live-feed tracking cameras assigned to her specific fighter to monitor his vitals.
Down below, the deafening roar of the thousands of spectators reached a fever pitch.𝓯𝓻𝓮𝙚𝙬𝓮𝙗𝒏𝙤𝒗𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝒐𝓶
Suddenly, a sleek glowing anti-gravity platform shot out from the side of the arena, hovering precariously over the center of the dirt pit.
Standing on the platform was a man wearing a violently bright, neon-purple suit adorned with flashing light-runes.
The Announcer.
He tapped a magically amplified microphone against his chin with the feedback booming like thunder across the colosseum.
"Ahem!"
He immediately cleared his throat, commanding the attention of every single soul in the place.
"Listen up people!"
He took his floating platform down slightly, hovering just ten feet above the heads of the filling field, feeding off the aggressive violent energy of the combatants.
"LADIES, GENTLEMEN, AND DEGENERATES OF THE UNDERWORLD!" the Announcer screamed into the microphone, his voice echoing with insane hype.
"Welcome to the grandest, bloodiest spectacle in Shogitown!
Welcome to the Black-Ash Blood-Sport!"
The crowd went violently feral.
They stomped their feet against the metal bleachers, the rhythmic booming sound vibrating the very bedrock of the city.
"Today, we do not deal in petty street credits!
We do not deal in empty promises!" the Announcer roared, spinning around on his platform to hype up every section of the arena.
"Today, we deal in flesh!
We deal in data!
We deal in what one might call... destiny!"
He pointed a dramatic glowing finger down at the massive, chaotic swarm of fighters standing in the dirt.
"You all know the grand prize waiting at the end of the bracket!
You all know the staggering unparalleled value of the asset on the line tonight!" the Announcer hyped the crowd further, refusing to say Jax’s name, letting the mystery fuel the greed.
"And you all know the exact unforgiving stakes!"
He raised both hands high into the air as the heavy steel hatches built into the arena walls slammed shut with a deafening final boom.
The locks engaged as there was no way out.
"Two hundred and thirty-four desperate souls stand in the dirt right now!" the Announcer screamed, his voice reaching a hysterical pitch that made even Evelyn surprised.
"But this is the preliminary Battle Royale!
There are no referees!
There are no rounds!
There is no mercy!
You fight until only the twelve strongest and most ruthless bastards remain breathing in the mud!"

chapters.title: Chapter 360: Battle Royale [I]
paragraphs: The towering fifty-foot-high bars of the Null-stone cage suddenly flared to life.
It wasn’t a subtle activation though... It was a violent shift in the very atmosphere of the cavern.
BZZZZZT!
A deep suffocating hum filled the arena.
The anti-magic field fully engaged, projecting a dome of absolute mana suppression over the packed dirt.
To a normal human, it might have just felt like a sudden drop in air pressure but to anyone with an Awakened core, it felt like being crushed.
The Null-stone pressed down on the fighters like a physical weight. It felt like trying to breathe liquid lead.
Silas stood perfectly still near the outer edge of the dirt ring.
CLANG!
The heavy reinforced iron hatches were sealed shut behind his back with the massive deadbolts grinding into the stone.
...There was no exit.
High above, the roaring crowd sounded like a distant muffled ocean of white noise, filtered through the thick metal casing of his Oni mask.
He didn’t look up at the VIP boxes or the blinding spotlights as he kept his gaze level.
He looked around at the massive chaotic mob surrounding him on all sides.
There were over two hundred men trapped in the dirt with him. It was a terrifying menagerie of the Underworld’s worst.
To his left, a muscled brute with skin dyed entirely crimson was cracking his thick knuckles with the joints popping like dry twigs.
To his right, a twitching emaciated cyborg was desperately tweaking a pressure valve on his mechanical forearm, the hydraulic fluid hissing and leaking into the mud.

Everywhere he looked, desperate assassins, debt-ridden slum-rats, and Syndicate enforcers were stretching their synthetic limbs, rolling their thick necks and eyeing each other with bloodthirsty murder.
They were feral animals backed into a corner, waiting for the cage to open.
’I really don’t want to be here...’ Silas thought.
He let out a long heavy sigh. The breath pushed through the slotted visor of his Oni mask, vibrating the silver metal fangs.
He didn’t want to be standing in the damp, blood-soaked dirt of a criminal fighting pit.
He wanted to be sitting at his dining table, reading a book, and ignoring the rest of the universe.
’But whatever...’ Silas concluded.
His deep hardened instincts finally overrode his mundane desire for rest.
Complaining wouldn’t change his location and whining wouldn’t magically forge a World Council identity for Vespera.
He was in the cage and the gates were locked so... it was time to work.
Beneath the dark, shadowed visor of his Oni mask, Silas closed his eyes for a microscopic fraction of a second.
He ignored the suffocating oppressive weight of the Null-stone bands clamped tightly around his wrists.
The bands only stopped external projection so they couldn’t stop the internal machine.
He reached deep into his chest, tapping into the vast oceanic reservoir of his Mythic Gold Core.
He pulled a dense razor-thin needle of internal mana straight up his spinal column and he pushed the pure concentrated energy directly into his optic nerves.
’It’s time...’
He vibrated the existing biological fluid resting inside his retinas, tuning the water in his own eyes to the exact perfect frequency of his Tide-Blade Arts.
Silas opened his eyes.
His irises gained a brilliant light blue color.
It was almost imperceptible in the chaotic flashing neon lighting of the arena. It was completely hidden behind the dark shadows of his metal mask.
But the magical effect on his visual cortex was immediate.
Instantly, the entire world slowed down to a crawl.
The chaotic twitching movements of the two hundred fighters surrounding him sharpened into flawless clarity.
He didn’t just see the men anymore... he saw the physical blueprints of their bodies instead.
He looked at the crimson-skinned brute to his left. Silas clearly saw the weak, deteriorating cartilage in the man’s left knee joint, worn down from years of carrying too much upper body weight.
He looked at the twitching cyborg.
He saw the microscopic hairline fractures spider-webbing across the man’s lower ribs, poorly healed from a previous fight.
He saw the exact, exposed pneumatic cables hidden just beneath the cheap synthetic skin of his mechanical arm.
He saw every pressure point... Every vital organ and every single flaw in the entire arena.
"LET THE SLAUGHTER BEGIN!" the neon-suited Announcer shrieked from his floating platform high above the dirt.
The Announcer slammed his fist down onto a massive red button on his podium.
BWWWWAAAAAAHHHHHH!
A deafening booming war-horn blasted through the colosseum, shaking the dust from the massive stalactites on the ceiling.

The place instantly descended into a brawl. The packed dirt of the arena floor immediately erupted into massive clouds of choking thick brown dust as over two hundred men charged at each other simultaneously.
There was no strategy and there was no hesitation. It was just immediate violence.
"DIE!" a man screamed.
"KILL HIM!" another roared.
Fists slammed into jaws with wet heavy impacts as heavy boots crushed violently into unprotected stomachs.
CRACK!
SNAP!
The sickening overlapping sounds of snapping bones, shattering teeth, and tearing cartilage echoed over the deafening roar of the spectator crowd.
Silas stood his ground, he didn’t rush forward to engage.
He observed the madness swirling around him with cold detachment, letting his blue eyes process the chaos.
Ten feet to his left, the violence peaked instantly.
A massive brute that was heavily augmented with oversized industrial-grade mechanical hands designed for crushing concrete, grabbed a smaller completely normal human fighter by the shoulders.
"Hahahaha!"
The normal guy screamed, desperately clawing at the brute’s metal wrists but the brute just roared.
"DIE!" He pulled his right arm back as the heavy servos began whining with mechanical strain.
He swung the massive metal-plated fist directly into the normal guy’s face.
THWACK!
The impact sounded exactly like a sledgehammer hitting a ripe melon.
A massive spray of hot dark blood and shattered white teeth exploded into the air, raining down across the dirt.
The normal man’s face literally caved inward.

The bridge of his nose and his cheekbones were completely smashed flat against his skull as the brute released his grip, and the dead man dropped heavily to the dirt like a discarded ragdoll with his limbs completely limp.
It was a brutal environment.
Suddenly, the choking dust cloud directly in front of Silas parted.
A massive scarred street thug charged blindly out of the smog. The man’s eyes were wide and completely crazed with adrenaline.
He was gripping a smuggled jagged piece of rusted iron rebar tightly in his calloused hands.
The thug locked his crazed eyes onto Silas’s menacing Oni mask.
In the chaotic frenzy of the Battle Royale, the thug’s drug-addled brain made a fatal miscalculation.
He saw a lone stationary fighter standing perfectly still near the edge of the cage and he decided Silas was an easy distracted target.
"AAAAAGGGGHHH!" the thug roared a guttural battle cry with his spit flying through the air.

He charged the final three steps, raising the heavy rusted iron pipe high above his head as he threw his entire body weight forward, swinging the rebar down in a vicious sweeping arc aimed directly at the center of Silas’s skull.
Silas didn’t even shift his stance.
His light blue, enhanced eyes tracked the exact flawless trajectory of the swing in slow motion.
Through the lens of his Rip-Current Perception,
Silas saw the microscopic tearing strain in the thug’s abdominal muscles as he overcommitted to the swing.
’Heh... so this is how Morwenna feels...’
He saw the exact unbalanced pivot point of the man’s hips so Silas casually leaned his head exactly two inches to the right.
WHOOSH!
The heavy iron pipe whistled violently through the empty air, tearing through the space Silas’s head had occupied a millisecond prior.
The rusted metal missed the silver fangs of his Oni mask by a fraction of a single hair.
The momentum of the missed swing carried the thug forward as the rebar slammed uselessly into the dirt, burying itself three inches deep into the mud.
Before the thug could even process the complete failure of his ambush—
Before the man’s drug-addled brain could even send the electrical signals to his arms to pull the heavy weapon back out of the dirt...
Silas reacted.

He simply cocked his right hand back exactly six inches and he punched the man directly in the center of his stomach, targeting the exact microscopic weakness he had identified in the thug’s overextended abdominal wall.
KRA-THOOM!
The force of the punch was devastating... no it was more than devastating... It was a disaster.
Silas’s physical strength, completely unfiltered by any restraint or holding back, exploded violently into the man’s torso.
The thug’s bloodshot eyes literally bugged out of his skull, bulging against his eyelids.
CRUNCH!
His entire ribcage shattered instantly with the bones cratering inward to protect the spine as all the oxygen in his lungs was violently vaporized, escaping his mouth in a wet choked gasp.
The overwhelming concussive force of the Warlord blow didn’t just knock the man down.
It lifted the two-hundred-pound thug completely off his feet, defying gravity too.
WHOOSH!
He was blasted violently backward through the dusty air like a human cannonball fired from a siege weapon.
He flew backward through the air for twenty solid feet.
"Look out!" someone screamed in the dust.
BAM!
The flying thug crashed violently into a dense brawling cluster of five other fighters who were busy grappling near the center of the ring.
The impact was catastrophic. The human projectile bowled all five of them over like fleshy bowling pins.
They went down in a chaotic screaming tangle of broken limbs, shattered cybernetics, and heavy groans.
The massive impact caused a sudden violent ripple of chaos in that specific quadrant of the arena.
Silas slowly lowered his fist.
He looked down at his black leather-gloved hand. There was no pain in his knuckles and there was no strain in his wrist either.
There was only a genuine sense of disappointment settling in his chest.
He slowly flexed his fingers, testing the joints.
’Compared to the monsters in the Umbral Basin,’ Silas thought to himself, his blue eyes watching the cluster of groaning men desperately struggling to stand back up in the bloody dirt.
’Or even the trained women in my own territory...’ Silas continued his thoughts.
Tamsin, Brida, Gunnhild... any one of his people could have blocked that punch or at least rolled with the momentum.
’But this... this is just like breaking cheap fragile toys.’
These men possessed no dense refined mana shields to protect their organs and they had no lineage reinforcing their bones.
They were just regular humans wrapped in cheap, rusty scrap metal and fueled by cheap street drugs.
He wasn’t fighting an army of hardened soldiers... He was participating in a pathetic, messy playground brawl.
But his devastating physics-defying punch had drawn massive, unwanted attention from the rest of the playground.
The surrounding fighters within a thirty-foot radius suddenly stopped brawling with each other.
They lowered their fists and shivs.
They looked at the massive groaning pile of bodies and they looked at the long, dragging crater the flying man had carved into the dirt.
Then, they slowly turned their heads.
’Fuck, this is a lot of attention...’
They looked at the terrifying broad-shouldered young man standing completely calmly in the dust cloud as the silver demon mask stared back at them with glowing blue eyes.
They immediately recognized the biggest threat in the room.
In a massive free-for-all Battle Royale, the smartest move for the weak was always to form a temporary truce and swarm the strongest fighter first.
"Get the demon!" several men shouted in unison, their voices rough with panic and adrenaline.
They pointed their jagged blood-stained shivs and heavy metal-plated fists directly in his direction.
An uncoordinated gang of six massive augmented Syndicate enforcers immediately broke away from the main chaotic brawl.
They weren’t mindless street thugs like Silas expected.
’I’m surprised...’
They advanced toward Silas in a tight semi-circle, intentionally fanning out to cut off his escape routes.
They intended to completely surround him, pin him against the Null-stone cage, and overwhelm him with coordinated numbers.
’They actually have sense... though they don’t have the power.’
Silas didn’t back up.
His glowing blue eyes flicked rapidly between the six approaching men.
His Rip-Current Perception went into overdrive.
In a single second, he analyzed everything.

He read their wide combat stances... He identified the cheap refurbished cybernetics bolted to their limbs... He mapped out their exact physical flaws, their old injuries, and their terrible weight distribution.
Silas let out a quiet breath.
"Haah..."
He completely dropped his arms, letting them hang loosely at his sides as he relaxed his broad shoulders.
"Come then, I won’t hold back."
The first enforcer reached him.
The man possessed reinforced titanium plating bolted directly over his shins.
He lunged forward, planting his pivot foot and launching a devastating high-speed roundhouse kick aimed directly at Silas’s floating ribs.
It was a kick designed to snap a man in half.
WHOOSH!
The titanium leg sliced through the dusty air.
Silas didn’t dodge backward and he didn’t block with his arms either, instead the man stepped into the kick.
He moved faster than the human eye could track as he closed the distance in a fraction of a second, raising his own knee in a flawless perfectly timed interception.
’I’m sure I look cool...’
He didn’t aim for the titanium plating as his Rip-Current Perception saw the exact millimeter where the metal armor ended and the soft vulnerable flesh began.
Silas struck the man’s unprotected femur bone just above the cybernetics by driving his knee forward with the force of solid mythril.
SNAP!

chapters.title: Chapter 361: Battle Royale [II / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: "AHHHHHHHHH!"
The man clutched his ruined inverted leg.
Before the man’s scream even finished echoing off the Null-stone bars, Silas had already moved on.
He pivoted flawlessly on his heel with his cloth whipping around his knees.
"Ah! Fuck you!"
"You bastard!"
The second and third enforcers charged him simultaneously from the left and right flanks.
They roared, throwing a furious coordinated flurry of heavy brutal boxing hooks aimed at his jaw and temples.
SWISH! WHOOSH! SWIPE!
Silas moved like a ghost in the dust.
His Rip-Current Perception processed their muscle twitches and predicted their strikes a full half-second before their fists even fired forward.
He slipped seamlessly between their crossing punches. He wove his torso left, then right, ducking under a massive right hook with flawless millimeter-perfect precision.
They were swinging at a shadow.
"That won’t be enough... you know?"
Silas stepped directly between them. He reached his left hand out, grabbing the second man tightly by the throat.
He didn’t try to punch him as he simply used the man’s own forward momentum against him.
Silas twisted his hips, effortlessly lifting the heavy enforcer off his feet, and hurled him violently sideways directly into the charging path of the third man.
CRACK!
Their skulls collided mid-air with a sickening crack of bone against bone.
Both enforcers instantly went limp with their eyes rolling back into their heads.
They dropped simultaneously, falling completely unconscious into the blood-soaked mud at Silas’s feet.
Three down... Three left...
The fourth man stopped his charge. He stared at the three bodies on the ground, entirely terrified by the incomprehensible speed of the man in front of him.
Panic took over his training. The man reached into his waistband and pulled out a smuggled serrated hunting knife.
"Die, you freak!" the man screamed, abandoning the semi-circle formation. He lunged blindly, sprinting forward to plunge the steel directly into Silas’s exposed back.
Silas didn’t even turn around.
He didn’t need to see the man to know his exact coordinates and Silas simply planted his left boot into the dirt.
He executed a flawless blindingly fast spinning back-kick.
THUD!
His heavy combat boot caught the charging man squarely in the center of the chest.
The force didn’t just stop the man’s momentum as it completely caved in his sternum, driving the bone directly back into his lungs.
The man was launched backward through the air, flying ten feet across the dirt.
He slammed violently back-first into the towering glowing bars of the Null-stone cage.
BZZZZZT!
The anti-magic field reacted to the violent physical contact as a massive surge of blue electrical energy discharged from the stone bars, electrocuting the man instantly.
His body spasmed wildly against the cage for two seconds before slumping lifelessly to the ground with smoke rising from his tactical vest.
Only two men remained of the original six-man coordinated gang.
They completely froze in their tracks.
They lowered their fists, staring in soul-crushing horror at the masked demon standing amidst the carnage.
"Aren’t you going to... come at me?"
He had just dismantled their entire elite crew in less than four seconds.
The fifth man’s survival instincts finally kicked in as he dropped his brass knuckles into the dirt.
He turned around and began to sprint away, desperately trying to run back into the chaotic anonymity of the main Battle Royale.
"No you don’t." Silas muttered quietly to himself.
Silas closed the distance in a single explosive burst of raw speed. The dirt literally exploded beneath his boots, leaving a small crater where he had stood.
He crossed fifteen feet in the blink of an eye.
He grabbed the fleeing man forcefully by the thick Kevlar collar of his tactical vest but Silas didn’t slow down.
"Where do you get off thinking you can run?"
He effortlessly hauled the man’s entire two-hundred-and-twenty-pound body weight straight up into the air above his head, holding him suspended for a brief terrifying second.
With ruthless power, Silas brought his right leg up and then he drove his leg straight down in a devastating vertical axe kick.
The reinforced heel of his combat boot slammed precisely into the back of the suspended man’s skull.
KRA-CRUNCH!
Silas drove the man’s face violently straight down into the hard, packed dirt of the arena floor.
BOOM!
The impact caused the ground to physically shudder as a small circular crater formed in the packed earth around the man’s buried head.
The enforcer went instantly limp with his arms splayed out awkwardly, buried completely up to his ears in the mud.
He didn’t twitch anymore.
Silas slowly lowered his leg, turning his masked face toward the final survivor.
The sixth and final man didn’t even try to run... He didn’t try to fight.
He immediately dropped heavily to his knees in the dirt. He threw his hands high up into the air, trembling violently with tears of pure terror streaking down his dirty face in a desperate surrender.
’Damn...’
Silas stared down at the trembling man for a long second.
Then, Silas simply ignored him. He stepped casually past the sobbing thug, leaving him alive in the dust.
Suddenly, a subtle dangerous shift in the air currents caught Silas’s attention.
His Rip-Current Perception detected a minute flex of muscles thirty feet away.
The original street thug from the very first punch... the one he had blasted twenty feet into the crowd was not dead.
He was still groaning on the ground, clutching his shattered ribs but he was desperate.
He was utterly humiliated and he was enraged beyond all logical reason.
’Don’t tell me he’s going t—’
The thug slowly reached over with his good arm. He pressed a hidden release latch on his left forearm and a hidden compartment popped open in his cheap cybernetic arm.
’Why do I even try?’
He reached inside and pulled out a small illegal kinetic pistol.
The thug raised his trembling arm, aiming the barrel directly at the back of Silas’s dark clothes, fully intending to shoot the distracted demon in the back and claim the glory.
"I got you..." the thug whispered, his finger tightening on the trigger.
Silas didn’t even flinch.
He knew the unbreakable rules of the arena significantly better than the desperate drug-addled fool lying in the dirt did.
CRACK!
A heavy high-velocity kinetic slug rained down from the dark shadowed catwalks high above the Null-stone cage.
The sniper shot was flawless and it hit the thug squarely in his left shoulder.
SPLAT!
The massive caliber bullet didn’t just pierce the flesh.
It completely blew the man’s cybernetic arm and the illegal, smuggled pistol entirely off his torso in a horrifying explosion of hot blood, shattered bone, and sparking metal shrapnel.
"AGGGHHHHHH!" the thug shrieked, rolling in the dirt as arterial blood geysered from his missing shoulder socket.
The strict lethal enforcement of the Underworld snipers had cleared the cowardly threat before Silas even had to turn around to address it himself.
The overwhelming brutality of Silas’s blistering counter-attack, combined with the explosive sniper intervention, created a massive visible circle in his specific quadrant of the arena.

Dozens of brawling fighters had stopped their matches to watch the slaughter and now, they frantically backed away, pushing against each other just to put more distance between themselves and the terrifying man.
They completely refused to even look in the general direction of the silver Oni mask.
The place cleared up a bit, giving Silas a wide comfortable radius of room to breathe.
"Haah..."
He stood alone in the center of the carnage with a pile of broken bodies scattered around his boots.
But the empty peaceful space didn’t last long.
THUD! THUD! THUD!
Heavy mechanically enhanced footsteps echoed loudly over the packed dirt, cutting through the noise of the surrounding brawls.
The remaining crowd of fighters actively parted like water. They stumbled out of the way, making a wide path for the undisputed recognized apex predator of the fighting pit.
The massive tattooed Mantis guy approached Silas.
He walked with the slow arrogant swagger of a man who owned the very ground he stepped on.

His bulging steroid-pumped body looked incredibly grotesque up close. His muscles were so unnaturally massive that the tribal tattoos stretching across his chest and arms were physically warped and distorted.
His bright green angular metal Mantis mask gleamed sharply under the harsh stadium lights.
Silas stood perfectly still, watching the giant approach.
With his glowing blue enhanced eyes, Silas could see the thick, pulsing, purple veins bulging violently on the giant’s thick neck.
The Boss’s son was actively circulating his massive pool of internal mana.
He was pushing his physical strength, his bone density, and his muscle fibers to an unnatural extreme.
’Ah but it’s not enough...’
He was breaking every biological limit his body possessed but still... Silas was not impressed.
The giant stopped exactly ten feet away from Silas.
"You," the Mantis brute growled, his voice a deep rumble of pure arrogance.
He pointed a thick cybernetically reinforced finger directly at Silas’s Oni mask.
"You are making too much noise in my father’s pit," the Mantis guy declared. "And for that reason, you need to be eliminated immediately."
Silas didn’t say a single word.
He didn’t offer a witty retort as he just stood there with his hands in his pockets.
’So he’s the son of the Boss, huh? No wonder he smells like those cigarettes.’
He just stared silently through the narrow slits of his mask.
His light blue, enhanced eyes were rapidly reading the myriad of glaring structural flaws hidden within the giant’s over-pumped unbalanced muscles.
The giant was strong, yes but his mass made his joints stiff and his center of gravity completely top-heavy.
The silence infuriated the arrogant giant.
"I SAID DIE!" the Mantis guy roared with spit flying from behind his green mask.
He charged directly at Silas.
He moved with the unstoppable speed and massive crushing mass of a runaway freight train as the dirt literally shook under his heavy boots.
He closed the distance instantly and he planted his massive feet and threw a devastating wide haymaker punch aimed directly at the side of Silas’s head.
It was a brutal full-power blow specifically designed to decapitate a normal man but Silas simply took a calm, measured half-step back.
WHOOSH!
"You’re quite slow..."
The massive metal-plated fist whipped violently through the air, passing harmlessly just an inch past the silver horns of his Oni mask.
The wind pressure generated by the missed punch violently ruffled Silas’s dark hair and snapped the collar of his uniform backward but the physical fist never even grazed him.
’Is he perhaps in the second stage of Core Advancement too?’ Silas thought, the guy was quite strong.
The Mantis growled in frustration, quickly recovering his balance.
"HAAAAAAH!"
He immediately launched into a relentless high-speed overwhelming combo of devastating strikes.
SWISH! WHOOSH! SWIPE!
He threw heavy right crosses, brutal hooks, and sweeping devastating leg kicks aimed at Silas’s knees.
He was undeniably fast for his size and he was incredibly strong but against the flawless precognitive Rip-Current Perception of Silas?
He was painfully slow.
Silas dodged every single one of his strikes without breaking a sweat.
He slipped to the left, effortlessly weaving his torso under a massive crushing cross.
WHOOSH!
He leaned smoothly backward at the waist, letting a sweeping cybernetic kick sail mere inches from his chest plate.
WHOOSH!
He bobbed his head slightly to the right, easily ducking a massive, jaw-breaking uppercut that would have sent a lesser man to the morgue.
WHOOSH!
It was as though Silas was the wind itself... intangible, completely formless, and absolutely untouchable.
He didn’t even bother raising his hands to block the strikes since blocking meant absorbing force.
’Not like the forces of his attacks would do anything...’
He just moved his body, letting the furious screaming giant completely exhaust his massive stamina reserves punching at ghosts and empty air.
Behind the dark visor of his mask, Silas was getting genuinely annoyed.
He had honestly thought, based on the terrified rumors in the fitting room and the overwhelming physical size of the man, that the Boss’s son would be a good trained martial artist.
He had actually expected a decent physical challenge to test his stats against.
But he was absolutely not a martial artist.
He was just a spoiled overgrown brawler relying entirely on expensive, daddy-funded cybernetics and a rigged tournament script to win his fights.
There was no technique and there was no discipline.
WHOOSH!
The Mantis guy finally stopped his furious useless assault.
"Haah... Haah..."
He stood panting heavily, his massive chest heaving with deep ragged breaths as sweat poured down his tattooed torso.
’Fuck...’
He realized with a sinking terrifying dread that he couldn’t land a single, solid blow on the man wearing an Oni mask.
Frustration and deep public humiliation twisted his rigid posture as the entire arena was watching him swing at air.
Desperate to regain control of the narrative, he resorted to the lowest and most pathetic denominator of a losing street fighter.

"Stand still, you pathetic coward!" the Mantis guy roared furiously, spitting a massive wad of saliva onto the dirt between them. "Stop dancing around the ring like a frightened little woman! Put your hands up and fight me like a man!"

chapters.title: Chapter 362: Battle Royale [III / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Silas didn’t react as he just stared at the heaving giant with his blue eyes looking unimpressed.

"What’s wrong underneath that ugly demon mask?" the brute sneered, taking an aggressive step forward, pointing his finger again. "Did your mother not teach you how to properly throw a punch? Oh, wait, I know exactly your type of slum-rat. She was probably just a cheap gutter-trash whore who—"
Silas’s left eye twitched violently behind the dark metal of his mask.
It wasn’t a twitch of emotional devastation.
When Silas had suddenly woken up in this brutal world, he didn’t possess any actual living parents.
He had no lingering memories of a mother or a father raising him in this life so the insult itself had zero emotional weight attached to it.
It meant nothing to him.
’But still...’
It was the pathetic desperation of the tactic that offended him.
It was a disgusting insult to the pure art of combat... When a warrior couldn’t win with his fists, he shouldn’t resort to crying about mothers in the mud.
’Look at me talking like I’m a real warrior or something, I’d do the same if the situation arose.’
Not that it would, after all, he was strong and this guy was weak... That was the difference between them.
With only disappointment shining coldly in his glowing blue eyes, Silas decided to finally end this boring theatrical farce.
Silas dashed backward, retreating five quick, fluid steps across the dirt to create a wide gap of distance.
The Mantis, thinking he finally had his opponent on the run, took the bait completely.
’Hah... I knew it, now I just need to take a good shot at him and break his bones.’
His steroid-addled brain completely failed to process the blatant trap being laid out right in front of him.
WHOOSH!

Blinded by his own overwhelming arrogance and the blinding rush of adrenaline pumping through his thick mutated veins, he saw Silas’s fluid retreat not as a maneuver, but as an act of pure cowardly desperation.
"HAHA! WHERE ARE YOU RUNNING TO?!"

His massive combat boots tore massive chunks of mud and packed earth out of the ground with every single thunderous stride as he moved with the terrifying unstoppable momentum of a runaway siege engine and his bloodshot eyes fixated on the silver demon mask retreating before him.
’Y-you... I hate you...’
He dropped his guard, winding his cybernetic arm back and committing fully, one hundred percent of his massive body weight and internal mana into a full-power lunging punch designed to end the fight.
’I’ll end you... in one go...!’
It was a display of overkill.
The heavy industrial-grade hydraulic pistons built directly into his shoulder and elbow joints shrieked with a high-pitched metallic whine as they pressurized.
PSSSSH! PSSSSSH!

’So those snipers don’t see this?’ Silas thought as the thick purple veins bulging across Mantis’s tattooed neck throbbed violently as he forced every single ounce of his internal restricted mana into his right fist.
He wasn’t just trying to knock Silas out...
Mantis was trying to punch a hole straight through the man’s chest cavity and splatter his organs across the Null-stone cage!
However...
It was a terrible mistake.
’Got you.’
Through the flawless precognitive lens of his light blue Rip-Current Perception, Silas watched the entire clumsy sequence unfold in agonizing slow motion.

He saw the giant’s center of gravity shift dangerously far forward and he saw the massive gaping void in the brute’s defensive posture, leaving his entire centerline completely exposed to counter-attack.
The Boss’s son had sacrificed every single principle of martial balance for a single pride-fueled strike.
The exact second the giant lunged, Silas stopped retreating.
The sudden physics-defying halt in his backward momentum made Mantis’s eyes widen as he planted his boot into the dirt, anchoring his stance with the immovable density of a mountain.
WHOOSH!
The packed earth beneath his heel instantly compressed into solid stone beneath the weight of his frame.
He didn’t say a single word to Mantis as he executed a flawless sidestep, slipping perfectly inside the giant’s wide telegraphed guard.
’All I have to do now... is to hit him...’
The massive cybernetic fist whipped past Silas’s head, tearing through the empty air with a deafening sound.
WHOOSH!
The displaced wind pressure violently snapped the collar of Silas’s dark uniform, but the lethal metal didn’t even graze his skin.
Silas reared his right hand backward, twisting his hips to generate maximum torque.
"N-no, it’s not supposed to—"

Silas channeled the raw oceanic depths of his Mythic Gold Core then he drew the pure physical strength up from his anchored heel, spiraling it through his calves, his thighs, and his core, transferring the terrifying load flawlessly into his shoulder.
"B–ugh!"
He unleashed a devastating uppercut.
His fist bypassed the giant’s thick muscled chest completely, crashing cleanly and brutally upward into the bottom of the green Mantis mask.
He struck the exact perfect weak point of the man’s jawline.
KRA-BOOOM!
The explosion echoed through the entire colossal cavern.
The sound that followed was not that of flesh striking flesh.

It was the terrifying concussive boom of an artillery shell detonating in a closed space as a visible shockwave ripped outward from the exact point of impact, violently blasting a perfect ring of dust and dirt thirty feet into the air.
The green ultra-dense alloy of the Mantis mask instantly, violently shattered into a thousand spinning pieces of shrapnel as the reinforced bone of the giant’s jaw disintegrated into a fine powder.
The terrifying upward force of Silas’s strength didn’t just knock the giant backward. It defied gravity too!
The transfer was so overwhelmingly powerful that the Boss’s son didn’t even have the chance to stumble or fall.
His massive combat-booted feet were violently ripped entirely out of the dirt.
"AHHHHHHHHHHHHH!"
The three-hundred-pound cybernetically enhanced man was violently launched straight up into the air like a ballistic missile.
He blasted upward at a terrifying velocity, leaving a thick spiraling trail of dust in his wake.
His massive body blurred into a dark ascending streak, rocketing upward through the harsh glare of the stadium spotlights.
He bypassed the fifty-foot mark in a fraction of a second with his limp unconscious limbs flailing wildly against the intense air resistance.
"Ah!"
High above the arena, the neon-suited Announcer shrieked in terror.
He had been leaning over his podium, screaming into his microphone to hype up the brawl below, completely oblivious to the anti-aircraft strike that had just been unleashed.
He looked down just in time to see three hundred pounds of bleeding, pulverized meat rocketing directly toward his face.
"Nooo!"
He had to violently jerk the controls of his floating anti-gravity platform, swerving wildly out of the way to prevent a catastrophic mid-air collision as the unconscious giant rocketed past him.

The wind pressure generated by the giant’s ascending mass violently ripped the microphone directly out of the Announcer’s hand and tore the lapels off his ridiculous neon-purple suit and the floating platform spun wildly, sparking with magical feedback as the Announcer clung desperately to the guardrail, screaming for his life.
The Mantis continued his terrifying ascent until he met the thick reinforced rock ceiling of the cavern.
BAM!
He smashed directly into the stalactites with a sickening bone-shattering crunch and the impact physically shook the underground cavern.
Massive chunks of jagged stone broke off the ceiling, raining down in a dangerous shower over the packed crowd below.
For one horrifying second, the momentum of Silas’s uppercut literally pinned the three-hundred-pound giant flush against the solid rock roof which was a hundred and fifty feet in the air.
"Ugh!"
He coughed out a massive visible spray of hot blood that rained down over the crowd in a horrific, crimson mist, before gravity finally reclaimed him as he peeled off the shattered rock face.
And then the son of the Boss fell back down toward the arena floor like a broken meteor.
The descent was terrifying.
The wind howled around his limp form as terminal velocity took over, dragging the pulverized bleeding mass of the Boss’s son back down toward the bloody dirt of the cage.
Silas however wasn’t finished.
"Don’t think you’re escaping that easy... I still have something for you."
He hadn’t even looked up to watch the man hit the ceiling as he already knew exactly where the body was going.
Silas had already pivoted his body with his glowing light blue eyes tracking the falling trajectory with flawless precision.
He shifted his weight, digging his left boot firmly into the cratered dirt as he raised his right leg, coiling his muscled thigh and hip like a massive spring.
WHOOSH!
The exact second the falling giant descended into striking range, Silas unleashed a devastating horizontal roundhouse kick.
The heavy leather of his combat boot whipped through the air, creating a shockwave with a sharp sound as his heavy boot caught the Mantis guy squarely in the side of the face.
He kicked him directly across the horizontal axis of the arena!
The secondary impact sounded like a bomb detonating.
BOOOOOOOOOOOOOM!
The concussive shockwave from the kick blew a second massive ring of dust outward, forcing the nearest brawlers to shield their eyes.

The giant’s plummeting vertical trajectory was violently altered into a horizontal one as he was blasted laterally across the massive dirt arena, flying over the heads of the shocked brawlers like a skipped stone.
He sailed through the air for a staggering eighty feet.

Entire gangs of brawling street thugs and cybernetic assassins completely stopped fighting, their jaws dropping as they watched a three-hundred-pound giant fly cleanly over their heads in a shower of blood and sparking wires.
He slammed directly into the towering glowing Null-stone wall of the cage.
The massive collision sounded like a speeding train plowing directly into a solid brick wall.
BOOOOOOM! BZZZZZT!
The impact physically warped the magical bars, creating a massive crater in the stone perimeter.
The thick glowing blue Null-stone shrieked under the kinetic trauma, violently discharging arcs of raw lightning that scorched the surrounding dirt black.
The entire fifty-foot cage visibly shuddered from the force of the blow.
The Boss’s son slumped to the dirt, completely unresponsive with his mask shattered and his cybernetics sparking uselessly.
His right arm was bent at a horrifying unnatural angle and his chest didn’t rise.
He was a crumpled pulverized heap of broken metal and shattered bone, utterly decimated in front of his father’s entire empire.

The entire colossal arena... all two hundred surviving fighters, the thousands of screaming spectators, and the elite VIP Managers sitting safely in the luxury boxes above went completely, absolutely, breathlessly silent.
The booming Taiko drums ceased their thumping.
The violent chaotic brawl in the mud completely stopped as dozens of shivs and metal fists were slowly lowered to the sides of terrified men.
Even the ruthless Syndicate snipers perched on the dark catwalks froze with their fingers lingering on their triggers, unsure of how to process the slaughter they had just witnessed.
The undisputed favorite, the Boss’s own blood, a genetically enhanced monster pumped full of black-market combat steroids, had just been swatted like an annoying insect in less than thirty seconds.
The neon-suited Announcer, recovering from his near-death experience, gripped the railing of his floating platform with white-knuckled trembling hands.
"Haah... Haah... I need...."
He slowly looked down from his spinning platform and he stared down at the terrifying man in the dark uniform.
Silas was simply standing in the center of the ring, slowly lowering his leg and his silver demon mask gleaming under the stadium lights, completely unfazed by the violence he had just wrought.
The Announcer swallowed hard.
His job was to hype the crowd so he reached down with a shaking hand and picked up a secondary backup microphone from the floor of his platform as he brought the device to his lips.
And then, the Announcer’s hysterical shrieking voice echoed through the massive speakers, declaring the victor’s utterly ridiculous moniker.
"AND THAT’S ONII-CHANNNNNN!!!"
The crowd was first struck with a wave of deep apprehension.
"Huh?"
"What kind of name is that?"
They heard the name.
Their brains struggled to connect the cutesy degenerate anime term with the terrifying broad-shouldered man in the silver demon mask who had just defied the laws of physics.
But nobody laughed. Not a single person in the massive stadium dared to chuckle at the name...
Instead, a low rumbling murmur swept through the tiered seating.
The apprehension rapidly dissolved into something much more dangerous and volatile.
It turned into pure financial rage!
"My credits!" a man screamed from the lower bleachers, gripping his hair in despair.
"No! No, no, no! He was the favorite to win!" another spectator roared, throwing his half-empty beer directly at the reinforced glass of the cage.
They began cursing wildly.

The crowd realized they had just lost their entire life savings... Because the tournament was famously rigged in favor of the Black-Ash family, almost ninety percent of the stadium had dumped their entire betting pools directly onto the Mantis’s head to survive the Battle Royale.
The roaring curses quickly turned away from the bleeding giant and shifted directly toward Silas.
"Fuck you, Onii-chan!"
"I’ll kill you! You cost me everything!"

His massive combat boots tore massive chunks of mud and packed earth out of the ground with every single thunderous stride as he moved with the terrifying unstoppable momentum of a runaway siege engine and his bloodshot eyes fixated on the silver demon mask retreating before him.
’Y-you...
I hate you...’
He dropped his guard, winding his cybernetic arm back and committing fully, one hundred percent of his massive body weight and internal mana into a full-power lunging punch designed to end the fight.

It was a display of overkill.
The heavy industrial-grade hydraulic pistons built directly into his shoulder and elbow joints shrieked with a high-pitched metallic whine as they pressurized.

Through the flawless precognitive lens of his light blue Rip-Current Perception, Silas watched the entire clumsy sequence unfold in agonizing slow motion.

He saw the giant’s center of gravity shift dangerously far forward and he saw the massive gaping void in the brute’s defensive posture, leaving his entire centerline completely exposed to counter-attack.
The Boss’s son had sacrificed every single principle of martial balance for a single pride-fueled strike.
The exact second the giant lunged, Silas stopped retreating.
The sudden physics-defying halt in his backward momentum made Mantis’s eyes widen as he planted his boot into the dirt, anchoring his stance with the immovable density of a mountain.
WHOOSH!
The packed earth beneath his heel instantly compressed into solid stone beneath the weight of his frame.
He didn’t say a single word to Mantis as he executed a flawless sidestep, slipping perfectly inside the giant’s wide telegraphed guard.
’All I have to do now... is to hit him...’
The massive cybernetic fist whipped past Silas’s head, tearing through the empty air with a deafening sound.
WHOOSH!
The displaced wind pressure violently snapped the collar of Silas’s dark uniform, but the lethal metal didn’t even graze his skin.
Silas reared his right hand backward, twisting his hips to generate maximum torque.
"N-no, it’s not supposed to—"

Silas channeled the raw oceanic depths of his Mythic Gold Core then he drew the pure physical strength up from his anchored heel, spiraling it through his calves, his thighs, and his core, transferring the terrifying load flawlessly into his shoulder.
"B–ugh!"
He unleashed a devastating uppercut.
His fist bypassed the giant’s thick muscled chest completely, crashing cleanly and brutally upward into the bottom of the green Mantis mask.
He struck the exact perfect weak point of the man’s jawline.
KRA-BOOOM!
The explosion echoed through the entire colossal cavern.
The sound that followed was not that of flesh striking flesh.

It was the terrifying concussive boom of an artillery shell detonating in a closed space as a visible shockwave ripped outward from the exact point of impact, violently blasting a perfect ring of dust and dirt thirty feet into the air.
The green ultra-dense alloy of the Mantis mask instantly, violently shattered into a thousand spinning pieces of shrapnel as the reinforced bone of the giant’s jaw disintegrated into a fine powder.
The terrifying upward force of Silas’s strength didn’t just knock the giant backward.
It defied gravity too!
The transfer was so overwhelmingly powerful that the Boss’s son didn’t even have the chance to stumble or fall.
His massive combat-booted feet were violently ripped entirely out of the dirt.
"AHHHHHHHHHHHHH!"
The three-hundred-pound cybernetically enhanced man was violently launched straight up into the air like a ballistic missile.
He blasted upward at a terrifying velocity, leaving a thick spiraling trail of dust in his wake.
His massive body blurred into a dark ascending streak, rocketing upward through the harsh glare of the stadium spotlights.
He bypassed the fifty-foot mark in a fraction of a second with his limp unconscious limbs flailing wildly against the intense air resistance.
"Ah!"
