chapters.title: Chapter 363: Battle Royale [IV / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Thousands of people were screaming death threats at the man in the uniform, their faces red with fury.
Far above the chaos, sitting comfortably in a private security booth overlooking the arena, the wicked black-haired receptionist from the dive bar leaned back in her squeaking leather chair.
She took a slow deep drag of her Red-Lotus cigarette.
"Hm?"
She exhaled a thick cloud of cherry-scented smoke with her dark eyes glued to the live holographic feed of the demon-masked young man.
She raised a pierced eyebrow.
’Oh,’ the receptionist thought to herself with a smirk curling on her black-painted lips. ’He’s that strong? What a terrifying monster.’
Back down in the filthy blood-soaked field of the Null-stone cage, Silas completely ignored the thousands of death threats raining down from the bleachers.
He let out a sigh with the sound vibrating through his mask.
’Is this enough to prove a point...?’

Silas looked around at everyone else in the dirt. The Battle Royale was still technically ongoing as there were still over two hundred desperate fighters trapped in the cage, and only twelve were allowed to survive.
But upon decimating the Mantis guy with such casual brutality, an invisible perimeter had formed around Silas.
Apparently, there were no more idiots left in the pit who were willing to challenge him.
The surrounding street thugs, cybernetic assassins, and Syndicate enforcers actively pressed their backs against the Null-stone bars just to stay as far away from him as physically possible.
They resumed fighting each other, but they kept one terrified eye glued to his mask.
’I need to make myself more scary so that even the idiots don’t approach me...’ Silas thought.
He didn’t want to waste his stamina chasing down terrified rats for the next hour as he wanted them to leave him alone entirely until the timer ran out.
And so, Silas did the most disrespectful and intimidating thing a fighter could possibly do in the middle of a two-hundred-man death match.
He sat down.
Right there, in the dead center of the blood-stained muddy arena. Silas slowly lowered his massive frame, folding his long legs into a casual cross-legged sitting position.
He was wearing the smart-fabric Black-Ash uniform which repelled grime, so he wasn’t particularly worried about getting his gear permanently dirty.
"Haah... What an exhausting boring fight..."
Silas let out a slow breath, slumping his head forward slightly as he closed his golden-ringed eyes behind the silver mask.
The surrounding brawls momentarily paused with dozens of fighters frozen mid-punch, staring at the man in horrifying disbelief.
It seemed that he had literally just fallen asleep in the middle of a slaughterhouse!
It was a display of such crushing arrogance and overwhelming confidence that it shattered the morale of everyone looking at him.
If he was willing to sleep while surrounded by armed killers, it meant he viewed them as less than insects.
Nobody dared to approach him... Not a single fighter took a step toward his seated form.
They swallowed hard, turned away, and desperately went back to fighting and killing each other on the outer edges of the arena, abandoning the center ring to the sleeping demon.
’When will this end...?’ Silas thought, listening to the wet sounds of flesh tearing and bones snapping around him.
As of right now, he was genuinely bored out of his mind.
High above the carnage, in the crowded luxurious VIP viewing box, Evelyn stood frozen near the reinforced glass.
A single drop of cold sweat rolled down her pale temple, hidden behind her Kitsune mask.
’He’s... he’s that strong?’ Evelyn thought, her brain struggling to process the math of what she had just witnessed.
Even she, a classic Lord who was directly affiliated with him was still surprised by his strength.
’Is he even a regular Lord at this point...?’
She knew Silas was strong, the Lord of Blessed Land had to be strong beyond belief but this was different.
This was completely without outer mana enhancement.
The Null-stone bands on his wrists strictly forbade external projection and sure, she knew he could have manipulated the rules and enhanced his inner muscles and bone density, but still...
To launch a three-hundred-pound man a hundred and fifty feet straight up into solid rock using nothing but raw power?
Suddenly, a deep laugh echoed from the front of the viewing box.
"Hah... Hahahaha."
It was the Boss.
The silver-haired Syndicate leader sat in his leather throne, staring down at the shattered bleeding body of his own cybernetically enhanced son but he didn’t look angry.
He seemed to let out a genuine entertained laugh.
The sound instantly made the entire crowded room feel icy cold.
The temperature in the luxury suite seemed to plummet twenty degrees as the other Managers froze, lowering their expensive drinks, terrified by the Boss’s reaction to his own blood being pulverized.
Evelyn turned her masked head toward him with her hand instinctively twitching toward her thigh holsters.
The other Managers turned as well, but the Boss’s dark gaze was solely fixed on Evelyn.
He smiled at her.
It was a cold razor-sharp smile that didn’t reach his dead eyes.
Even though this man didn’t possess a Lord Core, even though he couldn’t summon heroes or cast massive area-of-effect spells, he could clearly use internal mana.
He was a mundane underworld kingpin, and despite Evelyn being an Classic Lord who commanded an army... she was suddenly frightened.
A cold shiver raced down her spine.𝐟𝚛𝕖𝚎𝕨𝗲𝐛𝚗𝐨𝐯𝐞𝕝.𝐜𝗼𝗺
’Is there something else going on here?’ Evelyn thought. Why would she be afraid...?
The concentrated weight of the killing intent radiating from the Boss was suffocating.
It was the aura of a man who had murdered thousands of people with his bare hands to build his empire but why was it affecting her?
The Boss slowly stood up from his chair as he walked gracefully toward the back of the room, stopping a few feet away from Evelyn’s chair.
"Manager of Contestant Onii-chan, I presume..." the Boss stated, looking down at her Kitsune mask.
Evelyn forced her body to remain rigid as she gave him a single stiff nod.
The man smiled wider, exposing perfectly white teeth.
"Welcome to the Top Twelve list," the Boss told her smoothly, acknowledging Silas’s dominance of the pit.
He simply raised a hand and snapped his fingers, calling for the hospitality staff which was surprising considering Eveyn had thought the man would want revenge or something.
The young maid in the black-and-white uniform immediately rushed over, bowing deeply.

"Direct the Manager of that amazing man to a private exclusive suite," the Boss ordered the maid with his eyes never leaving Evelyn’s mask. "She no longer needs to prove herself by sitting out here with the general rabble. She has earned a quiet room..."
The maid bowed lower.
"Right away, Sir. I will oblige the errand."
The maid turned, gesturing politely for Evelyn to follow her toward a side door leading out of the general VIP box.
Evelyn didn’t hesitate. She stood up and followed the maid, eager to escape the suffocating pressure of the Syndicate leader’s gaze.
She walked down the plush crimson-carpeted hallway in silence.
Only after she had completely left that crowded room, only after the heavy oak doors shut behind her, cutting off the Boss’s line of sight, did Evelyn feel a lot calmer.
The icy grip on her lungs finally loosened.
The maid smiled warmly as they walked.
"Congratulations on your Fighter’s incredible performance, Ma’am. It was truly a historic strike..."
However, the polite words fell entirely on deaf ears. Evelyn wasn’t listening at all as she looked down at her own hands.
Her leather-gloved fingers were slightly trembling.
’What...’ Evelyn thought to herself, swallowing hard behind her mask. ’What made me so afraid of him?’
She was a Lord but standing in front of that mundane, silver-haired mafia boss had triggered an instinctual terror in her brain.
There was something terribly wrong with the Black-Ash Syndicate.
[An Hour Later]
Deep in the arena, the deafening chaotic noise of the Battle Royale finally ceased.
The heavy booming Taiko drums rolled to a dramatic final halt as the harsh blinding white stadium spotlights shifted to a dim moody crimson glow.
Silas sat up properly from his cross-legged position.
He didn’t stretch because he was trying to shrug off any sort of physical tiredness as his stamina was perfectly full.
He sat up simply because the wet sounds of absolute slaughter had finally stopped.
He opened his golden-ringed eyes and looked around the Null-stone cage.
The packed dirt was completely saturated with dark coagulating blood to the point that it honestly looked like a freshly tilled graveyard.
People had killed each other a lot to secure their spots.
There were dozens of people scattered across the dirt who were just deeply, critically wounded, groaning and clutching severed limbs or shattered cybernetics.
And on the other hand, there were a far greater amount of people that were just dead.
They were completely deceased. Bodies were piled on top of each other, their faces caved in with their chests pierced by jagged shivs.
Just like that.
Two hundred men had walked into the cage, and over a hundred and fifty of them had been brutally massacred in the span of sixty minutes.
The neon-suited Announcer, having acquired a new un-crushed microphone, hovered his anti-gravity platform down from the ceiling.
"TIME IS UP!" the Announcer’s magically amplified voice boomed across the silent bloody arena. "THE PRELIMINARY ROYALE IS OFFICIALLY OVER!"
The surviving crowd in the stands let out a roaring bloodthirsty cheer, stamping their feet against the metal bleachers.
The Announcer hovered lower, sweeping his platform across the carnage.

"Through the blood! Through the shattered steel! There are exactly twelve participants that have made it through the meat-grinder!" the Announcer screamed, hyping the survivors. "Welcome to the Top Twelve! These elite bastards will be pitted against each other in one-on-one bracket matches for your gambling enjoyment!"
The people cheered louder, throwing empty cups and betting slips into the air.
The Announcer floated his platform directly down to the center of the ring, hovering just a few feet away from Silas first.
The spotlights snapped onto the oni.
The Announcer pointed dramatically at Silas.

"Coming out of the center ring untouched! The man who broke the Boss’s bloodline! The Demon of the Dirt! The Apex Predator who defied gravity itself!" the Announcer shrieked. "If you want to get rich tonight, if you want to rob the house blind... ALWAYS BET ON ONII-CHAN!"
The crowd, their previous anger completely forgotten in the face of overwhelming power, erupted into a massive deafening chant.
"O-NII-CHAN! O-NII-CHAN! O-NII-CHAN!"
Silas stared blankly at the Announcer.
The absurdity of thousands of hardened criminals chanting a degenerate anime moniker was almost too much for his brain to process.
’The hell is going on here...? I like it though.’

The Announcer quickly pivoted his floating anti-gravity platform with the harsh blinding white stadium spotlights violently sweeping across the blood-soaked dirt to highlight the other eleven survivors who had managed to claw their way out of the meat-grinder alive.
"From the Eastern slums, with fists forged of pure depleted mythril, give it up for KURO THE MANGLER!"
The stadium spotlights slammed down onto a literal mountain of a man.
Kuro stood triumphantly atop a jagged bleeding pile of crushed cyborgs.
He was shirtless, his dark skin covered in a roadmap of jagged white scars.

His arms from the elbows down were entirely replaced by massive oversized blocks of solid dull-gray mythril and his glowing red cybernetic eyes flared as he raised those heavy metal arms and pounded them violently against his own bare chest.
CLANG! CLANG! CLANG!
The concussive metallic sound echoed through the arena like a blacksmith’s hammer, driving the crowd into a roaring frenzy.
"WE LOVE YOU KURO!"
"RAHHHHHH!"
"Next one, The shadow in the smog! The man who bleeds his enemies dry before they ever even see his blade... VIPER-TOOTH!"
The spotlight snapped to the dark edges of the Null-stone cage.
A thin hyper-agile assassin wearing a sleek, form-fitting tactical suit stepped out of the shadows.
He held two wickedly curved daggers.
The rusted steel was coated in a glowing, corrosive green neurotoxin that dripped audibly onto the dirt.
Viper-Tooth casually wiped the flat of his poisoned blade across the torn shirt of a dead man at his feet, looking up at the roaring stands and delivering a sweeping mocking bow.
"Be sure to praise me too..."

She took a slow deep drag of her Red-Lotus cigarette.
"Hm?"
She exhaled a thick cloud of cherry-scented smoke with her dark eyes glued to the live holographic feed of the demon-masked young man.
She raised a pierced eyebrow.
’Oh,’ the receptionist thought to herself with a smirk curling on her black-painted lips. ’He’s that strong?
What a terrifying monster.’
Back down in the filthy blood-soaked field of the Null-stone cage, Silas completely ignored the thousands of death threats raining down from the bleachers.
He let out a sigh with the sound vibrating through his mask.
’Is this enough to prove a point...?’
Silas looked around at everyone else in the dirt.
The Battle Royale was still technically ongoing as there were still over two hundred desperate fighters trapped in the cage, and only twelve were allowed to survive.
But upon decimating the Mantis guy with such casual brutality, an invisible perimeter had formed around Silas.
Apparently, there were no more idiots left in the pit who were willing to challenge him.
The surrounding street thugs, cybernetic assassins, and Syndicate enforcers actively pressed their backs against the Null-stone bars just to stay as far away from him as physically possible.
They resumed fighting each other, but they kept one terrified eye glued to his mask.
’I need to make myself more scary so that even the idiots don’t approach me...’ Silas thought.
He didn’t want to waste his stamina chasing down terrified rats for the next hour as he wanted them to leave him alone entirely until the timer ran out.
And so, Silas did the most disrespectful and intimidating thing a fighter could possibly do in the middle of a two-hundred-man death match.
He sat down.
Right there, in the dead center of the blood-stained muddy arena.
Silas slowly lowered his massive frame, folding his long legs into a casual cross-legged sitting position.
He was wearing the smart-fabric Black-Ash uniform which repelled grime, so he wasn’t particularly worried about getting his gear permanently dirty.
"Haah...
What an exhausting boring fight..."
Silas let out a slow breath, slumping his head forward slightly as he closed his golden-ringed eyes behind the silver mask.
The surrounding brawls momentarily paused with dozens of fighters frozen mid-punch, staring at the man in horrifying disbelief.
It seemed that he had literally just fallen asleep in the middle of a slaughterhouse!
It was a display of such crushing arrogance and overwhelming confidence that it shattered the morale of everyone looking at him.
If he was willing to sleep while surrounded by armed killers, it meant he viewed them as less than insects.
Nobody dared to approach him...
Not a single fighter took a step toward his seated form.
They swallowed hard, turned away, and desperately went back to fighting and killing each other on the outer edges of the arena, abandoning the center ring to the sleeping demon.
’When will this end...?’ Silas thought, listening to the wet sounds of flesh tearing and bones snapping around him.
As of right now, he was genuinely bored out of his mind.
High above the carnage, in the crowded luxurious VIP viewing box, Evelyn stood frozen near the reinforced glass.
A single drop of cold sweat rolled down her pale temple, hidden behind her Kitsune mask.
’He’s... he’s that strong?’ Evelyn thought, her brain struggling to process the math of what she had just witnessed.
Even she, a classic Lord who was directly affiliated with him was still surprised by his strength.
’Is he even a regular Lord at this point...?’
She knew Silas was strong, the Lord of Blessed Land had to be strong beyond belief but this was different.
This was completely without outer mana enhancement.
The Null-stone bands on his wrists strictly forbade external projection and sure, she knew he could have manipulated the rules and enhanced his inner muscles and bone density, but still...
To launch a three-hundred-pound man a hundred and fifty feet straight up into solid rock using nothing but raw power?
Suddenly, a deep laugh echoed from the front of the viewing box.
"Hah...
Hahahaha."
It was the Boss.
The silver-haired Syndicate leader sat in his leather throne, staring down at the shattered bleeding body of his own cybernetically enhanced son but he didn’t look angry.
He seemed to let out a genuine entertained laugh.
The sound instantly made the entire crowded room feel icy cold.
The temperature in the luxury suite seemed to plummet twenty degrees as the other Managers froze, lowering their expensive drinks, terrified by the Boss’s reaction to his own blood being pulverized.
Evelyn turned her masked head toward him with her hand instinctively twitching toward her thigh holsters.
The other Managers turned as well, but the Boss’s dark gaze was solely fixed on Evelyn.
He smiled at her.
It was a cold razor-sharp smile that didn’t reach his dead eyes.
Even though this man didn’t possess a Lord Core, even though he couldn’t summon heroes or cast massive area-of-effect spells, he could clearly use internal mana.
He was a mundane underworld kingpin, and despite Evelyn being an Classic Lord who commanded an army... she was suddenly frightened.
A cold shiver raced down her spine.𝐟𝚛𝕖𝚎𝕨𝗲𝐛𝚗𝐨𝐯𝐞𝕝.𝐜𝗼𝗺
’Is there something else going on here?’ Evelyn thought.
Why would she be afraid...?
The concentrated weight of the killing intent radiating from the Boss was suffocating.
It was the aura of a man who had murdered thousands of people with his bare hands to build his empire but why was it affecting her?
The Boss slowly stood up from his chair as he walked gracefully toward the back of the room, stopping a few feet away from Evelyn’s chair.
"Manager of Contestant Onii-chan, I presume..." the Boss stated, looking down at her Kitsune mask.
Evelyn forced her body to remain rigid as she gave him a single stiff nod.
The man smiled wider, exposing perfectly white teeth.
"Welcome to the Top Twelve list," the Boss told her smoothly, acknowledging Silas’s dominance of the pit.
He simply raised a hand and snapped his fingers, calling for the hospitality staff which was surprising considering Eveyn had thought the man would want revenge or something.
The young maid in the black-and-white uniform immediately rushed over, bowing deeply.
"Direct the Manager of that amazing man to a private exclusive suite," the Boss ordered the maid with his eyes never leaving Evelyn’s mask.
"She no longer needs to prove herself by sitting out here with the general rabble.
She has earned a quiet room..."
The maid bowed lower.
"Right away, Sir.
I will oblige the errand."
The maid turned, gesturing politely for Evelyn to follow her toward a side door leading out of the general VIP box.
Evelyn didn’t hesitate.
She stood up and followed the maid, eager to escape the suffocating pressure of the Syndicate leader’s gaze.
She walked down the plush crimson-carpeted hallway in silence.
Only after she had completely left that crowded room, only after the heavy oak doors shut behind her, cutting off the Boss’s line of sight, did Evelyn feel a lot calmer.
The icy grip on her lungs finally loosened.
The maid smiled warmly as they walked.
"Congratulations on your Fighter’s incredible performance, Ma’am.
It was truly a historic strike..."
However, the polite words fell entirely on deaf ears.
Evelyn wasn’t listening at all as she looked down at her own hands.
Her leather-gloved fingers were slightly trembling.
’What...’ Evelyn thought to herself, swallowing hard behind her mask. ’What made me so afraid of him?’
She was a Lord but standing in front of that mundane, silver-haired mafia boss had triggered an instinctual terror in her brain.
There was something terribly wrong with the Black-Ash Syndicate.
[An Hour Later]
Deep in the arena, the deafening chaotic noise of the Battle Royale finally ceased.
The heavy booming Taiko drums rolled to a dramatic final halt as the harsh blinding white stadium spotlights shifted to a dim moody crimson glow.
Silas sat up properly from his cross-legged position.
He didn’t stretch because he was trying to shrug off any sort of physical tiredness as his stamina was perfectly full.
He sat up simply because the wet sounds of absolute slaughter had finally stopped.
He opened his golden-ringed eyes and looked around the Null-stone cage.
The packed dirt was completely saturated with dark coagulating blood to the point that it honestly looked like a freshly tilled graveyard.
People had killed each other a lot to secure their spots.
There were dozens of people scattered across the dirt who were just deeply, critically wounded, groaning and clutching severed limbs or shattered cybernetics.
And on the other hand, there were a far greater amount of people that were just dead.
They were completely deceased.
Bodies were piled on top of each other, their faces caved in with their chests pierced by jagged shivs.
Just like that.
Two hundred men had walked into the cage, and over a hundred and fifty of them had been brutally massacred in the span of sixty minutes.
The neon-suited Announcer, having acquired a new un-crushed microphone, hovered his anti-gravity platform down from the ceiling.
"TIME IS UP!" the Announcer’s magically amplified voice boomed across the silent bloody arena.
"THE PRELIMINARY ROYALE IS OFFICIALLY OVER!"
The surviving crowd in the stands let out a roaring bloodthirsty cheer, stamping their feet against the metal bleachers.
The Announcer hovered lower, sweeping his platform across the carnage.
"Through the blood!
Through the shattered steel!
There are exactly twelve participants that have made it through the meat-grinder!" the Announcer screamed, hyping the survivors.
"Welcome to the Top Twelve!
These elite bastards will be pitted against each other in one-on-one bracket matches for your gambling enjoyment!"
The people cheered louder, throwing empty cups and betting slips into the air.
The Announcer floated his platform directly down to the center of the ring, hovering just a few feet away from Silas first.
The spotlights snapped onto the oni.
The Announcer pointed dramatically at Silas.
"Coming out of the center ring untouched!
The man who broke the Boss’s bloodline!
The Demon of the Dirt!
The Apex Predator who defied gravity itself!" the Announcer shrieked.
"If you want to get rich tonight, if you want to rob the house blind...
ALWAYS BET ON ONII-CHAN!"
The crowd, their previous anger completely forgotten in the face of overwhelming power, erupted into a massive deafening chant.
"O-NII-CHAN!
O-NII-CHAN!
O-NII-CHAN!"
Silas stared blankly at the Announcer.
The absurdity of thousands of hardened criminals chanting a degenerate anime moniker was almost too much for his brain to process.
’The hell is going on here...?
I like it though.’

The Announcer quickly pivoted his floating anti-gravity platform with the harsh blinding white stadium spotlights violently sweeping across the blood-soaked dirt to highlight the other eleven survivors who had managed to claw their way out of the meat-grinder alive.
"From the Eastern slums, with fists forged of pure depleted mythril, give it up for KURO THE MANGLER!"
The stadium spotlights slammed down onto a literal mountain of a man.
Kuro stood triumphantly atop a jagged bleeding pile of crushed cyborgs.
He was shirtless, his dark skin covered in a roadmap of jagged white scars.

His arms from the elbows down were entirely replaced by massive oversized blocks of solid dull-gray mythril and his glowing red cybernetic eyes flared as he raised those heavy metal arms and pounded them violently against his own bare chest.
CLANG!
CLANG!
CLANG!
The concussive metallic sound echoed through the arena like a blacksmith’s hammer, driving the crowd into a roaring frenzy.
"WE LOVE YOU KURO!"
"RAHHHHHH!"
"Next one, The shadow in the smog!
The man who bleeds his enemies dry before they ever even see his blade...
VIPER-TOOTH!"
The spotlight snapped to the dark edges of the Null-stone cage.
A thin hyper-agile assassin wearing a sleek, form-fitting tactical suit stepped out of the shadows.
He held two wickedly curved daggers.
The rusted steel was coated in a glowing, corrosive green neurotoxin that dripped audibly onto the dirt.
Viper-Tooth casually wiped the flat of his poisoned blade across the torn shirt of a dead man at his feet, looking up at the roaring stands and delivering a sweeping mocking bow.
"Be sure to praise me too..."

chapters.title: Chapter 364: End Of The Battle Royale
paragraphs: The Announcer immediately moved on to the next person, they had no time to waste at all.
"Next, Forged in the deepest industrial fires, coated in unyielding steel... HIS NAME IS IRONHIDE REX!"
A towering wall of a man stepped forward into the light.
He wasn’t just wearing armor... his entire skeletal structure and dermal layer had been surgically replaced with heavy riveted iron plating.
A jagged piece of broken rebar was literally impaled three inches deep into his metallic shoulder from the Battle Royale but Ironhide Rex didn’t even flinch.
"Heh."
He reached over, grabbed the rebar, and ripped it out with a spray of black synthetic blood, snapping the thick steel pipe over his knee like a fragile twig.
"RAHHHHH! WE LOVE YOU REX!"
"Why are only the men cheering...?" Rex wondered, were they all gay?
"The man who will surgically dismantle your favorite fighter... THE SURGEON!"
A tall unnervingly calm man stood amidst the carnage, he looked so creepy that Silas couldn’t help but feel a chin run down his spine as he looked at him.
How did someone manage to look so thin?
The Surgeon wore a pristine translucent vinyl medical apron that was now horrifyingly painted in fresh wet gore.
"Than– gh... Thank you Mr. Announcer."
He adjusted a pair of glowing multi-lens surgical goggles strapped to his face and with a delicate terrifying flick of his wrist, he snapped a mono-molecular wire whip through the air.
The invisible wire cleanly sliced a falling drop of blood perfectly in half.
"As for the next one, He who drinks the pain! He who praises the slaughter! Make way for the BLOOD-SAINT!"
The crowd went feral as the spotlight illuminated a terrifying zealot.
’Is he famous or something?’ Silas thought as he looked at the guy.
The Blood-Saint was literally lounging lazily on a makeshift, gruesome throne made of stacked dead Syndicate enforcers.

He wore tattered priest’s robes that were entirely soaked in red as he reached down, dragged two bare fingers through a thick puddle of fresh blood pooling on a corpse’s chest, and slowly painted a crude jagged cross directly across his own pale forehead.
"Hehehehehehe...."
He licked the excess blood off his fingers, smiling with manic delight.
’...Yeah, miss me with that shit.’
"Our next contestant is a machine built for one singular purpose! Eradication! GOLIATH-9!"
HISSSSSS!
A hulking nine-foot-tall monstrosity of raw hydraulic power stepped into the center of the ring.
He was more tank than man with thick plumes of white exhaust steam vented violently from the heavy brass pipes bolted to his spine.
A singular glowing red ocular visor locked onto the VIP boxes as his massive, integrated rotary chain-gun arm whirred with terrifying speed.
"Our next contestant... His blade burns brighter than the Shogitown neon! NEON-BLADE!"
A wave of blistering heat washed over the dirt.
A sleek athletic swordsman drew a high-frequency katana from a magnetic scabbard on his back.
The blade instantly ignited with a blinding searing pink plasma edge that hummed like an angry hornet.
Neon-Blade smoothly pulled a cigarette from his pocket, placed it between his lips, and casually lit the tip directly on the super-heated flat of his glowing sword.
’What’s with these people and smoking?’
"Next, He rules the scrap heaps! He is the king of the decay! THE RUST-KING!"
Clad in jagged tetanus-laced scrap metal that looked like a walking junkyard, the Rust-King stepped forward.
He ground his metallic teeth together as the sound scraped like sandpaper and he dragged a massive heavy iron meat hook attached to a thick, rusted chain directly across the packed dirt.
SKRRRRRRT!
The heavy grinding noise set the teeth of everyone in the stadium completely on edge.
"Whoo! We’re down to our last three contestants, The man who leaves absolutely nothing in his wake! NULL-VOID!"
A completely silent figure stood perfectly still.
He wore a featureless matte-black helmet that absorbed the stadium light however he didn’t flex or pose like other contestants.
He simply kept his heavy spiked combat boot planted firmly on the completely pulverized flattened remains of a fighter he had just caved in.
"A ghost in the machine! The cybernetic nightmare! And the most wanted Class-A criminal in Sector Four... CYBER-GHOST!"
The spotlight hit a sleek agile fighter wearing a highly advanced, matte-black stealth suit.
Cyber-Ghost casually reached up with a gloved hand and unclasped his visor.
He pulled the mask away to reveal a devastatingly handsome sharp-jawed face, accented by a single glowing silver cybernetic eye and a rugged roguish scar across his cheek.
’This fucker looks like a noble... I’m still better looking though.’
He looked directly up at the luxury VIP viewing boxes, flashing a brilliant million-credit smile as he delivered a slow cocky wink.
High above the arena, a collective shrill scream of swooning female Managers, wealthy corporate heiresses, and elite sponsors echoed loudly through the colosseum.
The Announcer then hovered his platform away from the main cluster, pointing toward a dark shadowed corner of the Null-stone cage.
"And finally! The shadow of death himself! The harvester of souls! ZARCH THE REAPER!"
Silas blinked behind his Oni mask.
’ZarchTheReaper?’ Silas thought to himself, completely deadpan.
He stared at the cloaked edgelord.
That was quite literally the most cringeworthy twelve-year-old video game username he had ever heard in his entire life.
It sounded like a kid he used to body in first-person shooters back on Earth...
With the introductions complete, the Announcer waved his hand.
"FIGHTERS, YOU ARE DISMISSED TO THE LOCKER ROOMS! REST UP! THE BRACKETS BEGIN IN TWENTY MINUTES!"
The heavy steel hatches built into the arena walls groaned open.
Immediately, the designated Underworld clean-up crews flooded into the arena.
"Hup... Hup... Get a move on!"

They were dressed in heavy rubber aprons and masks, pushing massive metal carts and wielding high-pressure water hoses to handle the staggering pile of bodies and wash the thick blood out of the dirt.
Silas stood up from the mud.
He turned around and began walking toward his designated exit hatch.
As he moved, he could physically feel the heavy stares of the other eleven surviving fighters burning directly into his back.
They were all studying his gait, probably looking for weaknesses but he ignored them.
’It’s clear... they won’t be able to beat me, this whole thing is in the bag.’
He crossed the threshold into his own dark hatch and kept going down the concrete tunnel.
’I really hope she bet on me...’ Silas thought practically.
This was a massive illegal underground operation, which meant there was staggering amounts of gambling involved.
Evelyn was a bit of a genius so she would be stupid not to bet heavily on his initial survival.
The only issue with his terrifying performance was that the secret was out.
With this overwhelming display of strength, all the other spectators and Managers in the stands would undoubtedly begin to bet on him as well.
The house odds on his name were going to completely plummet.
’Is there some way to maximize the winnings to myself?’ Silas thought, stroking his chin beneath his mask.
He needed a way to manipulate the betting lines back in his favor.
As he reached the end of the tunnel and stepped back into the massive, sterile locker room, a figure was waiting for him.
It was a maid in the black-and-white uniform.
’What the hell is a maid doing here?’
She bowed deeply as he approached.
"Congratulations for reaching the Top Twelve, Contestant Onii-chan."
Silas gave her a single tired nod and sighed as the stress of the environment was finally getting to him.

"The table for the person you will be facing next is currently being prepared," the maid informed him smoothly. "As a Top Twelve finalist, you are officially free to roam around the designated fighter areas... However, I have been sent directly by your Manager to bring you up to her private suite."
The maid reached into her apron and handed him a sealed pristine plastic bottle of cold water.
Silas stared at the bottle and his paranoia instantly flared.
’Nope.’
He completely ignored the water, refusing to take it from her hand.
"Just take me there," Silas told her bluntly.
The maid smiled politely, unaffected by his rudeness, and turned around. She took him out of the main preparation room, leading him down a narrow guarded corridor.
Apparently, there was a secondary hidden side-way staircase that bypassed the teleportation wards and took the VIPs directly to the higher floors of the complex.
’Though it’s quite guarded... It’s not like anyone could have forced their way out, and also not to mention the snipers too.’
As they walked up the carpeted stairs and arrived in the upper Manager’s corridor, Silas witnessed the brutal reality of the Syndicate.
There were different people... wealthy Managers in expensive suits being aggressively escorted out of the viewing boxes by massive Black-Ash enforcers.
One Manager in particular was sobbing hysterically, pleading with the enforcers for more time to pay off his massive gambling debts.
"Please! I can get the credits!" the man begged, grabbing the enforcer’s vest.
CRACK!
The enforcer didn’t say a word.
He just grabbed the Manager by the back of the neck and drove a brutal, armored knee directly into the man’s face, shattering his nose and dropping him unconscious to the plush carpet.
The enforcers dragged his limp body away by the ankles.
Silas watched them go with cold eyes.

He could easily guess that these were the Managers who had bet on the Boss’s son and completely lost everything as well as their people, triggering the lethal debt-collection clauses in their contracts.
The maid ignored the violence entirely, maintaining her polite smile.
She guided him down the hall and stopped in front of a luxurious gilded oak door.
"Your Manager is inside, Sir," the maid said, bowing once more before turning and immediately dashing off down the hallway to tend to other duties.
Silas didn’t bother knocking. He just grabbed the brass handle, turned it, and opened the door.
FWOOSH!
Immediately, an incredibly thick suffocating wall of aromatic cherry-scented smoke rolled out of the suite and filled his nose.
"Gah!"
Silas coughed aggressively, furiously swatting the air in front of his face with his black-gloved hand to clear the toxic smog.
"Could you stop...?" Silas groaned, stepping into the room and quickly closing the heavy door behind him to trap the ventilation.
He looked around the private suite.
It was incredibly luxurious, featuring plush velvet seating, a fully stocked crystal bar, and a massive private holographic window overlooking the arena below.
Evelyn was seated comfortably on a luxurious, curved velvet sofa in the center of the room.

She had pushed her painted Kitsune mask up slightly, resting it on the top of her dark hair to expose her mouth and chin and she was still wearing the gray hoodie that swallowed her frame as her thighs were tucked beneath her on the cushions.
Evelyn held a burning Red-Lotus cigarette between her fingers, taking a deep victorious drag.

"Welcome back," Evelyn smiled, exhaling a thin stream of smoke toward the ceiling. "You sure were strong-headed down there... Come sit down. You should take one and smoke, it takes the edge off the adrenaline."
Silas stood by the door, glaring at her through the slits of his Oni mask.
He raised a judgmental eyebrow.
"If you hand me a cigar," Silas sighed. "I will stick it straight down your ass."
Evelyn violently choked on her smoke.
She coughed violently, her face instantly turning a bright burning crimson red that spread all the way down her neck.
"You—!" Evelyn sputtered, pointing her cigarette at him accusingly. "I take back my compliment! You pervert!"
Silas completely ignored her blushing outrage.
He walked over to the seating area and slumped heavily down into a plush leather chair opposite her, resting his elbows on his knees.
Evelyn cleared her throat, recovering her composure as she reached over to the crystal bar cart sitting next to the sofa.

"Congratulations on the win," Evelyn told him sincerely, grabbing a sleek aluminum can of water. "I know you didn’t take anything the maid gave you... I assumed everything provided by the Syndicate staff was spiked with paralyzing agents."
She held her hand over the can.
A pure white glow of purification mana pulsed from her palm, shooting into the aluminum to eradicate any poisons or foreign substances.
She tossed the purified can to him.
"Here, it’s good to drink."
Silas caught it effortlessly. He popped the tab, tilted his mask up a fraction of an inch, and drank the entire can down in three massive thirsty gulps.
"How were things going over here?" Silas asked, crushing the empty aluminum can in his massive fist and tossing it onto the table.
Evelyn smirked, leaning back into the velvet cushions.
"It was just fine being a Manager," Evelyn bragged, tapping a button on the wall console to increase the coolness of the room’s air conditioning and clear the smoke.
She reached down, picked up her personal glowing holographic datapad, and turned the screen around to show him.
She proudly displayed her live balance tab.
[Manager 155]
[Account: Anonymous Shell Corp]
[Balance: 5,500,000 Spirit Credits]
Silas looked at the staggering number glowing on the screen.
"Not bad," Silas nodded. ’Like the Announcer said, Always bet on Onii-chan...’
Evelyn took another victory puff of her cigarette, her dark eyes shining with greedy delight.
"This was a very generous payout from the house," Silas noted, leaning forward in his chair. "But it’s not going to be as easy to rob them next time."
Evelyn’s smile faded slightly as she nodded in complete agreement.

"Exactly," Evelyn said, tapping the edge of her datapad. "With your overwhelming performance in the Royale just now, every single surviving spectator and Manager in this entire stadium is going to bet on you to win your next match. You are the new favorite so the house odds on ’Onii-chan’ are going to tank completely. A million-credit bet might only yield a ten-thousand-credit return."
They needed to artificially manipulate the betting lines to make the crowd think Silas was vulnerable.

"Why don’t we fake a severe injury?" Evelyn suggested. "What if we fake that you have a very bad illness or suffered massive internal organ damage from the Boss’s son? If you stumble and limp down the tunnel to the cage, the crowd will think you are a dead man walking. The odds will skyrocket back in our favor, and I can bet the entire five million on a massive underdog multiplier."
They were similar in this regard... Both of them were thinking of how to multiply their money.

Silas blinked behind his Oni mask.
’ZarchTheReaper?’ Silas thought to himself, completely deadpan.
He stared at the cloaked edgelord.
That was quite literally the most cringeworthy twelve-year-old video game username he had ever heard in his entire life.
It sounded like a kid he used to body in first-person shooters back on Earth...
With the introductions complete, the Announcer waved his hand.
"FIGHTERS, YOU ARE DISMISSED TO THE LOCKER ROOMS!
REST UP!
THE BRACKETS BEGIN IN TWENTY MINUTES!"
The heavy steel hatches built into the arena walls groaned open.
Immediately, the designated Underworld clean-up crews flooded into the arena.
"Hup...
Hup...
Get a move on!"

They were dressed in heavy rubber aprons and masks, pushing massive metal carts and wielding high-pressure water hoses to handle the staggering pile of bodies and wash the thick blood out of the dirt.
Silas stood up from the mud.
He turned around and began walking toward his designated exit hatch.
As he moved, he could physically feel the heavy stares of the other eleven surviving fighters burning directly into his back.
They were all studying his gait, probably looking for weaknesses but he ignored them.
’It’s clear... they won’t be able to beat me, this whole thing is in the bag.’
He crossed the threshold into his own dark hatch and kept going down the concrete tunnel.
’I really hope she bet on me...’ Silas thought practically.
This was a massive illegal underground operation, which meant there was staggering amounts of gambling involved.
Evelyn was a bit of a genius so she would be stupid not to bet heavily on his initial survival.
The only issue with his terrifying performance was that the secret was out.
With this overwhelming display of strength, all the other spectators and Managers in the stands would undoubtedly begin to bet on him as well.
The house odds on his name were going to completely plummet.
’Is there some way to maximize the winnings to myself?’ Silas thought, stroking his chin beneath his mask.
He needed a way to manipulate the betting lines back in his favor.
As he reached the end of the tunnel and stepped back into the massive, sterile locker room, a figure was waiting for him.
It was a maid in the black-and-white uniform.
’What the hell is a maid doing here?’
She bowed deeply as he approached.
"Congratulations for reaching the Top Twelve, Contestant Onii-chan."
Silas gave her a single tired nod and sighed as the stress of the environment was finally getting to him.
"The table for the person you will be facing next is currently being prepared," the maid informed him smoothly.
"As a Top Twelve finalist, you are officially free to roam around the designated fighter areas...
However, I have been sent directly by your Manager to bring you up to her private suite."
The maid reached into her apron and handed him a sealed pristine plastic bottle of cold water.
Silas stared at the bottle and his paranoia instantly flared.
’Nope.’
He completely ignored the water, refusing to take it from her hand.
"Just take me there," Silas told her bluntly.
The maid smiled politely, unaffected by his rudeness, and turned around.
She took him out of the main preparation room, leading him down a narrow guarded corridor.
Apparently, there was a secondary hidden side-way staircase that bypassed the teleportation wards and took the VIPs directly to the higher floors of the complex.
’Though it’s quite guarded...
It’s not like anyone could have forced their way out, and also not to mention the snipers too.’
As they walked up the carpeted stairs and arrived in the upper Manager’s corridor, Silas witnessed the brutal reality of the Syndicate.
There were different people... wealthy Managers in expensive suits being aggressively escorted out of the viewing boxes by massive Black-Ash enforcers.
One Manager in particular was sobbing hysterically, pleading with the enforcers for more time to pay off his massive gambling debts.
"Please!
I can get the credits!" the man begged, grabbing the enforcer’s vest.
CRACK!
The enforcer didn’t say a word.
He just grabbed the Manager by the back of the neck and drove a brutal, armored knee directly into the man’s face, shattering his nose and dropping him unconscious to the plush carpet.
The enforcers dragged his limp body away by the ankles.
Silas watched them go with cold eyes.

He could easily guess that these were the Managers who had bet on the Boss’s son and completely lost everything as well as their people, triggering the lethal debt-collection clauses in their contracts.
The maid ignored the violence entirely, maintaining her polite smile.
She guided him down the hall and stopped in front of a luxurious gilded oak door.
"Your Manager is inside, Sir," the maid said, bowing once more before turning and immediately dashing off down the hallway to tend to other duties.
Silas didn’t bother knocking.
He just grabbed the brass handle, turned it, and opened the door.
FWOOSH!
Immediately, an incredibly thick suffocating wall of aromatic cherry-scented smoke rolled out of the suite and filled his nose.
"Gah!"
Silas coughed aggressively, furiously swatting the air in front of his face with his black-gloved hand to clear the toxic smog.
"Could you stop...?" Silas groaned, stepping into the room and quickly closing the heavy door behind him to trap the ventilation.
He looked around the private suite.
It was incredibly luxurious, featuring plush velvet seating, a fully stocked crystal bar, and a massive private holographic window overlooking the arena below.
Evelyn was seated comfortably on a luxurious, curved velvet sofa in the center of the room.

She had pushed her painted Kitsune mask up slightly, resting it on the top of her dark hair to expose her mouth and chin and she was still wearing the gray hoodie that swallowed her frame as her thighs were tucked beneath her on the cushions.
Evelyn held a burning Red-Lotus cigarette between her fingers, taking a deep victorious drag.
"Welcome back," Evelyn smiled, exhaling a thin stream of smoke toward the ceiling.
"You sure were strong-headed down there...
Come sit down.
You should take one and smoke, it takes the edge off the adrenaline."
Silas stood by the door, glaring at her through the slits of his Oni mask.
He raised a judgmental eyebrow.
"If you hand me a cigar," Silas sighed.
"I will stick it straight down your ass."
Evelyn violently choked on her smoke.
She coughed violently, her face instantly turning a bright burning crimson red that spread all the way down her neck.
"You—!" Evelyn sputtered, pointing her cigarette at him accusingly.
"I take back my compliment!
You pervert!"
Silas completely ignored her blushing outrage.
He walked over to the seating area and slumped heavily down into a plush leather chair opposite her, resting his elbows on his knees.
Evelyn cleared her throat, recovering her composure as she reached over to the crystal bar cart sitting next to the sofa.
"Congratulations on the win," Evelyn told him sincerely, grabbing a sleek aluminum can of water.
"I know you didn’t take anything the maid gave you...
I assumed everything provided by the Syndicate staff was spiked with paralyzing agents."
She held her hand over the can.
A pure white glow of purification mana pulsed from her palm, shooting into the aluminum to eradicate any poisons or foreign substances.
She tossed the purified can to him.
"Here, it’s good to drink."
Silas caught it effortlessly.
He popped the tab, tilted his mask up a fraction of an inch, and drank the entire can down in three massive thirsty gulps.
"How were things going over here?" Silas asked, crushing the empty aluminum can in his massive fist and tossing it onto the table.
Evelyn smirked, leaning back into the velvet cushions.
"It was just fine being a Manager," Evelyn bragged, tapping a button on the wall console to increase the coolness of the room’s air conditioning and clear the smoke.
She reached down, picked up her personal glowing holographic datapad, and turned the screen around to show him.
She proudly displayed her live balance tab.
[Manager 155]
[Account: Anonymous Shell Corp]
[Balance: 5,500,000 Spirit Credits]
Silas looked at the staggering number glowing on the screen.
"Not bad," Silas nodded. ’Like the Announcer said, Always bet on Onii-chan...’
Evelyn took another victory puff of her cigarette, her dark eyes shining with greedy delight.
"This was a very generous payout from the house," Silas noted, leaning forward in his chair.
"But it’s not going to be as easy to rob them next time."
Evelyn’s smile faded slightly as she nodded in complete agreement.
"Exactly," Evelyn said, tapping the edge of her datapad.
"With your overwhelming performance in the Royale just now, every single surviving spectator and Manager in this entire stadium is going to bet on you to win your next match.
You are the new favorite so the house odds on ’Onii-chan’ are going to tank completely.
A million-credit bet might only yield a ten-thousand-credit return."
They needed to artificially manipulate the betting lines to make the crowd think Silas was vulnerable.
"Why don’t we fake a severe injury?" Evelyn suggested.
"What if we fake that you have a very bad illness or suffered massive internal organ damage from the Boss’s son?
If you stumble and limp down the tunnel to the cage, the crowd will think you are a dead man walking.
The odds will skyrocket back in our favor, and I can bet the entire five million on a massive underdog multiplier."
They were similar in this regard...
Both of them were thinking of how to multiply their money.

chapters.title: Chapter 365: How To Scam Your Fans [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Silas stroked his beardless chin beneath the metal mask, genuinely considering the deceitful strategy.
"That’s not a bad idea," Silas agreed as he fully endorsed the scam. "I can slow my heart rate down to mimic extreme fatigue and cough up some fake bloo—"
BZZZZZT!
The Announcer’s magically amplified voice suddenly rang out from the massive speakers embedded in the walls of their private suite, interrupting their scheming.
"LADIES AND GENTLEMEN!" the Announcer declared to the stadium. "THE TIMETABLES HAVE BEEN DECIDED AND THE BRACKETS ARE LOCKED!"
A large glowing blue hologram suddenly materialized in the center of their private room, projecting directly from a projector in the ceiling.
It displayed the official tournament bracket.
"In exactly twenty minutes, the first match on the list will officially begin in the dirt!" the Announcer hyped.
Silas looked at the glowing hologram.
At the very top of the bracket, his absurd moniker was listed in bold glowing letters.
[MATCH 1: ONII-CHAN vs. ZARCH THE REAPER]
Silas and Evelyn both stared at the bracket, and then slowly looked across the coffee table at each other.
"Well," Evelyn muttered, taking a slow drag of her cigarette. "You are up against the edgelord with the video game name."
’That’s what I said...’
"He was incredibly skinny," Silas noted, recalling the cloaked figure from the lineup. "He didn’t possess any heavy cybernetics or visible mutations. How did he survive the meat-grinder?"

"Chemical enhancement I think," Evelyn deduced instantly with her experience recognizing the archetype. "He is probably going to spike his own bloodstream with a massive overdose of illegal combat steroids right before the match, right?"
Silas nodded slowly, leaning back in his chair.

"Undoubtedly," Silas agreed. "There was nothing in the receptionist’s official rules that explicitly said performance-enhancing drugs were prohibited. Only external mana and weapons... He is going to juice himself into a frenzy but I have an idea on how we can use this to our advantage."
"Oh?"
Meanwhile, on the exact opposite side of the VIP level, in a much smaller and significantly dirtier private viewing room...
Zarch sat heavily on a metal folding chair.
He had thrown his dark edgy cloak onto the floor to reveal his full body.
"Ugh... Where is he?"
Scratch! Scratch!
He was a pale violently trembling young man with sunken eyes and twitching fingers.
He stared down at his own glowing datapad, looking at the official bracket list with an expression of pure terror trembling on his sweaty face.
"I’m finished..."
He was matched against the monster... He had to fight the demon who had punched the Boss’s son through the ceiling. Unless those things came, it was over.
The heavy metal door of the room suddenly barged open.
Zarch’s Manager, a sleazy desperate-looking man in a cheap suit, rushed into the room.
He was carrying a heavy black duffel bag.
"Here, I’ve arrived Zarch!"
He unzipped the bag and dumped the contents directly onto the metal table in front of Zarch.
Dozens of sleek large medical syringes spilled across the table.
They were filled with a thick bubbling pitch-black liquid and Zarch knew what it was... it was Black-Ash hyper-stimulant.
It was one of the most illegal and volatile combat drug on the black market.
It forced the human heart to beat at four hundred beats per minute, granting terrifying strength at the cost of literally shredding the user’s internal organs.
This was what he would need when faced with a terrifying monster like Onii-chan.
"I brought as many injections as I could find from the medical bay," his Manager panted, looking terrified.
He hesitated with his hand hovering over the deadly black liquid. "Zarch... are you sure about this? A double dose of this shit will stop your heart after the match."
Zarch didn’t hesitate.
He aggressively snagged the heavy black bag and the syringes right out of his Manager’s trembling hands.
"I am sure..." Zarch whispered, his voice cracking with terrified desperation. "I need to win..."
If he won the tournament then he could save her... He could save his mother!
He grabbed the largest and thickest black syringe from the pile however he didn’t bother finding a vein in his arm.
’Let’s take it straight to the neck!’
He raised the needle and brutally injected the thick steel directly into the side of his own neck.
He slammed the plunger down, forcing the bubbling black liquid straight into his jugular vein.
PSSH!
Instantly, Zarch’s sunken eyes widened to impossible terrifying proportions.
The dark sickly veins on his pale neck instantly bulged, turning a glowing toxic purple.
His sunken cheeks flushed violently red as his heart rate exploded into a faster rhythm as white foam began to gather at the corners of his mouth.
"Not en... ough."
He grabbed a second syringe then a third.
He stabbed more and more of the black liquid into his arms, his chest, his legs with his body completely rejecting human limitations as the dark magic shredded his nervous system.
"I NEED TO BEAT ONII-CHAN!" Zarch yelled, his voice warping into a demonic roar of pure insanity.
The heavy booming Taiko drums echoed aggressively through the massive cavern, signaling the beginning of the actual tournament bracket.
High above the freshly cleaned, blood-stained dirt of the Null-stone cage, the neon-suited Announcer hovered on his anti-gravity platform.
He tapped his magically amplified microphone with the harsh feedback cutting through the restless murmurs of the thousands of spectators packed into the stadium seating.
"LADIES AND DEGENERATES!" the Announcer shrieked, throwing his arms wide open to embrace the violent atmosphere. "THE PRELIMINARIES ARE OVER! THE MEAT HAS BEEN TRIMMED! WELCOME TO THE ROUND OF SIX!"
The crowd erupted into a deafening feral roar.
They stomped their boots against the reinforced metal bleachers as the pressure of their stomps vibrated the thick glass of the VIP viewing boxes suspended high above.

"For our very first bracket match of the night, we have a clash of undisputed Underworld titans!" the Announcer hyped up the two fighters, spinning his platform rapidly in the air. "In the red corner... the shadow of death himself! ZARCH THE REAPER!"
The heavy reinforced steel hatch on the far side of the arena groaned loudly as the thick iron chains clanked as the gate was hauled upward.
Out of the dark concrete tunnel stepped Zarch.
The crowd offered a lukewarm mildly confused cheer.𝐟𝐫𝕖𝗲𝘄𝚎𝗯𝕟𝐨𝕧𝐞𝚕.𝕔𝕠𝐦
Zarch hadn’t exactly been a terrifying highlight of the massive Battle Royale.
In fact, most of the people who had survived the first hour had completely ignored him while he hid in the shadows near the perimeter.
But as he stepped fully into the harsh blinding white stadium spotlights, the crowd’s collective breath caught in their throats.
He didn’t look like a scrawny cloaked coward anymore...
He looked terrifyingly buff!
The hyper-stimulant combat drugs had completely rewritten his biological structure.
His previously thin arms were now bulging with thick overlapping slabs of dense muscle as the dark sickly veins crisscrossing his pale neck and chest pulsed with a glowing toxic purple light.
Furthermore, there was a literal visible aura of pitch-black darkness radiating off his skin.
It was a vile mixture of evaporating sweat and the illegal chemical exhaust of the Black-Ash drugs actively shredding his internal organs.
He looked like a cornered, rabid beast, making him appear surprisingly formidable.
Though, despite the sudden, terrifying physical upgrade, everyone in the stadium was still going to bet their entire life savings on Onii-Chan.
The Lord had punched a cyborg through a rock ceiling... Drugs while powerful on their own couldn’t beat gravity.
The Announcer cheered Zarch on, feeding the spectacle.
"Look at the mass on the Reaper!" the Announcer commented into the microphone while hovering lower. "He looks quite strong tonight, folks! He looks ready for a slaughter!"
The Announcer then dramatically pivoted his platform toward the opposite side of the massive dirt ring.
"AND IN THE BLUE CORNER!" the Announcer screamed, his voice reaching a fever pitch. "THE DEMON OF THE DIRT! THE FAVORITE TO WIN IT ALL! ONII-CHAN!"
The heavy steel hatch on Silas’s side of the arena slowly ground open.
The crowd went wild, waiting for the terrifying young man in the dark uniform to step out and unleash hell.
But... nothing happened.
The dark tunnel remained completely empty.
The Announcer called upon Onii-Chan from his hatch a second time, raising his hand dramatically.
Only to be met with deafening silence.
The crowd’s cheering slowly died down, replaced by confused, restless murmurs.
Thousands of heads craned forward, trying to peer into the pitch-black depths of the open tunnel.
Suddenly, a young maid in a black-and-white uniform sprinted frantically out of a side-access door near the lower stands.
She waved her arms wildly, calling the Announcer down to the side of the reinforced glass barrier.
The Announcer frowned, hovering his platform down to meet her. He leaned over the railing, pulling the microphone away from his mouth.
"What is the delay?" the Announcer hissed impatiently.
The maid looked up with her face pale.
She reported the situation in a hushed whisper, but the magically amplified microphone still faintly picked up her words, echoing them softly across the quiet stadium.

"Contestant Onii-chan seemed to have digested something terrible," the maid reported, sounding genuinely concerned. "He is hunched over in the locker room. He became very, very sick just a few moments ago..."
The Announcer’s eyes widened.
Both of them, and everyone in the criminal Underworld who possessed a functional brain, knew exactly what that specific phrasing meant.
He hadn’t eaten bad fish.
He had obviously taken a massive handful of untested, black-market performance-enhancing pills to boost his strength, and his body was aggressively rejecting the toxic mixture.
"Is he forfeiting?" the Announcer asked sharply. "Is he still coming out to the dirt?"
"He is," the maid confirmed while nodding rapidly. "He is walking to the hatch now."
The Announcer straightened up, instantly floating his platform back up into the center of the arena.
He brought the microphone back to his lips with his voice taking on a tone of dramatic manufactured concern.

"Ladies and gentlemen, it seems we have a slight unexpected delay!" the Announcer announced to the massive crowd. "Contestant Onii-chan seemed to have some severe issues with something he digested in the locker rooms! He is currently extremely sick, but the Demon refuses to yield! He is coming to the pit!"
Up in the tiered luxury boxes, a lot of the wealthy Managers and corporate sponsors gave each other knowing looks.
’Ah.’ the collective crowd realized.
It was quite clear to them now... It made perfect logical sense!
Onii-chan had obviously been using high-tier performance-enhancing pills during the Battle Royale.
That was the only logical reason a human could have possibly possessed the raw physical strength to punch a three-hundred-pound cyborg into the ceiling.
There was nothing in the official rules of the Null-stone cage that said a fighter couldn’t chemically augment their own bloodstream.
It was a perfectly legal strategy in Shogitown.
But still... to suffer a total crash right before the brackets? How many illegal pills did the idiot have to take to get that violently sick?!
Down in the dirt, Zarch the Reaper heard the announcement.
His chemically dilated pupils twitched.
He rolled his heavy mutated shoulders as he was feeling vastly more confident now.
The monster wasn’t a god, he was simply just another junkie who had pushed his dosage too far.
Zarch took a low unstable attacking stance, digging his boots into the mud.
"Come then... I’ll make it quick..."
The Announcer raised his hand, officially giving the crowd a massive glowing blue holographic timer that appeared above the center of the cage.
"THREE MINUTES TO PLACE YOUR WAGERS!"
However, the entire field fell completely silent as heavy, dragging footsteps echoed from the dark tunnel.
Someone finally walked out from the opposite hatch.
It was Onii-chan.
But he truly did look incredibly sick.
Silas stepped out into the harsh stadium lights.
His broad shoulders were completely slumped forward, utterly ruining his intimidating posture.
He was dragging his feet through the dirt, staggering a bit to the left as if his inner ear equilibrium was completely destroyed.
He kept his head tilted downward and he clutched his stomach with one black-gloved hand, letting out a weak pathetic-sounding cough that vibrated hollowly through his Oni mask.
The stadium stared at him in disappointment.
Even the signature piercing light-blue glow of his eyes was gone.
Behind the narrow slits of his metal mask, there was nothing but dull, empty darkness.
Nobody could see anything resembling the Apex Predator from an hour ago.
As the heavy iron hatches slammed and locked closed behind him, the stadium’s silence shattered.
"BOOOOOOOOO!"
Thousands of spectators began viciously booing him, throwing their empty beer cups and crumpled betting slips against the Null-stone glass.
They felt cheated... They thought they were going to see a monster but instead, they were looking at a dying addict!
The Announcer hovered closer, genuinely unsure if the match should proceed.
"Are you alright to fight, Contestant?" the Announcer asked.
Silas stood in the dirt. He didn’t answer him as he just let out another weak rattling cough with his knees buckling slightly.
"Very well! The betting window is open!" the Announcer declared, slamming his hand on his podium.
The personal holographic betting panels instantly appeared in front of every single spectator and Manager in the stadium.
"BEGIN THE MATCH!"
Just as the Announcer screamed, Zarch didn’t waste a single millisecond.
FWISH!
