His physical resemblance to Talia was unmistakable... the same sharp jawline and the same dangerous posture.

’So this is Jax’s father,’ Silas noted internally, analyzing the man’s facial structure. ’Which means that shut-in hacker is probably going to have the exact same silver hair and sharp face once we scrape the basement dirt off him.’
The moment Silas stepped fully across the threshold, the air in the room suddenly grew heavy.
HUMMM!
A subtle invisible pressure rippled through the space.

Silas felt a sharp, intrusive mental tendril... an ethereal probe attempting to bore directly through his skull to pry into his thoughts, read his surface intentions, and measure the depth of his internal energy.
’Prying into a Lord’s mind?’ Silas scoffed internally. ’Amateur.’
Silas didn’t even need to use an active counter-spell.
He simply flexed the power of his Core.
SNAP!
A pulse of pure internal mana flared through his neural pathways as the invisible mental probe was shattered like a thin pane of glass struck by a warhammer.
Across the desk, the Boss’s slate-gray eyes widened by a fraction of a millimeter.
A sharp intake of breath hissed past his teeth as the feedback of the broken mental probe snapped back into his own mind.
He masked his shock instantly, smoothing his expression back into an immaculate professional smile.
"Welcome, Champion," the Boss spoke.
"And welcome back, Talia."
PSSH-CHUNK!
The heavy ironwood doors slammed shut behind Silas, locking with a series of heavy deadbolts.
The four guards remained outside in the hallway, leaving only Silas, Talia, the Boss, and a single figure seated on the leather lounge chair to the side.
Silas glanced over.
Evelyn was sitting on the left side of the obsidian desk.
She was still wearing her hoodie and her painted porcelain Kitsune mask but something was visibly wrong.
Her exposed skin was deathly pale.
Her small, leather-gloved hands were clenched tightly into fists on her knees, and Silas could clearly see her slender frame trembling with subtle tremors.
’What happened to her?’ Silas thought, frowning behind his Oni mask. ’She was screaming about winning sixty million credits not too long ago.
Why is she shivering like she just got pulled out of a frozen lake?’
The Boss leaned back in his high-backed leather chair, steepling his fingers over the black obsidian surface.
"First and foremost, allow me to extend my personal gratitude, Contestant," the Boss said smoothly, his eyes tracking Silas as the young man walked toward the seating area.
"It was entirely because of your... aggressive efficiency in the cage that my syndicate managed to eliminate several problematic elements from our books."
Silas didn’t say a word as he just listened.
"Zarch was an unstable chemically-altered maniac skimming from our distribution channels," the Boss continued casually, as if discussing the weather.

"The Blood-Saint was an uncontrollable religious lunatic who was beginning to attract unwanted heat from the higher sects and Goliath-9 was a corporate spy operating on behalf of the Iron-Core Cartel...
You saved my enforcers weeks of messy cleanup work."
From that brief cold explanation, Silas could immediately deduce what this entire underground tournament had actually been designed for.

’The whole bloodbath was just a glorified corporate restructuring,’ Silas thought. ’The guy used a tournament bracket to lure all his internal rivals and problematic assets into a suppressed cage so they could kill each other off under the guise of public entertainment...
I’m impressed.’
Though, Silas really didn’t see how any of those fighters could have ever posed a legitimate existential threat to an organized syndicate.
To Silas, they had all been laughably weak.
’Or maybe...’ Silas paused, correcting himself with a mild shrug. ’Maybe my Gold Core just makes everyone else look like tissue paper.’
Well that was the truth.
"Please, take a seat," the Boss offered, gesturing toward the empty leather chair directly beside Evelyn.
Silas walked over and dropped into the chair.
His boots thumped against the floor, leaving a small cloud of arena dust in the pristine executive air.
Talia walked around the desk, taking her place standing directly beside her father’s right shoulder, crossing her arms and maintaining a sharp watchful gaze on the two masked Lords.
The Boss cleared his throat, leaning his forearms against the obsidian desk.
"You two are here to collect your official tournament reward, correct?" the Boss asked, his slate-gray eyes shifting between Silas and the trembling Evelyn.
"Given how exceptionally stiff both of you appear, I am going to assume you expect me to renege on our agreement and make this process exceptionally difficult for you."
Silas tilted his masked head upward, watching the man’s micro-expressions.
"I am well aware," the Boss continued in a calm tone, "that you almost decapitated my eldest son during the preliminary qualifiers."
Silas didn’t flinch.
"However," the Boss smiled with a thin sharp grin that lacked any paternal warmth, "the Black-Ash Syndicate did not rise to rule Shogitown by breaking our contractual word...
We pride ourselves on being honorable businessmen.
The asset you requested... my disgraced runaway son will be formally handed over to your custody.
His tracking chips have been surgically extracted, and the administrative master control of his Slave Rune will be transferred to you directly...
After that, whatever you choose to do with him outside of Shogitown is entirely your concern."
Silas let out a quiet internal sigh of relief behind his metal mask.
’Good,’ Silas thought. ’But I’m still surprised...’
He didn’t have a good feeling about this, his life was full of drama...
Did the Boss seriously not want to do anything?

"However," the Boss cleared his throat, tapping a holographic interface embedded directly into the obsidian desk, "before we discuss the transfer of assets, we must settle the financial matter of your betting earnings."
Silas glanced sideways at Evelyn.
She hadn’t moved an inch.
Her breathing was shallow, and her fingers were digging so violently into the leather of her gloves that her knuckles were popping.
’Seriously, what is her problem?’ Silas wondered. ’Evelyn is a Classic Lord so why is she completely frozen in front of an Underworld boss?’

chapters.title: Chapter 373: Haggling Is An Art
paragraphs: Then, Silas saw an immediate golden opportunity.

’Wait a minute...’ Silas realized with the corners of his mouth curling beneath the Oni mask. ’She made me lay my head in her lap for fifteen straight minutes while she laughed and called me cheap...’
It was time for payback.
Silas gave Evelyn a sharp pointed look.
Evelyn slowly turned her porcelain Kitsune mask toward him. Beneath the painted fox face, her posture radiated pure cold dread.
Without saying a single word of warning, Silas reached across the armrest.

He wrapped his massive black-gloved hands firmly around Evelyn’s slender waist, lifted her entire body cleanly off her chair with effortless strength, and pulled her sideways, placing her directly onto his own lap.
The entire room went completely still.
Talia’s dark eyes went wide with pure shock.
The Boss’s silver eyebrows shot up to his hairline with his fingers freezing mid-air over his holographic keyboard.
Even Evelyn gasped beneath her mask, her body going completely rigid as she found herself sitting squarely across Silas’s armored thighs.

She instinctively tried to scramble backward to get off him, but Silas casually locked his thick left arm around her waist, anchoring her firmly in place with the unyielding strength of a hydraulic clamp.
Silas leaned comfortably back into the plush leather cushions of his chair, relaxing completely as if he were sitting in his own living room.
"We are in the middle of an executive business meeting," Silas told her through the mask. "You are my Manager and you handled the wagers so start talking."
Beneath the painted porcelain Kitsune mask, Evelyn’s entire face flared into a brilliant scalding shade of crimson.

’You shameless bastard!’ Evelyn cursed him furiously in her thoughts with her heart hammering against her ribs. ’Doing this in the middle of the Black-Ash headquarters?! I am going to murder you in your sleep when we get back to the Sovereign Realm!’
The Boss recovered his composure, letting out a low amused chuckle from behind the desk.
"Well, well," the Boss mused, his slate-gray eyes glittering with intrigue. "It seems the two of you share an exceptionally... intimate working relationship."
Evelyn opened her mouth, desperate to deny it and salvage her professional dignity.
"We are strictly—"
"We are very close," Silas cut her off smoothly, tightening his arm around her waist. "In fact, we are planning to be officially married in the near future."
Evelyn choked on her own breath with her blush deepening until her ears burned hot against her mask.
The bastard was literally quoting the exact ridiculous cover story she had fed to the mask vendor earlier.
The Boss offered a polite respectful nod.
"Then allow me to offer my early congratulations on a prosperous and bloody union."
Beside the desk, Talia’s sharp jaw tightened.
Her dark eyes twitched in visible frustration as she stared at Evelyn sitting comfortably on Silas’s lap.

’She wants to capitalize that entire magnificent ass for herself?!’ Talia thought with indignity, her manicured nails digging into her palms. ’A holy asset like that belongs to the public! I never knew such greedy hoarding devils existed in this world!’
The Boss cleared his throat again, turning his attention back to the holographic console.
"Now, let us examine the total payout," the Boss said, tapping the glass.
PING!
As the Boss looked down at his screen, Evelyn took a slow breath against Silas’s chest.
The moment Silas had pulled her onto his lap, the suffocating pressure that had been crushing her chest had miraculously vanished.
With her senses cleared, Evelyn’s mind instantly analyzed what had just happened.

’The Boss was using an artifact,’ Evelyn realized with chilling clarity. ’He doesn’t have an internal Lord Core, but he is wearing a high-tier relic pinned beneath his necktie... a Dread-Aura Seal, I don’t even need to use the System.’
It was an item that projected a frequency of psychological terror designed to induce submissive paralysis in anyone with a weakened mind... she had not realized that her mind was that weak.
Maybe because she was comfortable with Silas... she was no longer affected by this.
Evelyn rested her gloved hand against Silas’s broad shoulder plate.
’I will never ever admit this out loud to his arrogant face,’ Evelyn thought with her pulse steadying. ’But... thank you, Silas.’
She needed a long well-deserved vacation after this nightmare of a mission, and she was fully intending on taking three straight weeks off the moment they stepped back into the Sovereign Realm.
The Boss pulled up the official Black-Ash betting logs, and a low appreciative whistle escaped his lips.
"Incredible," the Boss murmured, shaking his head.
He flipped the holographic projector around so the numbers floated in the center of the room.
[Manager ID: 155]
[Account Tag: Black-Lotus-Holdings]
[Gross Tournament Balance: 90,050,000 Spirit Credits]
It was an astronomical sum of wealth.

Ninety million credits was enough to purchase an entire private district in Shogitown, fund a private mercenary battalion for three years, or buy several high-grade territories that were for sale outright.
"Ninety million," the Boss stated, looking directly into Evelyn’s Kitsune mask. "A truly historic payout... Please provide your secure offshore routing coordinates."
Evelyn, fully composed now and operating in pure business mode, reached out and tapped a secure encrypted ten-digit routing code into the obsidian terminal.
It was a dummy corporate shell account she specifically maintained for high-stakes laundering... cleared to receive massive, eight-figure sums without triggering World Council tax audits.
The Boss reviewed the routing clearance and nodded slowly.
Then... a thin smirk spread across his silver-bearded face.

"Everything appears in order," the Boss said smoothly, resting his chin in his palms. "However... as I am sure an experienced Manager such as yourself understands, processing ninety million credits through our underground liquidity pools incurs a mandatory operational clearance fee."
Evelyn let out a quiet tired internal sigh.
’Of course,’ Evelyn thought, looking unimpressed. ’The classic Underworld shakedown. Sleazy to the very end...’
"And what, precisely, is your standard clearance fee?" Evelyn asked.

"Given the unprecedented volume of the transaction," the Boss replied casually, "the Syndicate will require a standard thirty percent clearance deduction. That is twenty-seven million credits. Leaving you with a clean sixty-three million..."
The Boss leaned back, waving his hand magnanimously. "Though, as honorable business partners, I am naturally open to a reasonable counter-negotiation."
The Boss wasn’t desperate for the money.
The Black-Ash Syndicate had just raked in over two hundred million credits from the aggregate betting pools on the final match alone.
But mafia bosses didn’t become mafia bosses by leaving twenty-seven million credits sitting on a table.
He was feeling greedy.
Evelyn shifted slightly on Silas’s lap, leaning forward toward the obsidian desk.
Her dark eyes flashed behind the Kitsune mask, completely entering her element.

"Thirty percent is an insulting amateurish opening bid, Boss," Evelyn countered coldly. "Your standard Black-Ash charter explicitly caps executive clearance fees at fifteen percent for registered Tier-One tournament sponsors..."
She was going to use everything that she had studied about the Syndicates, especially this one for this argument.
The Boss smiled thinly.
"You are not a registered Tier-One sponsor, Manager 155. You are an anonymous outside entity..."

"I am an anonymous outside entity whose fighter just saved you millions of credits in syndicate cleanup costs," Evelyn shot back with surgical precision. "You admitted yourself five minutes ago that Onii-chan eliminated three major internal threats for your organization... If Zarch had lived, he would have leaked your distribution routes to the Northern Cartel. If Goliath-9 had survived, your security schematics would currently be on an encrypted server in the Iron-Core Cartel’s headquarters and not to mention the others."
The Boss’s smile faded slightly.

"Furthermore," Evelyn pressed ruthlessly, "we placed our sixty-million-credit wager through your terminal before the sudden-death rule change was announced. By the official laws of the Shogitown Gaming Commission... laws your own father drafted thirty years ago... any match restructured by the house without a forty-eight-hour notice is completely exempt from administrative taxation."
’I hope he also doesn’t ask about the original 1 million I used to bet.’ Evelyn thought after saying that, that was a free million!
Talia glanced at her father, genuinely surprised by the masked woman’s encyclopedic knowledge of the syndicate’s legal loopholes.

"If you attempt to withhold thirty percent," Evelyn concluded, crossing her arms with authority. "we will simply route the payment through Iron-Bank. They charge a flat eight percent wire fee, and they will publicly flag the Black-Ash Syndicate for liquidity failure... Your stock value will drop five percent by morning."
’I don’t even know what I’m saying at this point. I just want my money...’
The Boss stared at Evelyn in stunned silence.
For three long seconds, the only sound in the executive office was the hum of the air filtration system.
Then... the Boss threw his head back and burst into a loud genuine belly laugh.
"Hahahahaha!"
The Boss slammed his hand onto the obsidian desk, thoroughly entertained.
"Well played, Manager!" the Boss chuckled, shaking his head with immense respect. "It has been at least a decade since an outsider has quoted my own father’s charter back to my face. Brilliant..."
The Boss tapped his interface, adjusting the payout parameters.

"Ten percent," the Boss offered, his tone final. "Nine million credits for standard transaction clearance including the original amount you used to bet, and eighty-one million transferred directly to your offshore shell account. That is my final offer."
’Fuck, he remembered!’
"Deal," Evelyn agreed instantly.
BEEP!
A high-pitched confirmation chime rang through the console.
[TRANSACTION COMPLETE]
[TRANSFERRED: 81,045,000 SPIRIT CREDITS]
[RECIPIENT: BLACK-LOTUS-HOLDINGS]
"Thank you for your business," Evelyn said smoothly, inclining her head.
Down on the chair, Silas just sat there, looking between the two of them with utter bewilderment behind his Oni mask.
’What the fuck just happened?’ Silas thought with his brain spinning. Was that haggling?
The Boss closed the holographic financial tab and straightened his posture.
"Now," the Boss spoke into his desk comms unit. "Bring in the secondary asset."
PSSH-CHUNK!
The heavy ironwood doors hissed open once more.
Two burly syndicate enforcers stepped into the office, dragging a heavily bound prisoner between them.
The prisoner’s hands were clamped behind his back in massive iron suppression cuffs.

He possessed long unkempt silver-and-white hair that hung in greasy tangles around his face and a scruffy patchy beard covered his sharp jawline as he was also wearing stained threadbare prisoner overalls.
The Boss looked at the disheveled prisoner with disgust.
"On your knees, Ryan," the Boss commanded coldly.
The guards shoved the young man down onto the carpet in front of the desk.

"You are a disgrace to the family bloodline," the Boss spat, glaring at his son. "A pathetic, shut-in rat who spends his life hiding behind data screens... These two individuals have purchased your contract however so they are now your new owners."
Ryan... the hacker formerly known as Jax scoffed loudly, tossing his silver hair out of his eyes with a sneer.
"Good to see you too, you decrepit old fossil," Ryan insulted his father smoothly, his voice dripping with venom. "I hope you choke on your clearance fees."
Ryan slowly lifted his head, scanning his new buyers.
His eyes landed directly on the porcelain Kitsune mask sitting squarely on the lap of the massive dark-coated demon in the leather chair.
Ryan blinked.𝒇𝓻𝓮𝓮𝙬𝙚𝒃𝒏𝓸𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝓬𝓸𝒎
Then, the young hacker had to visibly bite the inside of his cheek to stifle a loud hysterical laugh.
"Pfft—" Ryan snorted, his shoulders shaking. "Well, well. Look at this power dynamic."
Evelyn’s face flared red again. She frantically tried to scramble off Silas’s lap, pushing against his chest with both hands.
"Let me down." Evelyn hissed under her breath.
Silas didn’t budge. He tightened his arm around her waist, keeping her firmly planted on his thighs just to spite her.
The Boss narrowed his slate-gray eyes, looking suspiciously at his son. "Do you know these people, Ryan?"
"Never seen them before in my miserable life, Dad," Ryan lied smoothly, winking slightly toward the Kitsune mask. "Just appreciating the scenery."
The Boss sighed, waving his hand toward Talia.
"Talia... Release the physical suppression bindings."
"With pleasure," Talia muttered.
Talia walked over to her brother, drawing a small high-frequency vibro-knife from her blazer pocket.
With two clean slices, she severed the reinforced locking mechanisms on the iron suppression cuffs.
CLANG!
The heavy iron cuffs dropped to the carpet.
Ryan groaned, rolling his sore shoulders and flexing his pale scarred fingers in the open air with a massive grin spreading across his bearded face.
"Ah, sweet freedom."
Talia immediately reached down, grabbed a fistful of his greasy silver hair, and violently yanked his head forward, forcing him to expose the back of his pale neck.
"Ow! Watch the hair, you psychotic bitch!" Ryan complained loudly.
On the pale skin directly beneath Ryan’s hairline, an intricate glowing crimson tattoo was etched deep into the flesh... A Slave Rune.
The Boss looked across the desk toward the leather chair.

"I can sense the dormant mana coursing through both of you," the Boss instructed. "Either the Manager or the Fighter must step forward and channel their personal mana directly into the core of the rune. Once your energetic signature binds with the formula, the control of Ryan will be permanently transferred to you."

"Just appreciating the scenery."
The Boss sighed, waving his hand toward Talia.
"Talia...
Release the physical suppression bindings."
"With pleasure," Talia muttered.
Talia walked over to her brother, drawing a small high-frequency vibro-knife from her blazer pocket.
With two clean slices, she severed the reinforced locking mechanisms on the iron suppression cuffs.
CLANG!
The heavy iron cuffs dropped to the carpet.
Ryan groaned, rolling his sore shoulders and flexing his pale scarred fingers in the open air with a massive grin spreading across his bearded face.
"Ah, sweet freedom."
Talia immediately reached down, grabbed a fistful of his greasy silver hair, and violently yanked his head forward, forcing him to expose the back of his pale neck.
"Ow!
Watch the hair, you psychotic bitch!" Ryan complained loudly.
On the pale skin directly beneath Ryan’s hairline, an intricate glowing crimson tattoo was etched deep into the flesh...
A Slave Rune.
The Boss looked across the desk toward the leather chair.
"I can sense the dormant mana coursing through both of you," the Boss instructed.
"Either the Manager or the Fighter must step forward and channel their personal mana directly into the core of the rune.
Once your energetic signature binds with the formula, the control of Ryan will be permanently transferred to you."

chapters.title: Chapter 374: Smile
paragraphs: Silas finally loosened his grip, allowing Evelyn to stand up.
’You better...’
Evelyn smoothed down her coat, took a deep steadying breath, and walked calmly over to where Ryan was kneeling on the carpet then she raised her black-gloved right hand.
HUMMMM!
A controlled pulse of pure refined mana flared at the tips of her fingers as she pressed her palm firmly against the glowing crimson tattoo on the back of Ryan’s neck.
"GHK—!" Ryan gasped, his back arching violently in pain.
HISSSSSSS!
The crimson tattoo flared with blinding white light as Evelyn’s mana forcefully overwrote the rune to fit her signature.
The magical binding burned into the deeper layers of Ryan’s nervous system, finalizing the ownership transfer with a dull echoing chime.
Evelyn stepped back, lowering her hand.
"The asset is secured," Evelyn confirmed, looking over at Silas. The Boss looked at the three of them for a long silent moment.
He didn’t offer a farewell handshake nor did he offer any parting words.
"Tch."
He simply raised his right hand and gave a lazy, dismissive wave across the obsidian desk.
VRAAAAAM!
A massive blinding flash of spatial teleportation magic erupted beneath their feet.
POP!

In a fraction of a second, Silas, Evelyn, and Ryan as well as his own daughter were instantly displaced, reappearing in the cold, rain-slicked alleyway outside the Black-Ash headquarters with the neon lights of Shogitown buzzing overhead.
Back in the expansive, dead-silent executive penthouse.
The Boss sat completely motionless behind his obsidian desk.
He reached into his tailored breast pocket, pulled out a thick pitch-black cigar wrapped in dried lotus leaves, and lit it with a small gold lighter.
Flick!
"Haah..."
He exhaled a thick cloud of pungent gray smoke into the empty room, watching the wisps drift toward the reinforced glass window overlooking the neon city.
"Ya hear...?"
He slowly leaned back in his leather chair, tilting his silver-haired head upward.
Hovering silently in the dark, empty space directly behind his back was a translucent ethereal spirit.
Nobody in the room had been able to see it and nobody in the city possessed the spiritual sight to perceive its terrifying existence.
To call it a ’spirit’ or a ’ghost’ was a grotesque understatement.
It was a Shinigami... a horrifying death deity that had taken the twisted, rotting physical form of his late deceased wife.
Her skin was an ashen, decayed gray, her jaw unhinged with razor-sharp rows of needle-like teeth, and hollow empty black voids occupied her eye sockets.
The Boss took another slow steady drag of his black cigar with his slate-gray eyes reflecting the neon lights below.
"I did exactly what you wanted," the Boss spoke into the empty room, his voice dropping all pretense of authority, sounding like an exhausted man.
He paused, letting the silence hang in the air.
"Are you happy now?" the Boss asked softly.
The grotesque Shinigami hovering behind him did not move at first.
For nearly thirty years, the entity had remained entirely mute... a silent parasitic specter bound to his life force that had never once spoken a single word in his presence.
The Boss slowly tilted his face forward, preparing to stand up from his desk.
A soft and melodic feminine whisper brushed directly against the back of his ear, it was as cold as the grave.
Silas blinked.
One single fraction of a second prior, his heavy boots were firmly planted on the polished marble floor of the Syndicate Boss’s opulent penthouse office.
In the very next heartbeat, a sharp disorienting pull yanked at the base of his skull, and the atmospheric pressure violently shifted.
The sterile scent of expensive synth-tobacco and leather was instantly replaced by the biting humid chill of the undercity.

Silas found himself standing squarely on the wet, cracked asphalt of an empty alleyway, surrounded by flickering holographic billboards, rusted exhaust pipes, and the looming silhouette of the Black-Ash colosseum spire towering overhead.
Pop!
Silas shook his head, clearing the lingering static from his perception.

’Space magic, huh?’ Silas noted dryly to himself, adjusting his posture. ’The old man just waved his hand and tossed three grown adults through half a mile of solid rock bedrock. That’s at least a Tier 3 or 4 spatial artifact pinned to his lapel...’
HZZZZT!
A sudden sharp sizzle crackled against his skin.
Silas looked down at his torso.

The sleek, form-fitting smart uniform... the standard-issue synthetic tournament combat gear the Black-Ash Syndicate had forced almost every qualifier to register and wear before stepping into the arena cage began to aggressively break down.
The smart-fabric dissolved into an unstable, bubbling puddle of pitch-black liquid nanites.
Drip! Slosh!

The black sludge peeled completely off his frame, pooling around the soles of his boots before rapidly slithering across the damp asphalt like a colony of metallic ants, vanishing directly through a drainage grate set into the base of the arena fortress to be reclaimed by the house.
Silas rolled his broad shoulders, completely unbothered.
’Good thing I didn’t trust their garbage gear...’ Silas thought with a quiet smirk beneath his silver Oni mask. ’Or I might have been half naked by now.’

Underneath the dissolving tournament suit, Silas had already layered his actual heavy-duty trench coat and reinforced combat trousers as well as his shirt before the sudden-death final royale commenced.
He was completely cleared to move.
Beside him, Evelyn adjusted the collar of her dark coat, letting out a sharp exhale into the cold air.
"Haah... Finally..."
The pale trembling that had seized her frame in the Boss’s office was entirely gone, replaced once more by her regular presence.
She turned her porcelain Kitsune mask toward Silas and the disheveled hacker standing beside them.
"We’re done here," Evelyn said, her voice dropping into a crisp no-nonsense executive tone. "Let’s move before the betting mobs swarm the perimeter."
"Agreed," Silas rumbled through his voice modulator.
Ryan, still rubbing the sore crimson skin on the back of his neck where the Slave Rune had just been forcefully overwritten by Evelyn’s mana nodded eagerly.
"Lead the way, boss-lady. The sooner I get out of sniffing distance of my old man’s headquarters, the better my lungs are going to feel."
The three of them turned on their heels, preparing to pull back toward the road.
"Hold on a second, Onii-chan."
Click! Clack! Click!
The sharp echoing sound of high heels striking the wet pavement cut through the ambient hum of the alleyway.
Silas paused with his boots halting on the cracked asphalt.
Evelyn stopped as well, turning her masked head back over her shoulder with an irritated narrow tilt.
Emerging from the shadowed access door of the private VIP exit was Talia.
The Boss’s black-haired daughter walked with fluid confidence, her tailored charcoal blazer accentuating her sharp silhouette against the flickering neon lights.
She stopped barely two paces in front of Silas, looking up at his towering frame through long dark eyelashes as a wicked amused smirk curled across her plum-painted lips.

"You put on quite a show in the pit today, Onii-chan," Talia purred smoothly, tilting her head as she looked straight into the narrow eye-slits of his silver Oni mask. "Splitting cyborgs, decapitating blood cultists... it’s been years since someone made my father laugh like that during a match."
"I did what I came to do," Silas replied flatly, keeping his hands buried deep inside his coat pockets. "We have our asset so we’re leaving."
"Not so fast," Talia chuckled, taking half a step closer. "The Syndicate always settles its debts in full. You did exceptionally well, and for that... I think you deserve a proper personal reward."
Silas didn’t move an inch.
"I don’t need a reward... The credits are already cleared."
Talia ignored him as she slipped two manicured fingers into the inner lapel of her tailored suit jacket and pulled out a sleek matte-black card trimmed with polished platinum foil.
She extended it forward, pressing the edge directly against Silas’s chest.
Silas looked down.
Etched into the metallic surface in clean glowing silver font was her official executive title and a direct number too.
[TALIA V. ASH]
[EXECUTIVE ASSET DIRECTOR]
Silas raised a black-gloved hand, taking the card between two fingers to get it off his chest.

"My private number," Talia said, her voice dropping to a low murmur that barely carried over the wind. "There are no middlemen and no filters... If you ever find yourself back in Shogitown looking for high-tier work... or looking for something significantly more entertaining to pass the night... you call that number."
Before Silas could step back, Talia smoothly reached up and placed her bare warm hand flat against his left shoulder.
Silas stiffened slightly beneath his coat with his eyes sharpening behind the metal mask as he looked down at her.
Talia leaned in a fraction of an inch closer, her dark eyes flashing with a dangerous teasing light.
"Make sure you actually use it, okay?" Talia whispered, her breath brushing the silver edge of his demon jaw. "Don’t make me have to track you down across the whole city."
In that exact split second, Silas felt something bizarre ripple across the surface of his skin.
It wasn’t a physical strike, and it wasn’t a hostile spell either.

It was an alien foreign pulse... a strange microscopic vibration that bypassed his outer clothes or and briefly danced across the layer hovering just beneath his Oni mask, tingling against his cheekbones and the bridge of his nose like static electricity.
Silas didn’t know what kind of covert technique it was, but he wasn’t about to stand around and let an underworld mafia princess experiment on him.
’I just want to get out of here...’
Silas violently rolled his shoulder backward, effortlessly shrugging her hand completely off his coat with a sharp dismissive motion.
He stepped back two full paces, casually sliding the black platinum card into the deep pocket of his trousers.
"I’ll keep it in mind," Silas stated dryly, unaffected by the display.
He turned his back on her, walking alongside Evelyn.
Beside them, Ryan couldn’t contain himself.
The hacker turned around as he walked backward, throwing his head back and extending two aggressive middle fingers directly toward his sister with a wide manic grin plastered across his bearded face.
"Fuck you, Talia, you psychotic bitch!" Ryan howled gleefully into the alleyway. "I’m never stepping foot back in this rat-hole! Tell Dad I’m spending all his money on bad takeout!"
Talia didn’t even flinch at the crude insult.

She completely ignored her brother’s existence, crossing her arms beneath her chest as she stood under the flickering amber streetlamp, watching Silas’s broad receding back disappear into the streets.
As the shadows swallowed the man in the trench coat, a slow radiant smile spread across Talia’s sharp wicked face.
A distinct rosy pink blush bloomed across her pale cheeks as well.
Flick!
A tiny microscopic spark of mana flared at the very tips of her manicured fingernails before dissolving into the air.
’Got him,’ Talia thought to herself, her pulse skipping with genuine excitement.

It was a sensory imprint technique... a rare illegal trick she had purchased from a foreign illusionist specifically designed to map facial bone density and facial structure straight through metallic and runic disguises with a single point of physical contact.
In her mind’s eye, the silver demon mask peeled away, revealing the crisp flawless mental image of Silas’s actual face.

’Well, well, well...’ Talia mused internally with a predatory glint igniting in her dark eyes as her tongue traced her lower lip. ’He isn’t just a brutal monster in the dirt. He is actually stunningly handsome. Sharp jaw, striking eyes... and that ridiculous magnificent ass to go with it. What a prize.’
She turned smoothly on her high heels, walking back toward the private executive entrance where four armed guards stood waiting at attention.
"Ma’am?" the lead guard inquired.

"Contact the primary information broker on Sector Two," Talia commanded sharply, her voice instantly snapping back into its cold tone that was fit for an executive. "Tell him to drop whatever petty corporate espionage he’s working on... He is going to run a full facial biometric sweep through every database in the city."
"Understood, Mistress Talia," the guard barked, tapping his comms unit and jogging off into the corridor.
Talia stepped through the doorway, glancing back one final time into the dark foggy alleyway with a wicked chuckle.
’Whoever you really are under that coat, Onii-chan...’ Talia thought, adjusting her blazer. ’You are not getting rid of me this easily... Not by a long shot.’

chapters.title: Chapter 375: Claire
paragraphs: Twenty minutes later, the sounds of the buildings faded behind them as they navigated the decrepit back-alleys of the lower residential area.
They had even passed by the Sniper that died and his body was still there and rotting though everything had been stolen off him.
The three of them stepped through a door, entering Ryan’s private apartment.
Silas stopped in the doorway, scanning the interior through his Oni mask.
The living conditions were, to put it mildly, a disaster.
It was a single cramped studio apartment smelling strongly of cheap instant noodles and burnt wiring.
Stripped power cables snaked across the bare concrete floor like tangled vines, connecting to improvised surge protectors taped directly to the water pipes.
There wasn’t even a proper bed... just a ratty sleeping bag thrown haphazardly into a corner beside empty nutrient pouches.
Silas took a slow breath, shaking his head slightly.

’It’s a pretty rough living space,’ Silas thought, his mind briefly drifting back to his earlier memories of waking up in the squalor of the lower slums. ’Though I really don’t have room to judge... I crawled out of the exact same gutter when I first dropped into this universe. At least this place has working electricity.’
Ryan completely ignored the state of the room.
The hacker sprinted straight through the clutter, rushing toward the far corner where an enormous multi-tiered workstation was set up.
Six massive custom-built high-performance CPU towers stood humming on iron brackets, connected to an array of eight glowing holographic monitors flickering with endless streams of encrypted code.
THUD!
Ryan dropped violently to his knees onto the bare concrete floor, throwing his arms wide open to embrace the glowing rigs like a man reuniting with his long-lost children.

"My babies!" Ryan wept dramatically, tears welling in the corners of his eyes as he pressed his cheek directly against the warm humming exhaust fan of the main server tower. "Oh, sweet, beautiful silicon gods, you’re safe! Did the bad mafia men hurt your memory caches? Did they touch your overclocked cooling tubes?!"
Mwa! Mwa! Mwa!
Ryan began passionately planting wet kisses all over the metallic chassis of each individual CPU, rubbing his bearded chin against the illuminated acrylic panels.

"Daddy’s home, Betsy!" Ryan cooed, kissing the primary hard-drive bay. "Daddy’s here, sweet little Megan! I swear to God I will never let that decrepit fossil of a father touch your motherboard ever again!"
Silas stood frozen near the door, his left eye twitching erratically behind the metal slit of his Oni mask.

’Is this... is this really the legendary hacker we just fought through an entire colosseum of psycho cyborgs and people to rescue?’ Silas thought, his brain physically struggling to process the degeneracy unfolding before him. ’I almost caught a minigun barrel to the teeth for a guy who gives his graphics cards female names and kisses cooling vents?’
As if possessing a sixth sense for his exact internal crisis, Evelyn slowly turned her head toward Silas, offering a long exhausted look through her Kitsune mask.
"Yes," Evelyn confirmed bluntly, answering his unasked question with absolute resignation. "He is the person. And yes, he is just irreversibly weird like that."
Ryan finally finished his passionate reunion with his hardware.
He wiped a smudge of paste from his nose, turned around, and sat cross-legged on the floor, leaning his back against the server rack.
"Haah... I’m happy to be home..."
He reached into a hidden compartment carved into the underside of the desk and pulled out a thick crumpled cigar.
Flick.
He struck a match against his thumbnail and lit the tip, exhaling a foul cloud of cheap synth-tobacco smoke into the cramped room.
Silas pinched the bridge of his nose beneath his mask, letting out a silent, pained groan.

’Fuck me...’ Silas cursed internally, looking between Evelyn and Ryan. ’Why am I entirely surrounded by heavy smoking addicts? First my manager, now the hacker... My lungs are going to turn into charcoal before I even reach the Sovereign Realm.’
They wouldn’t but he still had a right to complain.
Ryan took a deep drag, pointing the glowing ember of the cigar toward the two masked figures.
"Alright, let’s get formal," Ryan grinned, flashing his yellowed teeth. "You can call me Jax... You can call me Fortune... You can even call me Tech-Wiz if you’re feeling classy."
"We will refer to you as Ryan only, thank you very much," Evelyn interrupted instantly, her icy tone leaving zero room for debate.
Ryan’s face instantly twisted into an annoyed scowl.
"Oh, come on, lady! What happened to creative branding?! ’Ryan’ sounds like an accountant who files taxes for a dry-cleaning business! That’s corporate slave talk!"

"We just saved your miserable life from an execution cell and bought your slave contract..." Evelyn countered coldly, crossing her arms over her chest. "The very least you could do is show a basic shred of professional gratitude."

"Hey, I am grateful!" Ryan argued back, waving his arms in the air. "Which is the exact reason why I’m sitting here agreeing to do high-tier federal cybercrime for you completely free of charge. You have no idea what they put me through back in that holding block... It was this pitch-black concrete cube with no Wi-Fi, no stimulants, and two guards who didn’t even know what a proxy node was! It was pure torture!"
Ryan puffed on his cigar, letting out an exasperated sigh before leaning forward, resting his elbows on his knees.
"So," Ryan asked, his eyes sharpening with genuine focused intellect. "What’s the actual job you need done?"
Silas opened his mouth to explain the situation, but before he could speak a single syllable, Ryan let out a loud snort.
"Let me guess," Ryan smirked, pointing his cigar directly at Silas. "You need a completely bulletproof untouchable digital identity forged from scratch for Lord Vespera, right?"
Silas and Evelyn both froze in unison.
Behind their respective masks, both of their eyes widened in genuine momentary shock.
Ryan threw his head back and burst into a loud triumphant cackle at the stunned silence of the two Lords.

"Hah! Look at your faces!" Ryan laughed, slapping his knee. "Come on, it wasn’t that hard to figure out! I’m the best data broker in three sectors, remember? I’ve been tracking Evelyn’s streams from the exact second The Unmovable Wall arrived there."
Ryan tapped the side of his temple with a grin.

"I ran a deep cross-reference through the World Council central registry," Ryan explained. "And what did I find? Nothing... Lord Vespera literally did not exist in any mortal database prior to her stream debut. No birth records, no family registry, no citizen IDs either. That kind of blank slate is a massive red flag... It would have set the World Council auditors into a complete frenzy, convincing them that she was an unregistered anomaly or she was probably in a disguise."
Silas listened intently, leaning his shoulder against the doorframe.

"So, being the generous genius that I am," Ryan continued casually, "I proactively created seven different phantom identities across three regional servers just to keep the World Council’s hounds chasing their own tails in circles. You’re welcome, by the way..."
Ryan then turned his sharp gray eyes directly onto Silas, scanning the broad shoulders and towering height of the dark-coated Warlord.

"And looking at you now..." Ryan mused, tapping his chin thoughtfully. "I assume you’re Vespera in your true physical form, right? So the terrifying female Lord on the screen is actually a dude in real life? Wild."
Ryan shook his head with an appreciative chuckle.
"Gotta admit though, man... you make a surprisingly hot woman when you’re on stream."
Silas stared at him in complete deadpan silence for three long seconds.
’I am going to throw this man off a roof,’ Silas thought with terrifying calmness.
Silas took a slow breath, forcing the violent impulse back down.
"Why did you go out of your way to help cover my tracks before we even met? You didn’t know who I was."

"I knew someone representing Vespera would eventually have to come down to Shogitown to fix the paperwork," Ryan shrugged, tapping the ash from his cigar onto the concrete floor. "It’s basic operational necessity and more importantly... I wanted the rising Lord of the Blessed Land to owe me a massive personal favor. Having a powerhouse in my pocket is better than a million credits."
Silas looked at the scruffy hacker for a moment with the tension in his shoulders easing.
A genuine smile touched the corners of Silas’s lips beneath his Oni mask.
"Fair enough," Silas conceded smoothly, giving a single nod. "I owe you one."

"Damn right you do," Ryan chuckled, pushing himself up off the floor and dusting the grime from his trousers. "Well then! If we’re doing this, we need to forge a high-tier administrative identity. We need verified Council lineage, forged ancestral land deeds, and a clean banking lineage... It’s going to be exceptionally complicated, but for a genius like me, it’s just another Tuesday."
Ryan grabbed the squeaking leather swivel chair, spun it around, and reached for the main power switch on his central terminal to boot up the system.
"Don’t bother powering it on," Evelyn’s voice cut in smoothly from the doorway.
Ryan paused with his hand hovering over the switch.
Both Ryan and Silas turned their heads in confusion, looking at the masked woman.
"What do you mean ’don’t bother’?" Ryan asked, raising an eyebrow. "I can’t forge World Council registry keys on a piece of paper, lady."
HONK-HONK!
A vehicle horn echoed from the narrow alleyway directly outside the apartment window.
Click!
The apartment door swung open smoothly.
Stepping across the threshold was a striking impeccably composed woman in her late twenties and she possessed sharp elegant features with her auburn hair pulled neatly back into a professional bun.
She was dressed in an immaculate high-end maid uniform... a crisp white apron layered over a tailored black dress, paired with polished leather low-heels and white cotton gloves.
’Who is she?’ Silas thought.
She stopped just inside the room, placing her hands neatly over her waist, and offered a perfectly practiced forty-five-degree bow toward Evelyn.
"Master Evelyn," the woman spoke, her voice sounding melodious and very respectful. "I have arrived with the transport as instructed."
Silas’s pale-blue eyes sharpened instantly behind his mask, his combat perception locking onto the newcomer.
’A maid?’ Silas thought with his senses picking up the subtle hum of energy radiating beneath her skin. ’And she just called Evelyn "Master." Does that mean Evelyn has a slave too?’
Evelyn stepped forward, gesturing toward the open doorway.
"We are leaving this disgusting slum behind right now," Evelyn announced, looking between Silas and the confused hacker. "I already prepared full accommodations in advance."
As both men stared at her, Evelyn smiled beneath her Kitsune mask.

’I already fully intended to secure him today one way or another,’ Evelyn thought to herself, satisfied with her foresight. ’However the tournament came up and I’m glad... it was just the most cost-effective method to clean his record.’
The maid stepped forward into the room, inclining her head politely toward Silas and Ryan.

"Allow me to introduce myself," the maid said smoothly. "My name is Claire. Master Evelyn has already procured a secure fully furnished luxury penthouse for you in the upper district of Valoria City. You will be operating under Master Evelyn’s direct corporate umbrella on a permanent basis."
Ryan blinked in wide-eyed astonishment and a massive opportunistic grin spread across his face as he looked at Evelyn.
"A penthouse in the main city?!" Ryan gasped, clapping his hands together. "Full corporate sponsorship?! Oh, thank you, Master! You’re the greatest Master in the entire universe!"
Evelyn visibly flinched, a sharp shudder of pure disgust rippling down her spine.
"Do not call me that either, you weirdo," Evelyn snapped, crossing her arms defensively. "Call me Manager, or I will personally adjust your Slave Rune to shock you every time you breathe."
Ryan burst out laughing, unfazed by the threat.
"Whatever you say, Boss!"
Claire stepped toward the massive workstation in the corner. "Mr. Ryan, please step back. I will secure your hardware."

"Whoa, whoa, hold on, sweetheart!" Ryan warned frantically, raising his hands. "Those server racks are hyper-sensitive! If you drop one of those cooling tubes, three months of uncompressed data is going to—"
Snap!
Claire raised her gloved right hand and cleanly snapped her fingers.
VZZZZZZT!
A vibrant blinding dome of deep-purple energy flared into existence, enveloping the entire workstation.

The heavy steel desks, the eight holographic monitors, the six massive server towers, and every single tangled power cable smoothly, weightlessly detached from the floor and walls, rising four feet into the air in a state of frictionless levitation.
Claire swiped her hand through the air, and the entire multi-ton workstation drifted toward the door like a collection of balloons.
Silas watched the purple light with sharp interest.

Flick.

chapters.title: Chapter 376: Evelyn’s Choice [I / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: ’Telekinesis,’ Silas thought in surprise, reading the energetic flow. ’She definitely possesses a Lord Core... but she doesn’t have a territory.’
As a Lord himself, there was just a feeling she gave off... or rather a lack of the feeling, Silas was able to tell that she didn’t have a Territory anymore even though he couldn’t explain it.
Which meant she was an Adventurer.
"Well, I’ll be damned," Ryan muttered, watching his life’s work float out the door. "That saves me twenty minutes of unplugging cables."
Claire guided the floating workstation out into the alleyway, pausing at the threshold to look back at the empty room.
"Mr. Ryan," Claire asked politely. "What of your personal effects? Your clothing, your bed, and your remaining furniture?"
Ryan snorted, waving his hand dismissively.

"Didn’t you look at this place? It’s completely bare. I already pawned all my furniture and clothes on the black market two days ago. I was planning to stage an escape before my Dad caught me anyway."
Evelyn tilted her Kitsune mask, raising an eyebrow. "And what about your landlord? Did you settle your lease?"
Ryan cackled loudly, stepping out into the alley. "What landlord? I put a bullet in the back of the guy’s head three weeks ago when he tried to double my rent. I’ve been squatting here for free!"
Evelyn let out a long exhausted sigh, slowly shifting her footing to stand closer to Silas.
"There are really far too many insane people in this district," Evelyn muttered under her breath.
"You’re the one who hired him," Silas reminded her dryly.

Parked in the narrow alleyway was an enormous high-end armored transport vehicle... a sleek black luxury SUV featuring reinforced ballistic plating, tinted one-way glass, and heavy anti-grav dampeners.
Claire snapped her fingers once more.
The massive levitating workstation smoothly drifted into the vehicle’s expansive rear cargo bay.
CLUNK!
The automated hydraulic trunk sealed shut with a pressurized lock.
"Cargo secured," Claire reported, bowing slightly before moving toward the driver’s side. "Please enter the vehicle."
"I call shotgun!" Ryan yelled, sprinting forward and instantly diving into the front passenger seat before anyone could argue.
Silas and Evelyn walked to the rear passenger door.
Silas opened it, allowing Evelyn to slide into the plush heated leather interior before stepping in and pulling the heavy armored door shut behind him.
’I’m still surprised this stingy woman has a vehicle like this.’
VROOOOOM!
The luxury transport hummed to life, its high-performance magnetic engine purring with power.
Claire smoothly shifted gears, pulling out of the narrow alleyway and accelerating down the damp cracked streets of the lower slums.
The vehicle rapidly wove through the dark neon-lit labyrinth of Shogitown, bypassing the shaded checkpoints, the syndicate patrols, and the decaying industrial sectors.
Within ten minutes, the transport broke through and merged onto the wide multi-tiered expressways leading out of the undercity and climbing toward the surface.
Behind the tinted rear window, the glowing remnants of the underground festival slowly shrank in the distance.
Evelyn leaned her head back against the soft leather headrest, letting out a slow quiet breath.
She reached up with both hands and unlatched the side clasps of her porcelain Kitsune mask, pulling the heavy disguise off her face.
Her striking beautiful features emerged into the soft ambient light of the cabin with her dark hair tumbling loosely over her shoulders.
Beside her, Silas reached up and unsealed the locking bolts of his silver Oni mask.
PSSH-T!
The mask broke with a soft hiss, he had used mana to put a lot of pressure on it to prevent it from being hit off his face.

Silas pulled the heavy metal faceplate away, tossing it onto the middle seat as he ran a heavy black-gloved hand through his damp dark hair, wiping the accumulated sweat and grime of the fights from his forehead with the edge of his sleeve.
Evelyn turned her head slightly, her dark eyes resting quietly on Silas’s exposed profile.
She watched the steady rise and fall of his chest, remembering the terrifying sight of him standing completely untouched amidst a hailstorm of supersonic machine-gun fire.
A soft uncharacteristic warmth flickered in her chest.

’Next time...’ Evelyn thought to herself with her lips parting slightly as she looked out the window at the passing neon skyline. ’Maybe... if you actually want to... we could come back to a festival like that together. Just... to walk through the lights. Only if you want to, Silas.’
She didn’t say the words out loud. Evelyn just kept the thought locked safely in her heart, turning back to watch the road ahead.
By the time the armored transport finally crossed the grand suspension bridges into the pristine towering metropolis of Valoria City, the morning sun had fully crested the horizon.
It was exactly 9:00 AM.
The golden morning light reflected brilliantly off the crystalline glass skyscrapers, illuminating the clean tree-lined boulevards and the gleaming corporate spires of the upper district.
HISS!
Claire smoothly brought the heavy transport to a stop inside the private, underground parking garage of an ultra-luxurious high-security high-rise residential complex.
Claire shifted the car into park and glanced into the rearview mirror.
In the back seat, Evelyn was completely out cold.
Her head was resting heavily against Silas’s broad left shoulder with her breathing slow and a tiny trail of drool visibly pooling at the very corner of her parted lips.
Silas was sitting completely rigid with his head tilted sideways, giving the sleeping Lord on his shoulder a perplexed unimpressed look.
Claire cleared her throat with a polite smile.
"Master Evelyn."
Evelyn snapped awake instantly, her eyes flying open as she violently jerked her head upright off Silas’s shoulder, wiping her chin with the back of her sleeve in a frantic blur.
"I wasn’t sleeping!" Evelyn declared loudly, her face instantly flaring bright red. "I was conducting a deep-state assessment of our route!"
Claire maintained a completely neutral expression. "Uh-huh. Of course, Master."
Claire turned her gaze to the front passenger seat.
Ryan was completely slouched against the window, snoring loudly with his mouth wide open with a thick puddle of drool coating the glass.
Tap-tap!
Claire reached over and firmly tapped the hacker’s shoulder.
"Mr. Ryan. We have arrived."
Ryan snorted, violently jerking awake. "Gah! I didn’t fuck he—... oh. We’re here."
The four of them stepped out of the vehicle into the cool, immaculate air of the private garage.
Claire led them toward the private elevator landing, explaining the layout of the complex in her smooth professional tone.

"This is the Apex Heights residence," Claire explained, pressing the call button. "Master Evelyn has leased a fully renovated high-security two-bedroom executive suite on the seventy-fourth floor. It features independent encrypted power grids, dedicated satellite links, and top-tier computational hardware pre-installed in the secondary office for Mr. Ryan’s immediate use."
Claire snapped her fingers, using her purple telekinesis to smoothly float the massive custom-built server rig out of the vehicle’s trunk, guiding the floating hardware behind her.

"Before we can begin forging the new World Council registry," Claire noted, leading the way toward the elevator doors, "we must first transfer and synchronize Mr. Ryan’s existing data caches with the secure local mainframe."

"Oh, baby, a dedicated satellite uplink?!" Ryan cheered, his eyes glittering with excitement as he jogged alongside his floating servers. "Come on, big guy! Let’s get up there and start crafting your fake identity before the World Council auditors finish their morning coffee!"
Silas took a step forward to follow them toward the elevator, but paused, glancing back over his shoulder.
Standing beside the rear bumper of the SUV, Evelyn was holding her glowing smartphone in both hands.
Her brow was furrowed in deep visible anxiety with her thumbs trembling slightly as she stared down at an incoming encrypted caller ID flashing on the screen.
Silas frowned, taking half a step back toward her.
"Evelyn?" Silas called out, his voice calm and grounded. "You coming up?"
Evelyn blinked, startled out of her trance.
She quickly locked the phone screen, slipping it into her coat pocket, and looked up at him with a strained hurried smile that didn’t quite reach her dark eyes.
"Don’t worry about me, Silas," Evelyn said softly, waving her hand dismissively. "Go ahead up with Ryan. I just have... an exceptionally important call to make."
The sound of the lecture hall’s climate control did little to ease the mounting tension behind Matt’s temples.

He sat in the third row of the steeply tiered auditorium with the synthetic leather of the desk chair squeaking faintly under his shifting weight as he reached up with his index finger to nudge his thin-rimmed glasses back up the bridge of his nose.
Around him, fifty other second-year students at the Valoria Imperial Institute of Alchemical Technologies sat in varying states of focus.
Holographic styluses clicked rapidly against polished glass tablets, casting a strobe of pale blue across the darkened room.
At the front of the hall, pacing behind a massive slate-black workbench, stood Professor Elmi.

The man was a veteran of the industrial sector... his brown hair clipped ruthlessly short and his lab coat immaculately pressed while the cybernetic prosthetic that served as his left arm hummed with a dull low-frequency vibration whenever he moved.

"Pay attention to the class," Elmi’s gravelly voice projected effortlessly across the room, amplified by the micro-transceiver clipped to his high collar. "Most of you here were born without a Lord Core... You failed the awakening trials. You will never step through a gateway to a Secret Realm, you will never plant a flag in the soil of the Sovereign Realm, and you will certainly never command an army of summoned entities."
A collective quiet grimace rippled through the rows of students.
It was the harsh inescapable truth that governed modern human society.
Lords conquered dimensions and commanded reality while the unawakened engineered the scrap left behind.

"However," Elmi continued, slamming a scarred palm against the slate workbench, "that does not make you useless... Humanity does not survive on divine intervention alone. We survive on infrastructure. And infrastructure requires craftsmen... Awakened Scientists who can forge, stabilize, and mass-produce the gear that keeps our frontlines from crumbling."
Elmi turned, nodding toward the heavy double doors at the side of the stage.
"Bring it in, Daniel."
His teaching aide, a nervous-looking graduate student wearing heavy insulated leather gloves, pushed a wheeled stainless-steel cart out onto the platform.
Resting atop the reinforced surface was a complex mechanical assembly roughly the size of a suitcase.
Its chassis was forged from a black titanium alloy, intricately etched with spiraling conduits that terminated in a central circular vacuum-sealed chamber.
Mounted along its flanks were four articulated mechanical calipers, each tipped with finely polished quartz focusing crystals.
Matt leaned forward with his amber eyes scanning the instrument set through his lenses.
His fingers tightened around his digital stylus as this was the core foundation of his major... the Type-4 Ambient Mana Condenser and Imbuement Array.

"As commoners," Elmi explained, gesturing to the machine, "your bodies cannot naturally store, cycle, or release mana without suffering fatal cellular necrosis. You try to channel a raw current through your veins, and you will turn your central nervous system into burnt ash before you can cast a single spark. To circumvent our biological limitations, we utilize external mechanical manifolds."
Elmi reached out, flipping a heavy toggle switch on the side of the apparatus.
CLACK!
The mechanical calipers hissed softly as valves engaged.
The quartz crystals at the tips flared with a blinding incandescent azure light.
Within seconds, the air inside the lecture hall grew noticeably thinner as a metallic tang resembling ozone and petrichor began prickling the back of Matt’s throat.
Above the central chamber, a visible vortex of glowing blue vapor began to swirl, drawn forcefully from the atmosphere of the room.
The glowing particles condensed into a tight shimmering sphere of liquid mana that hovered steadily between the magnetic stabilizers.

"This is unrefined mana," Elmi stated, watching the blue light reflect off the faces of his students. "Drawn directly from the planetary atmospheric bleed of the Sovereign rifts... With this array’s runic board, an unawakened technician can guide this current with micrometer precision, cleanly imbuing raw metals, textiles, and core components without suffering magical backlash... Later this afternoon, we will proceed down to the underground foundry to initiate your first practical imbuement trials on tempered steel ingots."
Elmi paused, his sharp gaze sweeping over the tiered seating.

"I trust every single one of you has already submitted your requisitions to the bursar’s office to acquire your personal workstation kits. If you do not have your own array by the midterm practicals, you will fail the class. Am I understood?"
"Yes, Professor," the room chorused in unison.
Matt chimed in with the rest, though a confident smirk touched the corner of his lips.
He didn’t need to worry about the requisition fees.

The Valoria Imperial Institute was the most prestigious alchemical academy in the entire metropolitan district, boasting a guaranteed one-hundred percent placement rate within high-ranking guild laboratories upon graduation.
Its tuition was astronomical, a figure so absurd that normal families would have to mortgage three generations of labor just to afford a single semester.
Yet, Matt had never had to worry about a single credit.

sentences.text: ’Telekinesis,’ Silas thought in surprise, reading the energetic flow. ’She definitely possesses a Lord Core... but she doesn’t have a territory.’
As a Lord himself, there was just a feeling she gave off... or rather a lack of the feeling, Silas was able to tell that she didn’t have a Territory anymore even though he couldn’t explain it.
Which meant she was an Adventurer.
"Well, I’ll be damned," Ryan muttered, watching his life’s work float out the door.
"That saves me twenty minutes of unplugging cables."
Claire guided the floating workstation out into the alleyway, pausing at the threshold to look back at the empty room.
"Mr.
Ryan," Claire asked politely.
"What of your personal effects?
Your clothing, your bed, and your remaining furniture?"
Ryan snorted, waving his hand dismissively.
"Didn’t you look at this place?
It’s completely bare.
I already pawned all my furniture and clothes on the black market two days ago.
I was planning to stage an escape before my Dad caught me anyway."
Evelyn tilted her Kitsune mask, raising an eyebrow.
"And what about your landlord?
Did you settle your lease?"
Ryan cackled loudly, stepping out into the alley.
"What landlord?
I put a bullet in the back of the guy’s head three weeks ago when he tried to double my rent.
I’ve been squatting here for free!"
Evelyn let out a long exhausted sigh, slowly shifting her footing to stand closer to Silas.
"There are really far too many insane people in this district," Evelyn muttered under her breath.
"You’re the one who hired him," Silas reminded her dryly.

Parked in the narrow alleyway was an enormous high-end armored transport vehicle... a sleek black luxury SUV featuring reinforced ballistic plating, tinted one-way glass, and heavy anti-grav dampeners.
Claire snapped her fingers once more.
The massive levitating workstation smoothly drifted into the vehicle’s expansive rear cargo bay.
CLUNK!
The automated hydraulic trunk sealed shut with a pressurized lock.
"Cargo secured," Claire reported, bowing slightly before moving toward the driver’s side.
"Please enter the vehicle."
"I call shotgun!" Ryan yelled, sprinting forward and instantly diving into the front passenger seat before anyone could argue.
Silas and Evelyn walked to the rear passenger door.
Silas opened it, allowing Evelyn to slide into the plush heated leather interior before stepping in and pulling the heavy armored door shut behind him.
’I’m still surprised this stingy woman has a vehicle like this.’
VROOOOOM!
The luxury transport hummed to life, its high-performance magnetic engine purring with power.
Claire smoothly shifted gears, pulling out of the narrow alleyway and accelerating down the damp cracked streets of the lower slums.
The vehicle rapidly wove through the dark neon-lit labyrinth of Shogitown, bypassing the shaded checkpoints, the syndicate patrols, and the decaying industrial sectors.
Within ten minutes, the transport broke through and merged onto the wide multi-tiered expressways leading out of the undercity and climbing toward the surface.
Behind the tinted rear window, the glowing remnants of the underground festival slowly shrank in the distance.
Evelyn leaned her head back against the soft leather headrest, letting out a slow quiet breath.
She reached up with both hands and unlatched the side clasps of her porcelain Kitsune mask, pulling the heavy disguise off her face.
Her striking beautiful features emerged into the soft ambient light of the cabin with her dark hair tumbling loosely over her shoulders.
Beside her, Silas reached up and unsealed the locking bolts of his silver Oni mask.
PSSH-T!
The mask broke with a soft hiss, he had used mana to put a lot of pressure on it to prevent it from being hit off his face.

Silas pulled the heavy metal faceplate away, tossing it onto the middle seat as he ran a heavy black-gloved hand through his damp dark hair, wiping the accumulated sweat and grime of the fights from his forehead with the edge of his sleeve.
Evelyn turned her head slightly, her dark eyes resting quietly on Silas’s exposed profile.
She watched the steady rise and fall of his chest, remembering the terrifying sight of him standing completely untouched amidst a hailstorm of supersonic machine-gun fire.
A soft uncharacteristic warmth flickered in her chest.

’Next time...’ Evelyn thought to herself with her lips parting slightly as she looked out the window at the passing neon skyline. ’Maybe... if you actually want to... we could come back to a festival like that together.
Just... to walk through the lights.
Only if you want to, Silas.’
She didn’t say the words out loud.
Evelyn just kept the thought locked safely in her heart, turning back to watch the road ahead.
By the time the armored transport finally crossed the grand suspension bridges into the pristine towering metropolis of Valoria City, the morning sun had fully crested the horizon.
It was exactly 9:00 AM.
The golden morning light reflected brilliantly off the crystalline glass skyscrapers, illuminating the clean tree-lined boulevards and the gleaming corporate spires of the upper district.
HISS!
Claire smoothly brought the heavy transport to a stop inside the private, underground parking garage of an ultra-luxurious high-security high-rise residential complex.
Claire shifted the car into park and glanced into the rearview mirror.
In the back seat, Evelyn was completely out cold.
Her head was resting heavily against Silas’s broad left shoulder with her breathing slow and a tiny trail of drool visibly pooling at the very corner of her parted lips.
Silas was sitting completely rigid with his head tilted sideways, giving the sleeping Lord on his shoulder a perplexed unimpressed look.
Claire cleared her throat with a polite smile.
"Master Evelyn."
Evelyn snapped awake instantly, her eyes flying open as she violently jerked her head upright off Silas’s shoulder, wiping her chin with the back of her sleeve in a frantic blur.
"I wasn’t sleeping!" Evelyn declared loudly, her face instantly flaring bright red.
"I was conducting a deep-state assessment of our route!"
Claire maintained a completely neutral expression.
"Uh-huh.
Of course, Master."
Claire turned her gaze to the front passenger seat.
Ryan was completely slouched against the window, snoring loudly with his mouth wide open with a thick puddle of drool coating the glass.
Tap-tap!
Claire reached over and firmly tapped the hacker’s shoulder.
"Mr.
Ryan.
We have arrived."
Ryan snorted, violently jerking awake.
"Gah!
I didn’t fuck he—... oh.
We’re here."
The four of them stepped out of the vehicle into the cool, immaculate air of the private garage.
Claire led them toward the private elevator landing, explaining the layout of the complex in her smooth professional tone.
"This is the Apex Heights residence," Claire explained, pressing the call button.
"Master Evelyn has leased a fully renovated high-security two-bedroom executive suite on the seventy-fourth floor.
It features independent encrypted power grids, dedicated satellite links, and top-tier computational hardware pre-installed in the secondary office for Mr.
Ryan’s immediate use."
Claire snapped her fingers, using her purple telekinesis to smoothly float the massive custom-built server rig out of the vehicle’s trunk, guiding the floating hardware behind her.
"Before we can begin forging the new World Council registry," Claire noted, leading the way toward the elevator doors, "we must first transfer and synchronize Mr.
Ryan’s existing data caches with the secure local mainframe."
"Oh, baby, a dedicated satellite uplink?!" Ryan cheered, his eyes glittering with excitement as he jogged alongside his floating servers.
"Come on, big guy!
Let’s get up there and start crafting your fake identity before the World Council auditors finish their morning coffee!"
Silas took a step forward to follow them toward the elevator, but paused, glancing back over his shoulder.
Standing beside the rear bumper of the SUV, Evelyn was holding her glowing smartphone in both hands.
Her brow was furrowed in deep visible anxiety with her thumbs trembling slightly as she stared down at an incoming encrypted caller ID flashing on the screen.
Silas frowned, taking half a step back toward her.
"Evelyn?" Silas called out, his voice calm and grounded.
"You coming up?"
Evelyn blinked, startled out of her trance.
She quickly locked the phone screen, slipping it into her coat pocket, and looked up at him with a strained hurried smile that didn’t quite reach her dark eyes.
"Don’t worry about me, Silas," Evelyn said softly, waving her hand dismissively.
"Go ahead up with Ryan.
I just have... an exceptionally important call to make."
The sound of the lecture hall’s climate control did little to ease the mounting tension behind Matt’s temples.

He sat in the third row of the steeply tiered auditorium with the synthetic leather of the desk chair squeaking faintly under his shifting weight as he reached up with his index finger to nudge his thin-rimmed glasses back up the bridge of his nose.
Around him, fifty other second-year students at the Valoria Imperial Institute of Alchemical Technologies sat in varying states of focus.
Holographic styluses clicked rapidly against polished glass tablets, casting a strobe of pale blue across the darkened room.
At the front of the hall, pacing behind a massive slate-black workbench, stood Professor Elmi.

The man was a veteran of the industrial sector... his brown hair clipped ruthlessly short and his lab coat immaculately pressed while the cybernetic prosthetic that served as his left arm hummed with a dull low-frequency vibration whenever he moved.
"Pay attention to the class," Elmi’s gravelly voice projected effortlessly across the room, amplified by the micro-transceiver clipped to his high collar.
"Most of you here were born without a Lord Core...
You failed the awakening trials.
You will never step through a gateway to a Secret Realm, you will never plant a flag in the soil of the Sovereign Realm, and you will certainly never command an army of summoned entities."
A collective quiet grimace rippled through the rows of students.
It was the harsh inescapable truth that governed modern human society.
Lords conquered dimensions and commanded reality while the unawakened engineered the scrap left behind.
"However," Elmi continued, slamming a scarred palm against the slate workbench, "that does not make you useless...
Humanity does not survive on divine intervention alone.
We survive on infrastructure.
And infrastructure requires craftsmen...
Awakened Scientists who can forge, stabilize, and mass-produce the gear that keeps our frontlines from crumbling."
Elmi turned, nodding toward the heavy double doors at the side of the stage.
"Bring it in, Daniel."
His teaching aide, a nervous-looking graduate student wearing heavy insulated leather gloves, pushed a wheeled stainless-steel cart out onto the platform.
Resting atop the reinforced surface was a complex mechanical assembly roughly the size of a suitcase.

Mounted along its flanks were four articulated mechanical calipers, each tipped with finely polished quartz focusing crystals.
Matt leaned forward with his amber eyes scanning the instrument set through his lenses.
His fingers tightened around his digital stylus as this was the core foundation of his major... the Type-4 Ambient Mana Condenser and Imbuement Array.
"As commoners," Elmi explained, gesturing to the machine, "your bodies cannot naturally store, cycle, or release mana without suffering fatal cellular necrosis.
You try to channel a raw current through your veins, and you will turn your central nervous system into burnt ash before you can cast a single spark.
To circumvent our biological limitations, we utilize external mechanical manifolds."
Elmi reached out, flipping a heavy toggle switch on the side of the apparatus.
CLACK!
The mechanical calipers hissed softly as valves engaged.
The quartz crystals at the tips flared with a blinding incandescent azure light.
Within seconds, the air inside the lecture hall grew noticeably thinner as a metallic tang resembling ozone and petrichor began prickling the back of Matt’s throat.
Above the central chamber, a visible vortex of glowing blue vapor began to swirl, drawn forcefully from the atmosphere of the room.
The glowing particles condensed into a tight shimmering sphere of liquid mana that hovered steadily between the magnetic stabilizers.
"This is unrefined mana," Elmi stated, watching the blue light reflect off the faces of his students.
"Drawn directly from the planetary atmospheric bleed of the Sovereign rifts...

With this array’s runic board, an unawakened technician can guide this current with micrometer precision, cleanly imbuing raw metals, textiles, and core components without suffering magical backlash...
Later this afternoon, we will proceed down to the underground foundry to initiate your first practical imbuement trials on tempered steel ingots."
