chapters.title: Chapter 377: Evelyn’s Choice [II / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: His older sister, Evelyn, had shouldered every single expense since they were orphaned.

She was a Lord who spent weeks at a time in the hellish combat sectors of the Sovereign Realm, risking her life to haul back ancient artifacts and rare monster cores all the while battling other Lords.
He never had to work a job.
He never had to haggle for second-hand textbooks. He had the freedom to sit in clean, air-conditioned lecture halls and pursue his academic ambitions without a care in the world.
Elmi reached for a tray of unrefined silver ingots, ready to demonstrate the imbuement sequence.
"Now, observe the calibration sequence on the primary—"
BZZZZ-CLICK!
A grating burst of static violently tore through the high-end speakers mounted around the perimeter of the ceiling.
Professor Elmi frowned with his cybernetic hand halting in mid-air. The entire lecture hall fell dead silent as the PA system hummed to life.

"Attention, Lecture Hall B-4," a crisp emotionless female voice echoed over the intercom, carrying the authority of the administrative high council. "Will student Matthew Davis please report to the Chancellor’s Office immediately. Repeat: Matthew Davis, report to Chancellor Timothy’s executive suite on the top floor of the Central Administration Tower immediately."
BZZZZ-CHUNK!
The speaker cut off.
Fifty pairs of eyes instantly snapped in Matt’s direction as whispers erupted across the tiered rows like a swarm of angry hornets.

Being summoned over the general intercom was rare... being summoned directly to the Chancellor’s private office was practically unheard of, usually reserved for severe disciplinary tribunals or massive scholarship awards.
Matt blinked, his mind completely blanking out. He sat frozen in his seat with the blue light from the array flickering across his pale face.

’The Chancellor’s office?’ Matt thought with a cold bead of sweat suddenly forming at his hairline. ’What the hell did I do? I haven’t missed a single lecture. My laboratory safety record is pristine. Did one of my distillation reports flag an error? No, that wouldn’t go to the Chancellor...’
Professor Elmi let out an irritated sigh, adjusting his lab coat as he looked up into the third row.
"Well, Davis? You heard the directive. Don’t keep the administration waiting. Hurry up so you can return before we conclude the imbuement demonstration."
"Y-yes, Professor. Right away," Matt stammered.

He hurriedly packed his glass tablet and stylus into his sleek leather satchel, pushed himself up from his chair, and navigated the narrow stairs down to the exit under the intensely curious stares of his classmates.
Stepping out into the grand marble-paved corridors of the engineering wing, Matt adjusted his glasses with a trembling finger.
"Haah..."
His boots clicked rapidly against the polished floors as he made his way toward the sky-bridge connecting the academic facilities to the monolithic Central Administration Tower.
The tower was a towering spire of obsidian and reflective mirrored glass, radiating the immense wealth of an institution backed by the planetary elite.
High-speed mana-lifts carried him silently to the eighty-fifth floor.
When the lift doors chimed open, the bustling noise of the campus below was gone, replaced by the plush soundproofed serenity of the executive suite.
Thick velvet carpets swallowed his footsteps as he approached a set of towering double doors forged from lacquered dark oak and trimmed with solid gold filigree.
Behind a curved glass desk sat the Chancellor’s executive secretary, an immaculate woman in a tailored charcoal suit.
"Matthew Davis," Matt said, his voice cracking slightly before he cleared his throat. "I was called up from Lecture Hall B-4."
The secretary glanced up from her holographic interface with her expression completely neutral.
"Chancellor Timothy is expecting you... You may enter."
She tapped a hidden rune beneath her desk. With a soft hiss, the heavy oak doors unlocked and swung silently inward.
"Thank you," Matt murmured, swallowing the heavy lump in his throat as he stepped through the threshold.
The secretary stood up, followed him inside just long enough to close the heavy doors firmly behind him, and stepped back out, sealing the young man inside the massive private office.
The room was vast and imposing.
Floor-to-ceiling panoramic windows offered a dizzying view of the sprawling Valoria City skyline, where high-speed mag-trains wove between gleaming skyscrapers.
Sitting behind a massive, semi-circular desk carved from a single slab of petrified Ironwood was Chancellor Timothy.
The man was an intimidating figure... completely bald, with a broad thick-set frame that spoke of decades spent in military service before transitioning to academia.
Two deep scars cut diagonally across his weathered left cheek, ending just above a graying neatly trimmed goatee.
He was reviewing a series of floating red holographic ledgers and his dark eyes narrow and severe.
Seeing Matt enter, Timothy slowly dismissed the floating interfaces with a casual flick of his thick fingers.
He gestured toward a plush leather-bound armchair positioned directly opposite the massive desk.
"Sit, Davis," Timothy commanded.
Matt didn’t dare hesitate.
He moved quickly, perching himself nervously on the edge of the leather chair with his satchel clutched tightly against his knees.

"Chancellor Timothy, sir," Matt began, his voice laced with anxious deference. "Did something happen with my practical submissions? If there was an issue with my laboratory safety clearance or my research metrics, I can immediately—"
"This is not an academic inquiry, Davis," Timothy interrupted smoothly, leaning back in his heavy chair and interlacing his thick scarred fingers over his chest.
The older man fell completely silent for several agonizing seconds with his piercing gaze studying the young student with an unreadable detachment.
The silence in the vaulted office was suffocating, broken only by the distant sound of the city outside.
"Tell me," Timothy finally broke the silence, his tone entirely flat. "Have you spoken with your primary guarantor recently?"
Matt blinked with his brow furrowing in confusion.

"My... my primary guarantor? You mean my sister, Evelyn? No, sir. Not since yesterday afternoon. She was deployed in the Sovereign Realm for the past week, and we had a brief... disagreement when she returned. Why? Is she alright?"
"Lord Evelyn Davis is in perfect physical health as far as the Institute is concerned," Timothy stated calmly. He reached forward, tapping a node on his desk.
A glowing red parchment materialized between them, displaying the official digital seal of the Imperial Bursar’s Office.

"However," Timothy continued, his eyes locking onto Matt’s widening gaze, "less than a few minutes ago, Lord Davis officially invoked the Institute’s Guarantor Withdrawal Clause... She has forcefully reclaimed every single payment credited to your matriculation account."
The words hung in the air like a sudden drop in atmospheric pressure.
Matt stared at the red document.
His brain refused to parse the meaning of the words.
"I... I’m sorry, sir? What do you mean, reclaimed? She paid for my entire five-year program during my freshman orientation and the entire balance was locked into the trust fund."

"The trust fund was established under standard Lord Association sponsorship protocols," Timothy explained with a sigh. "Which explicitly grants the funding Lord total authority to liquidate and withdraw unspent capital via the semester refund policy at any point prior to the final academic audit of each cycle."
Timothy tapped the holographic ledger, causing the lines of financial data to scroll downward.

"She has completely cleared out your tuition trust for the remaining three years. Furthermore, while she left the maintenance fee for the current semester untouched... meaning you will not be physically escorted off the campus premises today... she specifically and deliberately executed a total clawback of your End-of-Year Practical Examination Fund."
Matt’s mouth parted in absolute horror.
"The... the examination fund?"

"Correct," Timothy said, his face entirely devoid of pity. "Which means that if you wish to sit for your practical imbuement assessments next month, you will be required to settle that balance out of your personal accounts. Otherwise, you will receive an automatic zero, your matriculation will be terminated, and your academic profile will be blacklisted across all premier manufacturing guilds."
Matt felt the blood instantly drain from his face.
The room seemed to tilt sideways as a high-pitched ringing buzzing violently inside his ears.
Evelyn... had taken the money back?
All of it?
Why? Because of what had happened in Shogitown yesterday?!
His thoughts spiraled backward in a frantic defensive panic.
He had just been trying to enjoy a normal day! He had finally secured a date with his beautiful girlfriend from his department... a girl whose family held influence in the inner districts.
And right in the middle of their date, Evelyn had showed up like an overbearing embarrassing phantom, watching him from across the street in her mask like a pathetic stalker!
He had been furious.
What else was he supposed to say?! She was suffocating! She was constantly hovering over him, treating him like a fragile child who needed to be shielded from the world!
Was she really this petty? Was she really going to throw away his entire future, destroy his scientific career, and drag him into the dirt just because he wanted some basic boundaries?!
"H-How..." Matt’s voice hitched with a violent stutter seizing his throat as his knuckles turned white against his satchel. "How much... is the practical examination fee, sir?"
Chancellor Timothy cleared his throat, leaning forward and resting his forearms against the petrified wood.

"The Assessment requires specialized Tier 2 raw mythril, high power mana crystals, and dedicated safety oversight from certified Guild Masters. The mandatory testing fee is exactly three million Spirit Credits."
"Three... three million?!" Matt gasped, his eyes bulging behind his glasses.
Three million Spirit Credits was a staggering fortune.
That was the price of a luxury hover-car or a high-end apartment in the lower sectors.

He frantically ran the mental calculations of his personal banking app. Over the past few years, he had saved bits and pieces of his generous monthly allowances, hoarding roughly three point two million in his private account.
If he emptied his entire life savings... every single credit he had to his name... he could barely scrape together enough to pay for the exams.
He would be left completely broke, without a single credit to buy food, passes, or coffee.
"And..." Matt choked with a cold terrifying dread gripping his chest as he looked at the older man. "What about... what about the upcoming semester, Chancellor? In the spring?"
Timothy’s expression hardened slightly, his scarred cheek twitching with a bit of sympathy.

"The Valoria Imperial Institute is a cream-of-the-crop elite institution, Davis. We maintain a flawless one-hundred percent post-graduation corporate employment rate because our tuition filters out those who cannot secure financial backing... The standard tuition for your third-year curriculum is exactly twenty-five million Spirit Credits. Due on the first of February."
Twenty-five million?
The number hit Matt with the physical force of a sledgehammer.
The plush office seemed to violently cave in around him with the walls pressing against his ribs until he couldn’t breathe.
Twenty-five million credits wasn’t an academic fee... it was an insurmountable mountain!
An unawakened commoner working a standard nine-to-five corporate shift in the Lower Ward earned barely forty thousand credits a year.
Even if he worked until he was ninety years old, he would never see twenty-five million credits in his entire life.

Without Evelyn’s Sovereign Realm expeditions... without her... he was nothing. He was just another broke useless peasant destined to sweep factory floors and assemble mundane scrap for forty credits an hour.
Chancellor Timothy watched the young man’s complete psychological collapse with a cold piercing gaze.
The scarred veteran let out a soft, dismissive breath, shaking his bald head.

"I do not know what transpired between you and your sister, Davis," Timothy said as he offered a rare piece of blunt advice. "And frankly, the administration does not care about domestic disputes but you would do well to remember that in this world, an unawakened commoner’s only true asset is the patron willing to invest in them. Whatever offense you caused Lord Evelyn... I strongly suggest you rectify it immediately. In fact, you may use my executive console to call he—"
Matt didn’t wait for the Chancellor to finish his sentence.
The terror, the shame, and the frantic, boiling anger inside him completely overrode his academic decorum.
He violently shoved himself out of the leather chair, nearly knocking his satchel to the floor.
"Excuse me, sir," Matt spat out in a ragged breath.

He reached forward, tapping a node on his desk.
A glowing red parchment materialized between them, displaying the official digital seal of the Imperial Bursar’s Office.
"However," Timothy continued, his eyes locking onto Matt’s widening gaze, "less than a few minutes ago, Lord Davis officially invoked the Institute’s Guarantor Withdrawal Clause...
She has forcefully reclaimed every single payment credited to your matriculation account."
The words hung in the air like a sudden drop in atmospheric pressure.
Matt stared at the red document.
His brain refused to parse the meaning of the words.
I’m sorry, sir?
What do you mean, reclaimed?
She paid for my entire five-year program during my freshman orientation and the entire balance was locked into the trust fund."
"The trust fund was established under standard Lord Association sponsorship protocols," Timothy explained with a sigh.
"Which explicitly grants the funding Lord total authority to liquidate and withdraw unspent capital via the semester refund policy at any point prior to the final academic audit of each cycle."
Timothy tapped the holographic ledger, causing the lines of financial data to scroll downward.
"She has completely cleared out your tuition trust for the remaining three years.

Furthermore, while she left the maintenance fee for the current semester untouched... meaning you will not be physically escorted off the campus premises today... she specifically and deliberately executed a total clawback of your End-of-Year Practical Examination Fund."
Matt’s mouth parted in absolute horror.
"The... the examination fund?"
"Correct," Timothy said, his face entirely devoid of pity.
"Which means that if you wish to sit for your practical imbuement assessments next month, you will be required to settle that balance out of your personal accounts.
Otherwise, you will receive an automatic zero, your matriculation will be terminated, and your academic profile will be blacklisted across all premier manufacturing guilds."
Matt felt the blood instantly drain from his face.
The room seemed to tilt sideways as a high-pitched ringing buzzing violently inside his ears.
Evelyn... had taken the money back?
All of it?
Why?
Because of what had happened in Shogitown yesterday?!
His thoughts spiraled backward in a frantic defensive panic.
He had just been trying to enjoy a normal day!
He had finally secured a date with his beautiful girlfriend from his department... a girl whose family held influence in the inner districts.
And right in the middle of their date, Evelyn had showed up like an overbearing embarrassing phantom, watching him from across the street in her mask like a pathetic stalker!
He had been furious.
What else was he supposed to say?!
She was suffocating!
She was constantly hovering over him, treating him like a fragile child who needed to be shielded from the world!
Was she really this petty?
Was she really going to throw away his entire future, destroy his scientific career, and drag him into the dirt just because he wanted some basic boundaries?!
"H-How..." Matt’s voice hitched with a violent stutter seizing his throat as his knuckles turned white against his satchel.
"How much... is the practical examination fee, sir?"
Chancellor Timothy cleared his throat, leaning forward and resting his forearms against the petrified wood.
"The Assessment requires specialized Tier 2 raw mythril, high power mana crystals, and dedicated safety oversight from certified Guild Masters.
The mandatory testing fee is exactly three million Spirit Credits."
"Three... three million?!" Matt gasped, his eyes bulging behind his glasses.
Three million Spirit Credits was a staggering fortune.
That was the price of a luxury hover-car or a high-end apartment in the lower sectors.
He frantically ran the mental calculations of his personal banking app.
Over the past few years, he had saved bits and pieces of his generous monthly allowances, hoarding roughly three point two million in his private account.
If he emptied his entire life savings... every single credit he had to his name... he could barely scrape together enough to pay for the exams.
He would be left completely broke, without a single credit to buy food, passes, or coffee.
"And..." Matt choked with a cold terrifying dread gripping his chest as he looked at the older man.
"What about... what about the upcoming semester, Chancellor?
In the spring?"
Timothy’s expression hardened slightly, his scarred cheek twitching with a bit of sympathy.
"The Valoria Imperial Institute is a cream-of-the-crop elite institution, Davis.
We maintain a flawless one-hundred percent post-graduation corporate employment rate because our tuition filters out those who cannot secure financial backing...
The standard tuition for your third-year curriculum is exactly twenty-five million Spirit Credits.
Due on the first of February."
Twenty-five million?
The number hit Matt with the physical force of a sledgehammer.
The plush office seemed to violently cave in around him with the walls pressing against his ribs until he couldn’t breathe.
Twenty-five million credits wasn’t an academic fee... it was an insurmountable mountain!
An unawakened commoner working a standard nine-to-five corporate shift in the Lower Ward earned barely forty thousand credits a year.
Even if he worked until he was ninety years old, he would never see twenty-five million credits in his entire life.
Without Evelyn’s Sovereign Realm expeditions... without her... he was nothing.
He was just another broke useless peasant destined to sweep factory floors and assemble mundane scrap for forty credits an hour.
Chancellor Timothy watched the young man’s complete psychological collapse with a cold piercing gaze.
The scarred veteran let out a soft, dismissive breath, shaking his bald head.
"I do not know what transpired between you and your sister, Davis," Timothy said as he offered a rare piece of blunt advice.

"And frankly, the administration does not care about domestic disputes but you would do well to remember that in this world, an unawakened commoner’s only true asset is the patron willing to invest in them.
Whatever offense you caused Lord Evelyn...
I strongly suggest you rectify it immediately.
In fact, you may use my executive console to call he—"
Matt didn’t wait for the Chancellor to finish his sentence.
The terror, the shame, and the frantic, boiling anger inside him completely overrode his academic decorum.
He violently shoved himself out of the leather chair, nearly knocking his satchel to the floor.
"Excuse me, sir," Matt spat out in a ragged breath.

chapters.title: Chapter 378: Evelyn’s Choice [III / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: He reached into his tailored slacks, ripping his sleek Spirit Phone from his pocket with trembling sweaty fingers.
He aggressively swiped his thumb across the glass interface, tearing open his contacts application.
His eyes darted across the screen.
Evelyn... Where was her number?!
It wasn’t in his recents and it wasn’t in his primary contact list.
With a sickening jolt of realization, Matt remembered.
She was blocked.
Gritting his teeth so hard his jaw ached, Matt navigated to his device settings, ripped her contact off the blocked list, and aggressively tapped the dial button.
He jammed the speaker against his ear, pacing across the plush carpet in front of the Chancellor’s desk.
Ring... Ring... Ring...!
Every single dial tone felt like a physical strike against his skull.

’What do I say to her?’ Matt thought frantically with his mind racing through a dozen desperate scenarios. ’Should I apologize? No... Why the hell should I apologize?! She’s the one who acted like a psychotic lunatic! She’s the one who ruined my date! She’s my older sister... it’s her legal, moral responsibility to take care of me! She can’t just abandon me like this!’
CLICK!
The line connected.
Before the person on the other end could even draw a breath, Matt completely lost all semblance of control.
The dam broke, and he exploded into the receiver at the top of his lungs.
"SIS! WHAT THE FUCK?!"
The unrestrained vulgarity of the scream bounced off the soundproofed walls of the executive office.

Chancellor Timothy flinched violently in his seat, his thick eyebrows shooting up in bewildered shock at the audacity of the nineteen-year-old student screaming like a feral animal in the Chancellor’s private sanctuary.
Matt didn’t give a damn about Timothy as his vision was red with rage.

"Are you completely out of your goddamn mind?!" Matt roared into the phone, his spittle flying across the glass screen. "You pulled my tuition trust?! You withdrew the examination funds?! What kind of sick manipulative psychotic game are you playing right now?! You are an idiot! Do you have any idea what you just did to my academic standing?!"
"Davis, cease this immediately—" Timothy barked, half-rising from his chair with his hand raised in warning.
Matt completely ignored the Chancellor, turning his back to the desk and pacing violently toward the panoramic window.

"You’re a miserable good-for-nothing stalker!" Matt screamed. "I told you yesterday, I don’t want to live with you and for a long time now! I don’t want to see your pathetic face hovering over my shoulder every time I try to have a normal life! But just because I set some basic boundaries, you’re going to try and ruin my entire life?! You’re pulling back on my—"
"—Are you seriously going to stand there and let this little ungrateful guy talk to you like that?"
The voice didn’t belong to Evelyn.
It was a deep masculine voice that cut through the line like a sharpened blade.
Matt froze mid-stride with his breath catching in his throat.
Over the speaker, the rustle of a heavy jacket could be heard, followed by Evelyn’s familiar flustered voice protesting in the background.
"Go away, dummy! I’m handling it!"

"Sure, sure... handle it," the deep voice replied with a dismissive chuckle that made the hairs on Matt’s arms stand on end. "Be quick about it, though... We still have to review the stuff that he’s doing, I’m only waiting out here because you’re here."
"I know, I know! Just give me a second, Silas!" Evelyn snapped back, her tone carrying an exasperated familiarity that completely shattered Matt’s reality.
Matt gritted his teeth until he tasted blood.
Silas.
It was him.
It was the broad-shouldered man wearing the menacing Oni mask from the Shogitown festival yesterday.
The mysterious man who had casually stood beside Evelyn while she watched him from the side.
Was he her boyfriend?! Was this the man she was sleeping with now?! Had this arrogant stranger convinced his sister to cut him off and leave him to rot?!
"Who the hell was that?!" Matt demanded, his voice trembling with a mixture of rage and terror. "Evelyn! Who is that guy?! Put him on the phone right now! What gives him the right to—"
"...Are you done yelling, Matt?"
Evelyn’s voice came through the receiver.
Matt stopped.

For the past five years, whenever Evelyn spoke to him, her voice had always carried a desperate edge... constantly walking on eggshells, constantly apologizing for being away in the Sovereign Realm, constantly begging for his approval and affection.
Whenever he raised his voice, she would crumble, asking what she had done wrong.
Today, there was no trembling and there was no stutter either.
Her tone was chillingly calm and full of confidence that Matt had never heard from her in his entire life.

"Evelyn, listen to me," Matt tried to assert his dominance with his words tumbling out fast. "You need to reverse the bursar request right now. The Chancellor is literally sitting right in front of me, and if you don’t authorize the tuition transfer—"
"I’m glad I cut it off," Evelyn interrupted. "Hearing you scream at me like an entitled rabid dog just confirmed that I made the absolute right decision."
Matt blinked.
"W-What?"

"Yesterday, after we spoke..." Evelyn continued, her words precise and cutting, "I thought for a very long time, and I realized something that should have been obvious to me years ago... Why do I even bother?"
The room fell dead silent.
Even Chancellor Timothy sat completely still, watching the young man grip the device with white knuckles.

"For four years, Matt," Evelyn said. "I have invited you to attend the Shogitown Cultural Festival with me... Every single year, I bought two VIP passes. Every single year, I rushed back from the fights with blood still under my fingernails, hoping that maybe... just maybe... my little brother would spend an afternoon with his sister and every single year, you made an excuse. You told me you were studying. You told me you were busy."
She let out a soft dry laugh over the line.

"And then yesterday, I saw you walking down the lantern boulevard, laughing, holding hands with a girl I’ve never seen before. If you have a girlfriend, why couldn’t you just introduce her to me? Why couldn’t you just say, ’Evelyn, I want you to meet someone’? We live under the same roof! I pay for the very clothes on your back! But you treat me like an embarrassing, dirty secret that you have to hide from your elite social circle."
"That’s not—"

"I don’t care, Matt," Evelyn shut him down instantly. "You want to be independent? You want to live a life separated from me? You don’t want to see my face or acknowledge that we share the same blood? Fine. You win. Everything is okay now... You have your freedom."
A cold wave of pure panic slammed into Matt’s chest. "Sis, wait—"

"Don’t ever contact me for tuition again," Evelyn stated. "We lost our parents when we were children. I was sixteen years old, Matt. Sixteen... I had to throw my life through jobs and when I was 18, I had to enter the meat grinder of the Sovereign Realm, taking contracts, getting my ribs shattered by beasts, and starving in the mud just to ensure that the two of us had a roof over our heads and a future to look forward to."
Her voice dropped.

"You have spent your entire adult life sitting in luxury, looking down your nose at the very combat that feeds you. Well, now it’s your turn. You are going to feel exactly what it feels like to struggle for every single credit tenfold... You want to graduate from the Imperial Institute? Get a job. Haul scrap or beg a corporate guild for an apprenticeship. Because not another single Spirit Credit from my account will ever touch your account."

"Evelyn, please!" Matt pleaded with the arrogant facade completely shattering as tears of terror pricked his eyes. "I have exams next month! It’s three million credits! I’ll be blacklisted! You can’t just do this to your own brother!"

"I am your sister legally, of course," Evelyn replied coldly. "But since you have made it abundantly clear that I am dead to you... you are dead to me as well and this time, little brother... I am going to be the one who blocks your number."
"Evelyn, don’t—!"
CLICK! BEEP! BEEP! BEEP!
The call disconnected.
Matt stood frozen in the center of the Chancellor’s office with his arm holding the silent phone against his ear.
His entire body was shaking violently, his knees felt like water and his breathing coming in shallow hyperventilating gasps.
He frantically pulled the phone away, tapping her name on the screen to dial back.
[Alert: The party you are attempting to reach has restricted incoming transmissions from this terminal.]
She had blocked him.
She had actually blocked him.
The reality of his situation crashed over him like a suffocating tidal wave.
He was completely alone. His apartment rent, his daily food delivery subscriptions, his designer clothes, his tuition... it was all gone. Gone in a single phone call.
Slowly, Matt turned around to face the desk.
Chancellor Timothy sat with his chin resting in his palm, his scarred face impassive, offering the young man a look of unvarnished pity.
"Well, Davis?" Timothy asked quietly.
Matt swallowed hard with his throat parched as he lowered his trembling hands.
"I... I can settle the three million credit fee for the practical examinations right now, Chancellor. From my personal savings."
Timothy studied him for a second, then nodded curtly. "Very well. Transfer the funds to the bursar portal before the end of the business day... Dismissed."
Matt didn’t say another word. He turned on his heel and stumbled blindly out of the office with his world reduced to ruins.
Across the city, in the quiet streets of the Silverleaf District, the early afternoon sun cast long angular shadows across the manicured lawns.
Sitting on a sleek polished dark-wood park bench positioned directly across the street from Silas’s gated apartment complex was Seraphina Bloom.
The crimson-haired noble was currently holding a wide oversized broadsheet newspaper entirely in front of her face, pretending to read the economic section.

She wore a wide-brimmed black designer sunhat and dark sunglasses, though the disguise did nothing to hide the striking, undeniable beauty of her sharp facial structure, nor the voluptuous curves wrapped tightly in a tailored crimson blazer.
Standing stiffly beside the bench, his hands folded neatly behind his back, was her family’s primary butler, Reginald.
The elderly man in the crisp black suit adjusted his collar, sweating slightly in the warm afternoon air as he glanced at his expensive pocket watch.

"My Lady," Reginald spoke softly, leaning down slightly toward the newspaper. "Why are we still waiting on this public bench? It has been nearly two hours since we got here... Perhaps we should simply ring the chime again or wait inside the limousine?"
Seraphina didn’t lower the newspaper.
Her vibrant crimson eyes, visible behind the dark tint of her sunglasses, remained locked onto the front entrance of the gated property.

"We wait right here, Reginald," Seraphina muttered through gritted teeth, her manicured fingers gripping the edges of the paper tightly. "The purple-haired harpy inside slammed the door in my face earlier, claiming Silas was out in the city on business... If I retreat to the limousine, he might slip past us through the garage so we stay until he returns."
Reginald let out a soft resigned sigh.
"O-Of course, Lady Seraphina."
Just as the butler finished speaking, the loud rattling of a failing combustion engine echoed down the quiet boulevard.
A beat-up canary-yellow public transit cab, spewing a small plume of gray exhaust, sputtered up to the curb directly in front of the apartment gates.
The vehicle came to an abrupt jerky stop with its rusted brakes squealing in protest.
The rear passenger door swung open, and Silas stepped out onto the concrete.
Silas took a deep exhausted breath, rolling his broad shoulders as the taxi rattled away into the distance.
’What a ridiculously long morning...’ Silas thought to himself, aggressively running a hand through his messy dark hair.
It was roughly noon now.

He had spent the last few hours inside a server room with Evelyn, Ryan, and Claire, meticulously reviewing the multiple false identities the elite hacker had forged to throw the World Council’s biometric tracking algorithms completely off course.

He was a wizard with code as he had successfully constructed an airtight multi-layered background profile for the alias ’Lord Vespera,’ complete with forged historical land deeds in the outer rim and fake sponsorship records.
With the false paper trail secured, he was in the process of creating the real one and then he would contact the world council.
’Now that the heavy lifting is done,’ Silas thought, turning toward the gates of his apartment, ’I can finally head back to the Blessed Land or maybe I should stay home for no—’
Silas paused.

’Another stalker?’ Silas thought with a groan of pure, unadulterated exasperation. ’Seriously? First it was Harper sitting on that damn bench some time ago, and now there’s a new one? And who is the guy in the suit?’
Before he could take a step toward the gate, the figure on the bench abruptly lowered the newspaper.
The woman stood up in a single fluid motion, gracefully removing her wide-brimmed sunhat and sliding her dark sunglasses down the bridge of her nose.
Her vibrant cascading crimson hair caught the brilliant afternoon sunlight, framing a breathtakingly gorgeous aristocratic face with sharp captivating red eyes.
Her tailored crimson blazer and high-waisted pencil skirt perfectly accentuated an hour-glass figure that commanded immediate suffocating attention.
She stepped off the curb with her designer stiletto heels clicking sharply against the asphalt as she strode purposefully across the street directly toward him.
Reginald followed two paces behind, carrying himself with rigid subservient poise.
Silas’s heart instantly dropped straight into his stomach.
’Fuck...’ Silas swore internally, his face freezing into a completely deadpan expression. ’Of all the people on this entire damn planet... why her?’
Seraphina Bloom was the last person he wanted to deal with today.
His mind was still entirely exhausted from balancing dimensional politics, managing his people in an Unknown Zone, and navigating Evelyn’s family drama.
The last thing he had the mental bandwidth for was high-society noble entitlement.
Seraphina came to an abrupt halt exactly three feet in front of him.
The subtle incredibly expensive scent of night-blooming jasmine and vanilla rolled off her skin, mingling with the crisp neighborhood air.
Silas remained perfectly still, resting his hands casually in the pockets of his black slacks.
He raised an eyebrow, keeping his tone carefully neutral.𝙧𝙚𝙚𝔀𝒆𝓫𝓷𝙤𝓿𝒆𝙡.𝒄𝙤𝓶
"Seraphina Bloom," Silas greeted smoothly. "To what do I owe the absolute pleasure of having the Bloom Clan’s heiress stake out my front porch?"
Seraphina eyed him from head to toe.
She took in his broad muscled frame, the golden rings lingering in his deep blue irises, and the effortless confidence radiating from his relaxed posture.
Despite herself, an involuntary visible rosy blush instantly crept up her neck, dusting her flawless pale cheeks with a warm crimson hue.
She quickly cleared her throat, crossing her arms beneath her voluptuous chest in a desperate attempt to maintain her haughty untouchable noble demeanor.
"You remember," Seraphina stated, her voice tight with a mixture of burning indignation and poorly concealed embarrassment. "Inside Ititius’s Secret Realm... you saw me naked."
Silas didn’t even blink.
"Here we go..."

"No amount of apologies from Valerius, nor any diplomatic reparations made on House Sterling’s behalf," Seraphina continued, stepping closer until she was looking directly up into his eyes, "can ever fundamentally erase the indisputable fact that you... a commoner from the Lower Ward slums, no less laid your eyes upon my unblemished, sacred body!"
Silas stared down at her, unimpressed by the dramatic noble monologue.

"It was literally only from the waist down," Silas corrected flatly. "And you were squatting in the sand behind a dune taking a piss while the rest of us were fighting for our lives against a Sand Guardian... I was sent flying during the confrontation so forgive me for having functioning eyes."

"WHAT DIFFERENCE DOES THAT POSSIBLY MAKE?!" Seraphina shrieked, her aristocratic composure instantly shattering as her face turned completely beet-red. "The exposure of a Bloom maiden’s flesh to an unrelated male carries unyielding societal weight! You saw everything!"
Silas let out a heavy soul-weary breath, pinching the bridge of his nose.
He didn’t want this nonsense escalating into a full-blown clan conflict.
The Bloom Clan was an ancient terrifyingly wealthy lineage of high-tier Lords with immense political leverage in the World Council.
If they decided to launch a blood feud over a compromised maiden’s honor, they would deploy high-ranking squads to scour the city.
Push came to shove, Silas knew he could easily protect himself.

He could shatter the masquerade, reveal his Mythic Gold Core, invoke the sovereign authority of his Lord Vespera persona, and use the weight of his #1 Newbie Leaderboard status to force the World Council to grant him total legal immunity.
But doing so would completely destroy his family’s peace... His little sister, Lia, was only eleven years old.
She deserved to grow up in a normal home, attend Valoria Academy with her friends, and eat dinner without having to look over her shoulder for noble assassins or corporate paparazzi.
Silas dropped his hand, his blue eyes hardening into a serious protective gaze.

"Look, Seraphina," Silas said, his voice dropping into a low, uncompromising tone. "I understand that your family traditions are strict. If the Bloom Clan feels insulted, and you want to extract some sort of personal punishment from me to settle your pride, fine. Challenge me to a duel in the Association arena, demand a fine, do whatever you need to do. But leave my sister and my household out of this."
Seraphina blinked, completely caught off guard by his ferocious protective declaration.
"Punish...?" Seraphina stammered, her voice suddenly losing all of its venom. "No... I am not here to... punish you, Silas..."
Silas furrowed his brow, looking down at her in genuine confusion. "You’re not?"
Seraphina’s blush exploded into an inferno.
The heat rushed all the way to the tips of her delicate ears, and she felt as though steam was literally about to whistle out of her scalp.
Unable to maintain eye contact with his piercing blue gaze for another second, she violently shoved the thick gold-embossed leather folder she had been clutching directly against his chest.
"Just read them!" Seraphina squeaked, her voice pitching up in pure mortification.
Silas caught the heavy leather binder against his ribs.
He cast a suspicious glance at the blushing noblewoman, slowly unclasped the brass lock, and flipped the heavy paper open.
He focused his eyes on the bold, elegant calligraphy stamped across the very first page, backed by the official notarized magical seal of the Valoria City High Registry.
[OFFICIAL BINDING ACCORD: CONJUGAL ALLIANCE & MATRIMONIAL CONTRACT]
[Parties Involved: Lady Seraphina Bloom of House Bloom & Lord Silas Graves]
Silas completely froze.
He stared at the page. He closed his eyes, rubbed them with his thumb, and opened them again to ensure the text hadn’t shifted.
"A... marriage contract?" Silas asked, his voice cracking in flabbergasted disbelief. "Are you out of your mind?!"

"YES!" Seraphina declared fiercely, throwing her hands up in dramatic, blushing defiance. "The fact that you laid your eyes upon my naked form is an unforgivable sin against my family’s sacred heritage! And the only way to cleanly extinguish that sin, preserve my honor, and prevent a catastrophic clan scandal is for you to take responsibility and marry me!"
"Uh..." Silas stood completely paralyzed on his own sidewalk, holding the multi-million-credit marriage accord in his hands.
His mind violently snapped backward to a specific memory.

A while ago, while he had been livestreaming his territorial expansion in the Umbral Basin alongside Evelyn, the global chat had exploded when a verified high-tier noble handle belonging to Lady Etilga Bloom... Seraphina’s notoriously unhinged mother had aggressively asked for him who had been in his Vespera form to marry Seraphina on the broadcast.
’If I remember...’
Etilga had publicly announced to millions of viewers that her daughter had mysteriously fallen in love with an unknown commoner, and that she was preparing to kill him.
Silas’s eyes widened into massive saucers as the horrifying realization hit him like a lightning strike.

’THAT WAS ME?!’ Silas screamed in the silent caverns of his own mind, a cold terrifying dread gripping his spine. ’Eleonora wants to butcher the guy Seraphina is trying to marry... and Seraphina is trying to marry ME?!’

Marrying Seraphina didn’t just mean dealing with a haughty blushing noblewoman... it meant putting a permanent, glowing red crosshair directly between his shoulder blades from the most violent matriarch in the entire Eastern Hemisphere!
Seraphina interrupted his frantic internal panic, stepping forward and aggressively tapping her manicured index finger against the contract.

"You do not have a choice in this matter, Silas Graves!" Seraphina insisted, puffing out her chest and trying desperately to look intimidating. "You will sign the registry, you will become my lawful husband, and if you dare reject this gracious proposal, I will personally—"
VROOOOOOOM!
The deep roar of a high-performance twin-turbo mana engine aggressively tore through the quiet boulevard, cutting Seraphina off mid-sentence.
A custom-built midnight-purple luxury sports coupe glided violently around the corner.
Its low-slung aerodynamic frame hummed with raw power as it drifted smoothly along the curb, coming to a sharp flawless halt directly behind Reginald’s obsidian limousine.
Silas, Seraphina, and Reginald all snapped their heads toward the vehicle.
The heavily tinted driver’s side window smoothly slid down with a soft, mechanical purr.
Resting her elbow comfortably against the window frame was Harper.

The energetic, purple-haired Lightning Lord wore oversized designer sunglasses perched on the bridge of her nose, her lips curving into a sharp competitive smirk as her glowing violet eyes locked onto the scene.

"Sorry for interrupting whatever little street drama is going on out here," Harper called out, her voice dripping with pure sarcasm. "But as you can see, I just drove all the way from the Central District for my official date with Silas."
Seraphina’s head snapped toward the sports coupe.
Her crimson eyes flared with incandescent, territorial fury as she recognized the woman who had answered Silas’s door earlier.

"Date?!... What’s that?! Whatever..." Seraphina snarled, taking two aggressive steps toward the car. "He is not going on a date with you! He is my prospective husband! He is the property of House Bloom! You don’t get any dates, you purple-haired vulture!"
CLICK-CHUNK!
The vertical scissor-door of the sports coupe smoothly swung upward.
Harper gracefully stepped out of the luxury vehicle onto the pavement.

She stood to her full height, her tailored trousers accentuating her long athletic legs as she reached up and dramatically slid her sunglasses off her face, letting them hang from the collar of her shirt.
She walked toward them with an amused dangerous swagger, her lips twitching with suppressed laughter as she looked Seraphina up and down.

"You want to force him into a marriage contract just because he saw you naked from the waist down behind a dune?" Harper asked, her violet eyes flashing with crackling static electricity as she stopped right beside Silas and crossed her arms.
Harper leaned her shoulder casually against Silas’s muscular arm, looking directly into Seraphina’s furious, widening eyes with a triumphant grin.

"Well, guess what, sweetheart?" Harper dropped the bombshell with ruthless glee. "He saw me completely naked, too! All over! From head to toe! And to make it even better, he literally grabbed both of my hips with his bare hands! So by your exact, flawless noble logic... I should be the one marrying him, shouldn’t I?"
Seraphina’s sharp jaw clenched until the pale skin across her cheeks turned bloodless.
Her vibrant crimson eyes, framed by perfectly curled lashes that had never once witnessed the grime of the lower wards, dilated into narrow furious pinpricks.
She knew about the incident inside the Secret Realm.

She remembered every agonizing humiliating second of it... how the whole tower had collapsed when she had been about to kill her and how Harper had been caught in the crossfire alongside Silas though she still didn’t understand why that happened.

’Did she have to scream it out in the middle of a public street?!’ Seraphina raged internally, her manicured nails digging into the soft leather of her family’s marriage accord until the seals groaned under the friction. ’Did this insolent unrefined common Lord actually just announce to my butler and the entire neighborhood that Silas saw her naked and held her hips?!’
The indecency of it bypassed Seraphina’s practiced noble composure entirely.
Decades of high-society etiquette, private tutoring under Imperial etiquette masters, and strict lessons on aristocratic detachment shattered into absolute dust.
"You shameless wretched gutter rat," Seraphina spat. "Back off before I incinerate every single hair on your empty skull once again."

chapters.title: Chapter 380: Let’s Get To Know Each Other [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: She took a slow deliberate step forward, her expensive crimson stilettos clicking like cocked hammers against the stone walkway.
FWOOM!
Seraphina didn’t merely channel her mana... she violently detonated it.
A dense swirling corona of incandescent red flames erupted from the pores of her right hand, crawling up her tailored designer sleeve without scorching the fabric.

The fire wasn’t standard elemental mana... it was the hyper-refined crimson ancestral flame of House Bloom, burning with such suffocating pressurized heat that the moisture in the air between them instantly hissed and turned into shimmering waves of vapor.
’I newly learned this specific spell just for a situation like this.’
Harper didn’t flinch.
In fact, the energetic, purple-haired Lightning Lord grinned... it was a feral smirk that bared her teeth like an apex predator catching the scent of fresh blood.

"Oh, look at you, getting all worked up because someone else touched your imaginary prize," Harper taunted, her violet eyes flaring with jagged arcing fractals of electrical energy. "You think you can flash a little lighter fluid and scare me off, Princess? What you pulled on me during the expedition isn’t going to happen again. I’ve had weeks of high-voltage core refinement since that Secret Realm, and I’ve been dying for a rematch."
CRACK-BZZZT!
Brilliant branching tendrils of violent purple lightning exploded outward from Harper’s shoulders.
The raw backwash caused the hem of Silas’s oversized dark hoodie to violently billow around her thighs.

The concrete beneath Harper’s sneakers began to pit and smoke as millions of micro-volts grounded into the sidewalk, filling the quiet suburban street with the sharp, overwhelming stench of ozone and scorched earth.
"My Lady! Miss Whitmore! Please, exercise diplomatic restraint!"
Reginald, the Bloom family’s veteran butler, finally broke his subservient silence.
The elderly man in the crisp three-piece suit lunged forward, his gloved hands raised in a desperate bid to create a physical barrier between the two converging mana storms.
"Step aside, Reginald!" Seraphina snarled without taking her eyes off Harper’s throat.
"Get out of the splash zone, old man, or your pacemaker is going to detonate!" Harper snapped back, her lightning coiling into a blinding sphere of plasma in her palm.
Both women simultaneously directed their unblinking glares squarely at the butler.
The suffocating pressure of the two women converging on a single point hit Reginald like an atmospheric sledgehammer.
The elderly man choked on his own breath, violently recoiling three full paces until his back slammed against the obsidian fender of the Bloom family limousine.
Panting softly, his heart hammering against his ribs, Reginald slowly turned his gaze away from the impending catastrophe and locked his eyes onto Silas.
Reginald wasn’t just a domestic servant.
Behind the polished manners, the pristine pocket watch, and the silver-cuffed sleeves, Reginald was an unyielding, high-tier enforcer who had served House Bloom for forty-five years.
He was the executioner Lady Etilga Bloom kept in reserve when family matters required untraceable discretion.

Before departing the Bloom estate this morning, Lady Etilga herself had pulled Reginald into her private parlor, her eyes burning with that terrifying psychotic protectiveness that terrorized the high nobility.

’Watch him, Reginald,’ Etilga had whispered, sliding a mana-nullifying stiletto into his coat pocket. ’Seraphina is my only masterpiece... If this commoner from the slums is weak, if he is cowardly, if he attempts to use my daughter’s innocence to crawl out of the mud and leech off our family’s wealth... you will slit his throat and dump his core into the incinerators. She will grieve for a month, and then she will marry who I want her to. Understood?’𝐟𝕣𝕖𝐞𝐰𝕖𝚋𝐧𝗼𝚟𝐞𝕝.𝗰𝐨𝐦
Reginald narrowed his eyes, tracking Silas’s every microscopic movement.
This was the test.
A commoner faced with two high-tier awakened women threatening to tear the neighborhood apart would either cower behind the gate, beg for mercy, or flee inside.

If Silas Graves showed even a fraction of hesitation... if he proved himself to be an opportunistic parasite lacking the backbone to command respect, Reginald’s hidden blade would sever his carotid artery before the police wards could even ping the district’s defense grid.
Silas stood in the eye of the brewing storm however he didn’t tremble.

’If these two psychotic women keep this up for another three seconds,’ Silas thought, letting out a bone-weary sigh that practically deflated his lungs, ’they are going to blow a five-meter crater into the front porch. The asphalt will melt, the property value of the Silverleaf complex will plummet, and the agency will literally hunt me down with a frying pan to make me pay for the landscaping.’
Silas did not have the patience for a middle-school catfight on his front lawn so he stepped forward.

His boots made no sound against the pavement as he seamlessly closed the distance, effortlessly stepping directly into the convergence zone between the raging red flames and the crackling purple plasma.
Before either woman could react, Silas shot both of his hands out.
His large calloused right hand clamped firmly around Seraphina’s burning wrist, while his left hand clamped around Harper’s electrified forearm.
FZZZZT!
The power of his Mythic Gold Core foundation acted like an elemental sponge.
The moment his bare skin made contact with their mana, his internal golden pathways flared to life beneath his flesh.

The blazing red fire licking Seraphina’s knuckles sputtered, choked, and extinguished as if smothered by an ocean, while Harper’s violently arcing purple lightning dissipated harmlessly into his palm with a soft, pathetic pop.
Both women gasped, freezing instantly.
"Silas!" Harper squeaked, frantically pulling her mana back into her sternum so she wouldn’t accidentally fry his nervous system.
"Let go, you idiot! You’ll burn your skin off!" Seraphina cried out in genuine panic, desperately extinguishing the last embers around her fingertips to keep from injuring him.

Silas didn’t let go. He held both of their wrists with an unyielding vice-like grip for two long seconds, ensuring the magical radiation had entirely cleared the air, before slowly releasing them and taking a step back.
He raised his right hand, aggressively rubbing the back of his neck as he glared at them with half-lidded irritated golden-ringed eyes.

"Are you two completely done throwing a tantrum in the middle of the street?" Silas asked, his deep voice cutting through the residual smell. "Look around. This is a residential neighborhood. People are trying to sleep, walk their pets, and live normal lives. You don’t need to fight over here. I really don’t want to have to pay the municipal association for property damages, and frankly, I don’t feel like watching two grown women beat each other to death over a misunderstanding..."
Harper took a step back, crossing her arms over her chest and pouting as she rubbed her wrist.
"She started it. She pulled up waving a legal document like a lunatic."

"You breached his personal residence and answered the door wearing his clothes, you insolent harpy!" Seraphina grumbled, brushing a strand of crimson hair from her flushed face as she adjusted her blazer.
Standing beside the limousine, Reginald stood completely paralyzed, his jaw subtly dropping beneath his manicured mustache.

’He... he grabbed their active conduits with his bare hands?’ Reginald’s mind screamed in total bewilderment. ’Lady Seraphina’s ancestral fire burns at three thousand degrees and Miss Whitmore’s lightning carries enough kinetic voltage to paralyze several men at once according to what I know. If I had stepped between them, my hands would have been reduced to carbonized bone yet he snuffed both spells out without a single scorch mark on his palms?!’
Reginald slowly unclasped his fingers from the concealed stiletto inside his coat pocket.
The terrifying physical resilience the young man had just displayed made the butler’s combat instincts scream a deafening warning: Do not engage... This man is a walking fortress.
Silas completely ignored the sweating butler, turning his full attention squarely toward Seraphina.
"Now, as for you," Silas began, gesturing toward the heavy gold-embossed leather folder resting under her arm. "If you want to get married... with a formal marriage contract, why not?"
Harper’s head snapped toward Silas so fast her neck audibly popped.
"WAIT! WHAT?! Silas, are you out of your goddamn mind?!"

Silas didn’t even look at Harper. He simply shot her a cold, sideways glare... a single chilling look that carried so much silent authority that the energetic Lightning Lord choked on her words and instantly snapped her mouth shut.
Silas turned back to the crimson-haired noblewoman with his expression turning very calm... almost too calm.

"Why don’t we wait a while, Seraphina?" Silas asked smoothly. "Marriage isn’t a business transaction you finalize over the counter at a guild exchange. Marriage is for an entire lifetime. Do you really want to legally bind yourself, your family’s ancient lineage, and your entire future to someone you barely even know?"
Seraphina blinked, her crimson eyes widening slightly as she processed his question.
She raised her chin, falling back on her elite noble upbringing.

"I don’t need to ’wait,’" Seraphina argued, her voice regaining a fraction of its haughty confidence. "I am an elite Lord of House Bloom... I have access to the city’s highest-tier surveillance archives, background investigators, and magical lineage registries. If there is something I need to know about your habits, your history, or your character, I can simply commission a research dossier and memorize it by tomorrow morning."
Silas let out a dry, amused chuckle, crossing his arms over his bare chest.
"A research dossier?" Silas asked, raising an eyebrow. "Alright. Let’s test that theory right now. What’s my favorite food?"
Seraphina opened her mouth to answer immediately and then instantly stopped.
Her lips remained parted as her mind frantically flipped through her mental archives.
She had memorized his birth date from the academy records, his official Blue Core awakening registry, his test scores from Valoria Academy, and his former residential address in the Sector 4 slums.

’What does a commoner eat?!’ Seraphina thought in a sudden rising wave of panic, her eyes darting frantically across the pavement. ’He lived in the lower wards for a decade on a scrap-hauler’s wage! What do slum-born peasants consider a luxury?! Nutrient paste? Boiled cabbage? No, wait... they eat cheap carbohydrates!’
Her crimson eyes lit up with triumphant certainty.
"Bread!" Seraphina declared proudly, puffing out her chest. "Fresh, unrefined wheat bread!"
Silas stared at her for three uninterrupted seconds of soul-crushing silence.

He slowly waved his hand through the air with his face turning blank. "It is not bread. I literally survived on cheap, tasteless bread for ten years, Seraphina. I despise bread. If I never see a loaf of dry bread again for the rest of my life, it will be too soon..."
Seraphina’s triumphant smile instantly vanished.
Her cheeks turned a violently bright shade of red, her mouth snapping shut as she looked down at her stilettos in shame.

"See?" Silas pointed out calmly, letting his words sink in. "You have access to all the government databases in the world, and you don’t even know what I like to put on my plate. This is exactly why actual couples take time to get to know each other. They go on dates. They talk. They learn what makes the other person tick, what annoys them, what their goals are, and whether they can actually stand being in the same room for more than five minutes without trying to murder each other..."
’And more importantly,’ Silas thought to himself with a small smirk hiding beneath his neutral expression, ’there is not a single timeline in the multiverse where I actually want to marry you.’
It wasn’t that Seraphina was ugly or inherently evil.
Objectively speaking, she was breathtaking... gorgeous crimson hair, an incredible figure, high-tier combat skills, and massive political influence.
But Silas was a realist.
In this world, a commoner marrying into a high-ranking noble clan wasn’t a romantic fairytale... it was an undisputed recipe for disaster.
The Bloom family was an ancient powerhouse packed with arrogant aristocrats, cutthroat politicians, and a matriarch who was actively plotting to decapitate anyone who touched her daughter.
If Silas signed that marriage accord, he would be subjected to endless clan audits, political maneuvering, and high-society subservience.
He would be expected to hand over his autonomy, bow to clan elders, and play the role of a trophy consort.
’I don’t want that...’

Reginald narrowed his eyes, tracking Silas’s every microscopic movement.

A commoner faced with two high-tier awakened women threatening to tear the neighborhood apart would either cower behind the gate, beg for mercy, or flee inside.

Silas stood in the eye of the brewing storm however he didn’t tremble.

The asphalt will melt, the property value of the Silverleaf complex will plummet, and the agency will literally hunt me down with a frying pan to make me pay for the landscaping.’
Silas did not have the patience for a middle-school catfight on his front lawn so he stepped forward.

His boots made no sound against the pavement as he seamlessly closed the distance, effortlessly stepping directly into the convergence zone between the raging red flames and the crackling purple plasma.
Before either woman could react, Silas shot both of his hands out.
His large calloused right hand clamped firmly around Seraphina’s burning wrist, while his left hand clamped around Harper’s electrified forearm.
FZZZZT!
The power of his Mythic Gold Core foundation acted like an elemental sponge.
The moment his bare skin made contact with their mana, his internal golden pathways flared to life beneath his flesh.

The blazing red fire licking Seraphina’s knuckles sputtered, choked, and extinguished as if smothered by an ocean, while Harper’s violently arcing purple lightning dissipated harmlessly into his palm with a soft, pathetic pop.
Both women gasped, freezing instantly.
"Silas!" Harper squeaked, frantically pulling her mana back into her sternum so she wouldn’t accidentally fry his nervous system.
"Let go, you idiot!
You’ll burn your skin off!" Seraphina cried out in genuine panic, desperately extinguishing the last embers around her fingertips to keep from injuring him.
Silas didn’t let go.
He held both of their wrists with an unyielding vice-like grip for two long seconds, ensuring the magical radiation had entirely cleared the air, before slowly releasing them and taking a step back.
He raised his right hand, aggressively rubbing the back of his neck as he glared at them with half-lidded irritated golden-ringed eyes.

chapters.title: Chapter 381: An Agreement [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: He was perfectly happy living his current life, and tying himself to the Bloom Clan was nothing more than an open invitation to get walked over by arrogant aristocrats.
But at the same time, he couldn’t simply tell the daughter of House Bloom to go screw herself.
Blatantly rejecting her on the street would wound her pride, trigger an immediate clan blood feud, and paint a massive target on his little sister’s back...
’I really despise dealing with nobles,’ Silas concluded mentally, letting out another silent groan.
Beside him, Harper was watching the exchange with wide, glittering violet eyes.
She was genuinely surprised.
She knew Silas was sharp, but watching him effortlessly dismantle Seraphina’s aggressive marriage proposal using pure undeniable logic was nothing short of a masterclass.

’That’s why I asked for a date,’ Harper thought happily, a warm competitive flutter rising in her chest. ’I don’t want a contract... I want him. I already spent three hours last night planning out the ultimate itinerary!’
Seraphina stood in the quiet sunlight for nearly a minute, her sharp mind processing Silas’s words.
Slowly, reluctantly, she nodded her head.
"You’re... you’re right," Seraphina admitted softly, her voice barely a whisper before she forced herself to look back up into his eyes.
Her pride fought violently against the concession, but the logic was unbreakable.
"I know next to nothing about your personal preferences, your habits, or your daily life. Therefore, I will not force the formal registration of the marriage contract today."
She stepped forward, closing the distance between them once more.

"However," Seraphina stated, her tone shifting back into a fierce one. "that does not change our reality... You have seen my unblemished form, Silas Graves. Under the sacred traditions of House Bloom, you are already my designated property. You belong to me."
Before Silas could pull away, Seraphina reached out with her manicured hand.
She grabbed his large calloused palm and held it tightly between both of her own, interlacing her slender fingers through his.
A radiant beautiful rosy blush bloomed across her pale cheeks, highlighting the fierce burning intensity in her crimson irises.

"I will learn everything there is to learn about you," Seraphina declared, her voice trembling slightly with genuine emotion. "I will learn your favorite foods, your combat styles, your ambitions, and your flaws. And once I know everything... I will marry you."
She paused, her fierce expression suddenly cracking into a look of childlike confusion.
She blinked her long eyelashes, tilting her head slightly as she looked between Silas and Harper.
"How... how exactly do people learn about each other anyway?" Seraphina asked, sounding completely lost.
Harper let out an exasperated, disbelieving laugh. "Dates, you sheltered noble princess! You go on dates!"
Seraphina’s brow furrowed, but she didn’t release Silas’s hand immediately.
She slowly let go of his palm, turned on her heel, and marched back over to the limousine.
She shoved the heavy leather folder containing the multi-million-credit marriage accord directly into Reginald’s chest.
"Hold these, Reginald," Seraphina ordered briskly.
Reginald caught the binder with practiced ease, but internally, his entire worldview had just been violently upended.

’He... he turned down the marriage contract?’ Reginald thought in flabbergasted shock. ’A commoner from Sector 4 was just handed the golden key to the apex of high society... an alliance that would grant him billions of credits, unlimited territorial resources, and political immunity and he pushed it aside because he wanted to "get to know her first"?!’

In Reginald’s forty-five years of service, every single man who had ever approached Lady Seraphina... including foreign dignitaries, corporate heirs, and even the Crown Prince of the World Alliance had scrambled desperately to secure her hand, completely unconcerned with trivial concepts like "getting to know each other."
They wanted the power of House Bloom.
Yet this young man, standing barefoot on the sidewalk in nothing but sweatpants and a trench coat, had casually brushed the most coveted maiden in the country aside, demanding basic mutual respect.
Reginald adjusted his glasses, staring at Silas’s relaxed broad-shouldered silhouette.

’Lady Seraphina is an untamable dragon that no patriarch in the city has ever managed to rein in,’ Reginald realized, a deep sense of genuine respect settling into his chest. ’And this boy just disciplined her in three sentences... I must reassess everything. Lady Etilga’s assassination directive is officially suspended.’
Seraphina turned back around, crossing her arms as she looked at the two of them with a deeply skeptical expression.
"What in the world is a ’date’?" Seraphina asked genuinely.
Silas and Harper both stared at the crimson-haired noblewoman as if she had just grown a second head.

"Are you serious right now?" Harper asked, throwing her hands in the air. "What kind of dystopian sheltered bubble did your parents raise you in?! What have you been learning at home for the past eighteen years?!"

"I was educated in high-tier arithmetic, ancestral elemental theory, multi-dimensional logistics, and aristocratic etiquette!" Seraphina defended herself fiercely with her cheeks burning. "My curriculum did not include commoner mating rituals!"
Harper rolled her eyes so hard it looked painful.

"A date is when two people who are interested in each other go out into the city, do fun activities together, eat good food, talk without stabbing each other, and see if they have romantic chemistry... And for your information, Princess, Silas and I already have a full, private date scheduled for today! So you can take your limousine and go back to your palace!"
Seraphina’s eyes narrowed into lethal slits.
"Cancel it."
"Excuse me?!" Harper barked.

"I said cancel it," Seraphina commanded with noble authority. "If a ’date’ is the required prerequisite to acquiring comprehensive information on Silas Graves, then I will be the one accompanying him today. You may leave."

"Fuck off, bitch!" Harper snarled, taking an aggressive step forward, her purple lightning sparking around her ears once more. "I asked him first! I drove all the way here! I planned the entire itinerary! You don’t get to hijack my afternoon just because you showed up with a notarized piece of paper!"

"I am the heiress of House Bloom!" Seraphina shouted back, stepping right into Harper’s face with her crimson aura flaring. "My time is exponentially more valuable than yours! If a date is to occur, it will be with me!"
"I don’t give a damn about your dusty family tree—"
BUZZZZZZZ-CLICK!
The sharp hum of the wrought-iron security gate unlocking cut straight through the escalating shouting match.
The heavy black gate smoothly swung inward.
Stepping out onto the threshold was Martha, the household maid.
The middle-aged woman was dressed in her neat, pressed outdoor coat, carrying an insulated shopping tote over her arm and holding the keys in her hand.
She took one step onto the concrete, stopped dead in her tracks, and blinked rapidly.
"Uhh... Master Silas?" Martha asked, her voice trembling slightly as she took in the absurd scene before her.

Standing on the sidewalk was her master, surrounded by a purple-haired woman and a crimson-haired noblewoman who looked like a supermodel, a luxury limousine, and an elderly butler in a tailored tuxedo who looked like he had seen a ghost.
Silas, Seraphina, Harper, and Reginald all instantly snapped their heads toward the housekeeper.
The moment Martha felt the collective gaze of two terrifyingly powerful, high-tier Lords locking onto her, the older woman’s motherly instincts short-circuited.
She immediately dipped into a deep, incredibly swift and respectful bow, practically trembling as she scurried across the pavement straight to Silas’s side.

"Master Silas!" Martha whispered frantically, keeping her head lowered. "I am so sorry to interrupt! I was just heading out to Valoria Academy to pick up little Lady Lia and her classmates. They finished their project, and I promised to walk them back safely for an early dinner."
Silas let out a relieved breath, nodding quickly.
"Right. Thank you, Martha. Go ahead and hurry up. Make sure they stay safe..."
"Of course, Master!" Martha replied as the gate shut behind her.
She turned to leave, took half a step toward the sidewalk, and then suddenly paused.
A look of frantic motherly realization flashed across her face.
"Uh... Master Silas," Martha murmured softly, stepping back into his personal space.
She reached into the deep pocket of her outdoor coat, pulled out a small, sleek foil-wrapped cardboard packet, and discreetly shoved it directly into Silas’s palm, wrapping his fingers around it.
Silas looked down at his hand in genuine confusion.
He opened his fingers, taking in the bold glowing branding stamped across the packaging.
[AURA-SHIELD: ULTRA-DENSE REINFORCED STAMINA PROPHYLACTICS - 12 PACK].
Silas froze. His brain completely flatlined for the third time today.
Standing two feet away, Reginald’s aristocratic composure completely shattered.
The elderly butler let out a choked, horrified cough, violently turning his head away and covering his mouth with a white handkerchief as his face twisted into a grimace of pure scandal.
Harper, who was standing right next to Silas, caught a crystal-clear look at the box.
A nuclear bright purple blush instantly exploded across Harper’s entire face, rushing all the way down to her collarbones.
She squeaked, clapping both of her hands over her mouth with her violet eyes bulging.

She only knew what that specific brand was because she had spent forty-five minutes secretly browsing the high-tier adult section of the pharmacy last night, frantically buying a packet of her own just in case her date with Silas went exceptionally well!
"Martha," Silas said, his voice dropping into a dangerously flat soul-dead monotone as he stared at the box. "What the hell is this?"

"I am just fulfilling my domestic duties, Master Silas!" Martha whispered loudly, completely ignoring the fact that everyone on the street could hear her. "You have been gone in the Sovereign Realm for far too long, and a Lord’s physical needs are very demanding! Master, remember what I told you in the kitchen~!"
Silas didn’t hesitate. He raised his index finger and forcefully flicked Martha right in the center of her forehead.
THWACK!
"Ow!" Martha yelped, clutching her forehead with both hands, though a massive mischievous grin spread across her face.
"Return this to the cabinet, stop reading degenerate internet forums, and go get my sister," Silas ordered ruthlessly, shoving the packet back into her shopping tote.
"Yes, Master! Have a wonderful vigorous afternoon!" Martha chirped happily.
She bowed once more, completely unbothered by the flick, and scurried down the sidewalk at top speed with her laughter echoing down the quiet street before she rounded the corner and vanished.
’She didn’t take the car?’
Silas stood in the awkward, suffocating silence left in her wake, pinching the bridge of his nose until his fingers went numb.
"Well..." Silas began, letting out a long breath.
Before he could even suggest going inside to put on a damn shirt, Seraphina stepped forward, her crimson eyes locked onto Harper with unyielding defiance.

"It is settled," Seraphina declared, crossing her arms. "I will be accompanying the two of you today. This will be a three-way date and naturally, given that Silas is the designated property of House Bloom, I will receive the vast majority of his attention throughout the afternoon... not the other girl."
"I am not ’the other girl,’ you arrogant noble jackass!" Harper roared back, pointing a furious finger at Seraphina’s nose. "I’m Harper! Get it right! And you’re not getting any of his attention!"
"You are an uninvited variable in an official matrimonial observation," Seraphina countered coldly, lifting her chin. "You should be grateful I am permitting your presence in our perimeter."
"I’M PERMITTING YOUR PRESENCE, YOU CRIMSON-HAIRED PARASITE!"
"ENOUGH!" Silas snapped, his voice ringing with enough force to rattle the gate.
Both women flinched, shutting their mouths simultaneously.
Silas looked between the furious sparking Lightning Lord and the haughty, blushing noble heiress.
He realized with terrifying clarity that if he left them alone on the street, they would literally level the block, and if he tried to go back inside, they would break the door down.

"Five minutes," Silas muttered, turning his back to them and walking toward the front door. "I am putting on a shirt. If you two are still screaming when I walk back out, I am going to lock the gates and spend the rest of the day sleeping."
Ten minutes later, Harper’s custom-built midnight-purple luxury sports coupe purred smoothly down the wide pristine avenues of the Central District.

The vehicle’s interior was a masterpiece of high-tier engineering... lined with dark supple leather, accented by ambient violet LED strips, and completely sealed against the exterior noise of the bustling metropolis.
Harper gripped the leather-wrapped steering wheel, her eyes locked on the road ahead.
’Fuck...’
Her jaw was set in a tight annoyed line as she glanced into the rearview mirror.
Sitting directly in the center of the plush leather back seat was Seraphina Bloom.

The crimson-haired noble sat with her spine perfectly straight with her legs crossed at the ankles and her designer blazer immaculately adjusted as she stared out the tinted window with an expression of pure detached superiority.
’Why do I have to do all of this?’
