"You’re... you’re right," Seraphina admitted softly, her voice barely a whisper before she forced herself to look back up into his eyes.
Her pride fought violently against the concession, but the logic was unbreakable.
"I know next to nothing about your personal preferences, your habits, or your daily life.
Therefore, I will not force the formal registration of the marriage contract today."
She stepped forward, closing the distance between them once more.
"However," Seraphina stated, her tone shifting back into a fierce one.
"that does not change our reality...
You have seen my unblemished form, Silas Graves.
Under the sacred traditions of House Bloom, you are already my designated property.
You belong to me."
Before Silas could pull away, Seraphina reached out with her manicured hand.
She grabbed his large calloused palm and held it tightly between both of her own, interlacing her slender fingers through his.
A radiant beautiful rosy blush bloomed across her pale cheeks, highlighting the fierce burning intensity in her crimson irises.
"I will learn everything there is to learn about you," Seraphina declared, her voice trembling slightly with genuine emotion.
"I will learn your favorite foods, your combat styles, your ambitions, and your flaws.
And once I know everything...
I will marry you."
She paused, her fierce expression suddenly cracking into a look of childlike confusion.
She blinked her long eyelashes, tilting her head slightly as she looked between Silas and Harper.
"How... how exactly do people learn about each other anyway?" Seraphina asked, sounding completely lost.
Harper let out an exasperated, disbelieving laugh.
"Dates, you sheltered noble princess!
You go on dates!"
Seraphina’s brow furrowed, but she didn’t release Silas’s hand immediately.
She slowly let go of his palm, turned on her heel, and marched back over to the limousine.
She shoved the heavy leather folder containing the multi-million-credit marriage accord directly into Reginald’s chest.
"Hold these, Reginald," Seraphina ordered briskly.
Reginald caught the binder with practiced ease, but internally, his entire worldview had just been violently upended.

’He... he turned down the marriage contract?’ Reginald thought in flabbergasted shock. ’A commoner from Sector 4 was just handed the golden key to the apex of high society... an alliance that would grant him billions of credits, unlimited territorial resources, and political immunity and he pushed it aside because he wanted to "get to know her first"?!’

In Reginald’s forty-five years of service, every single man who had ever approached Lady Seraphina... including foreign dignitaries, corporate heirs, and even the Crown Prince of the World Alliance had scrambled desperately to secure her hand, completely unconcerned with trivial concepts like "getting to know each other."
They wanted the power of House Bloom.
Yet this young man, standing barefoot on the sidewalk in nothing but sweatpants and a trench coat, had casually brushed the most coveted maiden in the country aside, demanding basic mutual respect.
Reginald adjusted his glasses, staring at Silas’s relaxed broad-shouldered silhouette.

’Lady Seraphina is an untamable dragon that no patriarch in the city has ever managed to rein in,’ Reginald realized, a deep sense of genuine respect settling into his chest. ’And this boy just disciplined her in three sentences...
I must reassess everything.
Lady Etilga’s assassination directive is officially suspended.’
Seraphina turned back around, crossing her arms as she looked at the two of them with a deeply skeptical expression.
"What in the world is a ’date’?" Seraphina asked genuinely.
Silas and Harper both stared at the crimson-haired noblewoman as if she had just grown a second head.
"Are you serious right now?" Harper asked, throwing her hands in the air.
"What kind of dystopian sheltered bubble did your parents raise you in?!
What have you been learning at home for the past eighteen years?!"
"I was educated in high-tier arithmetic, ancestral elemental theory, multi-dimensional logistics, and aristocratic etiquette!" Seraphina defended herself fiercely with her cheeks burning.
"My curriculum did not include commoner mating rituals!"
Harper rolled her eyes so hard it looked painful.

"A date is when two people who are interested in each other go out into the city, do fun activities together, eat good food, talk without stabbing each other, and see if they have romantic chemistry...
And for your information, Princess, Silas and I already have a full, private date scheduled for today!
So you can take your limousine and go back to your palace!"
Seraphina’s eyes narrowed into lethal slits.
"Cancel it."
"Excuse me?!" Harper barked.
"I said cancel it," Seraphina commanded with noble authority.
"If a ’date’ is the required prerequisite to acquiring comprehensive information on Silas Graves, then I will be the one accompanying him today.
You may leave."
"Fuck off, bitch!" Harper snarled, taking an aggressive step forward, her purple lightning sparking around her ears once more.
"I asked him first!
I drove all the way here!
I planned the entire itinerary!
You don’t get to hijack my afternoon just because you showed up with a notarized piece of paper!"
"I am the heiress of House Bloom!" Seraphina shouted back, stepping right into Harper’s face with her crimson aura flaring.
"My time is exponentially more valuable than yours!
If a date is to occur, it will be with me!"
"I don’t give a damn about your dusty family tree—"
BUZZZZZZZ-CLICK!
The sharp hum of the wrought-iron security gate unlocking cut straight through the escalating shouting match.
The heavy black gate smoothly swung inward.
Stepping out onto the threshold was Martha, the household maid.
The middle-aged woman was dressed in her neat, pressed outdoor coat, carrying an insulated shopping tote over her arm and holding the keys in her hand.
She took one step onto the concrete, stopped dead in her tracks, and blinked rapidly.
"Uhh...
Master Silas?" Martha asked, her voice trembling slightly as she took in the absurd scene before her.

Standing on the sidewalk was her master, surrounded by a purple-haired woman and a crimson-haired noblewoman who looked like a supermodel, a luxury limousine, and an elderly butler in a tailored tuxedo who looked like he had seen a ghost.
Silas, Seraphina, Harper, and Reginald all instantly snapped their heads toward the housekeeper.
The moment Martha felt the collective gaze of two terrifyingly powerful, high-tier Lords locking onto her, the older woman’s motherly instincts short-circuited.
She immediately dipped into a deep, incredibly swift and respectful bow, practically trembling as she scurried across the pavement straight to Silas’s side.
"Master Silas!" Martha whispered frantically, keeping her head lowered.
"I am so sorry to interrupt!
I was just heading out to Valoria Academy to pick up little Lady Lia and her classmates.
They finished their project, and I promised to walk them back safely for an early dinner."
Silas let out a relieved breath, nodding quickly.
"Right.
Thank you, Martha.
Go ahead and hurry up.
Make sure they stay safe..."
"Of course, Master!" Martha replied as the gate shut behind her.
She turned to leave, took half a step toward the sidewalk, and then suddenly paused.
A look of frantic motherly realization flashed across her face.
Master Silas," Martha murmured softly, stepping back into his personal space.
She reached into the deep pocket of her outdoor coat, pulled out a small, sleek foil-wrapped cardboard packet, and discreetly shoved it directly into Silas’s palm, wrapping his fingers around it.
Silas looked down at his hand in genuine confusion.
He opened his fingers, taking in the bold glowing branding stamped across the packaging.
[AURA-SHIELD: ULTRA-DENSE REINFORCED STAMINA PROPHYLACTICS - 12 PACK].
Silas froze.
His brain completely flatlined for the third time today.
Standing two feet away, Reginald’s aristocratic composure completely shattered.
The elderly butler let out a choked, horrified cough, violently turning his head away and covering his mouth with a white handkerchief as his face twisted into a grimace of pure scandal.
Harper, who was standing right next to Silas, caught a crystal-clear look at the box.
A nuclear bright purple blush instantly exploded across Harper’s entire face, rushing all the way down to her collarbones.
She squeaked, clapping both of her hands over her mouth with her violet eyes bulging.

She only knew what that specific brand was because she had spent forty-five minutes secretly browsing the high-tier adult section of the pharmacy last night, frantically buying a packet of her own just in case her date with Silas went exceptionally well!
"Martha," Silas said, his voice dropping into a dangerously flat soul-dead monotone as he stared at the box.
"What the hell is this?"
"I am just fulfilling my domestic duties, Master Silas!" Martha whispered loudly, completely ignoring the fact that everyone on the street could hear her.
"You have been gone in the Sovereign Realm for far too long, and a Lord’s physical needs are very demanding!
Master, remember what I told you in the kitchen~!"
Silas didn’t hesitate.
He raised his index finger and forcefully flicked Martha right in the center of her forehead.
THWACK!
"Ow!" Martha yelped, clutching her forehead with both hands, though a massive mischievous grin spread across her face.
"Return this to the cabinet, stop reading degenerate internet forums, and go get my sister," Silas ordered ruthlessly, shoving the packet back into her shopping tote.
"Yes, Master!
Have a wonderful vigorous afternoon!" Martha chirped happily.
She bowed once more, completely unbothered by the flick, and scurried down the sidewalk at top speed with her laughter echoing down the quiet street before she rounded the corner and vanished.
’She didn’t take the car?’
Silas stood in the awkward, suffocating silence left in her wake, pinching the bridge of his nose until his fingers went numb.
"Well..." Silas began, letting out a long breath.
Before he could even suggest going inside to put on a damn shirt, Seraphina stepped forward, her crimson eyes locked onto Harper with unyielding defiance.
"It is settled," Seraphina declared, crossing her arms.
"I will be accompanying the two of you today.

This will be a three-way date and naturally, given that Silas is the designated property of House Bloom, I will receive the vast majority of his attention throughout the afternoon... not the other girl."
"I am not ’the other girl,’ you arrogant noble jackass!" Harper roared back, pointing a furious finger at Seraphina’s nose.
"I’m Harper!
Get it right!
And you’re not getting any of his attention!"
"You are an uninvited variable in an official matrimonial observation," Seraphina countered coldly, lifting her chin.
"You should be grateful I am permitting your presence in our perimeter."
"I’M PERMITTING YOUR PRESENCE, YOU CRIMSON-HAIRED PARASITE!"
"ENOUGH!" Silas snapped, his voice ringing with enough force to rattle the gate.
Both women flinched, shutting their mouths simultaneously.
Silas looked between the furious sparking Lightning Lord and the haughty, blushing noble heiress.
He realized with terrifying clarity that if he left them alone on the street, they would literally level the block, and if he tried to go back inside, they would break the door down.
"Five minutes," Silas muttered, turning his back to them and walking toward the front door.
"I am putting on a shirt.
If you two are still screaming when I walk back out, I am going to lock the gates and spend the rest of the day sleeping."
Ten minutes later, Harper’s custom-built midnight-purple luxury sports coupe purred smoothly down the wide pristine avenues of the Central District.

The vehicle’s interior was a masterpiece of high-tier engineering... lined with dark supple leather, accented by ambient violet LED strips, and completely sealed against the exterior noise of the bustling metropolis.
Harper gripped the leather-wrapped steering wheel, her eyes locked on the road ahead.
’Fuck...’
Her jaw was set in a tight annoyed line as she glanced into the rearview mirror.
Sitting directly in the center of the plush leather back seat was Seraphina Bloom.

The crimson-haired noble sat with her spine perfectly straight with her legs crossed at the ankles and her designer blazer immaculately adjusted as she stared out the tinted window with an expression of pure detached superiority.
’Why do I have to do all of this?’

chapters.title: Chapter 382: Grand Celestia Mall [Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Silas occupied the front passenger seat.
He had finally changed into clean comfortable clothes... a well-fitted dark charcoal Henley shirt that accentuated his wide shoulders, dark denim trousers, and clean boots.
He leaned back against the headrest, staring blankly through the windshield with his mind actively questioning every single life choice that had led him to this exact moment.
Harper cleared her throat, tapping her fingers against the steering wheel to break the thick awkward silence.
She glanced sideways at Silas, her tone softening into a warm curious lilt.
"So, Silas..." Harper asked, a small genuine smile touching her lips. "Have you ever actually been on a proper date before?"
Silas turned his head slightly, raising an eyebrow.

"A date? No. I spent the last few years hauling rusted scrap in Sector 4 just to afford some stuff. I didn’t exactly have the disposable income or the free time to take girls out to fancy restaurants."
Hearing his answer, Harper’s violet eyes lit up with uncontainable joy.

’He’s never been on a date!’ Harper celebrated internally with a massive grin spreading across her face. ’I’m his very first date! That means everything we do today will be his first romantic memory!’

"I’m really glad to hear that," Harper beamed aloud, her energy instantly rebounding to its usual hyperactive state. "Because I did a ton of research last night! I watched this amazing ten-part viral guide on LordTube created by the city’s top lifestyle influencers... It laid out the ultimate, step-by-step itinerary for a high-tier romantic outing!"
Seraphina let out a loud disdainful scoff from the back seat.
"LordTube influencers. How exquisitely common. You are basing an entire social engagement on the algorithmic drivel of unawakened content creators."

"Shut up, Seraphina! Nobody asked you!" Harper snapped through the rearview mirror, before turning right back to Silas with an eager grin. "Ignore her. The guide is foolproof! It optimizes dopamine release, builds emotional vulnerability, and creates lasting memories through shared luxury experiences!"
Silas narrowed his eyes, a sudden suspicious feeling prickling at the back of his neck.
"Harper," Silas interrupted with his voice turning cautious. "What exactly is the first event on this ’foolproof’ itinerary?"
Harper puffed out her chest proudly, taking a sharp turn onto the prestigious Grand Aurelius Boulevard.
"The first phase is mass luxury shopping at the Grand Celestia Mall!" Harper announced with absolute glee. "We are going to give you a complete top-to-bottom high-society makeover!"
Silas nearly choked on his own saliva. He coughed, turning his head violently toward her. "Mass shopping? At the Grand Celestia?!"

"Yep!" Harper chirped, completely oblivious to his mounting horror. "And don’t worry about crowds or paparazzi, Silas! I pulled some strings through my corporate accounts and rented out the entire top-tier VIP couture floor for the next three hours! It’s completely private! Just us, the stylists, and unlimited clothes!"
Silas slowly pressed his palms against his face, letting out a muffled agonized groan.

’What did I do in my past life to deserve this?’ Silas lamented in the dark confines of his own mind. ’I know I asked for a slice of life but still... this isn’t how I wanted it to go... Now I am being dragged into an empty shopping mall by two billionaire heiresses to play dress-up.’
Before he could formulate a polite retreat, the sports coupe smoothly glided into the private VIP entrance of the Grand Celestia Mall.
The Grand Celestia was not a standard commercial shopping center.
Located in the hyper-exclusive Platinum Ward of Valoria City, it was a colossal architectural marvel constructed from white marble, imported elven crystal, and reinforced adamantine glass.
It was a facility built exclusively for the planetary elite... high-ranking directors, multi-millionaire guild masters, and sovereign nobility.
Standard citizens from the lower sectors weren’t even permitted past the perimeter security barriers without a verified eight-figure bank ledger.
Silas stepped out of the vehicle with his boots hitting the polished marble floor of the private underground valet bay.
He paused, his golden-ringed eyes sweeping over the grand vaulted ceilings, the glowing runic chandeliers, and the fountains of magically purified glowing blue water cascading down the walls.

Having spent the vast majority of his second life living in the rusted, smog-choked tenements of Sector 4, where the only entertainment was watching stray hounds fight over alchemical scrap, the vulgar display of astronomical wealth was genuinely jarring.
Seraphina stepped out of the back seat, her crimson blazer falling flawlessly into place.
She noticed Silas’s lingering gaze on the grand architecture.
A subtle condescending smirk touched her lips as she walked up beside him.

"It is passable for a regional facility," Seraphina commented casually, glancing at the marble arches with mild boredom. "Though frankly, the craftsmanship is rather crude compared to the Grand Spire in Rhyx City. The runic conduits here lack proper harmonic insulation..."
"Nobody cares about your architecture critique, Princess," Harper muttered, tossing her vehicle keys to an immaculately dressed valet who caught them with a deep terrified bow.
Waiting near the private express lift was a small contingent of private facility staff.
A tall man in a tailored silver-trimmed suit stepped forward, bowing deeply from the waist.

"Lady Whitmore and... ah Lady Bloom," the manager greeted them with trembling reverence. "The top-floor Haute Couture Sanctuary has been entirely cleared according to your directives. All external access has been locked down. The master stylists are standing by."
"Lead the way," Harper commanded briskly.
The group stepped into the massive private glass elevator.
The lift ascended silently, shooting past eighty floors of luxury boutiques and glowing displays until it finally chimed to a halt at the absolute apex of the structure.
DING!
The heavy frosted glass doors slid open, revealing a sprawling open-concept paradise of high-end fashion.
The floor was paved with pristine white quartz tiles that reflected the warm golden light of hovering mana-orbs.

Massive racks of tailored combat robes, alchemical silk suits, enchanted evening wear, and high-tier leather gear stretched out across the room, separated by plush velvet seating areas and private dressing chambers.
Reginald stopped exactly one step past the elevator doors.
The elderly butler bowed stiffly, placing his hands neatly behind his back.
"I shall remain stationed at the perimeter entrance, Lady Seraphina," Reginald stated with quiet professionalism. "To ensure your privacy remains absolute."
"Very good, Reginald," Seraphina replied with a curt nod.
Silas, Harper, and Seraphina advanced into the grand showroom.

Immediately, the head stylist... an impeccably groomed man with platinum-blonde hair, wearing an avant-garde asymmetrical coat stepped forward, flanked by a disciplined line of six young maids dressed in matching pristine black-and-white uniforms.

"Welcome, esteemed guests, to the Sanctuary," the head stylist beamed, bowing low. "I am Master Jean. We have curated the finest grade-A enchanted textiles from across the continental guilds. Every piece here is woven with adaptive mythril threads, tier-4 beast silks, and localized thermal runes. We are at your service."
Before Jean could even finish his introduction, Harper lunged forward.
She grabbed Silas’s large calloused hand, boldly and unapologetically entwining her slender fingers through his.
She pulled him toward the central display, her cheeks glowing with a triumphant satisfied smile.
Seraphina watched their joined hands.
A sharp audible TCH echoed from her throat as she aggressively clicked her tongue, her crimson eyes narrowing into slits of pure jealousy.
"We are here to find some proper clothes for this handsome—" Harper began enthusiastically, gesturing toward Silas’s broad frame.
"Hold on," Silas interrupted smoothly.
He didn’t pull his hand away, but he gently halted their momentum.
A dangerous amused smirk slowly spread across his rugged face as he looked between the energetic purple-haired woman and the glaring crimson-haired noblewoman.
’You two dragged me into this nightmare to play games?’ Silas thought, his golden-ringed eyes flashing with sharp wit. ’Let’s see how you handle being on the defensive.’
Silas turned, looking directly into Harper’s violet eyes, and then shifted his gaze to meet Seraphina’s blazing crimson irises.

"I already have plenty of clothes," Silas said, his voice dropping into a low one that showed his seriousness. "And frankly, shopping for myself is boring. What I actually want... is to see the two of you dressed in the most beautiful, stunning outfits this place has to offer."
The entire showroom fell dead silent.
Harper froze.
The words hit the energetic Lightning Lord like a direct strike from her own plasma bolts.

Her breath hitched in her throat, her grip on his fingers loosening as a catastrophic wave of burning heat violently rushed up her neck, painting her entire face, ears, and chest in a brilliant incandescent crimson blush.
"Y-You... what?!" Harper squeaked, her voice cracking as she instinctively let go of his hand, stumbling backward half a step like a flustered schoolgirl.
Beside her, Seraphina’s haughty noble facade completely disintegrated into ash.
The crimson-haired heiress gasped softly, her eyes widening into massive saucers.
Her hands flew up to her chest, clutching her blazer as steam practically whistled from the tips of her pointed ears.
The overwhelming flattery of having the man she desired look at her with such intense interest completely short-circuited her high-society training.
Master Jean, sensing the sudden chaotic shift in romantic atmospheric pressure, clapped his hands together with professional glee.
"A magnificent directive, my Lord!" Jean praised enthusiastically.

He immediately gestured to one of the senior maids standing beside him. "Lydia! Escort Miss Whitmore to the Royal Suite! Pull the celestial-weave evening silks and the enchanted battle-corsets immediately!"
"Right away, Master Jean!" the senior maid chimed, stepping forward and politely gesturing for Harper to follow.

"I—I’ll be right back!" Harper stammered, entirely unable to look Silas in the eye as she frantically allowed the maid to pull her away toward the eastern dressing chambers with her heart hammering wildly against her ribs.
Master Jean turned his attention toward Seraphina, his keen eyes scanning his remaining staff.

He gestured toward a young maid standing near the back of the line... a quiet, deeply timid girl with dark braided hair and oversized round glasses, who was currently trembling slightly under the oppressive noble aura radiating from the Bloom heiress.
"And for Lady Seraphina," Jean suggested smoothly, "our junior stylist, Emily, will assist you in the High Sovereign Pavilion. She specializes in ancestral noble cuts."
Seraphina didn’t wait for the maid to approach.
The crimson-haired noblewoman turned on her expensive heels, marching directly up to the trembling junior maid with terrifying purpose.
The poor maid, terrified of offending the high-ranking noble, immediately lowered her head, stubbornly refusing to meet Seraphina’s piercing crimson gaze as she stared at the floor.
Seraphina didn’t say a polite greeting.
She reached out with her manicured hand and aggressively grabbed the fabric of the maid’s sleeve, pulling the trembling girl closer until they were barely inches apart.
Seraphina’s crimson eyes burned with a terrifying inferno of pure competitive desperation.

"Listen to me very carefully," Seraphina demanded with her voice becoming a low focused hiss that shook with determination. "You are going to use every single piece of high-tier silk, every magical accessory, and every styling technique you know. You are going to make me look like the most breathtaking, undeniably gorgeous woman on this entire planet. Do you understand me?!"
The timid maid flinched, but as she looked up, the blazing unyielding fire in Seraphina’s crimson eyes violently reflected in her own wide lenses.
The timid facade of the junior stylist instantly shattered.
In its place, a sudden explosive surge of pride and artistic adrenaline flooded the maid’s veins.
She was an artisan of high fashion, and she had just been handed a living goddess who wanted to go to war!
"Leave it to me, Lady Seraphina!" the maid declared, her voice suddenly ringing with fierce, unshakable confidence.
The maid grabbed Seraphina’s hand in return, aggressively spinning around and literally pulling the stunned Bloom heiress toward the western dressing chambers at top speed.
"I swear on my license! I will make you so beautiful that his heart will stop the second you walk out!"
The VIP Haute Couture Sanctuary was dead silent, save for the soft, ambient chime of floating mana-orbs and the rhythmic scratching of a fountain pen against thick parchment-grade vellum.
Stationed immaculately beside the frosted glass elevator doors, Reginald stood with his spine ruler-straight.
He held a small, leather-bound journal embossed with the silver serpent crest of House Bloom in his left palm, his gloved right hand guiding the gold-nibbed pen with surgical precision.
The elderly butler adjusted his spectacles, his sharp weathered eyes flicking across the expansive showroom to track Silas Graves.
My Observations:

- Physical Assessment: He has an imposing frame and remarkably powerful biological foundation. His mana pathways remain stable under high-stress atmospheric pressure and he displays psychological immunity to noble intimidation.

- Interaction with Lady Seraphina: A calm measured tone with no visible submission to her rank. He deflected her marriage proposal without escalating to outright rejection and maintained eye contact throughout.
- Interaction with Miss Whitmore: This one is casual and familiar, he tolerates her physical advances without reciprocating and displays dominance in their dynamic.
- Combat Potential: Requires further assessment...
- Threat Level: Elevated. Caution advised... Lady Etilga’s assassination directive officially suspended pending further observation.
The elderly butler adjusted his spectacles, his weathered eyes flicking across the expansive showroom.
Silas had just effortlessly deflected the two powerful noblewomen, and now stood alone in the center of the showroom like a predator surveying his territory.
Reginald made a final note in his journal.
- Verdict: Do not engage.

"To ensure your privacy remains absolute."
"Very good, Reginald," Seraphina replied with a curt nod.
Silas, Harper, and Seraphina advanced into the grand showroom.

Immediately, the head stylist... an impeccably groomed man with platinum-blonde hair, wearing an avant-garde asymmetrical coat stepped forward, flanked by a disciplined line of six young maids dressed in matching pristine black-and-white uniforms.
"Welcome, esteemed guests, to the Sanctuary," the head stylist beamed, bowing low.
"I am Master Jean.
We have curated the finest grade-A enchanted textiles from across the continental guilds.
Every piece here is woven with adaptive mythril threads, tier-4 beast silks, and localized thermal runes.
We are at your service."
Before Jean could even finish his introduction, Harper lunged forward.
She grabbed Silas’s large calloused hand, boldly and unapologetically entwining her slender fingers through his.
She pulled him toward the central display, her cheeks glowing with a triumphant satisfied smile.
Seraphina watched their joined hands.
A sharp audible TCH echoed from her throat as she aggressively clicked her tongue, her crimson eyes narrowing into slits of pure jealousy.
"We are here to find some proper clothes for this handsome—" Harper began enthusiastically, gesturing toward Silas’s broad frame.
"Hold on," Silas interrupted smoothly.
He didn’t pull his hand away, but he gently halted their momentum.
A dangerous amused smirk slowly spread across his rugged face as he looked between the energetic purple-haired woman and the glaring crimson-haired noblewoman.
’You two dragged me into this nightmare to play games?’ Silas thought, his golden-ringed eyes flashing with sharp wit. ’Let’s see how you handle being on the defensive.’
Silas turned, looking directly into Harper’s violet eyes, and then shifted his gaze to meet Seraphina’s blazing crimson irises.
"I already have plenty of clothes," Silas said, his voice dropping into a low one that showed his seriousness.
"And frankly, shopping for myself is boring.
What I actually want... is to see the two of you dressed in the most beautiful, stunning outfits this place has to offer."
The entire showroom fell dead silent.
Harper froze.
The words hit the energetic Lightning Lord like a direct strike from her own plasma bolts.

Her breath hitched in her throat, her grip on his fingers loosening as a catastrophic wave of burning heat violently rushed up her neck, painting her entire face, ears, and chest in a brilliant incandescent crimson blush.
"Y-You... what?!" Harper squeaked, her voice cracking as she instinctively let go of his hand, stumbling backward half a step like a flustered schoolgirl.
Beside her, Seraphina’s haughty noble facade completely disintegrated into ash.
The crimson-haired heiress gasped softly, her eyes widening into massive saucers.
Her hands flew up to her chest, clutching her blazer as steam practically whistled from the tips of her pointed ears.
The overwhelming flattery of having the man she desired look at her with such intense interest completely short-circuited her high-society training.
Master Jean, sensing the sudden chaotic shift in romantic atmospheric pressure, clapped his hands together with professional glee.
"A magnificent directive, my Lord!" Jean praised enthusiastically.
He immediately gestured to one of the senior maids standing beside him.
"Lydia!
Escort Miss Whitmore to the Royal Suite!
Pull the celestial-weave evening silks and the enchanted battle-corsets immediately!"
"Right away, Master Jean!" the senior maid chimed, stepping forward and politely gesturing for Harper to follow.

"I—I’ll be right back!" Harper stammered, entirely unable to look Silas in the eye as she frantically allowed the maid to pull her away toward the eastern dressing chambers with her heart hammering wildly against her ribs.
Master Jean turned his attention toward Seraphina, his keen eyes scanning his remaining staff.

He gestured toward a young maid standing near the back of the line... a quiet, deeply timid girl with dark braided hair and oversized round glasses, who was currently trembling slightly under the oppressive noble aura radiating from the Bloom heiress.
"And for Lady Seraphina," Jean suggested smoothly, "our junior stylist, Emily, will assist you in the High Sovereign Pavilion.
She specializes in ancestral noble cuts."
Seraphina didn’t wait for the maid to approach.
The crimson-haired noblewoman turned on her expensive heels, marching directly up to the trembling junior maid with terrifying purpose.
The poor maid, terrified of offending the high-ranking noble, immediately lowered her head, stubbornly refusing to meet Seraphina’s piercing crimson gaze as she stared at the floor.
Seraphina didn’t say a polite greeting.
She reached out with her manicured hand and aggressively grabbed the fabric of the maid’s sleeve, pulling the trembling girl closer until they were barely inches apart.
Seraphina’s crimson eyes burned with a terrifying inferno of pure competitive desperation.
"Listen to me very carefully," Seraphina demanded with her voice becoming a low focused hiss that shook with determination.
"You are going to use every single piece of high-tier silk, every magical accessory, and every styling technique you know.
You are going to make me look like the most breathtaking, undeniably gorgeous woman on this entire planet.
Do you understand me?!"
The timid maid flinched, but as she looked up, the blazing unyielding fire in Seraphina’s crimson eyes violently reflected in her own wide lenses.
The timid facade of the junior stylist instantly shattered.
In its place, a sudden explosive surge of pride and artistic adrenaline flooded the maid’s veins.
She was an artisan of high fashion, and she had just been handed a living goddess who wanted to go to war!
"Leave it to me, Lady Seraphina!" the maid declared, her voice suddenly ringing with fierce, unshakable confidence.
The maid grabbed Seraphina’s hand in return, aggressively spinning around and literally pulling the stunned Bloom heiress toward the western dressing chambers at top speed.
"I swear on my license!
I will make you so beautiful that his heart will stop the second you walk out!"
The VIP Haute Couture Sanctuary was dead silent, save for the soft, ambient chime of floating mana-orbs and the rhythmic scratching of a fountain pen against thick parchment-grade vellum.
Stationed immaculately beside the frosted glass elevator doors, Reginald stood with his spine ruler-straight.
He held a small, leather-bound journal embossed with the silver serpent crest of House Bloom in his left palm, his gloved right hand guiding the gold-nibbed pen with surgical precision.
The elderly butler adjusted his spectacles, his sharp weathered eyes flicking across the expansive showroom to track Silas Graves.
My Observations:
- Physical Assessment: He has an imposing frame and remarkably powerful biological foundation.
His mana pathways remain stable under high-stress atmospheric pressure and he displays psychological immunity to noble intimidation.
- Interaction with Lady Seraphina: A calm measured tone with no visible submission to her rank.
He deflected her marriage proposal without escalating to outright rejection and maintained eye contact throughout.
- Interaction with Miss Whitmore: This one is casual and familiar, he tolerates her physical advances without reciprocating and displays dominance in their dynamic.
- Combat Potential: Requires further assessment...
- Threat Level: Elevated.
Caution advised...
Lady Etilga’s assassination directive officially suspended pending further observation.
The elderly butler adjusted his spectacles, his weathered eyes flicking across the expansive showroom.
Silas had just effortlessly deflected the two powerful noblewomen, and now stood alone in the center of the showroom like a predator surveying his territory.
Reginald made a final note in his journal.
- Verdict: Do not engage.

chapters.title: Chapter 383: The Hardest Choices...
paragraphs: Reginald paused with his pen hovering a millimeter above the paper as his mind involuntarily flashed back to the incident on the street twenty minutes ago... specifically, the moment Silas’s maid had shoved an entire twelve-pack of reinforced stamina prophylactics directly into the young man’s palm.
A microscopic bead of sweat formed beneath Reginald’s starched white collar.
Normally, an exhaustive surveillance report for Lady Etilga Bloom required every single microscopic detail to be documented without a filter.
But Lady Etilga was a matriarch who viewed male virility through a terrifyingly strict eugenics lens.
In her eyes, seed was an ancestral resource meant strictly for the continuation of noble bloodlines... squandering it via artificial latex was a degenerate sin worthy of public execution.

’Subject promptly ordered the immediate return and disposal of unauthorized domestic contraband...’ Reginald carefully noted, deliberately omitting the exact nature of the foil-wrapped box. ’Displays admirable discipline and restraint and does not succumb to base hedonistic impulses.’
Satisfied with the edit, Reginald closed the journal with a soft, muted snap and tucked it into the breast pocket of his tailored coat.
His gaze lingered on the dark-haired young man currently browsing the central displays.
’Lady Seraphina could have chosen a far worse consort...’ Reginald reflected quietly. ’The boy possesses steel.’
Out on the open showroom floor, Silas strolled slowly between the polished quartz pedestals, completely oblivious to the fact that an elite noble assassin had just given him a passing grade.
The room smelled faintly of lavender and perfumes.
Arranged across floating glass displays were rows of hyper-exclusive men’s combat jackets, enchanted silk dress shirts, and tailored trousers woven from exotic beast hides.
Silas stopped in front of a mannequin sporting a sharp midnight-black button-down shirt.
The fabric was breathtakingly smooth, subtly shifting its hue under the mana-lights like the scales of an abyssal serpent, with fine platinum thread lining the collar and cuffs.
"Not bad," Silas muttered, reaching out and brushing the fabric between his thumb and forefinger.
The texture was light as a feather yet carried the distinct mana-conductivity of high-tier defensive gear. "Clean cut and breathable, it wouldn’t look ridiculous under a leather duster either."
He casually flipped the small, crystal-embossed tag dangling from the left cuff to check the price.
’185,000 Spirit Credits.’
Silas’s hand instantly froze.
His eye twitched violently.
’One hundred and eighty-five thousand credits?’ Silas’s internal voice screamed in pure agony. ’For a single shirt?!’
He could buy an entire crate of tempered iron broadswords for that.
He could purchase thirty barrels of military-grade pitch, fifty days of grain rations too... He had the money but for a single shirt?
To drop nearly two hundred thousand credits on a piece of cloth you wore to dinner was nothing short of criminal insanity.
He quickly released the cuff as if the silk had suddenly caught fire, taking a half-step back and clearing his throat.
He glanced around at the other mannequins, checking tags at a distance.
[- Enchanted Trench Coat: 450,000 SC]
[- Drake-Leather Boots: 120,000 SC]
[- Mythril-Woven Tie Clip: 45,000 SC]
Silas cringed, violently rubbing his temples.
"Rich people are completely detached from reality," he whispered under his breath. "If I drop a million credits here just to replace a hoodie, I’m going to have a stroke."

Deciding his bank account couldn’t survive browsing the menswear any longer, Silas turned his attention toward the far end of the sanctuary, where two massive soundproofed changing pavilions stood draped in heavy velvet curtains.
The left curtain was a vibrant shimmering royal purple, pulsing faintly with the static electrical wards Harper’s aura tended to leave behind.
The right curtain was a deep velvet crimson, radiating the suffocating, dry heat of House Bloom’s ancestral flame.
Silas let out a slow, resigned sigh, walking over to a plush white leather sofa positioned directly between the two dressing suites.
He sat down, leaning his elbows on his knees and clasping his hands together.

’I need to be extremely careful with how I handle this,’ Silas strategized, his sharp mind treating the upcoming fashion show like a high-stakes diplomatic summit. ’Harper is competitive and easily ignited. If I favor Seraphina too heavily, Harper will probably electrify the sofa but Seraphina is a proud, unhinged noble heiress. If I don’t give her validation, she’ll view it as an insult to House Bloom and try to force that marriage contract down my throat again.’
He cracked his knuckles, locking his face into an expression of deadpan, objective neutrality.
’Honest balanced ratings,’ Silas resolved firmly. ’Critique the fit, praise the craftsmanship, and keep both of them from burning the mall to the ground.’
Inside the Royal Suite, the heavy purple velvet curtains shut out the rest of the world, creating a private brightly lit sanctuary of mirrors and velvet cushions.
Harper stood in the center of the plush carpet, wearing only her delicate, lace-trimmed sports undergarments as she stretched her arms over her head.
Her athletic flawlessly toned physique gleamed under the magical lighting... every muscle along her abdomen and thighs tightly coiled with the explosive power of a Purple core Lightning Lord.
Standing behind her was Lydia, the senior maid assigned by Master Jean.
The woman moved with practiced efficiency, holding an open velvet garment bag containing an exquisite two-piece ensemble.
"Lift your arms slightly, Lady Whitmore," Lydia instructed smoothly, draping a sleeveless, form-fitting crop-top corset forged from iridescent violet dragon-silk over Harper’s shoulders.
The fabric immediately hugged Harper’s torso like a second skin, accentuating her narrow waist and dramatically pushing up her generous bust line.
Intricate silver-threaded lightning glyphs were embroidered along the neckline, shimmering with a soft pulsing luminescence whenever Harper breathed.
Harper stepped in front of the full-length triple mirror, resting her hands on her hips and tilting her head.
She examined her reflection, her purple hair falling in messy energetic waves over her bare shoulders.
She reached up, adjusting the cut of the corset slightly, and then paused as a sudden competitive thought crossed her mind.
Harper turned her head toward the senior maid, her violet eyes narrowing with dead-serious curiosity.
"Hey, Lydia," Harper asked, gesturing directly toward her own chest in the glass. "Be completely honest with me. Are my breasts big?"
Lydia didn’t even blink.
Having dressed Lords and aristocrats for over a decade, she possessed the unflappable composure of a seasoned diplomat.
The maid stepped forward, expertly tightening the mythril-laced corset strings behind Harper’s back with a sharp professional tug.

"Lady Whitmore," Lydia stated with unwavering sincerity, "your proportions are nothing short of exceptional. The muscle-to-fat distribution across your thoracic frame provides an optimal elevated silhouette. They are generously sized, impeccably firm, and perfect."
Hearing the glowing assessment, Harper threw her head back and let out a loud, triumphant bark of laughter that bounced off the mirrors.
"AHA! I KNEW IT!" Harper cheered victoriously, flexing in front of the glass. "Take that, you flat-chested noble princess! Let’s see your fancy ancestral lineage compete with raw genetics!"
Lydia offered a polite amused smile as she knelt down to slip on the matching high-waisted split-leg silk battle skirt.
"If I may say so, Lady Whitmore, your companion will find it exceedingly difficult to maintain his composure."
"That’s the exact goal, Lydia!" Harper grinned, her violet eyes flashing with crackling static. "Make the slit in this skirt two inches higher! We’re going for a total knockout!"
Meanwhile, on the opposite side of the showroom, the Sovereign Pavilion was practically vibrating with a different kind of energy.
Inside the spacious, rose-gold dressing room, Seraphina stood atop a raised circular pedestal, her arms held out horizontally at her sides.

Emily, the timid junior maid with the oversized round glasses, was currently down on her knees, her hands blurring in a whirlwind of motion as she pinned, adjusted, and smoothed the hem of a breathtaking floor-length crimson evening gown.
The dress was a triumph of high-society haute couture.
Crafted from pure phoenix-feather silk, the rich red fabric cascaded down Seraphina’s hour-glass curves like flowing liquid rubies.

The back was cut daringly low, plunging all the way to the base of her spine to reveal her unblemished alabaster skin, while the front featured a structured sweetheart neckline that accentuated her elegant collarbones and voluptuous bust.
Intricate golden filigree snaked up the bodice, mimicking the ancestral crest of House Bloom.
Seraphina looked down at the junior stylist working frantically around her ankles.

The maid wasn’t just adjusting the fabric... she was actively channeling trace amounts of mana through an artifact to heat the hems, ensuring the silk draped over Seraphina’s hips with microscopic perfection.
Every touch was delicate, precise, and completely dedicated to maximizing her beauty.
Seraphina tilted her head with a rare expression of genuine noble satisfaction softening her sharp noble features.
"You have remarkable hands, girl," Seraphina noted smoothly, admiring the way the light caught the golden trim in the mirror.
She glanced down at the stylist. "Tell me... does your master compensate you adequately for this level of craftsmanship?"
Emily froze mid-pin. Her round glasses slid slightly down her nose, and her cheeks instantly flushed with nervous panic.

"I—uh... Lady Seraphina," Emily stammered, frantically pushing her glasses back up with a trembling wrist. "The... the Grand Celestia provides a standard stipend, my Lady! It is... it is sufficient, but... with the high cost of living in the city and dealing with bills, it is... not that much, honestly..."
Seraphina let out a soft elegant hum, turning her crimson eyes toward the mirror.

"Listen to me, Emily," Seraphina stated, her voice carrying the authority of an elite heiress. "When I walk out through those curtains, I am going to utterly annihilate the purple-haired woman sitting outside. If my appearance forces Silas to acknowledge my supreme superiority, I will not simply tip you a handful of credits."
Seraphina looked down, her crimson irises locking onto the maid’s trembling gaze.

"I will officially buy out your commercial contract from Master Jean. I will double your annual salary, grant you full diplomatic immunity under House Bloom’s charter, and appoint you as my personal, exclusive stylist. You will never have to scrape for rent in this city again..."
Emily stared up at the noblewoman, her breath catching entirely in her throat.
Her heart hammered against her ribs like a trapped bird.
’Double my salary?! Full diplomatic immunity under House Bloom?!’
The magnitude of the promise shattered the last remnants of the maid’s timid insecurity.
A terrifying burning flame of pure ambition ignited behind Emily’s round lenses.
She stood up, slapped both of her cheeks with a loud sound, and aggressively grabbed a glowing diamond-encrusted hairpiece from the vanity tray.

"Lady Seraphina," Emily declared fiercely, her voice shaking with intense, professional bloodlust. "Stand completely still... I am going to make you look so breathtakingly gorgeous that the man won’t just want to marry you... he will beg to worship the ground your stilettos touch!"
"Excellent," Seraphina smirked, the fire in her eyes matching the stylist’s perfectly. "Do not hold back."
Out in the central waiting area, Silas sat comfortably on the leather sofa, his chin resting in his hand as he watched the clock on his Spirit Phone tick forward.
’Seven minutes,’ Silas thought. ’Not bad. I figured they’d take at least an hour to—’
SWISH!
The heavy velvet curtains on both sides of the pavilion parted simultaneously with a synchronized rustle.
Silas blinked, straightening his posture as two distinct overwhelming waves of female authority flooded the open showroom floor.
From the left stepped Harper.
The energetic Lightning Lord carried herself with an athletic swagger that immediately demanded attention.
The two-piece violet dragon-silk ensemble was nothing short of lethal.

The crop-top corset hugged her toned torso, putting her rock-hard abs and generous cleavage on full unapologetic display, while the high-waisted skirt clung tightly to her muscular hips before splitting dramatically up her left thigh, revealing her long flawless leg with every confident step she took.
Her vibrant purple hair had been styled into loose, cascading waves that framed her flushed, radiant face.
Tendrils of static electricity danced playfully along the silver embroidery of her collar, making the fabric shimmer like a starlit storm cloud.
From the right stepped Seraphina.
The Bloom heiress moved with the slow, mesmerizing grace of high-society royalty.
The floor-length crimson phoenix-silk gown hugged every single curve of her hour-glass frame with suffocating precision.
The plunging open back accentuated the elegant curve of her spine, while the structured sweetheart bodice framed her voluptuous bust in glittering gold filigree.
Her fiery red hair had been pinned up in an intricate regal chignon, secured by diamond-encrusted pins, leaving two soft curled tendrils dangling along her pale slender neck.
Both women stopped exactly five paces in front of Silas’s sofa, striking their respective poses.
Harper planted her hand firmly on her hip, thrusting her chest forward and shooting Silas a bold, teasing wink.

"Well, Silas?" Harper smirked, her violet eyes glittering with competitive pride. "How do I look? Powerful, dangerous, and undeniably hot, right? You won’t find a woman in the entire city or country who looks this good in silk."
Seraphina raised her chin, turning slightly to the side to let the mana-lights catch the dazzling gold embroidery along her waist.
Her cheeks were dusted with a rosy blush, but her crimson eyes burned with fierce possessiveness.

"Observe the balance of the craftsmanship, Silas," Seraphina commanded softly, her melodic voice oozing with refined elegance. "The phoenix silk is an ancestral weave meant exclusively for sovereign nobility... It complements my unblemished complexion flawlessly. A man of your... refined eye can surely appreciate true untouchable perfection."

I am going to make you look so breathtakingly gorgeous that the man won’t just want to marry you... he will beg to worship the ground your stilettos touch!"
"Excellent," Seraphina smirked, the fire in her eyes matching the stylist’s perfectly.
"Do not hold back."
Out in the central waiting area, Silas sat comfortably on the leather sofa, his chin resting in his hand as he watched the clock on his Spirit Phone tick forward.
’Seven minutes,’ Silas thought. ’Not bad.
I figured they’d take at least an hour to—’
SWISH!
The heavy velvet curtains on both sides of the pavilion parted simultaneously with a synchronized rustle.
Silas blinked, straightening his posture as two distinct overwhelming waves of female authority flooded the open showroom floor.
From the left stepped Harper.
The energetic Lightning Lord carried herself with an athletic swagger that immediately demanded attention.
The two-piece violet dragon-silk ensemble was nothing short of lethal.

The crop-top corset hugged her toned torso, putting her rock-hard abs and generous cleavage on full unapologetic display, while the high-waisted skirt clung tightly to her muscular hips before splitting dramatically up her left thigh, revealing her long flawless leg with every confident step she took.
Her vibrant purple hair had been styled into loose, cascading waves that framed her flushed, radiant face.
Tendrils of static electricity danced playfully along the silver embroidery of her collar, making the fabric shimmer like a starlit storm cloud.
From the right stepped Seraphina.
The Bloom heiress moved with the slow, mesmerizing grace of high-society royalty.
The floor-length crimson phoenix-silk gown hugged every single curve of her hour-glass frame with suffocating precision.
The plunging open back accentuated the elegant curve of her spine, while the structured sweetheart bodice framed her voluptuous bust in glittering gold filigree.
Her fiery red hair had been pinned up in an intricate regal chignon, secured by diamond-encrusted pins, leaving two soft curled tendrils dangling along her pale slender neck.
Both women stopped exactly five paces in front of Silas’s sofa, striking their respective poses.
Harper planted her hand firmly on her hip, thrusting her chest forward and shooting Silas a bold, teasing wink.
"Well, Silas?" Harper smirked, her violet eyes glittering with competitive pride.
"How do I look?
Powerful, dangerous, and undeniably hot, right?
You won’t find a woman in the entire city or country who looks this good in silk."
Seraphina raised her chin, turning slightly to the side to let the mana-lights catch the dazzling gold embroidery along her waist.
Her cheeks were dusted with a rosy blush, but her crimson eyes burned with fierce possessiveness.
"Observe the balance of the craftsmanship, Silas," Seraphina commanded softly, her melodic voice oozing with refined elegance.
"The phoenix silk is an ancestral weave meant exclusively for sovereign nobility...
It complements my unblemished complexion flawlessly.
A man of your... refined eye can surely appreciate true untouchable perfection."

chapters.title: Chapter 384: ...Require The Strongest Wills
paragraphs: Silas sat entirely motionless on the leather sofa.
His eyes, rimmed with the golden rings, methodically scanned both women from head to toe.
He took in Harper’s wild breathtaking athletic allure... the exposed skin, the confident posture, the raw energy radiating from her smile.

Then he took in Seraphina’s regal jaw-dropping elegance... the aristocratic tailoring, the devastating curves accentuated by the crimson silk, the high-society presence that could silence an entire court.
Master Jean, Lydia, Emily, and even Reginald all held their collective breath, the entire room suspended in agonizing high-stakes anticipation.
Silas cleared his throat, leaning back against the cushions.

"Harper," Silas began calmly. "The cut is incredible. The violet silk matches your lightning mana perfectly, and the mobility on the split skirt fits your combat style... It highlights your strength without sacrificing aesthetics. It’s an easy 9 out of 10."
Harper’s face lit up with a massive beaming smile, her fists pumping slightly in victory.
Silas turned his head toward the crimson noble.
’Now let’s use a lot of grammar for this one, since I’m speaking to a noble, I’ll butter her up.’

"Seraphina," Silas continued, maintaining his objective tone. "The phoenix silk and the gold filigree are practically bespoke for your aura... The structure of the bodice and the open-back tailoring are flawless. It completely elevates your presence from an elite Lord to a literal empress. The craftsmanship and color harmony put it at a 9.5 out of 10."
The silence in the room violently snapped.
"YES!" Seraphina gasped softly, her hands flying to her chest as a brilliant radiant smile completely broke through her haughty noble face.
She shot Harper a look of pure undisputed triumph, her eyes gleaming with vindication.
"I won! The authority of House Bloom remains supreme!"
Behind her, Emily the junior maid aggressively pumped her fist in the air, silently celebrating her imminent double-salary promotion.
On the other side of the carpet, Harper’s energetic posture instantly deflated.
Her shoulders slumped, her lower lip puffing out into a massive, deeply irritated pout as she glared at the floor.
"A 9.5?!" Harper grumbled, crossing her arms tightly under her chest. "Half a point?! You gave her half a point just because she’s wearing three extra yards of curtain fabric?!"
"The tailoring was objectively cleaner, Harper," Silas pointed out, unbothered by her whining.
"Oh, hell no!" Harper snapped, her competitive fire roaring back to life with a vengeance.

She turned violently toward the racks of clothing. "That was just round one! We are not stopping here! Lydia, pull the leather battle-corsets! Pull the backless velvet evening gowns! Pull everything on the rack! We’re doing a full montage!"
Seraphina’s eyes narrowed into slits of pure aggression.
"You think you can surpass me with brute volume?! Emily, bring out the ancestral starlight collection! I will crush her in every single aesthetic metric!"
Silas blinked, a cold sweat suddenly breaking out on the back of his neck.
"Wait, hold on, that wasn’t an invitation to—"
SWISH! SWISH!
Both dressing room curtains violently slammed shut in his face.
What followed over the next ninety minutes was a grueling gauntlet of high-society warfare.
SWISH!
Harper emerged wearing a sleek midnight-black leather combat suit lined with glowing purple mythril conduits.
The trousers were painted on like liquid latex, emphasizing the athletic curves of her legs, while the cropped jacket featured an open neckline that drove the stylists into a frenzy.
"That’s a bit too aggressive for a formal dinner," Silas commented. "I’ll give you a 9.1."𝒻𝑟ℯℯ𝑤𝑒𝑏𝑛𝘰𝓋𝑒𝓁.𝒸𝑜𝘮
SWISH!
Seraphina stepped out in a daring, emerald-green velvet halter gown with a neckline that plunged nearly to her navel, held together by a single, enchanted diamond clasp.
Her crimson hair tumbled over her bare shoulders like liquid fire.
"Stunning color contrast," Silas rated, rubbing his chin. "9.3."
SWISH!
Harper walked out in a semi-translucent, white-and-silver starlight cocktail dress that shimmered with micro-auroras every time she took a step.
The back was completely non-existent, held up by two microscopic silver chains crossing her shoulder blades.
"Daring," Silas noted, nodding slowly. "9.4."
SWISH!

Seraphina appeared wearing a high-collared, form-fitting sapphire-blue qipao woven from lunar silk, featuring twin waist-high side slits that gave a clear view of her long pale thighs with every stride.
"It shows your high noble elegance," Silas sighed. "9.6."
Outfits flew across the showroom floor in a blur of colors, fabrics, and magical enchantments.
The maids sprinted back and forth with armfuls of designer silks, steam irons, and accessory cases.

By the time the frenzy finally began to wind down, five massive, gold-plated rolling clothing racks stood behind the sofa, completely packed to the brim with over eighty distinct designer outfits, evening gowns, and combat-silk ensembles.
Silas sat slouched on the leather sofa, sweatdropping profusely as he stared at the mountain of merchandise.
His eyes were glazed over, his brain practically fried from having to generate eighty distinct politically neutral fashion critiques in under two hours.
"Are you two finally done?" Silas groaned, holding his head in his hands. "Because I’m pretty sure we just bought out the GDP of a small nation."
Seraphina, currently wearing the sapphire-blue qipao, strode gracefully out of her dressing suite, looking completely energized by her string of high ratings.
She walked directly up to the sofa, grabbed Silas’s large hand, and forcefully pulled him up to his feet.

"We are finished with our selections," Seraphina declared proudly, turning her sharp gaze toward Master Jean and the gathered staff. "Now, it is his turn... Bring out your premier menswear collections immediately. I want him dressed in the finest enchanted silks this establishment has to offer."
Silas immediately tried to pull his hand back, shaking his head frantically.
"No. Absolutely not. I told you, I have plenty of clothes at home. I am not buying a hundred-thousand-credit shirt just to spill sauce on it."

"Silence, Silas," Seraphina shut him down with an authoritative flick of her wrist. "You are the prospective consort of House Bloom. You cannot wander through the city looking like an unawakened scrap-mechanic. It is an insult to my visual sensibilities."
Harper stepped up on Silas’s other side, wearing her white starlight cocktail dress. Surprisingly, she aggressively nodded in agreement with the noblewoman.

"For once, the bitch is right," Harper chimed in, crossing her arms and eyeing Silas up and down. "You have an amazing body, Silas, but your wardrobe is completely depressing... You wear the same three black hoodies every single day so we’re getting you styled."
Master Jean bowed deeply, a theatrical flourish accompanying his smile.

"Worry not, Lady Bloom, Lady Whitmore! The moment Lord Graves entered our sanctuary, I personally curated a bespoke collection of Tier-4 Shadow-Silk tunics, enchanted leather dusters, and mythril-threaded formal trousers tailored precisely to his physical form... They are waiting in the Master Suite."
"Excellent," Seraphina nodded.
She turned toward the dressing room with her crimson eyes flashing. "I will personally assist him with the fittings."
Harper’s head snapped toward Seraphina, her violet eyes flaring with instant violent hostility.
"Excuse me?! In your dreams, Princess! I am his official date today! I will be the one dressing him!"
"He is my designated property under ancestral law!" Seraphina argued fiercely, stepping into Harper’s space. "I have the right to inspect the fit of his garments!"
"You just want an excuse to see him shirtless again, you perverted red-haired stalker!" Harper yelled.
"And you don’t, you shameless lightning degenerate?!" Seraphina screamed back.
Silas let out a heavy exasperated breath, raising both hands to interject.
"I am a fully grown man. I possess fully functional arms and opposable thumbs... I can physically put a shirt on by myself without either of you hovering over me."
Both women simultaneously turned their heads, glared at him with terrifying unblinking intensity, and shouted in perfect unison.
"STAY OUT OF THIS, SILAS!"
Silas blinked, slowly closing his mouth.
’Right... Never mind.’
Harper aggressively planted her hands on her hips, leaning her face inches away from Seraphina’s nose. "We settle this right now! Standard rules!"
Seraphina sneered, lifting her chin. "State your terms."
"Rock, Paper, Scissors!" Harper challenged loudly. "One throw! Winner gets to dress Silas in the Master Suite, loser stays out here with the luggage!"
"A barbaric commoner game," Seraphina scoffed, though she instantly raised her right hand, her fingers coiling into a tight competitive fist. "Fine. Prepare to weep, Harper Whitmore."
Silas watched in flabbergasted disbelief as two of the most powerful Lords prepared to decide his physical autonomy through middle-school playground tactics.
"ROCK! PAPER! SCISSORS! SHOOT!" they shouted together.
THWACK!
Seraphina threw out a flat open palm... Paper.
Harper threw out a sharp two-fingered split... Scissors.
The room fell dead silent.
Seraphina stared down at her open hand in soul-crushing horror.
Her crimson eyes bulged, her mouth dropping open as her noble mind completely failed to process the reality of her defeat.
"N-No..." Seraphina choked out, her voice cracking. "That’s impossible... The probability..."
"AHAHAHAHAHA!"
Harper threw her head back in a deafening roar of pure triumph.
She violently turned toward Seraphina, pulling down her lower eyelid with her index finger and sticking her tongue out in the most immature, obnoxious victory taunt humanly possible.
"BLEEEEEEH! IN YOUR FACE, PRINCESS! SCISSORS CUTS PAPER! I WIN!"
"You cheated!" Seraphina shrieked, her face turning bright red with pure fury. "You delayed your release by three milliseconds! It was a false throw!"
"Sore loser! Stay mad!" Harper cackled.

Without wasting a single second, Harper spun around, grabbed Silas firmly by the wrist with one hand, snatched the heavy armful of bespoke designer menswear from Master Jean with the other, and forcefully dragged the towering Lord straight into the Master Dressing Suite.
SLAM!
The heavy mahogany doors slammed shut, and the lock clicked into place with a definitive chunk.

"HARPER Whitmore! OPEN THIS DOOR IMMEDIATELY!" Seraphina’s enraged voice hammered against the heavy wood from the outside, accompanied by the muffled thump of her stilettos kicking the frame. "I WILL BURN THIS SUITE TO THE GROUND!"
Inside the spacious, soundproofed dressing room, Harper paid the exterior threats zero attention.
She turned around, tossing the massive pile of expensive silk shirts, leather pants, and mythril belts onto a velvet chaise lounge with a casual flick of her wrist.
The energetic Lightning Lord stepped forward, stopping barely inches from Silas’s chest.
Her cheeks were flushed a brilliant, radiant shade of pink, but her glowing violet eyes sparkled with mischievous victorious delight.

She reached down, grabbing a crisp, form-fitting charcoal-black button-down shirt woven from enchanted shadow-silk, resting her other hand firmly on her hip as she looked Silas up and down with an unapologetic wicked grin.
"Alright, handsome," Harper purred, tossing the shirt lightly from one hand to the other. "Strip down. We don’t have all day."
Silas stood in the center of the plush hand-woven rug, looking down at Harper with an expression of pure deadpan resignation.

"You really enjoy playing with fire, don’t you?" Silas muttered, crossing his arms over his chest. "If Seraphina burns this establishment to the ground, I’m listing you as an accomplice on the damage reports... I’m not paying for shit."
Harper let out an amused melodic snort.

She casually tossed the armful of bespoke menswear onto the chaise lounge, resting one hand firmly on her slender hip while holding a charcoal-black button-down shirt woven from enchanted shadow-silk in the other.
Her glowing violet eyes danced with unchecked mischief.
"Let the princess kick the door until her heels snap," Harper purred, taking a slow, confident step closer.

Her lavender scent, laced with the sharp scent of her lightning mana, rolled over his senses. "She lost the throw fair and square. Now, stop stalling. I told you out there... strip down. We don’t have all day, and I am not letting you walk out of here looking like you just clocked out of a scrap-metal sorting facility."
Silas stared at her for a long quiet second.
’Haah... It’ll be a waste of time to argue.’
He realized that arguing with the energetic Lightning Lord in an enclosed space was a pointless exercise.
"Fine," Silas sighed. "Turn around."

"Not happening," Harper shot back instantly, flashing a shameless radiant grin that bared her small fangs. "I’m your official stylist for this round. A proper fitting requires visual oversight from step one."
Silas rolled his eyes, letting out a heavy breath.
’Whatever. It’s not like my body is the most perfect one in the world. I don’t mind either...’
