chapters.title: Chapter 385: An 8.8?!
paragraphs: Silas reached down, grabbing the hem of his dark charcoal Henley shirt.
With a single fluid motion, he pulled the fabric up over his broad shoulders and tossed it aside onto the velvet bench.
The moment the dark cloth peeled away, the light of the dressing suite caught the sculpted shape of his physique.
His torso was a masterclass in violence and refinement.

Because of the endless qualitative upgrades from his Mythic Gold Core, Silas’s musculature didn’t merely look athletic... It was packed with striating fibers that gave his chest, shoulders, and abdomen the appearance of an ancient war deity carved from bronze and polished marble.
His broad flared lats tapered down into a razor-sharp V-line, framing a rock-hard eight-pack that expanded whenever he drew a breath.
Harper’s smirk instantly froze.
Her parted lips parted slightly wider as a sudden involuntary hitch caught in the back of her throat, and the sharp playful banter died on her tongue.
Her violet eyes widened, tracking the sharp contours of his pectorals, the deep valleys of his serratus muscles, and the broad sweeping expanse of his clavicles.
A deep violent flush of crimson bloomed beneath her pale skin, rushing from her cheeks all the way down the exposed neckline of her violet dragon-silk corset.
"Well?" Silas asked, raising an eyebrow as he caught her stunned stare. "You going to hand me the shirt, or are you just going to stand there catching flies?"
Harper swallowed hard with her throat suddenly feeling parched.
The playful arrogance that usually defined her demeanor shattered, replaced by an instinctual magnetism that pulled her forward like a moth to a blazing flame.
"I..." Harper whispered, her voice dropping into a breathless one. "I have to... inspect the measurements first. For sizing accuracy."
Before Silas could step back, Harper boldly closed the remaining distance.
She reached out with both hands. Her warm, slender fingers pressed directly against the center of his chest.
Zzzzt.
A microscopic involuntary spark of purple static leapt from her fingertips, skittering across his skin with a faint tingling warmth that his Gold Core instantly absorbed.
Harper didn’t pull away. Instead, her palms flattened against his firm, chiseled pectorals, sliding slowly outward toward his shoulders.
Her breath hitched again as she felt the unyielding muscles beneath her hands.
"Holy hell, Silas..." Harper murmured, her fingers curling slightly as she traced the edge of his collarbone.

Her eyes were completely locked on his chest, her pupils blown wide with lust and awe. "What kind of monstrous training regimen are you running in that territory of yours? This isn’t normal. You feel like solid titanium wrapped in heated leather."
"It’s just core circulation," Silas answered dryly, though his jaw tightened slightly at the bold, intimate drag of her nails across his skin. "Now hand over the—"
Harper completely ignored him.
Her hands smoothly slid downward, trailing over his sternum before splaying wide across his sculpted upper abdomen.
Her thumbs traced the deep defined grooves between his abdominal plates, pressing firmly into the dense muscle.
"Stop squirming," Harper whispered, a wicked,flushed smirk returning to her lips as she leaned into his space.

Her breasts, barely contained by the dragon-silk crop top, brushed lightly against his bare forearm with every breath. "I’m checking the torso taper... If the waist isn’t measured properly, the enchanted silk will bunch at the hem."
She slowly stepped around him, her hands gliding seamlessly along his ribcage to grip his flared latissimus dorsi.
As she moved behind his back, her palms swept upward across the vast muscular terrain of his shoulder blades and trapezius.
She traced the long, powerful lines of his spine, marveling at the sheer width of his back.
"Your shoulders are ridiculously wide," Harper gasped softly, pressing her chest flush against his upper back for a fleeting deliberate second.

The heat radiating from his skin seeped straight through her corset, making her core thrum with a sudden dizzying spike of adrenaline. "It’s actually unfair. Most guys in the academy spend millions on alchemical body-sculpting elixirs and still look like bloated balloons. You look like a walking predator... The good kind..."
"Harper," Silas warned in a low voice, turning his head slightly over his shoulder to meet her hooded violet gaze. "You’re fondling, not styling."
"I am multitasking, Lord Graves," Harper shot back shamelessly, giving his lower back an appreciative firm squeeze before stepping back around to face him.
Her cheeks were burning a radiant shade of pink, but she wore her brazenness like a badge of honor. "And an elite stylist deserves compensation for her labor."
She picked up the charcoal shadow-silk shirt, shaking out the sleeves.
"Arms up," she commanded with mock authority.
Silas let out another quiet, resigned breath and raised his arms.
Harper stepped in close, carefully guiding his broad arms through the enchanted sleeves.

The fabric was extraordinary... the moment Silas’s skin made contact with the inner lining, the mythril-threaded runes hummed to life, automatically contracting and shaping itself to match the exact contours of his torso.
Harper moved her hands to the front of his chest with her fingers brushing lightly against his bare skin as she slowly, deliberately fastened each platinum button from the navel upward.
Click! Click! Click!
She took her sweet time, ensuring her knuckles dragged across his abs with every single button she secured.
By the time she reached the high mandarin collar, her breath was brushing against Silas’s jawline.
"There," Harper whispered, smoothing the lapels flat against his chest with both hands, her eyes glittering with pride. "Look at that. Pure untouchable perfection..."
Silas turned toward the triple gilded mirror.
The transformation was striking.

The charcoal shadow-silk shirt clung flawlessly to his frame, accentuating the width of his shoulders and the taper of his waist while subtly concealing the raw terrifying power beneath an aura of dark understated elegance.
The platinum trim along the cuffs and collar caught the ambient light with a refined metallic gleam.
"Not bad," Silas admitted, rolling his shoulders to test the fabric’s flexibility. "Doesn’t restrict movement at all and it feels like a combat tunic."
"Because it is, idiot," Harper laughed, stepping up beside him in the glass and linking her arm through his.
She leaned her head against his bicep, grinning at their reflection.
"It’s high-tier defense wear. Now come on, let’s go show the princess what she missed out on."
CLICK-CHUNK!
The heavy doors of the Master Suite unlocked and swung open.
Standing in the corridor with her arms tightly crossed over her chest was Seraphina Bloom.
The crimson-haired noblewoman had been tapping her stiletto against the quartz tile with the rhythmic fury of a ticking warhead.
Beside her, Reginald stood with his hands folded behind his back, maintaining an expression of stoic neutrality despite having listened to Seraphina’s low-volume curses for the past ten minutes.
The moment the doors parted, Seraphina’s head snapped toward the threshold.
Her crimson eyes flared with hostile fire which instantly, violently extinguished the second Silas stepped into view.
Seraphina froze.
Her breath hitched in her throat with her lips parting as her crimson eyes swept over the towering dark-haired Lord.
The bespoke shadow-silk shirt fit him like a dream, balancing his rugged intimidating presence with the aristocratic sophistication expected of high-tier nobility.

"Well, well, well," Harper gloated, walking out beside him with an insufferably smug grin plastered across her face. "Look who’s speechless. Care to offer a critique, Princess, or is your noble vocabulary too limited to handle how good he looks?"
Seraphina quickly caught herself, snapping her mouth shut as a radiant rosy blush exploded across her pale cheeks.
She raised her chin, desperately clawing back her dignity.

"The... the choice of shadow-silk is passable," Seraphina muttered, clearing her throat and looking away from Silas’s chest with great difficulty. "Though the platinum threading on the cuffs is slightly ostentatious. Still... it suits his natural frame adequately. An 8.8."𝓯𝓻𝓮𝙚𝙬𝓮𝙗𝒏𝙤𝒗𝙚𝙡.𝒄𝒐𝓶
"8.8 my ass, that’s an easy 9.5!" Harper argued loudly.
"Silence, woman!" Seraphina snapped back, her eyes flashing with renewed competitive hunger.
She stepped forward, pointing an aggressive, manicured finger at the dressing room. "Round one is over. It is time for round two! Master Jean, bring out the next ensemble!"
Master Jean, who had been watching the entire exchange with the giddy excitement of a theater director, immediately clapped his hands.
"Right away, Lady Bloom! For the second presentation, we have prepared an exquisite Imperial Midnight-Duster paired with white dragon-leather trousers!"
Harper and Seraphina instantly locked eyes with the invisible lightning and fire crackling between them once more.
"Same rules!" Harper challenged, raising her right hand. "Rock, Paper, Scissors!"
"Prepare to be annihilated," Seraphina hissed, raising her own fist.
"ROCK! PAPER! SCISSORS! SHOOT!"
THWACK!
Harper threw out a flat open palm... Paper.
Seraphina threw out a sharp two-fingered split... Scissors.
The showroom went silent.
Harper’s jaw dropped in horror.
"WHAT?! NO!"
"AHAHAHAHAHA!"
Seraphina’s melodic laugh echoed victoriously off the vaulted ceiling. She threw her head back, practically glowing with vindication as she looked down her nose at the crushed Lightning Lord.

"Scissors severs paper, you vulgar brute!" Seraphina declared proudly, stepping forward with the regal grace of a conquering monarch. "The balance has been restored! Now step aside and watch a true noblewoman handle styling!"

Without waiting for Harper to complain, Seraphina snatched the midnight-duster and dragon-leather trousers from the hovering tray, grabbed Silas firmly by the wrist, and aggressively hauled the towering young man straight into the Master Suite.
SLAM!
The heavy mahogany doors slammed shut once again, leaving Harper on the outside, frantically banging her fists against the wood while screaming bloody murder.
Inside the private sanctuary, the heavy click of the lock resonated with finality.
Seraphina let out a long satisfied exhale.
She set the white dragon-leather pants and the long midnight duster neatly onto the cedar dressing table, smoothing her crimson phoenix-silk gown as she turned to face him.
Her cheeks were still burning a soft beautiful shade of pink, but she forced her spine straight, attempting to project the authority of House Bloom’s future matriarch.

"Take that shirt off," Seraphina commanded smoothly, her melodic voice trembling with a microscopic edge of nervous anticipation. "The duster requires direct skin contact with the conduits on the shoulders for proper magical alignment."
Silas didn’t even sigh this time. He was completely numb to the absurdity of the afternoon.
"You nobles really love making up magical excuses to stare at people," Silas commented deadpan, reaching up and undoing the platinum buttons Harper had just fastened.
He shrugged the shadow-silk shirt off, tossing it onto the velvet sofa.
Seraphina stood completely paralyzed.

Seeing him in the chaos of the Secret Realm... covered in sand and dungeon grime was different from seeing him here, standing beneath the crystal-clear radiant illumination of the private dressing room.
Her crimson eyes drank in the sight.
The broad, muscular expanses of his shoulders, the deep, powerful cuts of his chest, and the terrifying chiseled definition of his abs made her mouth go completely dry.
Her heart hammered against her ribs at an alarming rate with a sudden intoxicating wave of heat pooling in the depths of her lower abdomen.

’He is... absurdly gorgeous,’ Seraphina’s thoughts raced wildly, her fingers clenching into the silk of her dress. ’Mother said men from the lower wards were unrefined and gaunt... This man looks like an ancient warlord sculpted by the gods themselves. How does someone who lived on cheap bread possess a body this magnificent?!’
Silas picked up the white dragon-leather trousers, looking over at her with a raised eyebrow.
"Are you going to help with the fitting, or are you going to keep staring at my ribs like they’re a geometry problem?"
Seraphina snapped out of her trance, a brilliant crimson flush spreading all the way to the tips of her pointed ears.

"I am... analyzing your proportions!" Seraphina defended herself frantically, stepping forward with brisk hurried steps. "As your future lawful wife, it is my duty to ensure your wardrobe adheres to the highest standards of the High Court!"
She grabbed the long, midnight-black duster from the table.
The coat was forged from the reinforced hide of a Void-Stalker, trimmed with shimmering silver runes that danced along the hem like liquid mercury.
Seraphina held the heavy coat open, stepping directly into his personal space.
Silas slid his broad arms into the sleeves.
The moment the coat settled over his shoulders, Seraphina moved in remarkably close.
Her trembling manicured hands reached up, resting flat against the broad expanse of his clavicles as she smoothed the heavy lapels down his chest.
Her touch was completely different from Harper’s bold aggressive fondling.
Seraphina’s hands were soft, deliberate, and reverent with her delicate fingers lingering over the dense muscle of his upper chest as if she were touching sacred, fragile relic glass.
’I feel like I like her touch better... Harper is just a pervert.’
As she worked the fastenings along his ribs, Seraphina looked up into his deep blue golden-ringed eyes.

"Silas," Seraphina began softly, her tone shedding its haughty armor in favor of genuine quiet curiosity. "Where did you learn your combat foundation? Your footwork... when we fought Ititius, it was very special."

paragraphs: Silas looked down at the beautiful noblewoman smoothing his coat, keeping his voice calm.
"I learn from experiences that I face... every single thing I have experienced reflects in my battle style, both the good and the bad."
He could have said Morwenna helped him out but what was the point of that?
Seraphina’s fingers paused over his chest.
A flicker of quiet uncharacteristic sorrow touched her crimson eyes.
"I see..." Seraphina murmured, her hands gently tracing the outline of his ribs through the inner lining of the coat. "And what of your parents? Did they teach you things about life?"
"They died when I was born," Silas answered flatly, his voice lacked any sort of self-pity. "I raised Lia by myself. Everything I know about life, I taught myself in a way."
Seraphina stared up at him, her heart aching with a sudden wave of respect.
In high society, nobles inherited power, land, and ancestral artifacts without lifting a finger.

Yet the man standing before her had clawed his way out of the bottom of human existence, carrying his little sister on his back through the filth and blood of the slums to stand as an equal before the elite.

’He is strong,’ Seraphina thought, a fierce protective warmth blooming in her chest as her hands slowly moved up to rest against his broad shoulders. ’Not just physically... but in his spirit. He didn’t break and he didn’t bow.’
She looked directly into his eyes, her rosy blush deepening.
"You won’t have to carry everything alone anymore, Silas. When we are wed, the entire treasury of House Bloom will be at your disposal. You will never have to scrape for scraps again."
Silas let out a small chuckle, reaching up and gently, firmly taking her wrists to lower her hands from his shoulders.
"I appreciate the sentiment, Princess," Silas said smoothly, stepping back toward the mirror. "But I prefer building my own empire with my own hands. I don’t need charity."
Seraphina looked down at her hands, where the ghost of his warm, calloused grip still lingered, and a slow radiant smile touched her lips.
’You truly are impossible to tame,’ she thought fondly. ’Which only makes me want you more.’
CLICK-CHUNK!
The doors swung open once more.
Silas stepped out into the main showroom, dressed in the full Imperial Midnight ensemble.
The long tailored duster flowed around his calves with every step, the deep midnight-black fabric contrasting brilliantly against the pristine white dragon-leather trousers and combat boots.
The silver runes along the collar gave his imposing frame the undeniable aura of a sovereign dark monarch commanding the battlefield.
Harper, who was sitting slouched on the velvet sofa with her arms crossed and her cheeks puffed out in a massive pout, slowly looked up.
Her jaw dropped open.
"Holy... shit," Harper breathed, her annoyance instantly evaporating into pure aesthetic worship. "Okay... okay, fine. The princess actually cooked. You look like a literal final boss."
Seraphina strode out behind him with her head held high, radiating smug triumph.
"Naturally. A Bloom maiden’s eye for sovereign elegance is without equal. That is an undisputed 9.8 out of 10."
"Don’t get cocky, Princess!" Harper yelled, leaping up from the sofa with renewed energy. "Round three! Let’s go!"
Silas pinched the bridge of his nose, letting out a soul-weary groan.
"Please, God, no..."
What followed over the next hour was a merciless gauntlet of fashion warfare.
The two competitive Lords dragged Silas through an endless dizzying montage of high-society attire.
SWISH.
He wore an enchanted crimson-and-gold formal vest woven from solar-serpent scales that accentuated his broad chest.
SWISH.
He wore a tailored abyssal-navy combat blazer with reinforced mythril shoulder pauldrons.
SWISH.
He wore a high-collared white martial robe trimmed with celestial wolf fur that made him look like an ancient elven warlord.

By the time the frenzy finally wound down, eight massive rolling garment racks stood behind the sofas, completely overloaded with dozens of bespoke designer suits, combat tunics, enchanted dusters, and leather trousers.
Silas stood in the center of the showroom, wearing the original charcoal shadow-silk shirt and dark trousers, looking like a man who had just marched fifty miles through an active artillery barrage.
His eyes were glazed over, his shoulders slouched in utter soul-crushing fatigue.
Stationed near the elevator doors, Reginald stood quietly, watching the exhausted young Lord with deep sympathy.
The veteran butler slowly shook his head, offering Silas a subtle, sorrowful look that practically screamed...
’Stay strong, young master. Survival is a victory.’
Ten minutes later, the group descended the private glass elevator and arrived at the grand marble-paved ground-floor reception lobby of the Grand Celestia.
The private staff had carefully packed the mountain of luxury garments into thirty-two heavy matte-black garment bags stamped with gold foil, stacking them onto four rolling brass luggage carts.
Silas shuffled behind the two women, dragging his feet like a condemned prisoner approaching the gallows.
Waiting behind the elevated obsidian reception desk was the chief cashier... an immaculate woman with pinned blonde hair, wearing a sleek silver uniform.
She offered a deep, reverent bow as the group approached.
"Welcome back, Lady Whitmore, Lady Bloom, Lord Graves," the cashier beamed professionally. "I trust your private session in the Sanctuary was thoroughly satisfactory?"
"It was exceptional," Harper smirked, casually leaning her elbow on the marble counter. "Ring everything up."
"Certainly, Lady Whitmore," the cashier replied, picking up a heavy, glowing crystal-optic scanner ledger.
BEEP! BEEP! BEEP! BEEP!
The crystal scanner flashed in rapid succession as it synchronized with the magical RFID tags embedded inside all thirty-two garment bags.
Lines of encrypted transaction data, itemized tax codes, and sovereign luxury levies scrolled rapidly down the glowing holographic display floating above the counter.
After several seconds, the scanner emitted a cheerful, high-pitched DING!
The final total materialized in massive, glowing golden numbers in the center of the lobby.
[GRAND CELESTIA HAUTE COUTURE SANCTUARY]
[TOTAL MERCHANDISE: 32 BESPOKE PIECES]
[VIP SANCTUARY RESERVATION FEE: INCLUDED]
FINAL BALANCE: 8,450,000 SPIRIT CREDITS
Silas stared at the glowing numbers.
His heart physically stopped beating for two full seconds. His pale eyes bulged behind his bangs with the color completely draining from his face.

’EIGHT POINT FOUR FIVE MILLION CREDITS?!’ Silas screamed in the silent horrified caverns of his own mind. ’FOR CLOTHES?! NOT AGAIN... NOT AGAIN... I COULD BUY AN ENTIRE DISTRICT IN THE LOWER SECTOR FOR THAT MUCH MONEY! THESE PEOPLE ARE OUT OF THEIR GODDAMN MINDS!’
Before Silas could open his mouth to demand they return thirty-one of the bags immediately, Harper reached into the pocket of her tailored trousers.
"Put it on House Whitmore’s primary corporate—" Harper began casually.

"Hold your tongue, commoner!" Seraphina interrupted sharply, stepping forward and shoving Harper’s shoulder aside with noble disdain. "Silas is the prospective consort of House Bloom. His wardrobe is an ancestral investment, and House Bloom will settle the ledger in full!"
Seraphina reached into the inner lapel of her tailored crimson blazer, feeling around for her platinum family crest card.
Her fingers grasped empty air.
Seraphina paused.

Her sharp crimson eyes blinked once, twice, three times. She frantically patted down her other pocket, then checked the side lining of her blazer with her face growing visibly stiffer by the microsecond.
Standing two paces behind her, Reginald cleared his throat with a soft, polite Ahem.
The elderly butler stepped forward, leaning down slightly toward Seraphina’s ear, speaking in a low discreet whisper that was unfortunately entirely audible to Silas’s sharp senses.

"My Lady..." Reginald murmured softly. "In your haste to intercept Lord Graves day before yesterday before the location ping... you departed the Bloom Manor without your primary ledger purse. You possess zero liquid capital on your person."
Seraphina froze.
A nuclear violently bright crimson blush instantly exploded across her entire face, rushing all the way down to her collarbones.
Her aristocratic composure completely disintegrated into ash as she stared at the marble floor in pure mortification.
Harper, who had caught every single word, let out a deafening, uproarious laugh that echoed through the grand lobby.

"AHAHAHAHAHA!" Harper cackled, holding her stomach as she pointed an accusatory, triumphant finger at the blushing noble. "The great, untouchable Princess of House Bloom forgot her wallet! You came to a high-society shopping spree with empty pockets! That is the most pathetic thing I’ve ever seen in my life!"
"Silence, you insufferable brute!" Seraphina shrieked, clutching her burning cheeks. "It was an administrative oversight! Reginald, summon the courier immediately—"
"Too late, broke-ass!" Harper grinned widely, slapping her sleek black corporate platinum card directly onto the cashier’s scanner pad.
BZZT-CHUNK!
[TRANSACTION APPROVED: 8,450,000 SPIRIT CREDITS DEDUCTED FROM Whitmore RESERVES.]
"Thank you tremendously, Lady Whitmore!" the cashier chimed, bowing so low her forehead nearly touched the counter. "We wish you all a magnificent, glorious afternoon!"
Seraphina clicked her tongue with immense venom, turning her back to the counter and storming toward the exit with her arms crossed as her heels practically gouging holes in the marble floor.
Out in the valet bay, the private staff carefully loaded all thirty-two luxury garment bags into the spacious, pressurized rear boot of Harper’s custom midnight-purple sports coupe.
CLUNK!
The hydraulic trunk sealed shut with a soft hiss.
Silas collapsed into the front passenger seat, letting out a massive, soul-draining sigh as he melted into the heated leather headrest.
He felt like he had just fought three consecutive Lord Wars without a mana potion.
Beside him, Harper slid behind the steering wheel, humming a cheerful victorious tune as she adjusted her rearview mirror.
Seraphina climbed into the back seat, sitting with rigid, icy silence as she stared out the tinted glass.
Harper pushed the ignition rune.
VROOOOOOOM!
The twin-turbo mana engine roared to life with a deep throaty rumble.
Harper shifted gears, smoothly navigating the sports coupe out of the garage and accelerating onto the sunlit avenues of the upper district.
Harper glanced sideways at Silas, her violet eyes glittering with high-energy excitement.

"Alright, handsome!" Harper announced cheerfully, tapping her manicured nails against the leather-wrapped steering wheel. "Phase One of the Ultimate LordTube Date Guide is officially complete! Now, we move on to the most important, critical phase of the entire afternoon!"
Silas turned his head slowly, raising a suspicious exhausted eyebrow. "Harper... what is Phase Two?"
Harper puffed out her chest with immense pride, taking a sharp turn onto the prestigious Skyline Promenade.
"Phase Two is fine dining!" Harper declared happily. "I pulled massive corporate favors and booked an exclusive, VIP reservation on the panoramic top floor of The Celestial Zenith!"
Silas’s face instantly paled.
The Celestial Zenith.
Even living in the deepest most isolated squalor of the Sector 4 slums, Silas had heard of that place.
It was the most ridiculously expensive, astronomically priced sky-restaurant in the entire metropolitan district.

Located at the pinnacle of the city’s tallest crystalline spire, it was a hyper-exclusive culinary temple where a single glass of vintage mana-wine cost more than an average commoner made in five years of manual labor.

’First eight million on shirts...’ Silas thought, a cold sweat breaking out across his forehead as he stared blankly through the windshield. ’Now we are going to eat gold-plated lettuce... Someone please shoot me.’
Fifteen minutes later, the luxury sports coupe glided into the private, hovering landing pad attached to the seventy-fifth floor of the Celestial Zenith Spire.
The moment the scissor-doors swung open, a contingent of six impeccably dressed waitstaff in white silk tailcoats stepped forward, offering deep synchronized bows.
"Welcome to The Celestial Zenith, Lady Whitmore, Lady Bloom, Lord Graves," the head maître d’ beamed reverently, leading the way across a transparent bridge forged from enchanted floating glass.
They entered the restaurant’s top-floor sanctuary.
The atmosphere was breathtaking.
Floor-to-ceiling panoramic glass walls offered a dizzying, three-hundred-and-sixty-degree view of the sprawling Valoria City skyline, bathed in the warm golden glow of the setting afternoon sun.

Suspended floating mana-orbs cast a soft, romantic golden ambiance across the spacious dining hall, while a live quartet of musicians in the corner played a smooth, relaxing, and soulful jazz melody on enchanted crystal instruments.
Reginald stopped precisely at the entrance of the private dining pavilion. The elderly butler bowed stiffly, placing his hands behind his back.
"I shall remain stationed at the threshold, Lady Seraphina," Reginald said with quiet dignity. "To ensure your dining experience remains entirely undisturbed."
"Thank you, Reginald," Seraphina muttered, still visibly sulking from her wallet humiliation at the mall.
Harper didn’t waste a single second.
She immediately grabbed Silas’s hand, pulling the dark-haired Lord toward the prime, private window booth overlooking the entire metropolis.

"Look at this view, Silas!" Harper gushed, sliding into the plush velvet curved booth and pulling him down right beside her. "I made sure they gave us the prime sunset table... You can see all the way to the outer barrier gates from here! And look... they have atmospheric filters so the air smells like fresh mountain blossoms!"
Seraphina gracefully slid into the booth on the opposite side of the table, her crimson eyes narrowing into slits of pure boiling jealousy as she watched Harper lean her shoulder against Silas’s arm.

’That purple-haired vulture is dominating every single interaction,’ Seraphina thought fiercely with her manicured nails digging into the white linen tablecloth. ’I need to turn the tide... I need to prove that I am the superior, attentive prospective wife.’

sentences.text: Silas looked down at the beautiful noblewoman smoothing his coat, keeping his voice calm.
"I learn from experiences that I face... every single thing I have experienced reflects in my battle style, both the good and the bad."
He could have said Morwenna helped him out but what was the point of that?
Seraphina’s fingers paused over his chest.
A flicker of quiet uncharacteristic sorrow touched her crimson eyes.
"I see..." Seraphina murmured, her hands gently tracing the outline of his ribs through the inner lining of the coat.
"And what of your parents?
Did they teach you things about life?"
"They died when I was born," Silas answered flatly, his voice lacked any sort of self-pity.
"I raised Lia by myself.
Everything I know about life, I taught myself in a way."
Seraphina stared up at him, her heart aching with a sudden wave of respect.
In high society, nobles inherited power, land, and ancestral artifacts without lifting a finger.

Yet the man standing before her had clawed his way out of the bottom of human existence, carrying his little sister on his back through the filth and blood of the slums to stand as an equal before the elite.
’He is strong,’ Seraphina thought, a fierce protective warmth blooming in her chest as her hands slowly moved up to rest against his broad shoulders. ’Not just physically... but in his spirit.
He didn’t break and he didn’t bow.’
She looked directly into his eyes, her rosy blush deepening.
"You won’t have to carry everything alone anymore, Silas.
When we are wed, the entire treasury of House Bloom will be at your disposal.
You will never have to scrape for scraps again."
Silas let out a small chuckle, reaching up and gently, firmly taking her wrists to lower her hands from his shoulders.
"I appreciate the sentiment, Princess," Silas said smoothly, stepping back toward the mirror.
"But I prefer building my own empire with my own hands.
I don’t need charity."
Seraphina looked down at her hands, where the ghost of his warm, calloused grip still lingered, and a slow radiant smile touched her lips.
’You truly are impossible to tame,’ she thought fondly. ’Which only makes me want you more.’

The doors swung open once more.
Silas stepped out into the main showroom, dressed in the full Imperial Midnight ensemble.
The long tailored duster flowed around his calves with every step, the deep midnight-black fabric contrasting brilliantly against the pristine white dragon-leather trousers and combat boots.
The silver runes along the collar gave his imposing frame the undeniable aura of a sovereign dark monarch commanding the battlefield.
Harper, who was sitting slouched on the velvet sofa with her arms crossed and her cheeks puffed out in a massive pout, slowly looked up.
Her jaw dropped open.
"Holy... shit," Harper breathed, her annoyance instantly evaporating into pure aesthetic worship.
"Okay... okay, fine.
The princess actually cooked.
You look like a literal final boss."
Seraphina strode out behind him with her head held high, radiating smug triumph.
"Naturally.
A Bloom maiden’s eye for sovereign elegance is without equal.
That is an undisputed 9.8 out of 10."
"Don’t get cocky, Princess!" Harper yelled, leaping up from the sofa with renewed energy.
"Round three!
Let’s go!"
Silas pinched the bridge of his nose, letting out a soul-weary groan.
"Please, God, no..."
What followed over the next hour was a merciless gauntlet of fashion warfare.
The two competitive Lords dragged Silas through an endless dizzying montage of high-society attire.
SWISH.
He wore an enchanted crimson-and-gold formal vest woven from solar-serpent scales that accentuated his broad chest.
SWISH.
He wore a tailored abyssal-navy combat blazer with reinforced mythril shoulder pauldrons.
SWISH.
He wore a high-collared white martial robe trimmed with celestial wolf fur that made him look like an ancient elven warlord.

By the time the frenzy finally wound down, eight massive rolling garment racks stood behind the sofas, completely overloaded with dozens of bespoke designer suits, combat tunics, enchanted dusters, and leather trousers.
Silas stood in the center of the showroom, wearing the original charcoal shadow-silk shirt and dark trousers, looking like a man who had just marched fifty miles through an active artillery barrage.
His eyes were glazed over, his shoulders slouched in utter soul-crushing fatigue.
Stationed near the elevator doors, Reginald stood quietly, watching the exhausted young Lord with deep sympathy.
The veteran butler slowly shook his head, offering Silas a subtle, sorrowful look that practically screamed...
’Stay strong, young master.
Survival is a victory.’
Ten minutes later, the group descended the private glass elevator and arrived at the grand marble-paved ground-floor reception lobby of the Grand Celestia.
The private staff had carefully packed the mountain of luxury garments into thirty-two heavy matte-black garment bags stamped with gold foil, stacking them onto four rolling brass luggage carts.
Silas shuffled behind the two women, dragging his feet like a condemned prisoner approaching the gallows.
Waiting behind the elevated obsidian reception desk was the chief cashier... an immaculate woman with pinned blonde hair, wearing a sleek silver uniform.
She offered a deep, reverent bow as the group approached.
"Welcome back, Lady Whitmore, Lady Bloom, Lord Graves," the cashier beamed professionally.
"I trust your private session in the Sanctuary was thoroughly satisfactory?"
"It was exceptional," Harper smirked, casually leaning her elbow on the marble counter.
"Ring everything up."
"Certainly, Lady Whitmore," the cashier replied, picking up a heavy, glowing crystal-optic scanner ledger.
BEEP!
BEEP!
BEEP!
BEEP!
The crystal scanner flashed in rapid succession as it synchronized with the magical RFID tags embedded inside all thirty-two garment bags.
Lines of encrypted transaction data, itemized tax codes, and sovereign luxury levies scrolled rapidly down the glowing holographic display floating above the counter.
After several seconds, the scanner emitted a cheerful, high-pitched DING!
The final total materialized in massive, glowing golden numbers in the center of the lobby.

FINAL BALANCE: 8,450,000 SPIRIT CREDITS

chapters.title: Chapter 387: The Learning About The Other Phase
paragraphs: SWISH!
The head maître d’ approached the table with quiet practiced elegance.
Resting across his forearms were three colossal leather-bound menu folios embossed with solid platinum lettering that looked more like ancient heavy encyclopedia volumes than food menus.
He gracefully set one massive book in front of each guest, bowing low.

"Welcome to The Celestial Zenith," the maître d’ spoke with deep melodious reverence. "Our executive culinary masters have curated the finest grade-AAA dimensional delicacies for your pleasure today. We have abyssal caviar harvested from the deep rift trenches, gold-leaf-crusted celestial wyvern tenderloins, and thousand-year aged mana-truffles imported directly from the elven enclaves... Please, take your time, and let us know whenever you are prepared to feast."
"Thank you," Harper chirped, flipping her massive menu open with excitement.
Across the table, Seraphina’s crimson eyes suddenly ignited with a brilliant, predatory spark of inspiration.

’This is it!’ Seraphina realized in a flash of pure triumph with her pulse quickening. ’This is my redemption! Silas said people learn about each other on dates... and he specifically tested me on his favorite food earlier and he told me during one of our clothing sessions! If I take complete control of the order and request his favorite meal without him having to utter a single word, it will prove that I truly care about him and pay attention to his needs!’
Filled with soaring confidence, Seraphina flipped open the heavy, leather-bound folio.
Her sharp crimson eyes scanned the gilded pages.
’Page 1: Pan-Seared Astral Leviathan Cheek with Saffron Foam - 120,000 SC.’
’Page 2: Braised Abyssal Drake Ribs in Mana-Infused Truffle Glaze - 250,000 SC.’
’Page 3: Golden Phoenix-Egg Soufflé with Lunar Honey - 95,000 SC.’
Seraphina frowned slightly and she turned the page.
’Page 4: Glazed Shadow-Stalker Loin with Crystal-Spiced Asparagus - 180,000 SC.’
’Page 5: Poached Silver-Scale Wyrm Fillet in White Mana-Wine - 310,000 SC.’
Her brow furrowed deeper. She rapidly flipped through the meat sections, the poultry sections, the specialty soups, and the regional delicacies.
She flipped to the back then to the appetizers and then to the chef’s private reserve.
It wasn’t there.
...Not a single line. There was not a single mention.
Seraphina’s jaw tightened.
Her lips thinned into a razor-sharp, furious line as a dangerous suffocating wave of heat began to radiate from her skin, causing the white linen tablecloth beneath her hands to faintly smoke.
She violently slammed the heavy leather menu shut with a resounding thud that echoed across the quiet jazz-filled dining room.
The live quartet of musicians stumbled slightly on their notes, and the head maître d’ instantly stiffened, sweating nervously as he looked at the furious crimson-haired heiress.
"Is... is there an issue with the selections, Lady Bloom?" the maître d’ asked with a trembling, nervous bow.
Seraphina looked up at the man, her crimson eyes burning with the terrifying, unyielding wrath of House Bloom’s ancestral flame.

"Yes, there is a severe, unforgivable issue," Seraphina demanded, her melodic voice cutting through the restaurant like a freshly honed blade. "I am looking for the premier dish for my prospective consort... so explain to me right now: Why the absolute hell is Seasoned Medium-Rare Basilisk Steak with Garlic Butter and Spicy Roasted Noodles not on your menu?!"
The head maître d’ of The Celestial Zenith stood frozen.
His starched white silk tailcoat remained impeccably aligned, but a single prominent bead of cold sweat rolled down the side of his pale temple, glistening under the ambient golden mana-lights.
His eyes darted from the smoking indentation on the linen where Seraphina’s flame had scorched the fibers, up to the blazing, unforgiving crimson irises of the Bloom family heiress.

"M-Medium-rare Basilisk Steak... with garlic butter and spicy roasted noodles, my Lady?" the maître d’ repeated, his voice cracking into a thin breathless tone before he cleared his throat in desperate survival mode. "A-A thousand pardons, Lady Bloom! The Celestial Zenith prides itself on adhering strictly to the haute culinary traditions of the Western Spires, but... but the sovereign palate of House Bloom takes unconditional precedence over our standard repertoire!"
He bowed so deeply from the waist that the silver watch-chain pinned to his vest swung freely in mid-air.

"I shall personally descend to the Grand Cold-Vaults immediately," the maître d’ stammered, his mind racing in wild frantic circles. ’Why in the name of the High Council does a noble house want a barbaric, low-tier meal like that?! Is this a trial? A secret audit?!’
He forced his most charming subservient smile back onto his face.

"We maintain whole Tier 3 preserved Shadow-Basilisk loins harvested from the Abyssal Trenches for specialized alchemical reductions... Our executive chef, Master Bartholomew, shall hand-carve the tenderloin, whip a clarified solar-garlic emulsion, and hand-pull the finest fire-spiced vermicelli noodles to your exact divine specifications. It shall be our signature off-menu masterpiece for the evening!"
Seraphina raised her chin, her haughty noble composure settling back over her breathtaking features like a mantle of cooled volcanic glass.
She smoothed the front of her crimson phoenix-silk gown, giving the trembling maître d’ a slow, dismissive wave of her manicured hand.

"Acceptable," Seraphina declared, her melodic voice oozing with refined, aristocratic magnanimity. "Ensure the spice balance is assertive, but do not allow the capsaicin to overwhelm the natural flavor of the meat. My consort has an exceptionally discerning palate."
"Right away, Lady Bloom! Right away!" the maître d’ chorused, rapidly scribbling notes onto his floating holographic ledger.
Silas sat dead center in the curved velvet booth, his large hands resting flat against his denim-clad thighs as he stared at Seraphina with a look of bewilderment.
’Consort? Discerning palate?’ Silas thought. ’Is she trying to order what I told her was my favorite food?’
That was kind of cute... but he didn’t have a favorite food in the first place, different kinds of food in this world were great and he hadn’t tasted enough to have an opinion.
Yet, as he looked at the proud focused gleam in Seraphina’s red eyes, Silas kept his mouth firmly shut.
The girl looked as if she had just successfully negotiated a planetary peace treaty.
To shatter her illusion now would only invite another sixty minutes of screaming, flame aura flare-ups, and structural property damage.
"And for the rest of the table?" the maître d’ asked, turning toward Harper and Silas while doing his absolute best to keep his knees from trembling.
Silas reluctantly picked up his leather-bound menu folio.
He flipped open the heavy vellum pages, scanning the itemized price listings beside the various appetizers and side dishes.
’Lunar-Crab Tartare: 85,000 SC.’
[’Smoked Astral Truffle Medley: 140,000 SC.’
’Crystal-Chilled Spring Nectar: 35,000 SC per glass.’
A deep violent twitch seized Silas’s left eyelid. His heart physically ached.
His instincts rebelled furiously against the vulgar absurdity of it all.

’Eighty-five thousand credits for raw crab meat the size of a golf ball,’ Silas cursed silently, taking a slow deep breath through his nose to steady his blood pressure. ’I am going to eat every single garnish on that plate... I will chew the decorative flowers and I will lick the porcelain clean too.’
After all, who wouldn’t with these kind of prices?
He looked up at the maître d’, locking his jaw into a grim stoic line.
"Bring a side of the smoked truffle medley and a pitcher of the chilled spring nectar. And make the basilisk portion large."
"Splendid choices, Lord Graves!" the maître d’ beamed.
Harper, sitting cozily beside Silas with her athletic thigh pressing firmly against his denim, casually tossed her menu down with a confident high-energy grin.

"Give me the whole-roasted solar-wyvern tenderloin," Harper ordered enthusiastically, pointing at a high-tier dish near the back of the folio. "Medium-rare, extra char on the exterior crust, and double the roasted mana-potatoes... Oh, and bring a bottle of the 84-vintage Sparkling Void-Berry Reserve. We’re celebrating a successful first phase today!"
"An exceptional vintage, Lady Whitmore!" the maître d’ praised, his quill blurring across the glowing parchment.
He closed his ledger with a sharp click, bowed low to the three seated Lords, and then turned toward the entrance of the private pavilion.
Standing stiffly beside the transparent glass double doors was Reginald.
The elderly butler remained perfectly upright, his hands clasped behind the small of his back, his sharp eyes surveying the perimeter with the cold detached vigilance of a dormant war golem.

"Pardon the intrusion, sir," the maître d’ murmured respectfully, stepping up to the elderly man. "May the kitchen prepare a beverage or a light course for yourself while you attend to the young masters?"
Reginald didn’t even blink.
He tilted his head a fraction of an inch. "I require nothing. Proceed with the young masters’ service."

"Of course, sir. Right away." The maître d’ bowed once more, spinning on his polished leather heels and practically sprinting toward the private service elevators to deliver the emergency custom ticket to the kitchen.
The quiet plush pavilion settled into a tranquil lull, accompanied only by the smooth rhythm of the jazz quartet playing in the far corner.

Outside the panoramic floor-to-ceiling glass, the skyline of Valoria City began to ignite with millions of neon lights, the golden rays of the setting sun bleeding into deep bruised purples and indigos along the horizon.
Seraphina rested her delicate elbows on the tablecloth, interlacing her slender manicured fingers beneath her chin.
She tilted her head, her crimson eyes sweeping across the opulent crystal fixtures, the private skyline view, and the plush velvet seating before locking onto Harper.

"So," Seraphina began, her melodic voice carrying an inquisitive noble lilt. "Explain the tactical objective of this phase. We have concluded the apparel acquisition so what is the fundamental purpose of sitting in a glass box waiting for sustenance?"
Harper let out an amused, slightly patronizing chuckle, leaning her shoulder back against the velvet cushion.

"It’s called the Conversation Phase, Princess," Harper explained, gesturing with her open palm. "A date isn’t just about buying expensive gear... It’s about creating a low-stress, intimate environment where two people can actually communicate, drop their public masks, and learn about each other’s personalities, backgrounds, and personal preferences. You know... normal human interaction?"
Seraphina’s eyes flashed with a spark of sudden comprehension as she nodded her head with intense, serious gravity.
"I see," Seraphina said firmly. "A strategic intelligence exchange... Very well. I shall initiate the briefing."
Silas raised an eyebrow. "The briefing?"
Before Silas or Harper could utter another word, Seraphina straightened her posture until her spine was locked into a rigid vertical line.
She smoothed the front of her phoenix-silk gown, cleared her throat, and looked directly into Silas’s eyes as if she were addressing a high-ranking plenary tribunal of the World Alliance.

"Fine. If you want to know about me, then listen closely," Seraphina declared with her voice sounding sharp and commanding. "I am eighteen and my core is Purple. I eat properly... high-quality rift beast proteins and organic elven produce. I don’t like rain, poorly insulated mana conduits, or vulgar commoners who interrupt me."
Harper’s mouth slowly dropped open in bewildered disbelief however Seraphina didn’t pause for breath.

"I require a minimum of four dedicated domestic staff members to maintain my wardrobe," she continued, ticking off points on her manicured fingers. "And I have decided that I prefer men with long, flowing dark hair... So you will grow yours out, Silas. That is not a request."
Silas stared at her, entirely deadpan. "I am not growing a ponytail, Seraphina."
"It is a non-negotiable spousal preference!" Seraphina insisted sharply, her cheeks already beginning to flush. "And I do not tolerate infidelity or tardiness or unverified financial expenditures."
She paused.
Her voice faltered slightly.
A violent crimson blush swept up her porcelain neck, painting her cheeks and the tips of her delicate ears in brilliant burning red.
She looked down at the white tablecloth with her manicured fingers tightly clutching her linen napkin.

"As for... the other part," Seraphina mumbled, her voice dropping into a tiny high-pitched squeak that was barely audible over the jazz music. "I... I haven’t done that before. My mother gave me some... alarming books before I left, but I find the whole thing deeply overwhelming. So if we... if we get married... you’ll have to be patient with me. That’s all I’m saying."

sentences.text: SWISH!
The head maître d’ approached the table with quiet practiced elegance.
Resting across his forearms were three colossal leather-bound menu folios embossed with solid platinum lettering that looked more like ancient heavy encyclopedia volumes than food menus.
He gracefully set one massive book in front of each guest, bowing low.
"Welcome to The Celestial Zenith," the maître d’ spoke with deep melodious reverence.
"Our executive culinary masters have curated the finest grade-AAA dimensional delicacies for your pleasure today.
We have abyssal caviar harvested from the deep rift trenches, gold-leaf-crusted celestial wyvern tenderloins, and thousand-year aged mana-truffles imported directly from the elven enclaves...
Please, take your time, and let us know whenever you are prepared to feast."
"Thank you," Harper chirped, flipping her massive menu open with excitement.
Across the table, Seraphina’s crimson eyes suddenly ignited with a brilliant, predatory spark of inspiration.
’This is it!’ Seraphina realized in a flash of pure triumph with her pulse quickening. ’This is my redemption!
Silas said people learn about each other on dates... and he specifically tested me on his favorite food earlier and he told me during one of our clothing sessions!
If I take complete control of the order and request his favorite meal without him having to utter a single word, it will prove that I truly care about him and pay attention to his needs!’
Filled with soaring confidence, Seraphina flipped open the heavy, leather-bound folio.
Her sharp crimson eyes scanned the gilded pages.
’Page 1: Pan-Seared Astral Leviathan Cheek with Saffron Foam - 120,000 SC.’
’Page 2: Braised Abyssal Drake Ribs in Mana-Infused Truffle Glaze - 250,000 SC.’
’Page 3: Golden Phoenix-Egg Soufflé with Lunar Honey - 95,000 SC.’
Seraphina frowned slightly and she turned the page.
’Page 4: Glazed Shadow-Stalker Loin with Crystal-Spiced Asparagus - 180,000 SC.’
’Page 5: Poached Silver-Scale Wyrm Fillet in White Mana-Wine - 310,000 SC.’
Her brow furrowed deeper.
She rapidly flipped through the meat sections, the poultry sections, the specialty soups, and the regional delicacies.
She flipped to the back then to the appetizers and then to the chef’s private reserve.
It wasn’t there.
...Not a single line.
There was not a single mention.
Seraphina’s jaw tightened.
Her lips thinned into a razor-sharp, furious line as a dangerous suffocating wave of heat began to radiate from her skin, causing the white linen tablecloth beneath her hands to faintly smoke.
She violently slammed the heavy leather menu shut with a resounding thud that echoed across the quiet jazz-filled dining room.
The live quartet of musicians stumbled slightly on their notes, and the head maître d’ instantly stiffened, sweating nervously as he looked at the furious crimson-haired heiress.
"Is... is there an issue with the selections, Lady Bloom?" the maître d’ asked with a trembling, nervous bow.
Seraphina looked up at the man, her crimson eyes burning with the terrifying, unyielding wrath of House Bloom’s ancestral flame.
"Yes, there is a severe, unforgivable issue," Seraphina demanded, her melodic voice cutting through the restaurant like a freshly honed blade.

"I am looking for the premier dish for my prospective consort... so explain to me right now: Why the absolute hell is Seasoned Medium-Rare Basilisk Steak with Garlic Butter and Spicy Roasted Noodles not on your menu?!"
The head maître d’ of The Celestial Zenith stood frozen.
His starched white silk tailcoat remained impeccably aligned, but a single prominent bead of cold sweat rolled down the side of his pale temple, glistening under the ambient golden mana-lights.
His eyes darted from the smoking indentation on the linen where Seraphina’s flame had scorched the fibers, up to the blazing, unforgiving crimson irises of the Bloom family heiress.

"M-Medium-rare Basilisk Steak... with garlic butter and spicy roasted noodles, my Lady?" the maître d’ repeated, his voice cracking into a thin breathless tone before he cleared his throat in desperate survival mode.
"A-A thousand pardons, Lady Bloom!

The Celestial Zenith prides itself on adhering strictly to the haute culinary traditions of the Western Spires, but... but the sovereign palate of House Bloom takes unconditional precedence over our standard repertoire!"
He bowed so deeply from the waist that the silver watch-chain pinned to his vest swung freely in mid-air.

"I shall personally descend to the Grand Cold-Vaults immediately," the maître d’ stammered, his mind racing in wild frantic circles. ’Why in the name of the High Council does a noble house want a barbaric, low-tier meal like that?!
Is this a trial?
A secret audit?!’
He forced his most charming subservient smile back onto his face.
"We maintain whole Tier 3 preserved Shadow-Basilisk loins harvested from the Abyssal Trenches for specialized alchemical reductions...

Our executive chef, Master Bartholomew, shall hand-carve the tenderloin, whip a clarified solar-garlic emulsion, and hand-pull the finest fire-spiced vermicelli noodles to your exact divine specifications.
It shall be our signature off-menu masterpiece for the evening!"
Seraphina raised her chin, her haughty noble composure settling back over her breathtaking features like a mantle of cooled volcanic glass.
She smoothed the front of her crimson phoenix-silk gown, giving the trembling maître d’ a slow, dismissive wave of her manicured hand.
"Acceptable," Seraphina declared, her melodic voice oozing with refined, aristocratic magnanimity.
"Ensure the spice balance is assertive, but do not allow the capsaicin to overwhelm the natural flavor of the meat.
My consort has an exceptionally discerning palate."
"Right away, Lady Bloom!
Right away!" the maître d’ chorused, rapidly scribbling notes onto his floating holographic ledger.
Silas sat dead center in the curved velvet booth, his large hands resting flat against his denim-clad thighs as he stared at Seraphina with a look of bewilderment.
’Consort?
Discerning palate?’ Silas thought. ’Is she trying to order what I told her was my favorite food?’
That was kind of cute... but he didn’t have a favorite food in the first place, different kinds of food in this world were great and he hadn’t tasted enough to have an opinion.
Yet, as he looked at the proud focused gleam in Seraphina’s red eyes, Silas kept his mouth firmly shut.
The girl looked as if she had just successfully negotiated a planetary peace treaty.
To shatter her illusion now would only invite another sixty minutes of screaming, flame aura flare-ups, and structural property damage.
"And for the rest of the table?" the maître d’ asked, turning toward Harper and Silas while doing his absolute best to keep his knees from trembling.
Silas reluctantly picked up his leather-bound menu folio.
He flipped open the heavy vellum pages, scanning the itemized price listings beside the various appetizers and side dishes.
’Lunar-Crab Tartare: 85,000 SC.’
[’Smoked Astral Truffle Medley: 140,000 SC.’
’Crystal-Chilled Spring Nectar: 35,000 SC per glass.’
A deep violent twitch seized Silas’s left eyelid.
His heart physically ached.
His instincts rebelled furiously against the vulgar absurdity of it all.

’Eighty-five thousand credits for raw crab meat the size of a golf ball,’ Silas cursed silently, taking a slow deep breath through his nose to steady his blood pressure. ’I am going to eat every single garnish on that plate...
I will chew the decorative flowers and I will lick the porcelain clean too.’
After all, who wouldn’t with these kind of prices?
He looked up at the maître d’, locking his jaw into a grim stoic line.
"Bring a side of the smoked truffle medley and a pitcher of the chilled spring nectar.

Standing stiffly beside the transparent glass double doors was Reginald.

chapters.title: Chapter 388: Feed Me... I Feed You!
paragraphs: The table went agonizingly silent.
Silas sat completely frozen with his brain working overtime to process the fact that the terrifying, flame-wielding heiress of House Bloom had just submitted a presentation on her own virginity.
Beside him, Harper’s shoulders began to shake.
A quiet muffled snort escaped Harper’s lips. She clapped both of her hands over her mouth, but it was entirely futile.
"PFFFFFT... HAHAHAHAHAHA!"
Harper threw her head back against the velvet cushions, exploding into a loud tear-inducing roar of pure laughter that echoed across the entire top floor of the restaurant.

"OH, SO YOU’RE NOT EXPERIENCED?" Harper cackled, clutching her stomach as her violet hair bounced wildly. "Holy shit! We can literally see it... but still... Who talks like that on a date?! Are you submitting an environmental impact report or trying to get a boyfriend?!"

"SILENCE, YOU SHAMELESS VULGAR HARPY!" Seraphina shrieked, slamming her palms onto the table as her crimson aura flared violently, threatening to set the floral centerpiece ablaze. "I AM PROVIDING FULL TRANSPARENCY! IT IS THE HEIGHT OF NOBLE EFFICIENCY! I WILL INCINERATE YOUR ENTIRE SKULL!"
"Try it, Princess! Let’s see if you can stop a lightning bolt!" Harper wheezed, wiping a genuine tear of laughter from her eye.
"Both of you, shut up," Silas commanded, his deep voice cutting through the brewing magical explosion with effortless authority.
Both women snapped their heads toward him, freezing instantly.
Silas rubbed the bridge of his nose, letting out a slow, tired exhale.

"Seraphina. Take a breath. Harper is obnoxious, but she’s right about one thing: a date isn’t an interrogation or an audit... You don’t hand people a list of demands and biometric stats. You just... talk like normal people."
Seraphina’s crimson eyes blinked rapidly, the fiery aura receding as her blush deepened in genuine mortification.
"Normal... people?"
"Yeah," Harper chimed in, leaning forward and resting her chin in her hands, her mocking tone softening into something surprisingly grounded.

"You ask questions. You talk about stuff that happened during your week. You ask Silas why he always looks like he wants to sleep for three months straight, or what kind of music he likes, or how he deals with his little sister when she acts like a brat."
Seraphina looked between Harper and Silas, her haughty expression giving way to a rare vulnerable curiosity.
She slowly unclasped her hands from the napkin, resting them neatly on the table.
"I... see," Seraphina murmured softly. She looked directly at Silas, her eyes softening. "Then... Silas. What was your life like before you entered the Sovereign Realm? In the lower ward?"
’Does she really have to ask about this?’
Silas paused, his golden-ringed blue eyes reflecting the flickering candlelight between them.
For the next twenty minutes, the tense volatile atmosphere of noble rivalry melted into something remarkably natural.

Silas spoke in a quiet steady tone about the reality of growing up in Sector 4... the daily grind of the scrap yards, the harsh winters where the heating wards failed, and the exhausting stubbornness required to keep Lia fed, clothed, and a lot more like life in the Academy too.

Harper listened with genuine quiet empathy, sharing stories of her own grueling, high-voltage training regimens under her father’s strict military instructors, where a single misstep meant taking thousands of volts through her central nervous system.

Even Seraphina dropped her arrogant noble facade, speaking candidly about the suffocating pressure of being House Bloom’s favorite heir... the constant political surveillance, the endless stream of arrogant suitors trying to use her bloodline for corporate leverage, and the terrifying psychotic expectations set by her mother, Lady Etilga.
For the first time since the afternoon had begun, they weren’t screaming, competing, or threatening to level a city block.
They were just three young powerful individuals who carried the crushing weight of their world on their shoulders, finding a rare moment of peace above the glowing clouds of Valoria City.
CLINK!
The soft elegant chime of a silver dome cover lifting broke the quiet reverie.
The tempo of the elven jazz quartet in the corner subtly shifted, building into a grand, celebratory crescendo as the service doors swung wide.

A procession of eight waitstaff in pristine white tailcoats marched into the private pavilion, led by the head maître d’ and a portly, red-faced man in a towering white chef’s toque... Master Bartholomew, the executive culinary master of The Celestial Zenith himself.
"Presenting the evening’s bespoke culinary showcase," the maître d’ announced with sweeping theatrical flair.
Silver platters were lowered onto the table with synchronized, micrometer precision.

First came Harper’s dish... It was a massive perfectly charred solar-wyvern tenderloin, sliced into thick succulent medallions that hissed with residual heat, resting atop a bed of golden, cream-whipped mana-potatoes and drizzled with a rich, ruby-colored demi-glace.

Next came Silas’s side selections... the smoked astral truffle medley, which released an intoxicating earthy aroma of oak and ancient moss, accompanied by crystal goblets filled with effervescent, glowing azure spring nectar.
Finally, Master Bartholomew stepped forward personally.
With trembling, reverent hands, the head chef lifted a massive, solid-silver cloche from the central platter directly in front of Seraphina and Silas.
FWOOSH!
A heavenly plume of fragrant steam exploded into the air, instantly overwhelming the delicate floral scents of the restaurant.
Resting on a colossal platter of hand-carved black obsidian was a massive, two-pound cut of high grade Shadow-Basilisk loin.

The exterior was crusted in a coarse aromatic blend of crushed peppercorns and dried volcanic sea salt, seared to a flawless glistening medium-rare with a deep pink center that practically wept with rich flavorful juices.
Melting over the top of the hot steak was a generous golden pool of solar-garlic herb butter, bubbling softly and cascading down the sides of the meat.

Surrounding the steak was a generous mountain of thick hand-pulled vermicelli noodles, tossed in a glistening, deep-crimson fire-chili oil, garnished with crispy fried scallions, toasted sesame seeds, and crushed spirit-peanuts.
The presentation was rustic and utterly magnificent... a high-society tribute to the bounty of a dungeon hunt.

"Shadow-Basilisk Loin, hand-seared over imported volcanic embers," Master Bartholomew announced, bowing so low his chef’s toque nearly brushed the table. "Paired with hand-pulled spicy rift-vermicelli and churned solar-garlic butter. Prepared exclusively for the sovereign pleasure of House Bloom and Lord Graves..."
Seraphina’s crimson eyes glittered with pure, triumphant joy. "Magnificent work, Chef."
"A thousand honors, Lady Bloom!" Bartholomew breathed, practically crying with relief as he and the waitstaff bowed in unison and retreated toward the service station.
Harper didn’t wait a single second.
She snatched her gold-plated fork and knife, expertly carving off a thick, juicy piece of the solar-wyvern tenderloin. She popped the meat into her mouth, chewing enthusiastically.
Her violet eyes rolled back in pure bliss.

"Mmmmph!" Harper groaned, slamming her fist lightly against the table. "Holy hell, that’s good! The char on the crust is completely insane! Silas, you have to try this wyvern meat, it literally melts on your tongue!"
Across the table, Seraphina picked up her own silver fork.

She delicately sliced a small, tender piece of the Basilisk steak, ensuring it was generously coated in the melted garlic butter and a few strands of the spicy roasted noodles, and lifted it to her lips.
She took a bite.
The intense richness of the dense monster protein exploded across her palate, perfectly balanced by the aromatic punch of the roasted garlic and the fiery, addictive heat of the chili-spiced noodles.
It was bold, hearty, and packed with an undeniable flavor that completely eclipsed the delicate, flavorless foams typical of noble cuisine.

"It is... extraordinary," Seraphina voiced her approval, her eyes lighting up with genuine delight. "The texture is remarkably firm, yet effortlessly succulent. The spice carries an exceptional kinetic resonance."
Hearing the noblewoman’s praise, the head maître d’ and Master Bartholomew, who were watching anxiously from the kitchen corridor, practically collapsed into each other’s arms in tearful celebration.
Silas reached for his own fork, carving off a generous slice of the steak and taking a massive bite of the spicy noodles alongside it.
The meat was tender, rich, and bursting with flavor.
The noodles had the perfect chewy snap, coated in a deep, layered chili oil that left a pleasant, tingling burn across his tongue.
It was, without question, the most flawless piece of cooked meat Silas had ever tasted on Earth.
Yet, as Silas chewed, an amused thought crossed his mind.
’It’s good. Really damn good,’ Silas thought, a fond smirk touching the corner of his lips. ’The ingredients cost more than an apartment building... but honestly? I still prefer Martha’s cooking.’
Before Silas could take a second bite, the rustle of silk drew his attention across the table.
Seraphina had stood up slightly from her seat.
She leaned gracefully across the white linen tablecloth, her plunging crimson neckline dipping daringly low as she held out a silver fork.
Speared on the tines was a perfectly cut, glistening piece of medium-rare basilisk steak, dripping with golden garlic butter and twirled with spicy noodles.
A deep radiant blush covered her cheeks, but she held her chin high, looking directly into his golden-ringed blue eyes.

"Silas," Seraphina commanded softly, her melodic voice trembling with a mixture of immense pride and nervous vulnerability. "Open your mouth... As your prospective wife, it is my ancestral duty to ensure you are properly nourished with your favorite dish."
Silas blinked, staring at the hovering fork. "Seraphina, I have two functional hands and my own fork."
"Silas Graves," Seraphina hissed, her red eyes narrowing in desperate blushing insistence. "Do not disgrace my offering in front of the waitstaff... Eat it."
Silas let out a defeated breath, leaning forward and accepting the bite from her fork.
The rich savory meat and spicy noodles filled his mouth, the intense flavors bursting across his palate.
He chewed and swallowed, giving her a slow, approving nod. "It’s great. Thank you."
Seraphina let out a breathless triumphant gasp, her entire face glowing with ecstasy as she settled back into her seat like an empress who had just conquered a new continent.
"Oh, hell no!" Harper’s voice cut in instantly.
Before Silas could even turn his head, Harper leaned her entire body against his side, spearing a massive steaming chunk of solar-wyvern tenderloin and shoving the fork directly against his lips.

"My turn!" Harper declared boldly, her violet eyes flashing with fierce competitive fire. "Wyvern meat has three times the kinetic mana density of basilisk! Open up, handsome, you need protein for endurance!"
Silas stared at the giant piece of wyvern meat hovering an inch from his nose.
Knowing that refusing would only trigger another round of screaming, he opened his mouth and took the tenderloin straight off her fork.
The wyvern was incredible... smoky, intensely savory, with a delicate citrus undertone that cut through the richness.
"Amazing," Silas muttered, chewing steadily.
"Hah! See?!" Harper gloated, shooting Seraphina an insufferably smug wink. "He liked mine better!"
"He did not, you unrefined woman!" Seraphina snapped. "Basilisk is his designated preference!"
Silas rolled his eyes, picking up his own fork.
He carved two generous portions from the central platter, spearing a piece of truffle-crusted meat on one fork and a forkful of spicy basilisk on the other.
"Here," Silas said flatly, holding one fork out toward Harper and the other across the table toward Seraphina. "Eat, and stop arguing before the food gets cold."
Both girls froze.
Harper’s jaw dropped slightly, a sudden bright pink blush rushing across her cheeks as she leaned in and gently bit the truffle meat from his fork, humming softly with immense satisfaction.
Across the table, Seraphina’s eyes widened into saucers. She looked at the offering as if Silas had just handed her a divine imperial scepter.
Her heart fluttered violently against her ribs as she leaned forward, delicately parting her glossed lips to accept the spicy basilisk bite from his hand.
"It... it is exceptionally flavorful," Seraphina whispered, clutching her chest as she swallowed, her crimson eyes locked on his face with starry-eyed adoration.
Standing quietly at the pavilion threshold, Reginald adjusted his gold-rimmed spectacles.
The veteran butler pulled his leather-bound surveillance journal from his coat pocket, clicked his pen, and meticulously wrote down his latest observation in elegant script.
’Haah... what a vibe it is to be young.’
Forty-five minutes later, the colossal feast was reduced to empty, polished silver platters.
