Even Seraphina dropped her arrogant noble facade, speaking candidly about the suffocating pressure of being House Bloom’s favorite heir... the constant political surveillance, the endless stream of arrogant suitors trying to use her bloodline for corporate leverage, and the terrifying psychotic expectations set by her mother, Lady Etilga.
For the first time since the afternoon had begun, they weren’t screaming, competing, or threatening to level a city block.
They were just three young powerful individuals who carried the crushing weight of their world on their shoulders, finding a rare moment of peace above the glowing clouds of Valoria City.
CLINK!
The soft elegant chime of a silver dome cover lifting broke the quiet reverie.
The tempo of the elven jazz quartet in the corner subtly shifted, building into a grand, celebratory crescendo as the service doors swung wide.
A procession of eight waitstaff in pristine white tailcoats marched into the private pavilion, led by the head maître d’ and a portly, red-faced man in a towering white chef’s toque...
Master Bartholomew, the executive culinary master of The Celestial Zenith himself.
"Presenting the evening’s bespoke culinary showcase," the maître d’ announced with sweeping theatrical flair.
Silver platters were lowered onto the table with synchronized, micrometer precision.
First came Harper’s dish...

It was a massive perfectly charred solar-wyvern tenderloin, sliced into thick succulent medallions that hissed with residual heat, resting atop a bed of golden, cream-whipped mana-potatoes and drizzled with a rich, ruby-colored demi-glace.

Next came Silas’s side selections... the smoked astral truffle medley, which released an intoxicating earthy aroma of oak and ancient moss, accompanied by crystal goblets filled with effervescent, glowing azure spring nectar.
Finally, Master Bartholomew stepped forward personally.
With trembling, reverent hands, the head chef lifted a massive, solid-silver cloche from the central platter directly in front of Seraphina and Silas.
FWOOSH!
A heavenly plume of fragrant steam exploded into the air, instantly overwhelming the delicate floral scents of the restaurant.
Resting on a colossal platter of hand-carved black obsidian was a massive, two-pound cut of high grade Shadow-Basilisk loin.

The exterior was crusted in a coarse aromatic blend of crushed peppercorns and dried volcanic sea salt, seared to a flawless glistening medium-rare with a deep pink center that practically wept with rich flavorful juices.
Melting over the top of the hot steak was a generous golden pool of solar-garlic herb butter, bubbling softly and cascading down the sides of the meat.

Surrounding the steak was a generous mountain of thick hand-pulled vermicelli noodles, tossed in a glistening, deep-crimson fire-chili oil, garnished with crispy fried scallions, toasted sesame seeds, and crushed spirit-peanuts.
The presentation was rustic and utterly magnificent... a high-society tribute to the bounty of a dungeon hunt.
"Shadow-Basilisk Loin, hand-seared over imported volcanic embers," Master Bartholomew announced, bowing so low his chef’s toque nearly brushed the table.
"Paired with hand-pulled spicy rift-vermicelli and churned solar-garlic butter.
Prepared exclusively for the sovereign pleasure of House Bloom and Lord Graves..."
Seraphina’s crimson eyes glittered with pure, triumphant joy.
"Magnificent work, Chef."
"A thousand honors, Lady Bloom!" Bartholomew breathed, practically crying with relief as he and the waitstaff bowed in unison and retreated toward the service station.
Harper didn’t wait a single second.
She snatched her gold-plated fork and knife, expertly carving off a thick, juicy piece of the solar-wyvern tenderloin.
She popped the meat into her mouth, chewing enthusiastically.
Her violet eyes rolled back in pure bliss.
"Mmmmph!" Harper groaned, slamming her fist lightly against the table.
"Holy hell, that’s good!
The char on the crust is completely insane!
Silas, you have to try this wyvern meat, it literally melts on your tongue!"
Across the table, Seraphina picked up her own silver fork.

She delicately sliced a small, tender piece of the Basilisk steak, ensuring it was generously coated in the melted garlic butter and a few strands of the spicy roasted noodles, and lifted it to her lips.
She took a bite.
The intense richness of the dense monster protein exploded across her palate, perfectly balanced by the aromatic punch of the roasted garlic and the fiery, addictive heat of the chili-spiced noodles.
It was bold, hearty, and packed with an undeniable flavor that completely eclipsed the delicate, flavorless foams typical of noble cuisine.
"It is... extraordinary," Seraphina voiced her approval, her eyes lighting up with genuine delight.
"The texture is remarkably firm, yet effortlessly succulent.
The spice carries an exceptional kinetic resonance."
Hearing the noblewoman’s praise, the head maître d’ and Master Bartholomew, who were watching anxiously from the kitchen corridor, practically collapsed into each other’s arms in tearful celebration.
Silas reached for his own fork, carving off a generous slice of the steak and taking a massive bite of the spicy noodles alongside it.
The meat was tender, rich, and bursting with flavor.
The noodles had the perfect chewy snap, coated in a deep, layered chili oil that left a pleasant, tingling burn across his tongue.
It was, without question, the most flawless piece of cooked meat Silas had ever tasted on Earth.
Yet, as Silas chewed, an amused thought crossed his mind.
’It’s good.
Really damn good,’ Silas thought, a fond smirk touching the corner of his lips. ’The ingredients cost more than an apartment building... but honestly?
I still prefer Martha’s cooking.’
Before Silas could take a second bite, the rustle of silk drew his attention across the table.
Seraphina had stood up slightly from her seat.
She leaned gracefully across the white linen tablecloth, her plunging crimson neckline dipping daringly low as she held out a silver fork.
Speared on the tines was a perfectly cut, glistening piece of medium-rare basilisk steak, dripping with golden garlic butter and twirled with spicy noodles.
A deep radiant blush covered her cheeks, but she held her chin high, looking directly into his golden-ringed blue eyes.
"Silas," Seraphina commanded softly, her melodic voice trembling with a mixture of immense pride and nervous vulnerability.
"Open your mouth...
As your prospective wife, it is my ancestral duty to ensure you are properly nourished with your favorite dish."
Silas blinked, staring at the hovering fork.
"Seraphina, I have two functional hands and my own fork."
"Silas Graves," Seraphina hissed, her red eyes narrowing in desperate blushing insistence.
"Do not disgrace my offering in front of the waitstaff...
Eat it."
Silas let out a defeated breath, leaning forward and accepting the bite from her fork.
The rich savory meat and spicy noodles filled his mouth, the intense flavors bursting across his palate.
He chewed and swallowed, giving her a slow, approving nod.
"It’s great.
Thank you."
Seraphina let out a breathless triumphant gasp, her entire face glowing with ecstasy as she settled back into her seat like an empress who had just conquered a new continent.
"Oh, hell no!" Harper’s voice cut in instantly.
Before Silas could even turn his head, Harper leaned her entire body against his side, spearing a massive steaming chunk of solar-wyvern tenderloin and shoving the fork directly against his lips.
"My turn!" Harper declared boldly, her violet eyes flashing with fierce competitive fire.
"Wyvern meat has three times the kinetic mana density of basilisk!
Open up, handsome, you need protein for endurance!"
Silas stared at the giant piece of wyvern meat hovering an inch from his nose.
Knowing that refusing would only trigger another round of screaming, he opened his mouth and took the tenderloin straight off her fork.
The wyvern was incredible... smoky, intensely savory, with a delicate citrus undertone that cut through the richness.
"Amazing," Silas muttered, chewing steadily.
"Hah!
See?!" Harper gloated, shooting Seraphina an insufferably smug wink.
"He liked mine better!"
"He did not, you unrefined woman!" Seraphina snapped.
"Basilisk is his designated preference!"
Silas rolled his eyes, picking up his own fork.
He carved two generous portions from the central platter, spearing a piece of truffle-crusted meat on one fork and a forkful of spicy basilisk on the other.
"Here," Silas said flatly, holding one fork out toward Harper and the other across the table toward Seraphina.
"Eat, and stop arguing before the food gets cold."
Both girls froze.
Harper’s jaw dropped slightly, a sudden bright pink blush rushing across her cheeks as she leaned in and gently bit the truffle meat from his fork, humming softly with immense satisfaction.
Across the table, Seraphina’s eyes widened into saucers.
She looked at the offering as if Silas had just handed her a divine imperial scepter.
Her heart fluttered violently against her ribs as she leaned forward, delicately parting her glossed lips to accept the spicy basilisk bite from his hand.
"It... it is exceptionally flavorful," Seraphina whispered, clutching her chest as she swallowed, her crimson eyes locked on his face with starry-eyed adoration.
Standing quietly at the pavilion threshold, Reginald adjusted his gold-rimmed spectacles.
The veteran butler pulled his leather-bound surveillance journal from his coat pocket, clicked his pen, and meticulously wrote down his latest observation in elegant script.
’Haah... what a vibe it is to be young.’
Forty-five minutes later, the colossal feast was reduced to empty, polished silver platters.

chapters.title: Chapter 389: Suite Primus
paragraphs: Harper leaned back against the plush velvet cushions, resting a contented hand over her flat toned stomach as she let out a long satisfied sigh.

"Man..." Harper groaned, rolling her shoulders. "I could honestly eat another entire plate of those roasted mana-potatoes... but we can’t afford to fall behind schedule. Phase Three waits for no one!"
Across the table, Seraphina sat with pristine noble poise.
In reality, her stomach was completely stuffed to maximum capacity... she had eaten three times her normal aristocratic portion just to ensure she didn’t leave a single scrap behind Harper.
"I concur," Seraphina stated smoothly, dabbing the corners of her mouth with her linen napkin. "A disciplined noblewoman understands the importance of temporal punctuality. I am ready to proceed."
SWISH!
The head maître d’ glided silently up to the table, holding a sleek, silver tray containing the finalized, leather-bound bill folio. He placed it gently in the center of the table, bowing low.
"Whenever you are prepared, esteemed guests," the maître d’ murmured.
Harper immediately reached into the pocket of her tailored trousers, pulling out her black corporate platinum card.
"Put it on House Whitmore’s—"
"Hold your hand, commoner!" Seraphina interrupted, her voice ringing with haughty authority as she raised her palm.
Harper frowned, turning her head. "What now, Princess? You gonna check your empty pockets again?"
Seraphina sneered, her crimson eyes flashing with triumphant disdain.
"I do not require liquid plastic cards to settle a basic dining ledger," Seraphina stated coldly.
She looked up at the maître d’, projecting the full unyielding weight of her ancestral lineage.

"Charge this entire balance directly to the primary corporate line of House Bloom... Tag the invoice under my personal authorization code: Crimson-Sovereign-77. Once I return to the Bloom Manor this evening, the family treasury will wire the funds in full, alongside a fifty-percent sovereign gratuity for Master Bartholomew’s kitchen staff."
The maître d’ froze. His eyes bulged as the numerical reality of a fifty-percent tip on a multi-million-credit bill processed in his mind.

"H-House Bloom’s direct corporate line?!" the maître d’ gasped, his voice trembling with hysterical joy. "With a fifty-percent sovereign gratuity?! Lady Bloom, you are the living embodiment of grace and celestial benevolence! May the ancestral flames forever illuminate your noble house!"
The maître d’ snatched the bill folio, bowing so low his nose practically touched his knees, and sprinted away down the corridor singing her praises at the top of his lungs.
Harper clicked her tongue in profound irritation, aggressively shoving her platinum card back into her pocket.
"Tch... Show-off."
Seraphina smirked, leaning back and resting her chin in her hand. "It is not showing off, Harper Whitmore. It is simply the undeniable reality of sovereign nobility."
Silas watched the entire transaction, letting out an exhausted breath.
’At least I didn’t have to sell a kidney to pay for the noodles.’
The group descended the express lift, greeted by the entire floor staff bowing in synchronized, reverent lines as they walked out into the private landing bay.
Harper unlocked the custom midnight-purple sports coupe with a casual tap on her Spirit Phone.
The scissor-doors hissed open, and Silas collapsed into the front passenger seat, while Seraphina gracefully slid into the back.
Harper pushed the ignition rune.
VROOOOOOOM!

The twin-turbo mana engine roared to life with an aggressive throaty snarl. Harper shifted the gear lever, expertly drifting the vehicle out of the floating landing bay and merging onto the high-speed skyway that wove between the glowing neon towers of the Central District.
The city beneath them was a sea of glittering holographic billboards, towering corporate spires, and streams of floating mag-vehicles.
Silas leaned his head back against the leather headrest, a sudden involuntary shiver running down his spine as he glanced sideways at Harper.
"Harper..." Silas began, his voice dripping with deep cautious dread. "What is Phase Three?"
Harper’s lips curved into a mysterious mischievous smirk. Her violet eyes flicked toward him in the rearview mirror.
"Phase Three is a total surprise, handsome," Harper teased, tapping her fingers rhythmically against the steering wheel. "Just sit back, relax, and let the magic happen."
Silas’s left eye twitched. "Every time you say ’surprise,’ my lifespan decreases by five years."
From the back seat, Seraphina leaned forward, crossing her arms over the front console as her brow furrowed in deep noble annoyance.

"Cease this childish obfuscation, Harper," Seraphina nagged sharply. "A proper operational itinerary requires clear, transparent milestones... Disclose the coordinates and nature of the destination immediately."𝙛𝒓𝓮𝒆𝔀𝒆𝙗𝓷𝒐𝙫𝒆𝙡.𝒄𝓸𝓶
Harper gripped the steering wheel, her annoyance finally snapping as she glared at the crimson noble through the rearview mirror.
"We’re going to watch a damn movie, alright?!" Harper shouted back with her patience evaporating. "It’s a luxury theater! Now shut your royal mouth and just fuck off for five minutes so I can drive!"
Seraphina gasped in aristocratic outrage. "How dare you use such vulgar language in my presence—"
"Quiet, both of you," Silas muttered tiredly, staring blankly out the window. "A movie. Fine. As long as nobody asks me to try on another luxury coat, I don’t care."
Ten minutes later, the sports coupe glided down from the skyway, pulling into the private VIP valet of The Astraea Imperial Holo-Cinema.

Located in the heart of the cultural theater district, The Astraea was a monolithic palace of black obsidian and glowing violet crystal, catering exclusively to high-ranking Awakened Lords, corporate executives, and guild masters.
They walked through the grand, velvet-lined entrance lobby.

Silas looked around at the towering crystal chandeliers, the private security wards humming silently in the walls, and the floating holographic movie posters displaying larger-than-life battles and dramatic romances.

’We literally have a seventy-inch smart TV in the living room...’ Silas thought, rubbing the back of his neck with a deadpan sigh. ’I could be sitting on the sofa in my sweatpants watching anything right now. Why do rich people have to turn sitting in a dark room into an eight-figure military operation?’
Harper walked up to the private VIP concierge desk, flashing a golden digital ticket from her Spirit Phone interface.
"Reservation for Suite Primus," Harper stated smoothly.
The receptionist... a beautiful young woman in a gold-trimmed uniform bowed instantly.
"Welcome, Lady Whitmore. Suite Primus has been fully sterilized and calibrated to your preferences. Please, follow the luminescent path to the top tier."
The group proceeded down a wide, soundproofed corridor lined with deep purple carpeting and soft, recessed floor lights.
As they walked, Seraphina stepped up beside Harper, her crimson eyes scanning the holographic promotional banners floating along the walls.
"So," Seraphina asked, her melodic voice laced with skeptical curiosity. "What genre of cinematic simulation have you selected for this engagement?"
Harper puffed out her chest, tilting her chin up with unshakable confidence.

"Horror, obviously," Harper announced proudly with a sharp smirk on her lips. "It’s an exclusive, unrated screening of an ancient Rift incident. Psychological terror, gore, dimensional entities... it’s literally my favorite genre."
In reality, Harper’s internal organs were clenching in cold-sweat terror.
She despised horror movies.
She was terrified of ghosts, cursed relics, and creepy dimensional entities that didn’t have physical bodies she could punch with lightning.
But the LordTube Ultimate Date Guide had been crystal clear...
Horror movies induce adrenaline spikes, causing female companions to instinctually seek physical shelter against their male partner’s chest, accelerating romantic intimacy by four hundred percent.
Harper was fully prepared to endure psychological trauma if it meant spending two hours clinging to Silas’s muscular arm.
Seraphina, however, let out a loud displeased scoff.

"Horror?" Seraphina complained, crossing her arms with disdain. "How utterly barbaric and devoid of artistic merit. We should be viewing an Imperial Historical Epic... specifically, ’The Crimson Empress of the Eastern Spires,’ a sweeping multi-part masterpiece depicting a high-born noble maiden who conquers the continental courts alongside her devoted common-born consort!"

"Nobody wants to watch your three-hour historical propaganda self-insert fanfiction, Princess!" Harper fired back, baring her teeth. "Horror builds character! It tests awareness and combat readiness under delicate situations!"

"It is a cheap sensationalist drivel designed for low-tier mercenaries!" Seraphina argued fiercely, stepping directly into Harper’s path. "A historical drama provides cultural refinement and moral elevation!"
"I’m the one who paid for the suite, so we watch what I picked!"
"I will buy the entire cinema right now and replace the film reel with twenty copies of the Crimson Empress!"
"Will you two shut up?!"
Silas’s voice snapped through the corridor like a thunderclap. Both girls halted instantly, turning their heads toward him.
Silas looked between the furious, sparkling Lightning Lord and the haughty, glaring noble heiress with his golden-ringed blue eyes looking very steady.
"I want to watch the horror movie," Silas said flatly. "I’ve spent the last few weeks fighting actual monsters in the mud so let’s see if movies can make anything that actually looks dangerous."
Hearing his definitive verdict, both girls instantly snapped their mouths shut.
Harper’s face lit up with smug, silent victory, while Seraphina’s cheeks dusted with a soft compliant pink blush as she quietly lowered her chin.
"Very well," Seraphina conceded in a tiny, surprisingly obedient voice. "If... if that is your preference, Silas... I shall permit it."
They reached the end of the corridor, where a set of heavy, runic-engraved double doors parted smoothly to reveal Suite Primus.
The private viewing chamber was massive.
Instead of standard theater seating, the room featured a colossal U-shaped master recliner couch forged from deep burgundy velvet, piled high with silk cushions and plush throws.
Floor-to-ceiling wards were embedded into the dark acoustic walls, while a massive ultra-high-density holographic projection field spanned the entire front of the room.
Reginald stopped precisely at the entrance.
The elderly butler bowed stiffly, walking over to a solitary, high-backed leather armchair positioned in the far back corner of the suite, well outside the primary viewing zone.
"I shall remain stationed in the observation perimeter, Lady Seraphina," Reginald murmured, sitting with his spine straight and his hands folded neatly over his lap.
"Thank you, Reginald," Seraphina replied.
Silas walked down the short flight of carpeted steps and took a seat directly in the center of the massive burgundy velvet couch.
He leaned back into the plush cushions, stretching his long legs out over the footrest.
Immediately, the seating war began.
Harper lunged forward, sliding smoothly into the couch directly against Silas’s left side.
She tucked her legs beneath her, leaning her entire upper body firmly against his left bicep, her violet eyes flashing with a shy triumphant warmth.
Not to be outdone for a single second, Seraphina gracefully walked around the front, sliding onto the right side of the couch.
She smoothed her crimson gown and pressed her hip and shoulder snugly against Silas’s right arm, her cheeks glowing with a brilliant blush as she settled into his personal space.
Silas sat dead center between them, completely pinned by two high-tier awakened women clinging to his sides like heated velvet blankets.
’This couch is ten feet wide,’ Silas thought, staring blankly ahead. ’And yet I have exactly zero inches of personal space.’
HUMMMMM!
A sleek hovering silver service drone floated silently into the suite, descending gracefully over the central coffee table.

Mounted on the drone’s magnetic tray was a colossal gold-trimmed tub of warm, freshly popped mana-corn dusted in sweet caramel glaze, alongside three tall crystal glasses filled with chilled, sparkling berry elixir.
The drone set the refreshments down with a soft click and floated back into the shadows.
Seraphina looked down at the steaming, sweet-scented mana-corn.
Her crimson eyes flicked sideways toward Silas’s rugged jawline as a sudden bold idea took root in her blushing mind.
She reached out, gently picking up a piece of the golden caramel popcorn between her manicured fingers.
She leaned close to his ear with the subtle scent of jasmine rolling over him.
"Silas..." Seraphina whispered softly, her melodic voice carrying a sweet incredibly shy tremor as she held the popcorn near his lips. "Would you... feed me a piece? As a gesture of spousal harmony?"
Silas turned his head slightly, seeing the intense, hopeful glow in her red eyes.
He didn’t have the energy to argue.
He reached over, picked up a piece of the caramel mana-corn from the tub, and gently pressed it against her lips.
Seraphina parted her glossed lips, taking the sweet treat from his fingers with a delicate, breathtaking grace.
A radiant beautiful smile spread across her entire face, her crimson eyes shimmering with joy as she leaned her head affectionately against his shoulder.
Beside him, Harper’s jaw dropped.

"Hey!" Harper protested loudly, her competitive instincts roaring back to life as her face turned a bright jealous red. "That’s cheating! Silas, feed me one too! I’m the one who paid for the VIP tickets, so I get—"
Before Harper could finish her sentence, the entire private suite violently, abruptly plunged into pitch-black darkness.
CLICK.

The soft lights extinguished completely as the hum of the wards surged to maximum output, vibrating through the floorboards with a deep bone-chilling sub-frequency that made the air in the room feel instantly heavy and suffocating.
Harper froze mid-sentence, her mouth snapping shut as her fingers instinctively clamped around Silas’s left forearm with enough grip strength to crack standard steel.
HUMMMMM... FLASH!

"Nobody wants to watch your three-hour historical propaganda self-insert fanfiction, Princess!" Harper fired back, baring her teeth.
"Horror builds character!
It tests awareness and combat readiness under delicate situations!"
"It is a cheap sensationalist drivel designed for low-tier mercenaries!" Seraphina argued fiercely, stepping directly into Harper’s path.
"A historical drama provides cultural refinement and moral elevation!"
"I’m the one who paid for the suite, so we watch what I picked!"
"I will buy the entire cinema right now and replace the film reel with twenty copies of the Crimson Empress!"
"Will you two shut up?!"
Silas’s voice snapped through the corridor like a thunderclap.
Both girls halted instantly, turning their heads toward him.
Silas looked between the furious, sparkling Lightning Lord and the haughty, glaring noble heiress with his golden-ringed blue eyes looking very steady.
"I want to watch the horror movie," Silas said flatly.
"I’ve spent the last few weeks fighting actual monsters in the mud so let’s see if movies can make anything that actually looks dangerous."
Hearing his definitive verdict, both girls instantly snapped their mouths shut.
Harper’s face lit up with smug, silent victory, while Seraphina’s cheeks dusted with a soft compliant pink blush as she quietly lowered her chin.
"Very well," Seraphina conceded in a tiny, surprisingly obedient voice.
"If... if that is your preference, Silas...
I shall permit it."
They reached the end of the corridor, where a set of heavy, runic-engraved double doors parted smoothly to reveal Suite Primus.
The private viewing chamber was massive.
Instead of standard theater seating, the room featured a colossal U-shaped master recliner couch forged from deep burgundy velvet, piled high with silk cushions and plush throws.
Floor-to-ceiling wards were embedded into the dark acoustic walls, while a massive ultra-high-density holographic projection field spanned the entire front of the room.
Reginald stopped precisely at the entrance.
The elderly butler bowed stiffly, walking over to a solitary, high-backed leather armchair positioned in the far back corner of the suite, well outside the primary viewing zone.
"I shall remain stationed in the observation perimeter, Lady Seraphina," Reginald murmured, sitting with his spine straight and his hands folded neatly over his lap.
"Thank you, Reginald," Seraphina replied.
Silas walked down the short flight of carpeted steps and took a seat directly in the center of the massive burgundy velvet couch.
He leaned back into the plush cushions, stretching his long legs out over the footrest.
Immediately, the seating war began.
Harper lunged forward, sliding smoothly into the couch directly against Silas’s left side.
She tucked her legs beneath her, leaning her entire upper body firmly against his left bicep, her violet eyes flashing with a shy triumphant warmth.
Not to be outdone for a single second, Seraphina gracefully walked around the front, sliding onto the right side of the couch.
She smoothed her crimson gown and pressed her hip and shoulder snugly against Silas’s right arm, her cheeks glowing with a brilliant blush as she settled into his personal space.
Silas sat dead center between them, completely pinned by two high-tier awakened women clinging to his sides like heated velvet blankets.
’This couch is ten feet wide,’ Silas thought, staring blankly ahead. ’And yet I have exactly zero inches of personal space.’
HUMMMMM!
A sleek hovering silver service drone floated silently into the suite, descending gracefully over the central coffee table.

Mounted on the drone’s magnetic tray was a colossal gold-trimmed tub of warm, freshly popped mana-corn dusted in sweet caramel glaze, alongside three tall crystal glasses filled with chilled, sparkling berry elixir.
The drone set the refreshments down with a soft click and floated back into the shadows.
Seraphina looked down at the steaming, sweet-scented mana-corn.
Her crimson eyes flicked sideways toward Silas’s rugged jawline as a sudden bold idea took root in her blushing mind.
She reached out, gently picking up a piece of the golden caramel popcorn between her manicured fingers.
She leaned close to his ear with the subtle scent of jasmine rolling over him.
"Silas..." Seraphina whispered softly, her melodic voice carrying a sweet incredibly shy tremor as she held the popcorn near his lips.
"Would you... feed me a piece?
As a gesture of spousal harmony?"
Silas turned his head slightly, seeing the intense, hopeful glow in her red eyes.
He didn’t have the energy to argue.
He reached over, picked up a piece of the caramel mana-corn from the tub, and gently pressed it against her lips.
Seraphina parted her glossed lips, taking the sweet treat from his fingers with a delicate, breathtaking grace.
A radiant beautiful smile spread across her entire face, her crimson eyes shimmering with joy as she leaned her head affectionately against his shoulder.
Beside him, Harper’s jaw dropped.
"Hey!" Harper protested loudly, her competitive instincts roaring back to life as her face turned a bright jealous red.
"That’s cheating!
Silas, feed me one too!
I’m the one who paid for the VIP tickets, so I get—"
Before Harper could finish her sentence, the entire private suite violently, abruptly plunged into pitch-black darkness.
CLICK.

The soft lights extinguished completely as the hum of the wards surged to maximum output, vibrating through the floorboards with a deep bone-chilling sub-frequency that made the air in the room feel instantly heavy and suffocating.
Harper froze mid-sentence, her mouth snapping shut as her fingers instinctively clamped around Silas’s left forearm with enough grip strength to crack standard steel.
HUMMMMM...
FLASH!

chapters.title: Chapter 390: Luxury Arcade...?
paragraphs: Without a single second of warning, the massive holographic projection field at the front of the room ignited with horrifying intensity.
PCH!
There was no studio logo and there was no cinematic opening music.
Floating in the center of the pitch-black void was a colossal realistic severed human eye roughly the size of a minivan.
The eye was milky-white, laced with pulsing blackened veins that writhed beneath the cornea like parasitic worms.

Thick, viscous, dark-crimson blood oozed continuously from the torn, jagged optic nerve behind it, splashing against an invisible floor with sickening wet splatter sounds that resonated through the surround-sound speakers directly behind their ears.
Slowly... agonizingly... the massive blood-soaked pupil twisted.
It locked its unblinking, dead, rotting gaze directly onto the three people sitting on the velvet couch.
A high-pitched, agonizing chorus of distorted human screams tore through the theater’s spatial speakers, accompanied by the wet rhythmic sound of bones crunching in the dark.
The room’s temperature plummeted ten degrees in an instant.
Harper’s entire body went rigid as a board. Her violet eyes widened in pure horror with her breath hitching in her throat as she buried her face directly into Silas’s left bicep, trembling violently.
On the right side, Seraphina’s noble poise completely shattered into dust.

She let out a tiny, terrified shriek, frantically throwing both of her arms around Silas’s right arm and burying her face into his chest with her fingernails digging through the fabric of his shadow-silk shirt.

Even Reginald, sitting fifty feet away in the darkness, subtly gripped the armrests of his leather chair, his jaw tightening as his assassin instincts flared at the demonic feeling from the projection.
Silas sat entirely upright in the center of the couch, holding two trembling high-tier Lords against his ribs.
Across the bleeding screen, blood-dripping obsidian letters slowly materialized beneath the rotting eye, spelling out the title of the movie.
[CHRONICLES OF ROT (1)]
Silas blinked, staring at the screen as a slow skeptical breath escaped his nose.
"Come on," Silas muttered under his breath, shaking his head at the dramatic opening. "It’s just spatial CGI and sound design too... It can’t possibly be that scary, right?"
...Unfortunately for Silas Graves, he was very... very wrong.

The heavy soundproofed doors of Suite Primus slid open with a soft, mechanical hiss that sounded eerily like the dying breath of the grotesque abyssal entity they had just spent two agonizing hours watching on the massive holographic projection field.
Four people stepped out into the plush, dimly lit corridor of The Astraea Imperial Holo-Cinema.
Every single one of them was as pale as a freshly bleached sheet.
Silas walked in the center, his rugged jaw set in a rigid traumatized line however he wasn’t walking alone... he was practically carrying an entire vanguard unit.
Clinging desperately to his left bicep with a white-knuckled grip that threatened to snap his ulna was Harper Whitmore.
The fierce, usually unhinged Lightning Lord had her eyes darting frantically to every shadow, jumping half a foot in the air every time a carpet seam shifted under her boots.

Her purple hair was disheveled, and she looked thoroughly haunted with her mind still replaying the scene where the multi-jointed corpse-crawler had crawled backward out of a dimensional rift to harvest its victims’ spinal cords.
’I hope something like that abomination never makes way to my territory...’
On his right, Seraphina Bloom was plastered against his ribs with equal terrified desperation.
The proud untouchable heiress of House Bloom had completely forgotten all notions of aristocratic aloofness.
Her manicured fingers were bunched tightly into the enchanted fabric of Silas’s shirt, her crimson eyes wide and trembling as she repeatedly checked the ceiling corners for hidden fleshy tentacles.

For an elite noble who had grown up in sterile, guarded palaces and fought monsters with predictable attack patterns in the Sovereign Realm, being subjected to raw psychological body horror was a foreign brain-breaking experience.
Bringing up the rear was Reginald.
The veteran butler, a man who had slit throats in ancestral clan wars without blinking, was sweating profusely beneath his starched collar.
His hands, clasped behind his back, were visibly twitching and his sharp eyes scanning the emergency exit signs with paranoid calculations.
Silas took a deep, shuddering breath, shaking his head slowly as they reached the grand staircase leading down to the lobby.
"I am never," Silas stated, his voice sounding very flat and hollow. "watching a horror movie again for the rest of my life."

"Agreed," Harper squeaked instantly, her voice cracking into a pathetic high-pitched tone as she buried her face deeper into his sleeve. "Burn the film reel... Cast the studio director into the Abyss. If I see another severed eyeball floating in the dark, I’m discharging a hundred thousand volts right toward it."

"It was... an uncultured and profoundly barbaric abomination," Seraphina stammered, her teeth faintly chattering as she clutched Silas’s arm tighter. "There was no narrative integrity! The protagonist did not even deploy a spatial barrier before the entity severed her limbs! It was pure spiritual terrorism!"

"It was effective cinema, Lady Seraphina," Reginald rasped from behind them, his voice rougher than usual as he loosened his silk cravat. "Though I must recommend that House Bloom’s intelligence division never permits such demonic visual archives within our domestic perimeter..."
They descended the marble steps into the grand reception hall.
Behind the golden counter, the receptionist... the young woman with the sharp silver uniform looked up as they approached.

Seeing the towering Lord, the two trembling high-tier women hanging off him like frightened koalas, and the sweating butler trailing behind, the receptionist’s lips curved into an amused and almost sadistic grin.𝚏𝗿𝗲𝐞𝐰𝚎𝕓𝐧𝚘𝘃𝗲𝐥.𝐜𝚘𝕞
"Welcome back, esteemed guests," the receptionist greeted them with overly cheerful warmth. "Did Suite Primus’s arrays deliver a satisfactory experience? How did you find The Chronicles of Rot?"
Silas paused in front of the desk, looking the woman dead in the eye.
"The horror," Silas said with his eye twitching, "was a bit too good."
The receptionist’s grin widened by several millimeters, her eyes practically sparkling with malicious professional relish.

"We pride ourselves on immersion, Lord Graves," she beamed, taking immense pleasure in their collective suffering. "The psychological trauma protocols were updated just last week... Lady Whitmore’s account has already cleared the full VIP ledger. Please, do visit us again soon for the midnight director’s cut!"
"Not in this lifetime," Harper muttered under her breath, hastily dragging Silas toward the double doors.
The three of them practically bolted through the exit, desperate for the cool grounding breeze of the evening air.
Outside, the cool air did little to settle their racing pulses, but the familiar hum of traffic along the upper boulevards provided some much-needed reality.
They climbed into Harper’s custom midnight-purple sports coupe.
Silas sank into the front passenger seat, letting out a long heavy exhale as the heated leather supported his exhausted back.
Seraphina gracefully slid into the rear, sitting closer to the center console than usual, still looking slightly jumpy whenever a streetlamp flickered.
Harper pushed the ignition rune, and the twin-turbo engine rumbled to life with a steady reassuring purr.
She smoothly steered the vehicle out of the valet bay and merged onto the highway.
For several minutes, the cabin was dead silent as the trauma of the movie hung over them like a thick fog.
Silas turned his head, eyeing Harper with deep exhausted suspicion.
"Alright," Silas began, his voice cautious. "Where are we going next?"
Harper didn’t answer immediately as she kept her eyes on the neon-lit road ahead, tapping her fingers against the leather steering wheel.
Surprisingly, Seraphina didn’t nag or demand a briefing this time.
The crimson noble was simply leaning back against the plush leather, breathing slowly to re-center her ancestral flame aura.
Harper exhaled softly, rolling her shoulders as the last remnants of movie-induced terror finally began to fade.
A bright conspiratorial gleam sparked in her violet eyes.

According to the sacred texts of the LordTube Ultimate Date Guide, Phase Three was meant to break emotional barriers through shared terror, but Phase Four was the crucial setup... the energy-reset phase designed to build camaraderie, playful competition, and physical teamwork before the grand finale of Phase Five.
"Phase Four," Harper announced, her usual radiant grin breaking across her face, "is pure, unadulterated fun. We are going for games!"
Silas blinked. "Games? Like an arcade?"
"Yep! An arcade!"
Silas paused, his tense shoulders actually relaxing a fraction.
’An arcade?’ Silas thought, a wave of genuine nostalgia washing over him. ’That actually isn’t bad at all.’
Back in his past life on Earth, he had spent countless weekends in dingy, neon-lit arcades, hammering away at rhythm machines, air hockey tables, and light-gun shooters with his friends.

Even in this world, during his early years in Sector 4, he used to take Lia to the run-down coin-op centers in the lower districts to play claw machines whenever he scraped together a few spare copper tokens.
Arcades were simple.
They were loud, straightforward, and... most importantly cheap. You bought a cup of plastic tokens, played some games, and walked away.
It couldn’t possibly be that expensi—
"It’s The Grand Nexus Imperial Cyber-Pavilion," Harper added casually, adjusting her rearview mirror with a smug smirk. "The premier luxury entertainment arcade in the Diamond Sector!"
The brief color that had returned to Silas’s face instantly vanished. Silas stared at her with his eye twitching violently.

’When the hell did arcades become luxury?!’ Silas screamed internally, clutching his forehead. ’It’s an arcade! You put tokens into a box and press buttons! How do you make an arcade cost millions of credits?! Are the joysticks forged from ancient dragon bone?!’
Ten minutes later, the coupe went down a grand illuminated spiral ramp and pulled into the sprawling plaza of The Grand Nexus.
Silas stepped out of the vehicle, his boots hitting the polished glowing pavement.
He looked around in genuine surprise.
Unlike the hyper-exclusive Haute Couture Sanctuary or the stuffy isolated sky-lounge of The Celestial Zenith, the plaza here was alive with vibrant energy.
Neon holographic displays towered fifty feet into the air, projecting vibrant game characters, glowing scoreboards, and animated retro sprites.
The crowd was a fascinating eclectic mix.

There were high-society corporate heirs in tailored silk jackets, but there were also off-duty mercenaries in rugged combat pants, academy students in bright uniforms, and regular citizens from the mid-tier neighborhoods enjoying the evening.
The sound of synthetic synth-wave music, laughing crowds, and the mechanical clatter of prize dispensers filled the crisp evening air.
Harper parked the sports coupe in a designated VIP bay, while Reginald stepped out of the car.
Silas turned toward the elderly butler, expecting the man to follow them to the entrance as usual.
However, Reginald had come to an abrupt rigid halt ten paces from the entrance.
The veteran butler was staring at the flashing neon signs with a face that was almost as pale as it had been in the cinema.
A cold sweat glistened on his forehead as his fingers twitching against the seams of his trousers.
"My Lady," Reginald spoke, his voice unusually strained as he bowed stiffly. "I... I respectfully request permission to remain stationed outside with the vehicle for this portion of the engagement."
Silas raised an eyebrow, looking at the older man in confusion.
’Is this terrifying man afraid of an arcade?’

In reality, Reginald’s mind was flashing back thirty-five years to an undercover reconnaissance mission inside a lower-tier cyber-den, where he had been trapped inside a dance-simulation machine for four consecutive hours by an eccentric enemy informant.
The rhythmic flashing lights, the electronic chime sequences, and the catastrophic muscle fatigue had left scars on his warrior psyche that no healing potion could ever mend.
’I cannot survey this environment...’ Reginald thought in silent dignified horror. ’The chaos will compromise my operational discipline.’
Seraphina glanced at her butler, entirely unbothered. "You may remain at the perimeter, Reginald."
"Thank you, Lady Seraphina," Reginald exhaled, visibly slumping with profound relief as he retreated to the sanctuary of the limousine.
"Come on!" Harper cheered, grabbing Silas’s hand with an energetic tug. "Let’s go win some prizes!"
They stepped through the grand archway of The Grand Nexus, and the scale of the facility unfolded before them.
The pavilion spanned four colossal, tiered floors beneath a domed glass ceiling that projected an artificial shifting starry nebula.
Thousands of state-of-the-art gaming stations, battle arenas, holographic rhythm stages, and immersive simulation pods stretched out across the glowing floors.

chapters.title: Chapter 391: Game Date [I / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: The moment the trio crossed the threshold onto the polished quartz flooring, the energy of the grand lobby washed over them.
"Haah... I love this place."
Unlike the suffocating silence of high-society boutiques, this place thrummed with life.
Towering holographic banners suspended from the soaring glass ceiling flickered with vibrant game sprites, pulsing leaderboards, and animated championship brackets.
Stationed immediately beside the golden velvet-rope entryway was a reception desk forged from brushed obsidian and glowing azure crystal.
Behind the counter stood a pair of immaculately dressed receptionists in sleek gold-trimmed vests and crisp white shirts, their posture straight and welcoming.
The moment their eyes caught Harper’s unmistakable violet hair and Silas’s imposing presence, the head receptionist bowed deeply from the waist.

"Welcome to The Grand Nexus, esteemed Lords," the receptionist greeted them with practiced reverence. "Are we initiating a standard seasonal pass today, or shall I calibrate the sovereign corporate suites for your party?"
"Give us the full platinum package," Harper commanded with an energetic grin.
She stepped straight up to the automated platinum terminal embedded in the counter, pulling her sleek black corporate card from her pocket and tapping it against the runic sensor.
BEEP-CHIME!
The machine chimed in a rapid cheerful ascending trill.
A concealed mechanical dispenser slid open, neatly pushing forward three heavy gold-trimmed digital Nexus Cards that thrummed with pulsing magical current.

"Three unrestricted sovereign cards loaded with unlimited baseline credits," the receptionist announced, extending them on a velvet tray with a bow. "All tiers, private battle enclosures, and sensory simulation vaults are fully unlocked. Please enjoy your evening at The Grand Nexus..."
"Thanks!" Harper chirped, scooping up the cards.
She spun on her heel, thrusting one card into Silas’s chest and offering the second to Seraphina with a smug theatrical flourish.
Seraphina did not take the card immediately.
She reached out with two manicured fingers, gingerly pinching the glowing gold-rimmed rectangle as if it were a rare volatile alchemical sample.
She held it up to the light of the chandelier, turning it over with deep skepticism.

"What is the operational function of this plastic rectangle?" Seraphina asked, her melodic voice carrying an unmistakably haughty edge. "Am I required to channel my concentrated crimson flame into the circuitry to initiate the mechanisms?"

"No, Princess, it’s money," Harper laughed, shaking her head at the noblewoman’s sheltered cluelessness. "You tap it against the scanner, you play the games, and you try not to throw a royal tantrum when I completely crush you. Follow me... first up is the Titan Hammer Strikers!"
Harper led the way across the vibrant floor, her sneakers squeaking lightly against the immaculate tiles as Silas and Seraphina followed behind.

They arrived at a cordoned-off physical performance zone dominated by a towering, reinforced steel apparatus that looked less like a carnival attraction and more like an industrial siege weapon salvaged from a dwarven fortress.
The striking base was a colossal glowing anvil forged from enchanted dark-iron, bolted directly into the foundation.
Rising behind it was a massive segmented vertical column of crystalline light that stretched forty feet toward the vaulted ceiling.
A digital banner flickered brightly across the top of the rig:
[THE KINETIC IMPACT DECIMATOR - TITAN STRIKER RIG]
[TEST YOUR RAW MIGHT - NO MANA PERMITTED]
[YOUR STRENGTH IS THE ONLY THING THAT MATTERS]
Standing beside the safety railing of the strike platform was a dedicated game attendant... a burly broad-shouldered man wearing protective ear dampers and a heavy leather technician’s apron.
The attendant bowed respectfully as the three of them stepped onto the perimeter mat.

"Welcome to the Kinetic Impact Decimator, my Lords," the attendant introduced with a deep baritone. "The rules are entirely straightforward, yet brutally unforgiving... The platform beneath your feet emits an active null-field that completely suppresses internal mana circulation in case you are a true Lord or an Adventurer. You cannot rely on elemental enhancement, core reinforcement, or weight manipulation. This machine measures pure muscle power and explosive physical torque. The one with the highest kinetic yield claims the round..."
He turned to a magnetic weapon rack bolted beside the anvil, unlocking a heavy, two-handed alloy warhammer crafted from solid dense tungsten-steel.
The attendant offered the massive tool to Harper with two hands, grunting slightly beneath its deadweight.

"Here’s how it works," Harper explained to Seraphina, taking the heavy alloy hammer casually with a single hand and resting the sixty-pound head against the rubber floor. "You step onto the strike pad, grip the shaft, and deliver everything your muscles have got. Highest score takes the crown!"
Harper stepped firmly onto the center of the rubberized strike pad.
The moment her boots settled as a faint azure hum rippled through the floor... the null-field activating, sealing off her internal lightning reserves but Harper didn’t flinch.
Silas on the other hand rolled his eyes.
’It’s always mana suppression with these people... Tch...’
Her athletic legs planted wide, locking into a low stable center of gravity.
She rolled her shoulders, her competitive nature igniting as she hoisted the massive sixty-pound warhammer high above her head with both hands.
Her back muscles coiled tightly beneath her tailored jacket with her breath drawing in through her teeth.
"HAAAAH!"
With a fierce athletic grunt, Harper snapped her hips forward, bringing the tungsten warhammer down in a terrifying, full-body arc of pure momentum.
CLAAAANG!
The impact echoed across the open floor like the detonation of an artillery shell.

The dark-iron anvil shuddered violently on its bolts as the crystalline column of light surged upward in a blinding flash of white energy, rocketing past the 5,000-point mark, tearing through 8,000, and finally locking into place with a sharp chime.
STRIKE RATING: 9,450 POINTS
RANK: VANGUARD CLASS - HIGH-TIER
"Hah!" Harper gloated, tossing the heavy hammer toward Silas, who caught the spinning shaft effortlessly in mid-air.
She turned to Seraphina with a wide insufferably cocky grin. "Top ten on the daily facility leaderboard! Beat that with your fancy tea-party etiquette, Princess!"
Seraphina let out a cold sharp scoff, stepping onto the rubberized platform with her chin tilted high.

"A barbaric, unrefined display of peasant brute force," Seraphina declared, brushing a lock of crimson hair behind her shoulder. "However, House Bloom’s physical conditioning is flawless in every metric... Give me the implement."
Silas handed the warhammer over.
The moment Seraphina took the weapon, her slender arms dipped slightly beneath the sudden unassisted deadweight with the null-field instantly cutting off her internal flame mana.
’Ah... It’s quite heavy.’
Her jaw tightened in determination.
Despite her delicate hourglass frame, she was an awakened Lord... her power had been permanently elevated by years of high-tier core refinement.
Seraphina took a deep breath, planted her heeled boots firmly against the strike pad, and hoisted the hammer overhead.
"Yield to House Bloom!" Seraphina cried, bringing the weapon down with a sharp focused shout.
CRASH!
The hammer slammed into the anvil with a bright metallic crack.
The column of light shot up the glass tube, blazing through the mid-tiers before settling firmly at 7,800 POINTS - ELITE CLASS.
The machine chimed, dispensing a short ribbon of silver tickets.
Seraphina puffed out her cheeks in profound annoyance, glaring at the digital readout with sheer indignation.
"The gravitational calibration on this apparatus is clearly biased toward vulgar, unrefined brawlers! It failed to properly register the rotational torque of my strike!"
"Sure it did, Princess," Harper laughed, clutching her sides. "Keep telling yourself that! Your turn, Silas! Show her what a real strike looks like!"
The attendant stepped forward, looking at Silas with an appreciative nod. "Whenever you are ready... The platform is calibrated."
Silas stepped up to the rubber strike pad, casually holding the heavy sixty-pound warhammer in one loose grip.
He looked down at the dark-iron anvil and Silas didn’t activate his Mythic Gold Core.
’It’s probably going to end up the way it did in Shogitown...’
He didn’t attempt to channel a single fraction of mana against the platform’s null-field but his physical body was no longer that of a standard human.
Forged in the brutal crucible of multiple serious fights, his raw muscle fibers carried the terrifying power of a true Lord.
Silas shifted his stance slightly and he took a relaxed half-step forward with his broad shoulders dropping naturally into alignment.
’I should still hold back a bit... I can’t pay for broken equipment.’
Silas simply rotated his hips, coiled his core, and brought the hammer down in a clean, compact, and effortlessly violent arc.
BOOOOOOOOM!
The sound that detonated through the room was not the metallic ring of a hammer hitting an anvil.
It was a deafening sonic shockwave that rattled the teeth in everyone’s skulls and violently shook the rubber floorboards for thirty feet in every direction.
The attendant’s jaw dropped so fast his magnifying spectacles slid off his nose.
The vertical column of light didn’t climb... it exploded.

The energy beam violently shattered through the 10,000-point ceiling in a fraction of a millisecond, blew past the facility’s all-time historical high score, and completely fried the internal sensory conduits of the glass pillar.
BZZZZT-CRACKLE!
A shower of harmless, bright blue sparks rained from the top of the tower as the digital display violently strobed in crimson warning text.
[CRITICAL ALERT: STRUCTURAL OVERLOAD]
SCORE: 19,850 - TITAN MONARCH CLASS
[NEW ALL-TIME FACILITY RECORD]
CH-CH-CH-CH-CHUNK!
The ticket dispenser went completely haywire.
It began vomiting an unbroken, endless river of golden tickets that spilled over the platform, pooling around Silas’s heavy boots like a shimmering fountain.
Harper’s jaw dropped so low it looked as though it were about to detach from her skull.
Seraphina stood completely frozen, staring at the smoking, visibly dented dark-iron anvil. Her crimson eyes were wide with starry-eyed bewilderment.
"The... the output..." Seraphina whispered, her chest heaving as she stared at his broad shoulders in awe. "Without mana... that was purely his physical power..."
Silas casually stepped off the platform, setting the slightly warped hammer back onto the magnetic rack with a soft click.
He cleared his throat, rubbing the back of his neck.
"The balance on the grip is pretty good," Silas muttered deadpan.
The attendant scrambled forward, frantically hitting reset runes on the smoking console while staring at Silas as if an ancient dragon had just casually strolled into his arcade.
"A-A thousand honors! I... I shall preserve this impact crater for the archives!"

"That was a crude measurement of brute force," Seraphina declared firmly, turning her back on the broken anvil and crossing her arms with determined pride. "A true Lord relies on cognitive processing, spatial awareness, and immaculate reaction time so take us to an apparatus that tests mental acuity."
’Tch, what a sore loser.’
Harper rolled her eyes, but a competitive smirk returned to her face.
"Fine by me, Princess. Let’s see how fast that royal brain works when things start flying at your face."
They moved to the eastern wing of the second floor, arriving before a massive circular pavilion dominated by four sealed hemispherical domes forged from transparent, reinforced poly-crystal.
Above the central archway, a glowing holographic title spun in mid-air: The Holographic Reflex Dome.
Stationed at the entrance of the Dome zone was a sharp professional female attendant holding a digital tracking pad.
She bowed crisply as the three Lords approached.

"Welcome to the Holographic Reflex Dome," the attendant explained with a polite voice. "This simulation evaluates tracking, micro-reflexes, and selective cognitive processing... Once inside the active field, our light-projector arrays will launch high-velocity photon orbs at random vectors around your body. The rules are simple: you must strike Red orbs with physical force, dodge Blue orbs entirely, and cleanly catch Green orbs in mid-air. Striking a Blue orb or missing a Red orb results in immediate combo termination. The difficulty scales dynamically every ten seconds."
"Finally, a test worthy of noble intellect..." Seraphina declared smoothly.
She swiped her gold-trimmed Nexus Card at the entry turnstile and stepped gracefully into the center of the transparent glass dome.
BEEP-BEEP-GO!
The internal projection arrays flared to life.
Within a fraction of a second, dozens of luminescent fist-sized light-orbs exploded into motion, whizzing through the air around Seraphina’s head like a swarm of hyperactive, glowing hornets.
Seraphina’s demeanor shifted instantly into that of a high-tier combat prodigy.
’Let me impress my man...’
Her long crimson hair flowed like liquid fire as she danced across the circular platform with breathtaking elegance.

She ducked beneath a cluster of high-speed blue orbs with millimeters to spare, pivoted on the ball of her foot to shatter incoming red orbs with sharp precise palm strikes, and reached out with razor-thin focus to snatch green orbs straight out of the air.
Her movements were seamless, disciplined, and mesmerizing to watch.
The speed doubled, then tripled, the orbs blurring into streaks of light, but Seraphina’s focus remained ironclad until the final chime sounded.
DING-DING-DING!
[ROUND COMPLETE]
SCORE: 4,850 - GRANDMASTER REFLEX
ACCURACY: 98.4%
Seraphina glided out of the glass dome, casually brushing a stray lock of crimson hair behind her ear.
She looked down her nose at Harper, shooting the woman an arrogant triumphant smirk.
"Observe and despair, woman," Seraphina mocked smoothly. "Precision is bred through centuries of noble lineage."

chapters.title: Chapter 392: Game Date [II / Bonus - ]
paragraphs: Harper’s violet eyes narrowed into sharp dangerous slits. "Watch how a real woman handles a live swarm, Princess."
Harper swiped her card and marched into the dome.
The moment the countdown ended, Harper did not employ delicate elegant palm strikes.
She treated the whole thing like a high-voltage close-quarters street brawl.

She spun into low sweeps to let blue orbs sail over her head, threw explosive spinning heel kicks that obliterated red orbs with sharp cracks, and aggressively snatched green orbs out of the air with violent lightning-fast claw grips.
Her sneakers squeaked furiously against the floor as she chained together massive combo streaks, her athletic frame moving with raw explosive power.
DING-DING-DING!
[ROUND COMPLETE]
SCORE: 4,820 - MASTER VANGUARD
ACCURACY: 97.9%
The dome hissed open as Harper stepped out, wiping a drop of sweat from her brow.

"Thirty points short!" Seraphina gloated instantly, crossing her arms beneath her bust and raising her chin in victory. "The superiority of House Bloom’s cognitive reflexes remains absolute and undisputed!"

"You got a lucky spawn pattern on the green orbs!" Harper snapped back, her competitive pride boiling over. "Silas! Get in there and humble this arrogant red-haired peacock! And you there, make it maximum!"
Silas let out a faint sigh, swiping his card at the terminal and stepping into the center of the glass sphere.
The attendant tapped her screen.
"Initiating maximum threshold calibration for Sir Silas..."
BEEP-BEEP-GO!
The machine engaged at maximum tier immediately.
Over fifty light-orbs erupted from the walls simultaneously, converging on Silas from every conceivable angle at terrifying velocities.
Yet, the moment the orbs launched, Silas’s perception engaged.
He didn’t even need to use Rip-Current perception, the high-speed photon orbs did not look fast at all.
In fact, compared to tracking the claw strikes of beasts in the Umbral Basin, the glowing orbs looked like they were drifting lazily through thick molasses.
Silas didn’t jump around. He didn’t break into an athletic sweat, and he certainly didn’t perform theatrical martial arts katas.
He planted his feet in the dead center of the platform and barely shifted his weight.

His large hands blurred in microscopic hyper-efficient movements... casually swatting red orbs with the back of his knuckles, tilting his head half an inch to let blue orbs whistle past his ears, and plucking green orbs out of the air with the bored effortless precision of a man catching falling autumn leaves.
DING-DING-DING-DING!
The machine chimed in a frantic unbroken sequence of perfect scores.
[PERFECT CLEAR: ZERO FAULTS]
SCORE: 5,000 - MAXIMUM THRESHOLD CAP
ACCURACY: 100.0%
CHUNK-CHUNK-CHUNK!
Another massive overflowing mountain of golden tickets began spewing from the collection tray, burying Silas’s boots once again.
’Haah... again? What are these tickets even for at this point?’
Harper and Seraphina both stared through the glass dome in utter, paralyzed silence.
Silas pushed the door open, stepping out into the aisle and casually rubbing the back of his neck. He looked at the attendant with a puzzled frown.
"Is this machine experiencing input lag?" Silas asked genuinely. "The projection speed felt kind of slow."
The female attendant stared at him with wide, unblinking eyes, her hands trembling as she clutched her tracking pad.
"S-Slow...? My Lord... you just achieved a perfect score on the military calibration speed..."
"Oh," Silas muttered, looking away. "Never mind, then."
Determined to find a game that Silas couldn’t instantly conquer through superiority, Harper dragged the group across the third floor toward the Sovereign Claw Pavilion.
The entire sector was lined with colossal two-story-tall transparent prize vaults constructed from reinforced mana-glass.
Inside rested mountains of giant enchanted plush rift beasts, rare core elixirs in velvet cases, and limited-edition holographic Lord figurines.
Standing beside the primary vault was a young floor attendant wearing white gloves and a gold-trimmed visor.

"Welcome to the Grand Master Crane Vault," the attendant bowed. "Our mechanical gantries utilize multi-axis hydraulic winches... The prizes within are authentic and high-grade. Test your alignment and claim your prize."
Harper stepped forward, pointing an eager finger toward the center of the vault.

Resting at the very top of a massive pile of toys was a colossal, five-foot-tall plush Shadow-Panther crafted from midnight-black velvet, featuring glowing ruby eyes and wearing an intricately stitched, miniature golden crown.

"The ultimate test of precision and patience," Harper declared, crossing her arms with a challenging grin. "I’ve tried to win that exact crowned panther three times this month. The crane’s hydraulic grip strength is completely rigged to drop anything over ten pounds the second it lifts off the pile..."
Seraphina marched straight up to the control console, swiping her card with absolute noble confidence.
"A mere mechanical crane cannot resist calculated alignment," Seraphina stated haughtily. "Watch closely."
Seraphina gripped the joystick with intense focus.
She nudged the controls, maneuvering the giant, four-pronged steel claw across the top of the vault until it hovered precisely over the plush panther’s torso.
She lined it up to the exact millimeter, took a breath, and slammed the glowing drop button.𝐟𝐫𝕖𝗲𝘄𝚎𝗯𝕟𝐨𝕧𝐞𝚕.𝕔𝕠𝐦
The heavy claw descended smoothly, opened wide, and clamped firmly around the panther’s midsection.
"Hah!"
The cables tightened, lifting the massive five-foot beast three feet into the air.
Seraphina’s crimson eyes widened with triumphant excitement—
CLICK-FLUMP!
Right at the apex of the lift, the mechanical claw gave a violent deliberate shudder.
The hydraulic fingers loosened by an inch, and the heavy plush panther slipped free, tumbling back onto the pile with a soft, mocking thud.
"WHAT?!" Seraphina gasped in outrage.
She slammed both of her hands against the reinforced glass of the machine, her face flushing with pure fury.

"It intentionally disengaged its hydraulic pressure at the peak of the ascent!" Seraphina shrieked, pointing an accusatory finger at the terrified attendant. "This apparatus is a fraudulent criminal enterprise designed to swindle noble patrons! I demand an immediate judicial audit of this machine’s internal mechanisms!"
"M-My Lady, the crane’s grip variance is part of the challenge parameters—" the attendant stammered, raising his hands defensively.
"Let me show you how it’s done, Princess!" Harper laughed, shoving Seraphina aside and swiping her card.
Harper gripped the joystick, carefully guiding the crane over the plush panther.
Instead of aiming for the body, she attempted to hook one of the steel prongs directly beneath the panther’s golden crown.
The claw dropped, clamped, and began hauling the toy upward by its head.
But as the crane swung across the track, the momentum caused the claw to tilt, the smooth fabric of the crown slipped free, and the panther crashed back onto the pile once again.
"Dammit!" Harper groaned loudly, kicking the base of the machine with the toe of her sneaker. "I swear the operator in the back room is manually pressing a sabotage button!"
Silas stepped up to the console, pulling his card from his pocket and swiping it through the slot.
He didn’t aim for the panther’s center of mass, nor did he attempt to hook the crown.
Silas’s sharp eyes tracked the weight distribution of the entire prize pile.
’It seems the ones in the lower sectors and here are the same...’
He noticed that the shadow-panther’s heavy rear paw was lightly wedged beneath a smaller, three-foot plush bear sitting near the edge of the downward drop chute.
Silas deftly guided the joystick, ignoring the panther entirely. He positioned the claw directly over the smaller bear, aligned the winch, and pressed the drop button.
The claw descended, clamped securely around the lightweight bear, and hoisted it effortlessly into the air.
As the crane swung toward the chute, the sudden removal of the bear’s weight disrupted the balance of the pile.
The massive five-foot shadow-panther shifted, lost its footing, and rolled down the smooth velvet incline... tumbling straight into the wide open drop chute.
CHUNK-FLUMP!
The massive soft plush panther dropped out of the retrieval door at the bottom of the machine, landing squarely at Silas’s feet with its golden crown resting proudly on its head.
Silas bent down, scooping the colossal plush beast into his arms.
He turned around, holding the massive fluffy panther under one arm. He looked between the two stunned women, paused for a brief second, and then extended the giant toy directly toward Seraphina.
"Here," Silas said casually, his tone calm and unbothered. "You looked like you wanted it."
Seraphina froze.
Her crimson eyes widened into massive trembling saucers as she stared at the giant plush panther being offered to her.
Her breath hitched in her throat.
Her heart did a violent, erratic somersault against her ribs. The realization that Silas had just won the prize specifically to hand it to her completely shattered her noble defenses...
A nuclear radiant crimson blush exploded across her porcelain cheeks, rushing up to the tips of her delicate ears and down her slender neck.
She tentatively reached out, wrapping both of her slender arms around the massive, incredibly fluffy panther, pulling it tightly against her chest.
She buried her burning face into the soft black fur, inhaling the sweet clean scent of the fabric as her voice came out in a tiny overwhelmingly shy squeak.
"Silas..." Seraphina whispered, her melodic voice completely trembling with joy. "I... I shall treasure this ancestral tribute forever... It shall occupy the prime position upon my bed..."
Beside them, Harper’s jaw dropped in pure, incandescent jealousy.

"HEY!" Harper whined loudly, stomping her foot on the tiles like a petulant child whose dessert had just been stolen. "Where’s mine?! Silas, that’s blatant favoritism! Win me one too! Win me the giant electric fox right now or I’m going to cause a scene!"
Silas let out a quiet, amused chuckle.

He stepped back up to the console, swiped his card once more, and within forty-five seconds of calculated maneuvering, easily fished a giant, four-foot plush lightning fox from the secondary vault, dropping it straight into Harper’s eager arms.
Harper instantly beamed, hugging the fluffy yellow fox tightly against her chest, her cheeks flushed with a bright ridiculously happy pink glow.
"Alright," Harper declared twenty minutes later, having safely deposited their massive plushies into a secure VIP storage locker near the concourse.
Her violet eyes flashed with ultimate, high-stakes determination as she adjusted her jacket. "This is the true main event of Phase Four... The pinnacle of The Grand Nexus."
She led them to the heavily fortified, soundproofed fourth floor of the pavilion.
The floor opened into a vast circular amphitheater constructed from polished black basalt and illuminated by soft pulsing azure runic lines.
Resting in the center of the hall were three massive, egg-shaped Hyper-Immersive VR Sensory Pods.
The pods were forged from sleek obsidian alloy and reinforced silver conduits, their transparent canopies glowing with complex telemetry.
Standing beside the main console was a senior VR technician in a starched white lab coat, flanked by two assistants holding diagnostic clipboards.
The technician bowed respectfully as the three Lords approached.

"Welcome to Project... Dead Horizon," the lead technician introduced with a formal tone. "Our full-dive neural synchronization pods will perform a comprehensive biometric scan of your physical physiology and project your exact capabilities into a hyper-realistic and post-apocalyptic urban combat simulation... In this scenario, your elemental mana cores are suppressed... you will operate as elite black-ops operatives utilizing firearms and weaponry to survive waves of mutated undead. Pain receptors are calibrated to a standard five-percent feedback threshold for authentic feedback though nothing higher."
"A virtual war simulation?" Seraphina asked, her brow furrowing with refined curiosity as she examined the glowing pod. "Utilizing projectile combustion firearms rather than elemental spellcraft?"

"It’s pure gunplay, tactical positioning, and squad survival, Princess," Harper smirked, stepping up to the first open pod. "Let’s see how well your proud noble bloodline holds up when a hundred mutated corpses are sprinting down your throat in the dark..."

"House Bloom does not falter under pressure, regardless of the weaponry," Seraphina countered coldly, stepping gracefully into the second pod. "I will achieve the highest kill count in this engagement."
Silas climbed into the third pod, leaning his broad frame back against the ergonomic gel cushions.
HUMMMMM!
The heavy pressurized glass canopies of all three pods smoothly lowered, sealing shut with a pressurized mechanical hiss.
[SYSTEM INITIATING: FULL-DIVE NEURAL SYNCHRONIZATION]
[BIOMETRIC SCAN IN PROGRESS...]
[SCANNING SKELETAL STRUCTURE... 100%]
[SCANNING MUSCLE DENSITY... 100%]
[SCANNING SECONDARY PHYSICAL CHARACTERISTICS... 100%]
[CALIBRATING LOADOUTS...]
[ENTERING SERVER: LEVEL 1 - SECTOR ZERO OUTSKIRTS]
FLASH!
Silas opened his eyes.
The transition was instantaneous and utterly seamless.
The hum of the arcade pavilion was entirely gone, replaced by the choking stench of burning asphalt, rain-soaked concrete, and rotting organic decay.
They were standing in the middle of a shattered rain-slicked city intersection.
Crumbling skyscrapers towered into dark, storm-heavy skies, broken glass littered the streets, and overturned emergency vehicles burned with flickering orange flames.
Rain poured down in heavy, atmospheric sheets, drumming rhythmically against the ruined asphalt.
Silas looked down at himself.
