Here, the gleaming white marble of the upper city was entirely replaced by towering monoliths of reinforced dark-iron, colossal geothermal exhaust pipes hissing steam into the damp air, and massive automated blast doors.
Harper navigated the vehicle down an unmapped service tunnel that descended for nearly two kilometers beneath the bedrock.
’Why is it always underground...?’
Just like Shogitown too... did Valoria city have some sort of obsession with the underground?
At the end of the dark tunnel stood a fortified security checkpoint forged from solid adamantine plating.
Mounted along the reinforced bulkheads were four automated heavy-caliber mana-cannons glowing with charged azure energy.
Six elite, heavily armored mercenaries in unmarked black exosuits stood guard, holding high-power kinetic assault rifles equipped with suppression runes.
Harper slowed the vehicle to a halt, rolling down her window.
A tall mercenary commander with a scarred cybernetic eye stepped forward, raising a glowing sensor machine.
Without uttering a single word, Harper extended her hand, flashing a heavy, diamond-encrusted silver token bearing the crest of House Whitmore.
The mercenary tapped the token with his scanner.
BZZT-BEEP!
[IDENTITY VERIFIED: VIP SECTOR SECURED]
[CLEARANCE LEVEL: TIER-1 SOVEREIGN GUEST]
[WELCOME TO THE OBSIDIAN SANHEDRIN]
The mercenary stepped back, snapping a crisp respectful military salute.
He raised his hand, and with a deep groaning hydraulic rumble, the massive adamantine blast doors parted, revealing a sprawling lit pavilion beyond.
Harper accelerated through the threshold.
They pulled into a vast, private underground parking bay paved with polished black basalt.
Waiting at the base of the red carpet was a team of four impeccably dressed valets wearing matching crow masks and white silk gloves.
Harper brought the coupe to a smooth halt.
The scissor-doors hissed open, and the four masked figures stepped out onto the basalt floor.
Silas adjusted his cloak, his sharp senses immediately expanding.
Even beneath the polished veneer of the valet bay, he could feel the overlapping mana signatures of high-tier Awakened Lords and hidden defense arrays humming within the thick stone walls.
This was The Obsidian Sanhedrin... the most notorious and exclusive black-tier auction house in the entire continental hemisphere.
A tall elderly head butler wearing a flawless black tailcoat, white gloves, and a polished silver crow mask stepped forward from the private elevator archway.
He bowed deeply, extending an arm toward the gilded lift.
"Welcome to The Obsidian Sanhedrin, honored delegates of House Whitmore," the butler spoke in a low magically altered baritone that masked his natural voice.
"Your private suite has been fully prepared so please, allow me to escort you to the high tier."
Reginald, wearing his own crow mask and black cloak, stepped up beside Silas, maintaining his disciplined rigid posture as the group entered the private glass elevator.
The lift ascended silently, arriving at the highest VIP tier of the colossal amphitheater.
The butler led them down a private soundproofed corridor of black marble and gold trim, stopping before a set of towering double doors forged from lacquered dark-iron.
He tapped an authorization rune on the frame and the heavy doors swung smoothly open, revealing VIP Suite Seven.
The suite was vast, opulent, and breathtakingly luxurious.

The floor was paved with deep emerald quartz, covered in plush velvet rugs and furnished with massive, curved leather seating lounges, private banquet tables, and an expansive bar stocked with rare, glowing vintage mana-elixirs.
The entire front wall of the suite consisted of a colossal panoramic pane of enchanted, one-way transparent obsidian glass that looked out over the massive auction colosseum below.

From inside the suite, they had a crystal-clear, commanding view of the entire multi-tiered place yet from the outside, the glass appeared as a flat, impenetrable sheet of reflective black stone, completely concealing the occupants from the thousands of masked spectators gathered in the general admission floor below.
Reginald stopped precisely at the entrance of the suite.
The veteran butler turned on his heel, folding his hands behind his back as he took up his guard post directly outside the threshold.
"I shall secure the exterior perimeter," Reginald stated with quiet professionalism.
"Enjoy the proceedings."
"Thank you, Reginald," Seraphina replied, stepping into the suite.
The auction butler guided Silas, Harper, and Seraphina to the central leather lounge positioned directly before the observation glass.
Mounted on the low mahogany table in front of the lounge was an intricate, glowing console of polished brass and floating holographic glyphs.
"This is your dedicated bidding terminal," the butler explained smoothly, gesturing to the glowing interface.
The array allows you to place bids of any magnitude using virtual credits... a purely numerical representation tethered to your registered identity in the auction.

Should you successfully win a lot, the Sanhedrin will collect the full amount upon item delivery and failure to complete payment results in immediate termination of your bidding privileges and, depending on the severity, a retrieval team dispatched to your last known coordinates...
All transmissions are encrypted through three independent Leyline relays to ensure bidder anonymity.
He bowed low, stepping over to the banquet table.
"I have provided chilled celestial nectars and light seasonal delicacies for your comfort.
The formal proceedings shall commence in precisely three minutes.
Should you require further service, simply depress the silver chime on your armrest."
"That will be all.
Dismissed," Harper commanded with crisp authority.
The butler bowed once more and backed out of the room, the heavy iron doors sealing shut behind him with a pressurized click.
Harper let out a long satisfied breath, pulling down the lower half of her crow mask to expose her radiant smiling lips.
She walked over to the observation glass, looking down at the bustling multi-tiered amphitheater below with glowing violet eyes.
’Finally...’ Harper thought, a fierce triumphant thrill coursing through her veins. ’We made it right on time.’
Harper hadn’t picked this auction out of a random hat.

Behind her playful exterior, Harper Whitmore was an elite Lord who had recently been appointed as the Executive Director overseeing the four primary Lord Association Building Facilities in Valoria City.
House Whitmore and the High Council of the other four were currently in the delicate, high-stakes process of acquiring a fifth major administrative bastion in the northern sector.
’We will get it...’

Two days ago, her private intelligence network had flagged an encrypted classified manifest... an ancient foreign artifact weapon, smuggled across the continental borders from the shattered ruins of the Western Empires, was scheduled to be auctioned off as the grand finale of tonight’s auction.
Securing that weapon wasn’t just a personal luxury... it was a massive strategic power play that would solidify her undisputed military authority over the new sector.
Harper turned her head, looking at Silas, who had just sat down in the center of the plush leather lounge, his broad frame leaning comfortably against the cushions as he adjusted his crow mask.
Harper’s lips curved into a soft and intensely affectionate smile.
She walked over, sliding onto the leather sofa right beside him, boldly wrapping both of her arms around his left bicep and leaning her head against his shoulder.

’And the best part,’ Harper thought with a happy conspiratorial flutter in her chest, ’is that my handsome hubby gets to sit here in total luxury, watch the highest-stakes show in the city, and buy whatever crazy rare materials he needs to upgrade that mysterious territory of his...
It’s the ultimate win-win date!’
Beside them, Seraphina sat down on the right side of the lounge, her crimson eyes scanning the crowd below through her mask.
"The security wards in this facility are remarkably nice," Seraphina noted with her sharp senses picking up the latent magical arrays.
"There are at least twelve suppression spells embedded within the ceiling architecture."
"Black-tier syndicates don’t take chances, Princess," Harper replied, resting her chin on Silas’s shoulder.
"There’s too much money moving through one room."
Silas looked down through the one-way observation glass, taking in the grand spectacle of the subterranean arena.

The general floor below was packed with hundreds of masked figures seated in tiered rows of dark stone benches... wealthy merchants, rogue Lords, syndicate bosses, and foreign envoys, all draped in dark cloaks and identity-concealing visors.

Above them, circling the perimeter of the cavernous dome, hung forty private VIP suites identical to their own, their black-glass windows gleaming under the ambient light like the cold unblinking eyes of predators.
’An underground auction...’ Silas thought, a genuine electric spark of excitement igniting in his chest.

Back in his past life on Earth, he had read dozens of serialized cultivation and urban fantasy web novels featuring shadowy underground auction arcs where ancient treasures were unearthed and arrogant young masters threw fortunes around like pocket change.

But reading words on a glowing phone screen and actually sitting inside a real-world auction suite... surrounded by real mana-beasts, genuine spatial artifacts, and stakes were two different realms of reality.
The novelty of it made his blood pump with eager anticipation.
CLANG!
CLANG!
CLANG!
Three deep strikes of a heavy bronze bell echoed through the amphitheater, cutting straight through the murmurs of the crowd.
The lights across the general floor slowly dimmed, plunging the lower tiers into pitch-black shadow.
FWOOSH.
A massive blinding column of pure, white mana-light erupted from the center of the arena floor, illuminating a colossal circular stage forged from polished, blood-red obsidian.
Stepping into the center of the spotlight was the Chief Auctioneer of the Obsidian Sanhedrin.
The man was tall, slender, and immaculately dressed in a dark-crimson tailcoat trimmed with gold scales.
He wore an elaborate half-face porcelain mask depicting a laughing demon, his voice amplified by speakers that carried his booming voice directly into every corner of the colosseum.

"Honored Lords, sovereign delegates, esteemed syndicates, and distinguished guests of the shadows!" the auctioneer projected with grand sweeping gestures, bowing deeply to both the general floor and the elevated VIP suites.
"Welcome to the grand midnight conclave of The Obsidian Sanhedrin!"

chapters.title: Chapter 396: Obsidian Sanhedrin [II]
paragraphs: A low collective rumble of excitement rippled through the hundreds of masked spectators below.

"Tonight," the auctioneer continued, his eyes gleaming behind his porcelain mask, "we present a curated collection of rarity, harvested from the deepest rifts, the forgotten tombs of the Old World, and the borders of the foreign empires! Artifacts of war, forbidden alchemical blueprints, untamed beast cores, and dimensional relics that the World Council would rather bury in the dust of history!"
He raised his right hand, pointing dramatically toward the ceiling.

"And for those patient enough to endure the crucible of bidding until the final hour... our grand finale lot features a weapon of calamity... a relic forged across the continental divide, capable of altering the military balance of an entire sector!"
Murmurs of intense speculation and hushed whispers erupted across the lower tiers, while several VIP suites subtly flared with suppressed mana signatures.
"Let the shadows claim their prize!" the auctioneer roared, slamming his gold-headed gavel against a floating obsidian podium.
BANG!
"Bring forth the premier lot of the evening!"
From the subterranean lift beneath the stage, a circular anti-gravity pedestal rose smoothly into the center of the spotlight.
Resting atop a cushion of dark velvet was a jagged fist-sized crystal that glowed with a deep violet luminescence.
Thin arcs of crackling unstable plasma danced across its multifaceted surface, causing the air above the pedestal to warp and shimmer with uncontained pressure.

"Lot Number One!" the auctioneer announced with electric fervor. "The Heart of the Thunder-Wyrm! Harvested from the core of an Tier-1 Abyssal Wyrm in the Western Rift Expanse! This pristine unrefined core contains over five hundred thousand units of elemental lightning mana, perfectly suited for forging Vanguard armaments or powering an entire municipal defense barrier for half a decade!"
The auctioneer slammed his gavel onto the podium.
"Bidding commences at a baseline of Five Hundred Thousand Spirit Credits! Increments of fifty thousand! The floor is open!"
Silas, Harper, and Seraphina watched the glowing violet crystal through the observation glass.

"A decent core," Harper commented casually, leaning her cheek against Silas’s shoulder. "High purity, but the internal mana conduits are slightly fractured... It would take weeks of alchemical stabilization before you could use it in a weapon forge so it’s not worth the hassle."
"Agreed," Seraphina chimed in, crossing her legs. "House Bloom harvests dozens of similar cores from our southern territory rifts each quarter. It’s quite a crude entry piece."
Silas didn’t bid either.
’Do I even have any Lightning mages in my territory? Ah yes, I think there are one or two.’
Even then, this wasn’t really good for him either...
However, on the general floor below, the crowd did not share their noble indifference.
BEEP! BEEP! BEEP!
Glowing digital numbers lit up across the massive circular display ring suspended above the stage as masked bidders aggressively hammered their consoles.
[CURRENT BID: 650,000 SC - FLOOR TIER 3]
[CURRENT BID: 800,000 SC - FLOOR TIER 1]
[CURRENT BID: 1,100,000 SC - FLOOR TIER 2]
[CURRENT BID: 1,350,000 SC - FLOOR TIER 1]
The numbers climbed with furious breakneck speed.
Bidders shouted across the stone tiers, waving their transaction wands as the price easily doubled within sixty seconds.
"One point three five million to the gentleman in the raven visor!" the auctioneer shouted, his voice building the hype. "Do I hear one point four?! One point four million?!"
BZZZZT-CHUNK.
Suddenly, the massive holographic display above the stage flashed with a deep, authoritative crimson hue.
[BID: VIP SUITE TWELVE]
CURRENT BID: 2,500,000 SPIRIT CREDITS
A collective stunned hush instantly fell over the general floor.
The lower-tier bidders slumped back into their stone benches, muttering in bitter frustration as they lowered their wands.
Dropping two point five million credits on an entry-level core was an aggressive arrogant flex designed specifically to crush the competition in a single blow.
Silas glanced across the dark expanse of the colosseum toward VIP Suite Twelve.

The one-way glass of Suite Twelve was dark, but an arrogant aura of refined wind mana subtly leaked from the ventilation conduits, signaling the presence of a wealthy corporate scion or a high-ranking director.
"Two point five million credits from VIP Suite Twelve!" the auctioneer cried out, scanning the arena. "Going once... Going twice..."
BANG!
"Sold! To the sovereign patron of Suite Twelve!"
Beside Silas, Harper let out a sharp audible tch, aggressively clicking her tongue against her teeth as she glared at Suite Twelve through her crow mask.

"Arrogant prick," Harper muttered under her breath, rolling her eyes. "Dropping two point five mil on a cracked wyrm core just to flex on people. If you’re wondering, that’s House Thorne corporate box over there and they always act like obnoxious peacocks."
Silas leaned back into the plush leather cushions with a deeply thrilled smirk spreading beneath his crow mask as he watched the glowing stage reset for the next lot.
’This...’ Silas thought, his golden mana thrumming with eager anticipation. ’is going to be a very interesting night.’
The underground auction had officially begun.
Perched high upon the western mezzanine of the colossal amphitheater, suspended in the cold, cavernous shadows like a predatory nest, was VIP Suite Twelve.
The suite was bathed in the harsh flickering amber glow of enchanted gas sconces.
The air inside was suffocating, choked with the pungent acrid haze of imported dread-tobacco and the sharp sting of spilled alchemical spirits.

Polished mahogany tables were littered with crystal carafes, half-empty chalices of spiced brandy, and discarded trade manifests bearing the gilded insignia of the Blackwood Consortium’s thorny black briars intertwined with the storm-crested gale-hawk of House Thorne.
Lounging in the center of an expansive emerald-velvet sofa was Cedric Blackwood.
He was nineteen years of age, blessed with the sharp noble jawline and haughty bone structure characteristic of the High Spire bloodlines.
His hair... a lustrous vibrant golden-blond was meticulously combed and slicked straight back with fragrant pomade, gleaming like polished brass under the ambient mana-light.
His tailored three-piece suit was woven from shimmering gale-silk, fastened with diamond-encrusted silver buttons that bore the Thorne family crest.
By right of birth, Cedric was an untouchable sovereign scion.
His father was the heir of the Blackwood Consortium, while his mother was the direct heiress to the sprawling commercial empire of the Thorne Conglomerate.

As the sole recognized heir to the Blackwood lineage who also commanded the bottomless liquidity of the Thorne financial vaults, Cedric was accustomed to walking through the world as if every cobblestone had been laid specifically for his boots.
Yet, despite his astronomical pedigree, Cedric’s handsome face was currently twisted into a dark twitching scowl of pure venomous frustration.
’Fuck...’
His manicured fingers absentmindedly rose to his left cheek, lightly brushing the skin.
Beneath his fingertips, phantom heat seemed to burn against his flesh.

It had been weeks since the incident in the grand promenade of Weaver’s Spire, yet the memory of that humiliating thunderous slap delivered by a dirty common-born brute whose name had been forgotten still festered in Cedric’s mind like an infected wound.
Every time he closed his eyes, he could still hear the collective gasps of the onlookers, still feel the disgraceful impact that had thrown him backward like a discarded sack of flour.
"Where in the hell is Valerius?!" Cedric barked, his voice echoing sharply off the soundproofed obsidian walls.
He slammed his crystal glass onto the mahogany side table with enough violent force to crack the base, sending spiced brandy splashing across the lacquered wood.
Standing three paces behind the sofa, her hands clasped tightly over the starched white fabric of her apron, was his personal attendant.
She was a young woman with neat brown hair pinned into a modest bun, her delicate features pale and taut with anxiety.
Her gaze remained rigidly fixed upon the emerald carpet beneath her polished shoes, not daring to meet the young master’s volatile eyes.

"Young Master," the maid began softly, her voice carrying a fragile cautious tremor that she desperately tried to suppress. "Lord Valerius sent an encrypted transmission nearly an hour ago... His armored transport was unexpectedly detained at a junction by an inquisitor from the High Council. They initiated a full-scale contraband sweep across the northern lines..."
Cedric’s jaw clenched so hard his molars ground together audibly.
"And why has he not updated me?! We have an entire secure comm-array in this damn box!"

"The dampening wards of The Obsidian Sanhedrin, Young Master," the maid explained, swallowing the dry knot in her throat. "The moment the external blast doors cycled shut for the session, all wireless networks, satellite relays, and transponders were forcibly severed. No signals can penetrate these bedrock walls until the auction concludes and the master seals are disengaged... We are completely isolated."
Cedric let out a furious sharp hiss of air through his teeth, violently running both of his ring-adorned hands through his slicked-back blond hair.

"Incompetent fools," Cedric snarled, his eyes narrowing into cold slits. "The one evening my elder brother promised to personally mentor me on black-market leverage, the one night he was supposed to teach me how to manipulate the bidding spreads, and he gets himself locked outside the gate like a common vagrant in the rain."
He slumped back into the plush cushions of the sofa, crossing his legs and glaring down through the one-way obsidian observation glass at the circular stage below.

Down in the spotlight, the massive circular display had just flashed with the confirmation of Lot Number One... the Tier-1 Heart of the Thunder-Wyrm which Cedric had just secured for a staggering two point five million Spirit Credits with a single aggressive tap of his terminal.
Seeing the young master’s turbulent temper, the maid took a small hesitant step forward.
She knew the scale of the funds at play tonight, and more importantly, she knew the terrifying instructions Lord Valerius had given her prior to the auction.

"Young Master Cedric," she murmured, keeping her tone as deferential and non-threatening as possible. "If I may humbly offer a reminder... Lord Valerius and the elder council explicitly designated ninety percent of our vault reserves for the Grand Finale lot. The classified intelligence reports regarding the foreign weapon suggest that several continental cartels and foreign military proxies are present tonight... If we spend millions of credits flexing on beast cores and decorative curios in the early rounds, we risk depleting our liquidity before the true war begins."
The room went deathly silent.
Cedric did not move for several long seconds then, slowly his blond head rotated toward her.
His pale gray eyes locked onto the trembling maid with the frigid, unblinking disdain of a high-born lord staring down at an insect that had dared to crawl across his dinner plate.
"Are you lecturing me?" Cedric whispered with his voice sounding dangerously soft.
The maid’s breath hitched in her chest. "N-No, Young Master! I would never—"

"Are you, a nameless low-born servant whose entire bloodline survives on the copper scraps tossed from my family’s banquet tables, attempting to instruct an heir of the Blackwood Consortium on financial strategy?" Cedric’s voice dropped into a chilling purr as he uncrossed his legs and leaned forward, resting his forearms on his knees. "Did you truly just suggest that my household could go broke over a few million credits?"
"Forgive me, Young Master! I was only relaying Lord Valerius’s parameters—"
"Silence," Cedric snapped, the single word cutting through her frantic apology like a whip.
He pointed a single diamond-ringed index finger toward the emerald carpet directly at the base of his sofa.
"Get on your hands and knees," Cedric commanded smoothly.
The maid’s eyes widened in sheer, agonizing terror. Her lower lip began to tremble as hot tears of humiliation stung the corners of her eyes.
"Young Master, please... I have served your mother’s household for six years—"

"I said get down," Cedric repeated, his tone entirely flat, lacking of a single ounce of human warmth. "Your vulgar insolent mouth has grown entirely too comfortable in my brother’s absence... You seem to have forgotten your fundamental purpose in this room. You are not an advisor, you are not a strategist either. You are a domestic fixture and a footstool. Now get on the floor and act like one, before I have the enforcers toss you into the incinerator chutes below."
A shudder ran through the young woman’s entire body.
She knew that within the black-tier perimeter of The Obsidian Sanhedrin, an heir of the Blackwood Consortium could murder a servant with zero legal repercussions.
No court in Valoria would ever question a missing maid.
Slowly, her knees trembling so violently they nearly gave out beneath her, the young woman sank to the floor.
She crawled forward onto the plush emerald rug directly in front of the sofa, lowering her chest and placing her palms flat against the fabric.
She bowed her head, pressing her forehead against the floorboards and locking her spine into a flat horizontal bench.
Cedric watched her with a cruel triumphant smirk curving his lips.
He leaned back into the deep leather cushions of the sofa, reached out with his heavy leather boots, and rested both of his heels directly upon the back of the maid’s neck and shoulders.
He dug his heels in, applying his full body weight until the girl let out a muffled, choked gasp of pain beneath him.
"Much better," Cedric sighed comfortably, reaching over to the silver tray on the table to pluck a thick dark cigar. "I want to do this to that guy too... the next time I see him."

We have an entire secure comm-array in this damn box!"
"The dampening wards of The Obsidian Sanhedrin, Young Master," the maid explained, swallowing the dry knot in her throat.
"The moment the external blast doors cycled shut for the session, all wireless networks, satellite relays, and transponders were forcibly severed.
No signals can penetrate these bedrock walls until the auction concludes and the master seals are disengaged...
We are completely isolated."
Cedric let out a furious sharp hiss of air through his teeth, violently running both of his ring-adorned hands through his slicked-back blond hair.
"Incompetent fools," Cedric snarled, his eyes narrowing into cold slits.

"The one evening my elder brother promised to personally mentor me on black-market leverage, the one night he was supposed to teach me how to manipulate the bidding spreads, and he gets himself locked outside the gate like a common vagrant in the rain."
He slumped back into the plush cushions of the sofa, crossing his legs and glaring down through the one-way obsidian observation glass at the circular stage below.

Down in the spotlight, the massive circular display had just flashed with the confirmation of Lot Number One... the Tier-1 Heart of the Thunder-Wyrm which Cedric had just secured for a staggering two point five million Spirit Credits with a single aggressive tap of his terminal.
Seeing the young master’s turbulent temper, the maid took a small hesitant step forward.
She knew the scale of the funds at play tonight, and more importantly, she knew the terrifying instructions Lord Valerius had given her prior to the auction.
"Young Master Cedric," she murmured, keeping her tone as deferential and non-threatening as possible.
"If I may humbly offer a reminder...
Lord Valerius and the elder council explicitly designated ninety percent of our vault reserves for the Grand Finale lot.
The classified intelligence reports regarding the foreign weapon suggest that several continental cartels and foreign military proxies are present tonight...
If we spend millions of credits flexing on beast cores and decorative curios in the early rounds, we risk depleting our liquidity before the true war begins."
The room went deathly silent.
Cedric did not move for several long seconds then, slowly his blond head rotated toward her.
His pale gray eyes locked onto the trembling maid with the frigid, unblinking disdain of a high-born lord staring down at an insect that had dared to crawl across his dinner plate.
"Are you lecturing me?" Cedric whispered with his voice sounding dangerously soft.
The maid’s breath hitched in her chest.
"N-No, Young Master!
I would never—"

"Are you, a nameless low-born servant whose entire bloodline survives on the copper scraps tossed from my family’s banquet tables, attempting to instruct an heir of the Blackwood Consortium on financial strategy?" Cedric’s voice dropped into a chilling purr as he uncrossed his legs and leaned forward, resting his forearms on his knees.
"Did you truly just suggest that my household could go broke over a few million credits?"
"Forgive me, Young Master!
I was only relaying Lord Valerius’s parameters—"
"Silence," Cedric snapped, the single word cutting through her frantic apology like a whip.
He pointed a single diamond-ringed index finger toward the emerald carpet directly at the base of his sofa.
"Get on your hands and knees," Cedric commanded smoothly.
The maid’s eyes widened in sheer, agonizing terror.
Her lower lip began to tremble as hot tears of humiliation stung the corners of her eyes.
"Young Master, please...
I have served your mother’s household for six years—"
"I said get down," Cedric repeated, his tone entirely flat, lacking of a single ounce of human warmth.
"Your vulgar insolent mouth has grown entirely too comfortable in my brother’s absence...
You seem to have forgotten your fundamental purpose in this room.
You are not an advisor, you are not a strategist either.
You are a domestic fixture and a footstool.
Now get on the floor and act like one, before I have the enforcers toss you into the incinerator chutes below."
A shudder ran through the young woman’s entire body.
She knew that within the black-tier perimeter of The Obsidian Sanhedrin, an heir of the Blackwood Consortium could murder a servant with zero legal repercussions.
No court in Valoria would ever question a missing maid.
Slowly, her knees trembling so violently they nearly gave out beneath her, the young woman sank to the floor.
She crawled forward onto the plush emerald rug directly in front of the sofa, lowering her chest and placing her palms flat against the fabric.
She bowed her head, pressing her forehead against the floorboards and locking her spine into a flat horizontal bench.
Cedric watched her with a cruel triumphant smirk curving his lips.
He leaned back into the deep leather cushions of the sofa, reached out with his heavy leather boots, and rested both of his heels directly upon the back of the maid’s neck and shoulders.
He dug his heels in, applying his full body weight until the girl let out a muffled, choked gasp of pain beneath him.
"Much better," Cedric sighed comfortably, reaching over to the silver tray on the table to pluck a thick dark cigar.
"I want to do this to that guy too... the next time I see him."

chapters.title: Chapter 397: Obsidian Sanhedrin [III]
paragraphs: He snapped his fingers, conjuring a tiny spark of green wind mana to ignite the tip, and drew a long deep breath of the fragrant smoke.
He exhaled a thick, drifting cloud of blue haze toward the ceiling, crossing his arms behind his head while resting his heavy boots firmly upon the trembling girl’s spine.

"My family commands the combined financial supremacy of the Blackwood Consortium and House Thorne," Cedric sneered, looking down through the glass with supreme arrogance. "We possess more liquid Spirit Credits than thirty lower districts combined... I will bid on whatever catches my eye, whenever I please, and my father will settle the ledger without a second thought so let the commoners watch how a true sovereign spends."
Across the vast echoing expanse of the amphitheater, suspended high on the eastern wall in VIP Suite Seven, the atmosphere was different.

The massive soundproofed iron doors of the suite remained firmly sealed, while Reginald stood outside in the corridor like an unyielding shadow, his hands clasped behind his back as his sharp senses locked down the entire eastern hallway.
Inside the suite, Silas sat dead center on the enormous, curved emerald-leather sectional.
He was still draped in the heavy flowing black velvet cloak of House Whitmore, though he had tilted the obsidian crow mask upward so that it rested comfortably atop his dark messy hair.
His rugged jawline was relaxed, his broad shoulders resting back against the plush cushions as his deep blue golden-ringed eyes swept across the multi-tiered colosseum below.
Suddenly, the soft luxurious rustle of enchanted phoenix silk cut through the quiet sound of the suite’s ventilation.
Before Silas could even blink, Seraphina glided gracefully around the mahogany coffee table.
Without a single word of warning, the crimson-haired heiress turned around, gathered her voluminous skirts, and deliberately sat down directly on Silas’s lap.
FLUMP!
Silas’s entire body went rigid.
His breath hitched in his throat as two hundred pounds of pure muscle instinctively locked up.
Seraphina settled herself snugly between his thighs, leaning her entire upper back against his broad chest.
The radiant heat of her ancestral core radiated straight through the enchanted fabric of her crimson gown, warming his torso like an open hearth.
The rich intoxicating fragrance of crushed night-blooming jasmine and sweet vanilla rolled over his senses in an intoxicating wave.
She let out a soft unapologetic sigh of contentment, tilting her head back against his muscular shoulder.
Her long vibrant crimson curls spilled across his collarbone, brushing softly against his cheek.

"Ah..." Seraphina purred melodically, her long eyelashes fluttering shut as she reached down with her manicured fingers to rub the arch of her left foot through her sheer silk stockings. "My feet are positively throbbing with fatigue... We have been traversing this wretched metropolis since twelve o’clock this afternoon, and the marble flooring in that arcade lacked any semblance of shock absorption. As my designated prospective husband, it is only proper and natural that your frame serves as my primary resting cushion."
Silas sat completely paralyzed with his large hands hovering awkwardly in mid-air beside her slender corseted waist.
His left eye gave a violent involuntary twitch.

’Is this girl for real right now?’ Silas thought. ’There are literally three empty velvet armchairs, two chaise lounges, and an entire ten-foot leather couch in this room, and she chooses to park her noble ass directly on my kneecaps. I... don’t mind though.’
On the other side of the sofa, Harper’s head whipped around so fast her violet curls blurred.
Her glowing violet eyes dilated in pure, unadulterated, incandescent fury.

"GET OFF HIM, YOU SHAMELESS CRIMSON PARASITE!" Harper shrieked, lunging forward across the leather cushions with her hands curved like claws, bright purple sparks of static electricity visibly popping along the lapels of her black jacket. "Who authorized you to drop your royal backside onto his lap?! That is my territory! Move your ass right now, or I swear by the World Council I will discharge a hundred thousand volts straight through your tailbone!"
"I shall not move a single inch," Seraphina countered without even deigning to open her eyes.
She casually lifted one long, silk-clad leg and crossed it over the other atop Silas’s denim-clad thighs, deliberately nestling deeper into the crook of his neck.

"I established dominion over this seat first," Seraphina mocked smoothly as a small insufferably smug smirk playing at the corners of her glossed lips. "If you are so desperately starved for physical proximity, woman, you are entirely welcome to kneel upon the rug and rest your chin against my ankles."
"I WILL RIP YOUR EXPENSIVE EXTENSIONS OUT ONE BY ONE—"
"Harper. Seraphina. Calm down..." Silas commanded with his low voice vibrating straight through his chest and into Seraphina’s spine.
Both women froze instantly.
Silas let out a heavy soul-weary exhale, his hands finally descending to rest firmly against the sides of Seraphina’s hips to keep her from sliding around.
The touch caused the proud noblewoman’s porcelain skin to instantly erupt in a brilliant burning shade of pink, though she stubbornly refused to surrender her captured territory.
Down in the center of the arena below, the Chief Auctioneer raised his gold-headed gavel, bringing it down against the floating obsidian podium with a resounding bang.

"Lot Number One is officially concluded!" the auctioneer’s magically amplified voice reverberated through the amphitheater. "The Heart of the Thunder-Wyrm has been securely transferred to the holding vault corresponding to VIP Suite Twelve! As a reminder to all our esteemed patrons, all acquired items shall be held in private sealed retrieval chambers tagged with your specific suite numbers, accessible immediately upon the conclusion of tonight’s proceedings!"
The auctioneer raised his hands wide, his theatrical porcelain demon mask catching the harsh glare of the white spotlights.
"And now, honored delegates of the shadows... let us bring forth the second lot of the evening!"
From the depths of the stage’s subterranean hydraulic lift, a long horizontal display case lined with midnight-black velvet rose smoothly into the center of the arena.
Resting inside the case were a pair of slender curved katanas.
The blades were forged from a dark non-reflective obsidian-steel that seemed to actively devour the surrounding light.

The hilts were wrapped in the cured, scales of an abyssal shadow-serpent, and thin, wispy ribbons of shadowy mist continually bled from the razor-sharp edges, curling across the velvet cushions like living smoke.

"Lot Number Two!" the auctioneer announced with electric showmanship. "The Twin Phantoms of the Mist! A pair of Tier-2 Stealth Katanas recovered from an ancient hidden shinobi sanctuary deep within an Uncharted Rift Sector of the Sovereign Realm... These blades were traded to The Obsidian Sanhedrin by a high-ranking master from the Shadow Lotus Clan. They are permanently inscribed with dampening glyphs that completely erase all sound, vibration, and light reflection during high-speed swings, amplifying critical strike output by two hundred and fifty percent when striking from pure concealment!"
The auctioneer slammed his gavel.
"Bidding commences at a baseline of Three Million Spirit Credits! Increments of one hundred thousand! The floor is open!"
The moment the words left his mouth, Harper’s violet eyes ignited with raw hunger.
She sat bolt upright on the leather sofa, her entire body locking onto the display case.

As a high-mobility Lightning Lord whose combat style relied heavily on explosive speed, sudden flank maneuvers, and devastating close-quarters strikes, a pair of dual blades that completely erased sound and multiplied critical strike output was a dream weapon.

"Oh, those are exquisite," Harper whispered, her fingers practically vibrating with excitement as she hovered over the brass bidding terminal. "Those are coming home with me... I don’t care who I have to bankrupt."
It wasn’t like she was going to go bankrupt, even before this whole inheriting her Father’s business thing, Harper had hundreds of millions saved.
This would not be an issue after at all... which was why she was confident in paying for everything. Down on the floor, the bidding war erupted instantly.
BEEP! BEEP! BEEP!
[CURRENT BID: 3,400,000 SC - FLOOR TIER 2]
[CURRENT BID: 4,100,000 SC - FLOOR TIER 1]
[CURRENT BID: 5,500,000 SC - FLOOR TIER 3]
Across the amphitheater in VIP Suite Twelve, Cedric Blackwood casually tapped his console with the heavy heel of his boot, not even bothering to look down from the ceiling.
BZZZZT-CHUNK!
[BID: VIP SUITE TWELVE]
CURRENT BID: 10,000,000 SPIRIT CREDITS
Cedric let out a loud mocking laugh, exhaling a thick plume of cigar smoke as he ground his heels harder into the kneeling maid’s shoulders.
"Ten million," Cedric scoffed arrogantly. "Let the commoners choke on that... A pair of exotic ninja toys will look splendid mounted above the mantle in my secondary estate."
The lower-tier floor bidders groaned in bitter defeat, lowering their glowing transaction wands as the ten-million-credit barrier proved too steep for an entry-level Tier-2 weapon.
Harper, however, merely let out a dark wicked chuckle.
"Ten million? Cute." Harper grinned, her sharp canines flashing under the lights.
She didn’t touch the standard increment button.
Her slender fingers blurred across the numerical spatial grid of Suite Seven’s console, keying in a ruthless figure with pure malice.
BZZZZT-CHUNK!
[BID: VIP SUITE SEVEN]
CURRENT BID: 20,000,000 SPIRIT CREDITS
The entire amphitheater fell dead silent.
In Suite Twelve, Cedric choked violently on his cigar smoke.
He began coughing uncontrollably, his boots slipping off the maid’s head as he scrambled forward, nearly spilling his drink as he stared in disbelief at the glowing scoreboard.
"Twenty million?!" Cedric roared, his slicked-back blond hair falling messily over his forehead. "Who the hell drops twenty million on a pair of Tier-2 katanas?! Are they insane?!"
His pride stung, Cedric furiously hammered the console, entering 22,000,000 SC.
BZZZZT-CHUNK.
Before the numbers on the display could even settle, Suite Seven flashed instantly.
[BID: VIP SUITE SEVEN]
CURRENT BID: 35,000,000 SPIRIT CREDITS
Cedric’s jaw dropped open. His hand hovered over the console, trembling with pure fury.
Thirty-five million credits for Tier-2 stealth blades was madness.
To push higher would severely compromise his liquidity for the grand finale lot.
Down on the carpet, the kneeling maid subtly shifted her head with a tiny satisfying smirk dancing across her lips as she watched her arrogant master get thoroughly humiliated by Suite Seven.
BANG!
"Sold! To the sovereign delegates of VIP Suite Seven for Thirty-Five Million Spirit Credits!"
Harper threw both of her arms in the air, cackling wildly. "YES! Mine! That’s how a woman claims her steel!"
Silas looked at her, he looked very disgusted and she pinched his cheeks.
"You look so cute Silas~ Wanna kiss?"
Over the next two hours, the underground auction progressed into a relentless breathtaking spectacle of wealth and power.
Silas, Harper, and Seraphina watched with fascination as dozens of bizarre treasures crossed the circular red stage.
Not every item drew their interest, allowing the lower-tier syndicates and rival VIP suites to fight bitterly amongst themselves.

Lot Number Five... a sealed ceramic barrel containing fifty liters of Pure Wyrm-Marrow Elixir, capable of permanently increasing an awakened warrior’s bone density was claimed by a mercenary syndicate from the northern wastes for fourteen million credits.

Lot Number Eight... a set of four ancient Aero-Dynamic Flight Relics forged in the shape of mechanical falcon wings was snatched up by VIP Suite Four after a brutal bidding war that peaked at twenty-eight million credits.
Then, the mood in the amphitheater shifted dramatically as Lot Number Eleven was wheeled into the spotlight.

Resting inside a massive reinforced cylindrical containment vessel forged from enchanted poly-crystal and filled with swirling translucent liquid flame was a crimson orb roughly the size of a human skull.
Inside the orb, the roaring spectral silhouette of a miniature, four-winged fire chimera writhed in violent primeval fury.
The radiation leaking through the glass was so intense that the barrier around the circular stage visibly distorted and shimmered like a desert mirage.

"Lot Number Eleven!" the auctioneer projected, his voice booming with electric excitement. "The Primordial Will of the Blazing Chimera! A genuine Tier-3 Beast Will harvested from the core of an ancient rift beast in the Volcanic Trenches! For those unfamiliar with the ancient arts of beast binding... I’m here! A Beast Will is a dormant spiritual core. Upon infusing this relic with a massive volume of elemental mana, conquering its spiritual trial, and establishing soul resonance, the beast will awaken as a living permanent familiar bound directly to the user’s soul and core!"
The auctioneer raised his gavel high.
"Bidding commences at a baseline of Forty Million Spirit Credits! Increments of two million! The floor is open!"
The moment the description ended, Seraphina’s entire body went rigid on Silas’s lap.
Her crimson eyes, blazing with concentrated fire, locked onto the flaming chimera core with an intensity that seemed capable of melting the observation glass.
Her breath came in short rapid gasps with her fingers digging tightly into Silas’s denim-clad knees.

"That beast will..." Seraphina whispered, her melodic voice trembling with noble desire. "The purity of the flame... it is completely unblemished. If I infuse that core with my ancestral crimson flame and bond it to my Primordial Fire Spirit, the resulting familiar will possess destructive synchronization with my bloodline. The Spirit would amplify the chimera’s output, and the chimera would feed pure elemental fire back into my Spirit, creating an eternal loop of escalating flame. My core temperature could double. I must have it."
’Double...?’ Silas thought with sweat rushing down his face, her flames were hot enough already!

"The purity of the flame... it is completely unblemished.
If I infuse that core with my ancestral crimson flame and bond it to my Primordial Fire Spirit, the resulting familiar will possess destructive synchronization with my bloodline.
The Spirit would amplify the chimera’s output, and the chimera would feed pure elemental fire back into my Spirit, creating an eternal loop of escalating flame.
My core temperature could double.
I must have it."
’Double...?’ Silas thought with sweat rushing down his face, her flames were hot enough already!

chapters.title: Chapter 398: Obsidian Sanhedrin [IV]
paragraphs: "Then buy it, Princess," Silas said casually, his deep voice rumbling against her back. "You’ve got the card."
’As long as she doesn’t use it on me and doesn’t spend that much money... I’m okay...’
Seraphina didn’t hesitate for a single second.
She reached forward to the mahogany table, picked up the black executive card Reginald had provided, and tapped the terminal, entering a figure that made even Harper whistle in appreciation.
BZZZZT-CHUNK!
[BID: VIP SUITE SEVEN]
CURRENT BID: 100,000,000 SPIRIT CREDITS
The entire amphitheater collectively gasped.
Opening with a sixty-million-credit jump was a terrifying declaration of financial annihilation.
Across the arena in VIP Suite Twelve, Cedric Blackwood had just picked up his hand to enter a bid, intending to buy the chimera as a trophy.
But seeing the nine-figure hammer drop from Suite Seven, his hand froze mid-air.
His face turned a mottled,violent shade of scarlet as he hurled his crystal chalice across the room, shattering it against the dark-iron doors.
"Suite Seven AGAIN?!" Cedric shrieked, his voice cracking hysterically. "Are they stalking my bids?! Who the fuck is sitting in that booth?!"
Nobody on the floor dared challenge the hundred-million-credit barrier.
BANG!
"Sold! To VIP Suite Seven for One Hundred Million Spirit Credits!"
Seraphina settled back against Silas’s chest, letting out a soft triumphant purr of pure satisfaction.
"A magnificent acquisition... My mother will be thoroughly impressed."
Meanwhile Silas looked at her back with his face twitching through several expressions, he regretted coming here completely.
’Calm down Silas... Nobles... Nobles are different beings.’
Six lots later, Seraphina struck again.

When Lot Number Seventeen... a bespoke set of Ancient Void-Chrysolite Jewelry, consisting of two polished obsidian wrist cuffs and a heavy matching signet ring forged from indestructible abyssal alloy that passively accelerated internal mana recovery by thirty percent was displayed on the stage, Seraphina didn’t even blink.
’Mine.’
She casually dropped Fifty Million Spirit Credits to secure the set in a single bid.
Silas looked down at the top of her crimson head, raising an eyebrow.
"Black jewelry? That doesn’t match your red-and-gold noble aesthetic at all."
Seraphina turned her head slightly, looking up into his deep blue eyes through her long eyelashes as a radiant rosy blush sweeping across her porcelain cheeks.

"It is not for me, you oblivious brute," Seraphina mumbled, her voice dropping into a shy melodic whisper as she looked away. "It is a spousal tribute for a certain stubborn man who refuses to wear anything other than dark uncultured fabrics... You are mandated to wear it upon our return."
Silas blinked with a rare surprised warmth touching his chest.
He cleared his throat, rubbing the back of his neck as Harper groaned loudly in the background.
"What a shameless bribery... It doesn’t matter though, I’ll do better later." Harper said as she too began looking for jewelry.

To round out her personal shopping spree, Seraphina dropped another Seventy-Five Million Spirit Credits on Lot Twenty-One... an ancient five-hundred-year-old Phoenix-Ash Alchemical Crucible carved from petrified dragon bone, intended for refining high-grade core elixirs for House Bloom’s private laboratories.
’This woman is really rich...’ Silas thought, suddenly the amount that he received from Evelyn didn’t feel so big anymore. ’When am I going to see something that I want though?’
As the auction transitioned into the mid-twenties, Lot Twenty-Five was wheeled onto the circular stage.
Resting atop a cushion of pristine white silk was an exquisite, teardrop-shaped emerald necklace.
The central gemstone was roughly the size of a plum, suspended from a delicate shimmering chain woven from spun silver threads.
The moment the spotlight illuminated the jewel, a soft breathtaking emerald-green luminescence filled the amphitheater.
Through the audio speakers, the soothing melody of rustling leaves and the crisp clean aroma of morning dew seemed to drift into the room.

"Lot Twenty-Five!" the auctioneer announced with reverent eloquence. "The Tear of the Slumbering World! Recovered from the deepest sanctum of a petrified dying forest within an Uncharted Zone of the Sovereign Realm! While this relic possesses no direct offensive capabilities, it holds a vast, inexhaustible reservoir of ancient nature mana, capable of revitalizing barren sovereign soil, accelerating the growth of celestial herbs, and soothing wounded divine spirits."
The moment the words registered, Silas’s breath caught in his throat.
’The Tear of the Slumbering World...’ Silas thought, his golden-ringed eyes locking onto the glowing green pendant.

His mind immediately flashed back to the tranquil gardens of the Blessed Land in the Umbral Basin, where Eluned, the Former Spirit of the World Tree, spent her quiet days with him, tending to their crops, healing the troops, and watching over all of them with gentle unwavering divine loyalty.

’It belongs to her or rather it’ll fit her,’ Silas thought with a fierce protective warmth swelling in his chest. ’It would look breathtaking resting against her collarbone. And the pure nature mana will help her become stronger...’
Silas leaned forward, reaching out toward the brass bidding console on the mahogany table.
His fingers hovered over the keys, hesitating.

Despite having amassed millions of Spirit Credits through Evelyn, the deep-seated instincts of a young man who had spent years counting every single credit to make his life better made his fingers freeze.
Dropping tens of millions of credits on a decorative necklace felt completely foreign and almost terrifyingly reckless.
’It’s for Elu... so why won’t my hand move?’
A self-conscious flush crept up the back of Silas’s neck.
Harper, watching him like a hawk from the side, instantly spotted his hesitation.
A wide mischievous grin spread across her face as she leaned over, aggressively poking his muscular ribs with her elbow.

"Look at you!" Harper giggled delightedly, nudging his broad shoulder. "A terrifying Lord like you who who obliterates monster hordes without flinching is getting all shy over a pretty green necklace! What’s the matter, Silas? Afraid to spend a little pocket change on yourself? Go on, press the button! Or do I need to hold your big scary hand while you do it?!"
Seraphina glanced up from his lap, her sharp crimson eyes softening with a rare affectionate amusement as she rested her manicured hand gently over his.

"Do not hesitate, Silas," Seraphina encouraged softly, her voice sounding remarkably tender. "A true Lord takes whatever pleases his eye... If your private liquidity is insufficient, Reginald’s black card is at your disposal. You can consider it my personal gift to your territory."
"I have my own money," Silas grunted, his face turning slightly redder under their combined teasing.
Steeling his resolve, Silas firmly keyed his bid into the numerical grid.
BZZZZT-CHUNK.
[BID OVERRIDE: VIP SUITE SEVEN]
CURRENT BID: 45,000,000 SPIRIT CREDITS
Across the arena in VIP Suite Twelve, Cedric Blackwood’s eye twitched so violently it looked like a medical seizure.
But having already learned the brutal lesson of Suite Seven’s bottomless pockets, the young noble simply ground his teeth into dust and refrained from touching his console.
BANG!
"Sold! To VIP Suite Seven for Forty-Five Million Spirit Credits!"
Silas leaned back into the sofa, letting out a long satisfied breath.
’Eluned is going to love it...’
Once the dam was broken, Silas did not hold back.

When Lot Twenty-Nine arrived... a colossal reinforced adamantine shipping crate containing eight tons of newly discovered Astral Void-Titanium Alloy harvested from a fallen meteor in the Deep Wastes... The Upgrade System practically hummed with hungry anticipation inside his soul.
There was no tab but Silas could feel it.
’Or maybe that’s an excuse for me to get more ores...’

Recognizing the immense value the rare metal would provide for upgrading the Blessed Land’s defensive walls and forging high-tier weaponry for his troops, Silas hammered the console, securing the entire eight-ton shipment for Seventy Million Spirit Credits.
’I hate myself...’
Then, Lot Thirty-Two was brought to the stage. It was called the Scepter of the Dune-Sovereign.
It was a Tier-3 staff carved from petrified desert gold, topped with a swirling orb of concentrated earth mana that could manipulate tectonic currents and summon devastating sandstorms.

Silas immediately thought of Kadi, the sandy-haired earth mage who had absolutely demolished the Mage Royale tournament by going berserk on her opponents, then turned around and acted sweet and innocent immediately after.
She was his Second Secretary now.

’Fuck, she’s been making do with that cheap wooden training staff since the tournament,’ Silas thought as a flash of guilt crossing his mind. ’I gave her the Realm Seed and the Secretary title... She deserves something that can actually handle her raw output. This scepter is a perfect fit for someone who fights like she does.’
Silas dropped Sixty-Five Million Spirit Credits without a second thought, claiming the scepter for his loyal battle-hungry spellcaster.
Finally, as Lot Thirty-Six was wheeled into the spotlight, Silas’s eyes locked onto a massive multi-tiered display rack.
Resting on the velvet tiers was an entire military battalion set... There were Seventy Matching Frost-Drake Carapace Bucklers and Runic Short-Spears.

Forged from the indestructible ice-scales and razor fangs of sub-zero rift beasts, the shields were lightweight, impervious to elemental frost, and engraved with deflection runes, while the short-spears thrummed with piercing cold.
The entire set was tailored specifically for high-mobility melee shield-maidens.
’Haah... I remember I still owe the girls gifts from the Mage Tournament...’
He wanted to give them gifts as well, plus Thora as well as the new Dwarves could also mass produce this or so with the new alloy he bought for the mages.
"I am taking the entire set," Silas declared firmly as Seraphina as well as Harper gave him a proud nod. "Please don’t hate me..."
He slammed his palm against the terminal, entering an uncontested bid of One Hundred and Twenty Million Spirit Credits.
’I already hate myself enough. Look at how much money I’m spending!’
BANG!
"Sold! To VIP Suite Seven for One Hundred and Twenty Million Spirit Credits!"
By the time the auctioneer’s gavel struck the podium, the entire amphitheater had descended into an uproar of terrified speculation.
Masked merchants, syndicate bosses, and foreign Lords in the lower tiers were craning their necks, staring up at the dark impenetrable glass of Suite Seven in utter disbelief.
"Who in the gods’ names is in Suite Seven?!"
"They’ve spent over four hundred million credits in the last two hours alone!"
"Is that an Imperial Plenipotentiary from the Central Alliance?!"
"They’re buying weapons, beast cores, raw alloys, and entire battalion armories... whoever they are, they aren’t just rich... they’re outfitting an entire private army!"
Inside VIP Suite Twelve, Cedric Blackwood had completely collapsed into the cushions of his sofa.
His expensive cigar had tumbled from his limp fingers, burning a hole into the emerald rug.
His slicked-back blond hair was thoroughly disheveled with strands falling over his pale sweaty forehead and his hands were trembling with pure rage.
"Haaah..."
Every single item he had even glanced at had been ruthlessly, effortlessly snatched away by the unseen titan occupying Suite Seven.
Down on the floor, the kneeling maid buried her face deeper into the rug, desperately biting her lower lip to keep from bursting into loud triumphant laughter at her arrogant master’s expression.
CLANG!CLANG! CLANG!
Three deep, somber, and deafening strikes of a massive bronze bell echoed through the amphitheater, cutting through the chaotic murmurs of the crowd like a guillotine.
The ambient sconces across the entire colosseum abruptly extinguished, plunging the multi-tiered arena into pitch-black darkness.
HUMMMMM.
A massive multi-layered defensive barrier of glowing golden runes flickered to life around the perimeter of the circular stage, sealing the auction platform behind twelve feet of reinforced barriers.
The Chief Auctioneer stepped into the center of a singular azure spotlight once more.
His theatrical porcelain demon mask seemed to gleam with dark chilling gravity however this time, he did not smile and he did not bow as well.
His amplified voice dropped into a low electrifying baritone that made the air in every VIP suite feel heavy.

"Honored Lords, sovereign delegates, and masters of the shadows," the auctioneer began. "The preliminary lots are concluded. The time has finally arrived... We have reached the Final Three Lots of The Obsidian Sanhedrin."
A collective breathless roar of excitement erupted from the thousands of spectators, shaking the very bedrock of the cavern.
Inside Suite Seven, Silas, Harper, and Seraphina all leaned forward, their eyes locking onto the dark center of the stage.
CREAK... CHUNK!
The heavy central hydraulic lift groaned as a colossal reinforced adamantine pillar slowly rose from the bedrock beneath the arena.
Resting atop a cushion of dark velvet, bound securely beneath four layers of heavy mana-nullifying chains, was a single ancient weapon.
It was a heavily curved, single-edged pirate saber... a cutlass of magnificent terrifying proportions.
The blade was forged from an entirely unknown luminescent oceanic alloy that shimmered with shifting ethereal hues of seafoam green and liquid silver.

Intricate wave-like Damascus patterns rippled across the metal like living oceanic currents, and the hilt was wrapped in the dark calcified leather of an ancient sea serpent, guarded by a solid-gold basket hilt intricately sculpted in the likeness of a roaring leviathan’s jaws.
Even resting inert and bound beneath the suppression chains, the sound of crashing tidal waves and whistling coastal winds echoed from the steel.
"Lot Number Thirty-Eight!" the auctioneer projected, his voice carrying a weight that silenced the murmuring crowd. "The Tide-Bringer of the Leviathan’s Wake..."
The auctioneer stepped closer to the pedestal, his gloved hand hovering over the golden basket hilt.
He didn’t launch into a lengthy historical lecture as instead, he simply spoke one word.
"Observe."
He lightly tapped the golden hilt with a single, concentrated drop of his own mana.
FWOOOOOOOOOSH!
The transformation was instantaneous and terrifying.
The luminescent oceanic alloy of the curved blade flared with a blinding incandescent azure light that swallowed the entire stage.
BOOOOOOOOOM!
A colossal suffocating tidal wave of pure phantom oceanic mana detonated outward from the steel, completely shattering the stage’s dampeners in an instant.
Within a fraction of a second, the entire multi-tiered colosseum was violently submerged in a place that looked like it was the deep ocean floor.
Thousands of spectators gasped, frantically clutching their throats in sudden paralyzed terror as the air in their lungs felt as suffocating as pressurized seawater at ten thousand meters depth.

The deafening primeval roar of colossal abyssal leviathans echoed directly inside their skulls, accompanied by the chilling visual of towering hundred-meter-tall ghost waves crashing through the stone ceiling.
Even inside VIP Suite Seven, protected behind three layers of enchanted obsidian glass, Silas felt the crushing weight of the sea press against his ribs.
’It seems familiar...’

His Mythic Gold Core flared instinctively with golden sovereign conduits igniting beneath his skin to effortlessly neutralize the atmospheric pressure, while Harper and Seraphina both gasped, their elemental auras flaring to resist the crushing phantom tide.
FZZZT!
The auctioneer abruptly severed his mana flow.

The blinding azure light extinguished, the roaring phantom waves vanished into thin air, and the suffocating oceanic pressure instantly dissipated, leaving thousands of masked bidders coughing, sweating profusely, and clutching their chests in shock.
The auctioneer stood tall beside the silent, glowing saber. He let the silence stretch for a long, deliberate moment before he spoke again.

"Fragmented naval logs recovered alongside the wreckage suggest this blade belonged to an SSS-Rank being... one whose name has been struck from every official record... What remains is this... the steel remembers and... it is hungry."

The auctioneer abruptly severed his mana flow.

The blinding azure light extinguished, the roaring phantom waves vanished into thin air, and the suffocating oceanic pressure instantly dissipated, leaving thousands of masked bidders coughing, sweating profusely, and clutching their chests in shock.
The auctioneer stood tall beside the silent, glowing saber.
He let the silence stretch for a long, deliberate moment before he spoke again.
"Fragmented naval logs recovered alongside the wreckage suggest this blade belonged to an SSS-Rank being... one whose name has been struck from every official record...
What remains is this... the steel remembers and... it is hungry."

chapters.title: Chapter 399: Obsidian Sanhedrin [V]
paragraphs: The amphitheater of the Obsidian Sanhedrin hung suspended in a suffocating quiet.
Above the circular red-obsidian stage, the vapor of salt spray, briny sea-wrack, and freezing oceanic pressure still curled through the air, carrying the phantom aroma of the untamed deep.

Down upon the central display pedestal, the single-edged curved cutlass... The Tide-Bringer of the Leviathan’s Wake lay motionless, resting against its dark velvet cushion while bound beneath four heavy sets of mana-suppression chains.
The faint sound of crashing waves still hummed along its fuller with a whisper that resonated within the bone marrow of every Awakened Lord in the room.
The Chief Auctioneer stood proudly beneath the dazzling white spotlights.

He rested his gloved hands against the floating obsidian podium, his demon mask casting sharp theatrical shadows across his features as he looked up toward the surrounding tiers of private VIP suites and the crowded stone benches below.

"Honored patrons," the auctioneer’s booming voice rolled through the large room clearly. "Reasonably speaking, our historical scholars and appraisal masters cannot fully ascertain whether the legendary commander of The Leviathan’s Wake was an SSS-Rank Entity or a calamity walking the razor-thin border of that mythic realm! The records pulled from the depths are fragmented by centuries of corrosive abyssal tides. However, the undeniable presence and the majesty of this blade speak with authority! This is a Tier-4 Sovereign Relic of pure oceanic dominion!"
He reached out, his fingers wrapping around the polished haft of his gold-headed gavel, and brought it down against the sounding block with a sharp sound that echoed off the vaulted bedrock ceiling.
BANG!

"We shall open the bidding for Lot Number Thirty-Eight at an aggressive, premier valuation!" the auctioneer projected with electric showmanship, his arm sweeping across the dark expanse of the colosseum. "The starting price is One Hundred Million Spirit Credits! Increments of ten million! The floor is open!"
Inside VIP Suite Seven, Silas leaned forward on the emerald-leather sectional, his dark hair falling across his brow.
Through the one-way panoramic glass, his blue eyes ringed with the subtle dormant gold locked onto the curved shimmering steel resting on the stage.
’Ah... It still feels familiar.’
There was something undeniably magnetic about the cutlass.

It was not a sterile ornamental blade meant for sheltered aristocrats parading through academy halls... It was a brutal, weather-beaten instrument of pure conquest, built to cleave through roaring sea monsters and shatter hull plating amidst howling abyssal squalls.
’I don’t know why I think it’s something that Morwenna knows...’
The faint rhythmic crash of phantom waves that bled from its fuller seemed to call out to something deep within his soul.

For a man who was actively building his own domain from the ground up, the idea of claiming a maritime relic tied directly to the legendary central waters of the Sovereign Realm stirred an instinctive hunger in his chest.
’And not to mention I can make Morwenna happy too...’

He could already envision Morwenna’s reaction if he brought this blade back to the Blessed Land... the way her stormy gray eyes would widen, the way her weathered fingers would trace the golden basket hilt with a trembling look on her face.
’She’s so cute...’
Silas reached toward the polished brass bidding terminal resting on the mahogany coffee table before him.
Down on the lower tiers and across the mid-level corporate balconies, the arena erupted into immediate, chaotic activity.
BEEP! BEEP! BEEP!
[CURRENT BID: 140,000,000 SC - FLOOR TIER 1]
[CURRENT BID: 180,000,000 SC - VIP SUITE FOUR]
[CURRENT BID: 230,000,000 SC - FLOOR TIER 2]
[CURRENT BID: 300,000,000 SC - VIP SUITE NINE]
Within less than twenty seconds, the digital scoreboard suspended above the stage surged past the three-hundred-million mark, the flashing crimson runes climbing with unrelenting speed.
’I still think it’s a bit cheap... is it because they’re not sure or are they trying to highball it?’
Silas’s hand halted three inches above the polished interface.
His dark eyebrows drew together as he watched the numbers climb.
’Haah... Not again...’
Even with Harper constantly insisting that House Whitmore would cover the entire ledger, Silas possessed a bit of a stubborn pride.
’I can do hundreds of millions but at this rate, it’s going to go into a billion.’
Spending a billion on an impulse buy especially when the primary objective of Harper’s date was still waiting in the wings felt reckless.
Silas let out a quiet breath through his nose with his shoulders settling back against the leather cushions as he began to withdraw his hand.

’Three hundred million for a sidearm... as much as I want to see what that oceanic alloy can do under my system upgrades, there should be a reasonable limit to another person’s money. Or I’ll ask for permission an—’
Before his fingers could fully pull away, a pale slender hand shot past his shoulder.
Harper Whitmore didn’t just tap the console.

With a bright wicked grin spreading across her lips, the purple-haired Lightning Lord slammed her palm flat against the custom numeric grid, her fingers flying over the runes with effortless fluid speed.
BZZZZT-CHUNK!
A violent blinding flare of scarlet light detonated across the central holographic projection ring above the stage, completely overriding the active bid stream with an authoritative system chime.
[BID: VIP SUITE SEVEN]
CURRENT BID: 1,000,000,000 SPIRIT CREDITS
A heavy stillness dropped over the amphitheater like a falling guillotine.
Down on the lower tiers, masked syndicate leaders froze with their transponder wands held halfway in the air.
In the private merchant balconies, crystal wine chalices remained halted inches from open mouths.
Even the Chief Auctioneer stood entirely rigid upon the red obsidian platform, his mouth hanging open behind his demon mask as he stared up at the massive glowing ten-digit figure.
A direct leap from three hundred million straight to One Billion Spirit Credits?!
Inside VIP Suite Seven, Silas slowly turned his head, his deadpan gaze settling on Harper.
"Harper... did you really just drop one billion credits on a pirate saber?"
"I sure did!" Harper replied cheerfully, her voice brimming with glee as she propped her elbow on the mahogany table and tossed her violet curls over her shoulder.
The way she said it made it sound like she’d just bought a cup of coffee rather than a billion-credit relic.
Sitting directly on Silas’s lap, Seraphina shifted her weight, the silk of her crimson gown rustling softly against his trousers.
She adjusted her posture, resting her back firmly against his chest while her sharp crimson eyes narrowed at the glowing scoreboard.
A delicate and slightly irritated click of her tongue escaped her lips.

"You acted with excessive haste, Harper," Seraphina murmured, crossing her arms beneath her generous bust and looking sideways at the terminal. "I had already planned to do so... Fuck you. You deliberately intervened to deprive me of presenting Silas with a suitable tribute."
"Too slow on the trigger, Princess!" Harper laughed, leaning in close to Silas and boldly wrapping both of her arms around his muscular neck.

She pressed her cheek against his shoulder, her violet eyes sparkling with bright mischievous affection. "I saw the look in his eyes the second that blade started releasing phantom seawater. Silas likes pirates... Silas wanted the sword... Therefore, I am buying it for him. End of story!"

"Harper," Silas muttered, an awkward self-conscious warmth creeping up the back of his neck as he found himself caught between two noblewomen competing to casually throw generational fortunes at his feet.
"You have your own objective for being here right? You don’t need to burn a billion credits on an impulse purchase for me."
There had to be a limit to things.

"Don’t worry about my financial allocation, handsome," Harper whispered, her warm breath brushing against his ear as she gave his broad shoulder a reassuring squeeze. "Even after deducting a billion from our regional venture funds, I still have more than enough liquid capital to steamroll whoever stands between me and the grand finale. Besides... seeing that flustered, sheepish look on your face is worth ten times that amount."
Silas let out a low defeated chuckle with his lips curving into a reluctant touched smile.
The genuine warmth in her voice, the certainty with which she threw her resources behind him, made it impossible to stay annoyed.
Seeing him smile, Harper’s heart did a light happy flip in her chest.
’Ah cute... and he trusts me more now too, can I get a kiss this time?’
She opened her mouth, ready to deliver another smug, teasing remark—
BZZZZT-CHUNK!
A sharp abrasive mechanical chime echoed from across the arena.
Over on the western balcony, the holographic display of VIP Suite Twelve flared with golden runes.
[BID: VIP SUITE TWELVE]
CURRENT BID: 1,100,000,000 SPIRIT CREDITS
Inside Suite Twelve, Cedric Blackwood was breathing heavily, his neat, slicked-back blond hair falling into damp disordered strands across his forehead.
He was no longer reclining on the sofa with his boots resting on his maid.
He had bolted to his feet, his hands slamming down onto the mahogany console with enough violent force to rattle the brass fixtures, his pale gray eyes bulging with unhinged fury.

"I will not let them take it!" Cedric hissed through clenched teeth, his voice shaking with venom. "They have spent the entire night mocking me! Suite Seven thinks they can walk over House Blackwood without consequence?! I will buy this blade, drag it back to my estate, and use it as a fire poker just to spit on their arrogance!"
His fingers flew across the terminal, entering another frantic counter-bid without even consulting the maid.
The numbers on the screen blurred before his eyes...he didn’t care. He couldn’t let them win.
...Not again.
Down on the emerald carpet, the brown-haired maid remained on her hands and knees, her forehead pressed flat against the floorboards.

Her shoulders ached from having Cedric’s combat boots grinding into her neck for the past two hours, but as she listened to her master blindly commit over a billion credits to an emotional spite bid, a cold sickening dread settled into her chest.
If Lord Valerius arrived to discover that the Thorne family’s emergency reserves had been squandered on petty vengeance, the fallout would be catastrophic.
Yet, deep beneath that fear, an intoxicating quiet satisfaction began to stir in her stomach.
She had spent the entire night watching Suite Seven operate. She knew with terrifying certainty what was about to happen.
Back in VIP Suite Seven, Harper didn’t even flinch.
Her violet eyes narrowed with cold dismissive amusement as she looked across the vast amphitheater toward Suite Twelve.
"Oh, look at little House trying to puff his chest out," Harper sneered, her lips curving into a sharp smirk. "How utterly precious."
Without a second of hesitation, Harper reached down and pressed the maximum multiplier rune on the interface.
BZZZZT-CHUNK!
[BID: VIP SUITE SEVEN]
CURRENT BID: 1,500,000,000 SPIRIT CREDITS
In Suite Twelve, Cedric’s legs gave out completely.
He collapsed backward onto the velvet cushions, his mouth hanging open in paralyzed horror.
His throat worked soundlessly, his breath coming in dry wheezing gasps.
’I don’t want to bid higher... I still need to...’
Down on the floor, the kneeling maid buried her face into the emerald rug, biting down on her lip until she tasted copper to keep from laughing out loud at her master’s humiliating ruin.
Down on the circular stage, the Chief Auctioneer stared at the glowing display for three seconds before slamming his gavel onto the podium with a deafening crack.
BANG!
"One point five billion Spirit Credits! Going once! Going twice!"
BANG!
"SOLD! To the sovereign delegates of VIP Suite Seven!"
A deafening roar of awe and disbelief rippled through the spectators on the lower tiers.
The auctioneer bowed deeply toward the dark, reflective glass of Suite Seven, his voice carrying immense professional reverence.

"Our deepest congratulations to the esteemed patrons of Suite Seven," the auctioneer announced, gesturing toward the stage floor. "Our research division is currently finalizing the decryption of the naval logs recovered alongside the weapon. A comprehensive historical dossier detailing the known exploits of the pirate captain and The Leviathan’s Wake shall be delivered directly to your private reward vault alongside the blade upon the conclusion of tonight’s proceedings!"
With a deep hydraulic rumble, the adamantine pillar smoothly descended into the bedrock, carrying the glowing cutlass away.
The Chief Auctioneer took a slow measured breath, accepting a crystal glass of water from a masked stagehand.
He smoothed down the gold-embroidered lapels of his crimson coat, stepping back into the center of the brilliant white spotlight.
The atmosphere throughout the amphitheater, already charged with astronomical tension, grew noticeably heavier as the stage’s defensive runes flared with an intense violet hue.

"Honored Lords, sovereign delegates, and masters of the shadows," the auctioneer began, his voice dropping into a solemn reverence that commanded total silence. "We now bring forth Lot Number Thirty-Nine... the penultimate treasure of the Obsidian Sanhedrin."
CREAK... CHUNK!
